login.reset.passwordPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the New password field on the screen opened from a password-reset email, where a new password is chosen. Lower case in English on purpose.

login.reset.confirmLabel.description: Label of the field where the new password is typed a second time, on the screen opened from a password-reset email, where a new password is chosen. Confirm is a verb.

login.reset.confirmPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the Confirm new password field on the screen opened from a password-reset email, where a new password is chosen. Lower case in English on purpose.

login.reset.submit.description: Main button on the screen opened from a password-reset email, where a new password is chosen: saves the new password.

login.reset.back.description: Button under the form on the screen opened from a password-reset email, where a new password is chosen: returns to the sign-in form without changing the password.

login.reset.expired.text: This reset link is invalid or has expired. Go back to login and request a new one from "Forgot password?".
login.reset.expired.description: Error on the screen opened from a password-reset email, where a new password is chosen, when the link that opened it can no longer be used. The quoted words are the label of the Forgot password? link on the sign-in screen and must match its translation.

login.reset.passwordTooShort.text: Password must be at least 8 characters
login.reset.passwordTooShort.description: Error on the screen opened from a password-reset email, where a new password is chosen, when the new password is shorter than 8 characters.

login.reset.passwordMismatch.description: Error on the screen opened from a password-reset email, where a new password is chosen, when the two password fields differ.

login.reset.failed.description: Error on the screen opened from a password-reset email, where a new password is chosen, when the server refused the new password and gave no reason of its own.

signInSheet.account.welcome.description: Title of the sign-in sheet on the last step of making an account, in place of "Finish your account", when the person arrived by the link in the email saying they were let in from the waitlist and that link signed them in. {{email}} is their email address.

login.signup.finishing.description: Status on the last step of signing in with an email code while the account is being finished and signed in.

adult.title.description: Heading of the sheet asked the first time a person opens a wallet, tokens, staking, node or passport feature.

adult.lead.text: Wallets, tokens, staking, nodes and passport proofs are for adults only.
adult.lead.description: Sentence under the heading of the 18 or older sheet: says why it is asked.

adult.privacy.text: We only keep your answer, never your date of birth. We ask once.
adult.privacy.description: Small print on the 18 or older sheet: what is recorded.

adult.yes.description: Main button on the 18 or older sheet: records that the person is an adult and opens the feature.

adult.under.description: Second button on the 18 or older sheet: closes it without opening the feature.

adult.underToast.text: Wallets, tokens, staking, nodes and passport proofs are for people 18 and older. Everything else in Homeroom is still yours to use.
adult.underToast.description: Short notice shown after a person answers that they are under 18 on the 18 or older sheet.

adult.failed.text: Your answer could not be saved. Try again.
adult.failed.description: Error under the 18 or older sheet's text when saving the answer failed.

guest.hero.line.text: Look around and try what we're making.
guest.hero.line.description: Line under the welcome headline on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees, above the platform's public projects. Invites them to look around the projects below and try them; "we" is the people who make them on Homeroom.

guest.hero.joinWaitlist.description: Filled button for making an account while new accounts start on a waitlist: in the top bar of the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees, beside Sign in, and under the headline where the guest Discover is drawn in one of the looks. Opens the sheet that makes an account, which then waits to be let in to Homeroom.

guest.hero.signUp.description: Filled button under the welcome headline on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees, once new accounts no longer wait: opens the sheet that makes an account.

guest.hero.headline.text: The app library anyone can edit
guest.hero.headline.description: Headline of the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees, above the platform's public apps. Homeroom is a collection of apps that the people who use them can change, the way anyone can edit an article on Wikipedia.

guest.hero.sub.text: <0>Community apps you can build together.</0> <1>Like Wikipedia, but for software.</1>
guest.hero.sub.description: Line under the headline on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees, above the platform's public apps. Two short sentences, each drawn on a line of its own: <0></0> holds what the apps here are, <1></1> the comparison with Wikipedia, the encyclopedia anyone can edit. Keep the name Wikipedia as written.

guest.hero.explore.description: Button under the signed-out landing's headline. Pressing it scrolls the page down to the list of communities and their apps, which starts just below.

guest.hero.month.title.description: Title of the small card beside the headline on the guest Discover, and on a phone the label in front of the same two figures: they count the last 30 days across Homeroom's public apps.

guest.hero.month.changes_one.description: One of the two figures under "This month" on the guest Discover: how many changes to public apps went live in the last 30 days. {{total}} is that number, already formatted, and is drawn large inside <0></0>; the word after it is its label.

guest.hero.month.changes_other.description: One of the two figures under "This month" on the guest Discover: how many changes to public apps went live in the last 30 days. {{total}} is that number, already formatted, and is drawn large inside <0></0>; the word after it is its label.

guest.hero.month.contributors_one.description: One of the two figures under "This month" on the guest Discover: how many different people made the changes that went live in public apps in the last 30 days. {{total}} is that number, already formatted, and is drawn large inside <0></0>; the word after it is its label.

guest.hero.month.contributors_other.description: One of the two figures under "This month" on the guest Discover: how many different people made the changes that went live in public apps in the last 30 days. {{total}} is that number, already formatted, and is drawn large inside <0></0>; the word after it is its label.

guest.search.open.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the round magnifying-glass button on the "Communities" heading of the guest Discover: shows the search field, which filters this device's pinned apps and communities and the public communities below.

guest.search.close.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the × button at the end of the guest Discover's search field: empties the field and puts it away again.

guest.header.signIn.description: Button in the top bar of the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: opens the sign-in sheet for somebody who already has an account.

guest.header.signUp.description: Button at the right of the signed-out Discover's top bar, beside Sign in: opens the sheet that makes an account.

guest.search.placeholder.description: Placeholder in the search field on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome.

guest.search.label.description: Accessible name of the search field on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome.

guest.categories.label.description: Accessible name of the row of buttons that filter the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome by kind of app (Games, Tools and so on).

guest.category.all.description: Filter button on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: shows every kind of app.

guest.category.games.description: Filter button on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: shows only games.

guest.category.social.description: Filter button on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: shows only social apps.

guest.category.tools.description: Filter button on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: shows only tools.

guest.category.learning.description: Filter button on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: shows only apps for learning.

guest.category.creative.description: Filter button on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: shows only creative apps.

guest.category.money.description: Filter button on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: shows only apps about budgets, trading, splitting bills or a till.

guest.category.health.description: Filter button on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: shows only apps about gym logs, runs or habits.

guest.category.food.description: Filter button on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: shows only apps about recipes, baking, coffee or planning a meal together.

guest.category.other.description: Filter button on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: shows apps that are none of the other kinds.

guest.featured.description: Small heading over the row of apps the platform features, on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome.

guest.all.description: Small heading over the grid of every app on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome.

guest.showMore.description: Button under the More projects list on the signed-out Discover: shows the next twelve projects.

guest.results.description: Small heading over the grid of apps on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome while a search or a kind of app narrows it.

guest.sort.label.description: Accessible name of the control that orders the apps on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome.

guest.sort.trending.description: Sort option on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: the apps the most people use first.

guest.sort.new.description: Sort option on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: the newest apps first.

guest.sort.built.description: Sort option on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome: the apps the most people have built first.

guest.project.before.description: Small label on the left picture of a change up for a vote, on a project's page for people who are not signed in: how the project looks now.

guest.project.after.description: Small label on the right picture of a change up for a vote, on a project's page for people who are not signed in: how the project would look with the change.

guest.waitlist.lead.text: We'll email you when your spot is ready. Until then, every public project is open to you.
guest.waitlist.lead.description: On the card over the list of public projects, for a person who has an account but is still on the waitlist.

guest.waitlist.leadEmail.text: We'll email {{email}} when your spot is ready. Until then, every public project is open to you.
guest.waitlist.leadEmail.description: On the card over the list of public projects, for a person who has an account but is still on the waitlist. {{email}} is the address the invitation will go to.

guest.project.voteLater.text: You can vote once you're in
guest.project.voteLater.description: In place of the Vote button on a change, for a person who has an account but is still on the waitlist.

guest.project.joinLater.text: You can join once you're in
guest.project.joinLater.description: On a project's page, for a person who has an account but is still on the waitlist: under 'The chat is for members', in place of the Join button.

guest.card.week_one.description: On a project's card on the signed-out Discover, when its counts are too small to show: how many of its changes the group voted in and went live in the last seven days.

guest.card.week_other.description: On a project's card on the signed-out Discover, when its counts are too small to show: how many of its changes the group voted in and went live in the last seven days.

guest.card.changes_one.description: On a large featured community card of the signed-out landing, after its member count and a dot: how many of its changes the group has voted in, for example "1 change".

guest.card.changes_other.description: On a large featured community card of the signed-out landing, after its member count and a dot: how many of its changes the group has voted in, for example "34 changes".

guest.card.new.description: Small label on the picture of an app made in the last two weeks, on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome.

guest.card.peopleLabel_one.description: Screen-reader name of a project's card on Communities to join, on Home signed in or out, and on the signed-out landing: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together). The card's picture shows the number beside a profile glyph, the card's only count; this says it in words with the project's name, and that it counts people who used it lately, not members. {{name}} is the project's name. {{count}} is 1 in English; other languages may use this form for other numbers too.

guest.card.peopleLabel_other.description: Screen-reader name of a project's card on Communities to join, on Home signed in or out, and on the signed-out landing: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together). The card's picture shows the number beside a profile glyph, the card's only count; this says it in words with the project's name, and that it counts people who used it lately, not members. {{name}} is the project's name. {{count}} is the number.

guest.card.tryIt.description: Button that opens an app for a visitor with no account, on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome and on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together).

guest.loading.description: Accessible name of the placeholders shown while the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome loads its apps.

guest.loadFailed.text: The apps couldn't be loaded right now.
guest.loadFailed.description: Shown on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome when its list of apps could not be read.

guest.retry.description: Button under the failure line on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: reads the list of public apps again.

guest.empty.description: Shown on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: the platform's public apps ("projects" people build together) under a short welcome when a search or a kind of app leaves nothing.

guest.emptyAll.description: Shown on the guest Discover, the first screen a signed-out visitor sees, when the directory holds no apps at all and no search or kind of app is narrowing it.

guest.join.vote.title.description: One of three things an account adds, in the welcome at the top of the guest Discover (the first screen a signed-out visitor sees, over the platform's public apps): voting on the changes proposed to an app.

guest.join.vote.body.text: Every change to an app goes to its community for a vote.
guest.join.vote.body.description: The line under "Vote on what changes" in the welcome at the top of the guest Discover, shown on wider screens.

guest.join.ask.title.description: One of three things an account adds, in the welcome at the top of the guest Discover (the first screen a signed-out visitor sees): asking an app's community for a feature.

guest.join.ask.body.text: Post an idea, and the community can build it.
guest.join.ask.body.description: The line under "Ask for what you want" in the welcome at the top of the guest Discover, shown on wider screens.

guest.join.make.title.description: One of three things an account adds, in the welcome at the top of the guest Discover (the first screen a signed-out visitor sees): starting an app of your own.

guest.join.make.body.text: Start an app for your friends, family or club.
guest.join.make.body.description: The line under "Make your own" in the welcome at the top of the guest Discover, shown on wider screens.

guest.project.allCommunities.description: Chip at the top of the signed-out page of a public project: goes back to Home, where every community is listed.

guest.project.card.pause.description: Button on the project card's moving preview, on the signed-out page of a public project and a project's hub: pauses the silent loop of the real app.

guest.project.card.play.description: Button on the project card's paused preview, on the signed-out page of a public project and a project's hub: plays the silent loop of the real app again.

guest.project.card.previewLabel.description: Label on the project card's moving preview, on the signed-out page of a public project and a project's hub: the loop is a recording of the app itself.

guest.project.openNamed.description: Main button on the project card on the signed-out page of a public project, when the app can be used without an account. {{project}} is the project's name.

guest.project.signUpToOpen.description: Main button on the project card on the signed-out page of a public project, when the app needs an account: opens the sign-up sheet.

guest.project.needsAccountPlay.text: {{project}} needs a free account to play.
guest.project.needsAccountPlay.description: Line under the buttons on the project card of a game on the signed-out page of a public project, when it needs an account. {{project}} is the game's name.

guest.project.needsAccountUse.text: {{project}} needs a free account to use.
guest.project.needsAccountUse.description: Line under the buttons on the project card on the signed-out page of a public project, when the app needs an account. {{project}} is the project's name.

guest.project.activeWeek_one.description: Who is around on the signed-out page of a public project: how many people took part in the project this week. A number only, never a name.

guest.project.activeWeek_other.description: Who is around on the signed-out page of a public project: how many people took part in the project this week. A number only, never a name.

guest.project.audienceMembers_one.description: Who it is for and how many are in it, on the signed-out page of a public project. <0> is the audience's name in bold.

guest.project.audienceMembers_other.description: Who it is for and how many are in it, on the signed-out page of a public project. <0> is the audience's name in bold.

guest.project.whatItsLike.description: Small-caps label over a sideways row of pictures of the app, on the signed-out page of a public project.

guest.project.madeTogether.description: Small-caps label over the card that says how the project is made, on the signed-out page of a public project.

guest.project.madeByPlayers.text: Made by the people who play it.
guest.project.madeByPlayers.description: Title of the Made together card on the signed-out page of a game.

guest.project.madeByUsers.text: Made by the people who use it.
guest.project.madeByUsers.description: Title of the Made together card on the signed-out page of a public project that is not a game.

guest.project.madeHow.text: Anyone can ask for a change. Members vote on what goes in, and it's live a few minutes after the vote.
guest.project.madeHow.description: How a change gets in, on the Made together card of the signed-out page of a public project, when no change went live this month.

guest.project.madeHowMonth_one.text: Anyone can ask for a change. Members vote on what goes in, and it's live a few minutes after the vote. {{count}} change went live this month.
guest.project.madeHowMonth_one.description: How a change gets in, on the Made together card of the signed-out page of a public project, with how many changes went live in the last thirty days.

guest.project.madeHowMonth_other.text: Anyone can ask for a change. Members vote on what goes in, and it's live a few minutes after the vote. {{count}} changes went live this month.
guest.project.madeHowMonth_other.description: How a change gets in, on the Made together card of the signed-out page of a public project, with how many changes went live in the last thirty days.

guest.project.joinToVoteSuggest.description: Button on the Made together card of the signed-out page of a public project: opens the sign-up sheet to join the community.

guest.project.upForVoteCount_one.description: Small-caps label over the changes up for a vote on the signed-out page of a public project, with how many there are.

guest.project.upForVoteCount_other.description: Small-caps label over the changes up for a vote on the signed-out page of a public project, with how many there are.

guest.project.seeAllCount_one.description: Link beside the Up for a vote label on the signed-out page of a public project: shows every change up for a vote in the list.

guest.project.seeAllCount_other.description: Link beside the Up for a vote label on the signed-out page of a public project: shows every change up for a vote in the list.

guest.project.seeAll.description: Link beside the Recently live label on the signed-out page of a public project: shows every recent change in the list.

guest.project.beforeAfter.description: Small label on the picture of a change up for a vote on the signed-out page of a public project: the change has a before and after.

guest.project.yes_one.description: How many members voted yes on a change up for a vote, on its row on the signed-out page of a public project.

guest.project.yes_other.description: How many members voted yes on a change up for a vote, on its row on the signed-out page of a public project.

guest.project.morePill_one.description: Small badge leading the last row of a list on the signed-out page of a public project: how many more there are than the rows above.

guest.project.morePill_other.description: Small badge leading the last row of a list on the signed-out page of a public project: how many more there are than the rows above.

guest.project.moreVotes_one.description: Last row of Up for a vote on the signed-out page of a public project, after the first changes: how many more are up for a vote.

guest.project.moreVotes_other.description: Last row of Up for a vote on the signed-out page of a public project, after the first changes: how many more are up for a vote.

guest.project.recentlyLive.description: Small-caps label over the latest changes that went live, on the signed-out page of a public project.

guest.project.moreLive_one.description: Last row of Recently live on the signed-out page of a public project: how many more changes went live in the last thirty days than the rows above.

guest.project.moreLive_other.description: Last row of Recently live on the signed-out page of a public project: how many more changes went live in the last thirty days than the rows above.

guest.project.change.back.description: Accessible name of the chip at the top of a change opened from the signed-out page of a public project: back to the project's page. {{project}} is its name, which the chip shows.

guest.project.change.slider.text: Drag to compare before and after
guest.project.change.slider.description: Accessible name of the slider under a change's before and after pictures, on the signed-out page of a public project.

guest.project.change.tally.description: The votes so far on a change opened from the signed-out page of a public project: how many members said yes and no, and that members decide.

guest.project.change.joinToVote.description: Button on a change opened from the signed-out page of a public project: opens the sign-up sheet to vote on it.

guest.project.audience.description: Under a project's name on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): anyone can find and join it.

guest.project.builders_one.description: On a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): how many people built it. {{count}} is 1 in English; other languages may use this form for other numbers too.

guest.project.builders_other.description: On a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): how many people built it. {{count}} is the number.

guest.project.active_one.description: On a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): how many people used it lately. {{count}} is 1 in English; other languages may use this form for other numbers too.

guest.project.active_other.description: On a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): how many people used it lately. {{count}} is the number.

guest.project.signInToUse.description: Button on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together) when the app has no view for visitors yet: opens the sign-in sheet.

guest.project.join.description: Button on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): joining the project's community needs an account, so it opens the sign-in sheet. Join is a verb.

guest.project.share.description: Accessible name of the button on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together) that shares a link to it.

guest.project.linkCopied.description: Short notice after the Share button on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together) copied its link.

guest.project.tab.hub.description: Tab on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): the overview of what is happening in it.

guest.project.tab.workshop.description: Tab on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): the changes up for a vote and the requests.

guest.project.tab.discussion.description: Tab on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): its chat, which is for members.

guest.project.happening.description: Small heading over the list of what is going on in a project, on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together).

guest.project.votesOpen_one.description: Row on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): how many changes its community is voting on. {{count}} is 1 in English; other languages may use this form for other numbers too.

guest.project.votesOpen_other.description: Row on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): how many changes its community is voting on. {{count}} is the number.

guest.project.requestsOpen_one.description: Row on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): how many feature requests and bug reports are open. {{count}} is 1 in English; other languages may use this form for other numbers too.

guest.project.requestsOpen_other.description: Row on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): how many feature requests and bug reports are open. {{count}} is the number.

guest.project.requestsOpenMore.description: Row on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together) when it has more open requests than could be counted. {{total}} is the number counted, always large.

guest.project.updated.description: Row on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): when it last changed. {{when}} is a time such as "3 days ago" or a date.

guest.project.upForVote.description: Small heading over the changes a project's community is voting on, on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together).

guest.project.votedIn.description: Small heading over the last changes a project's community voted in, on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together).

guest.project.peopleLabel.description: Small heading over how many people built and use a project, on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together).

guest.project.fromChat.description: Small heading over the card about a project's chat, on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together).

guest.project.chatMembers.description: On a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): its chat cannot be read without joining.

guest.project.chatJoin.text: Join {{project}} to read along and say hi.
guest.project.chatJoin.description: Line under The chat is for members on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together). {{project}} is the project's name.

guest.project.untitledChange.description: Stands in for the title of a change that has none, on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together).

guest.project.tally.description: Under a change up for a vote on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): how many voted for and against it. {{yes}} and {{no}} are numbers.

guest.project.vote.description: Button on a change up for a vote on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): voting needs an account, so it opens the sign-in sheet. Vote is a verb.

guest.project.noVotes.text: Nothing is up for a vote right now.
guest.project.noVotes.description: Shown on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together)'s Workshop tab when no change is up for a vote.

guest.project.loading.description: Shown on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together) while its changes and requests load.

guest.project.requests.description: Small heading over a project's open feature requests and bug reports, on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together).

guest.project.ask.description: Button on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): asking for a feature needs an account, so it opens the sign-in sheet.

guest.project.moreRequests_one.description: Last row of the requests on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): how many more there are. {{count}} is 1 in English; other languages may use this form for other numbers too.

guest.project.moreRequests_other.description: Last row of the requests on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together): how many more there are. {{count}} is the number.

guest.project.noRequests.text: Nobody has asked for anything yet.
guest.project.noRequests.description: Shown on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together) when it has no open requests.

guest.project.requestsUnavailable.text: The requests can't be shown right now.
guest.project.requestsUnavailable.description: Shown on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together) when its requests could not be read.

guest.sheet.join.description: Title of the sign-in sheet opened by Join on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together). {{project}} is the project's name.

guest.sheet.vote.text: Sign up to vote on this change
guest.sheet.vote.description: Title of the sign-in sheet opened by Vote on a change up for a vote, on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together).

guest.sheet.ask.text: Sign up to ask for something
guest.sheet.ask.description: Title of the sign-in sheet opened by Ask for something on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together).

guest.sheet.chat.description: Title of the sign-in sheet opened from the chat card on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together). {{project}} is the project's name.

guest.sheet.waitlistJoin.text: Create your account to be part of {{project}}
guest.sheet.waitlistJoin.description: Title of the sign-in sheet when a visitor with no account presses Join on a public project's page, while new accounts start on Homeroom's waitlist: it asks them to create an account (which then waits on the waitlist), and they can join the project once they are let in. The sheet itself also signs returning people in. {{project}} is the project's name (a project is an app people build together).

guest.sheet.waitlistVote.text: Create your account to vote on changes
guest.sheet.waitlistVote.description: Title of the sign-in sheet when a visitor with no account presses Vote on a change up for a vote on a public project's page, while new accounts start on Homeroom's waitlist: it asks them to create an account (which then waits on the waitlist), and they can vote once they are let in. The sheet itself also signs returning people in.

guest.sheet.waitlistAsk.text: Create your account to ask for something
guest.sheet.waitlistAsk.description: Title of the sign-in sheet when a visitor with no account presses Ask for something on a public project's page, while new accounts start on Homeroom's waitlist: it asks them to create an account (which then waits on the waitlist), and they can post a request once they are let in. The sheet itself also signs returning people in.

guest.sheet.waitlistChat.text: Create your account to chat in {{project}}
guest.sheet.waitlistChat.description: Title of the sign-in sheet when a visitor with no account tries to chat on a public project's page, while new accounts start on Homeroom's waitlist: it asks them to create an account (which then waits on the waitlist), and they can chat once they are let in. The sheet itself also signs returning people in. {{project}} is the project's name.

guest.sheet.use.description: Title of the sign-in sheet opened by Sign in to use it on a public project's read-only page for a signed-out visitor (a project is an app people build together). {{project}} is the project's name.

signupOptIn.title.description: Heading of the small card on the sign-up form that holds the optional "Send me Homeroom news" checkbox (email or text). Shown only while an account is being created.

signupOptIn.email.text: Send me Homeroom news by email
signupOptIn.email.description: Checkbox on the sign-up form, unticked until the person ticks it: whether Homeroom may email them product news. Shown only while an account is being created, never at sign-in.

signupOptIn.emailNote.text: Product news and tips, now and then. Not required to use Homeroom. Unsubscribe anytime.
signupOptIn.emailNote.description: Small line under the sign-up form's "Send me Homeroom news by email" checkbox: what it means and that it is optional.

signupOptIn.sms.description: Checkbox on the sign-up form for a new account made with a phone number, unticked until the person ticks it: whether Homeroom may send product news by text message to that number.

signupOptIn.smsNote.text: Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to unsubscribe, HELP for help. Not required to use Homeroom.
signupOptIn.smsNote.description: Small line under the sign-up form's "Text me Homeroom news" checkbox: the disclosures marketing text messages need (frequency, costs, how to stop, help) and that it is optional.

facts.pair.description: Joins two short independent facts on one line of a change's page or in a tooltip, for example "Fix the header · by @maya · 3h ago". {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next fact. Only the separator between them is translated.

appBlocked.title.description: Title of the dialog shown when a person tries to open an app they blocked earlier. "Blocked" describes the app: this person chose not to see it.

appBlocked.message.text: You blocked this app. Unblock it in Settings → Blocked apps to open it again.
appBlocked.message.description: Body of the dialog shown when a person tries to open an app they blocked. "Settings → Blocked apps" is the path to a section of Settings; keep the arrow.

appBlocked.openSettings.description: Confirm button of the blocked-app dialog: goes to the Blocked apps section of Settings. "Open" is a verb.

preview.loader.rebuildingTitle.description: Heading on the loading screen of a change's preview (a running test copy of the app) when the preview had been paused and is being started again.

preview.loader.rebuildingSub.text: The preview was paused after a while of inactivity. Rebuilding it from the session’s latest changes. This usually takes 20–60 seconds.
preview.loader.rebuildingSub.description: Explanation under the heading on the loading screen of a change's preview while a paused preview is rebuilt. "Session" is the change being built.

preview.loader.loadingTitle.description: Heading on the loading screen of a change's preview (a running test copy of the app) while it opens.

preview.loader.loadingSub.text: Automated checks are running against this preview, so the first load may be a little slower.
preview.loader.loadingSub.description: Explanation under the heading on the loading screen of a change's preview when the platform's automated checks are using the same preview.

launch.cover.opening.description: Small note under an app's icon and name on the cover shown while the app is being opened.

launch.cover.slow.text: This is taking longer than expected…
launch.cover.slow.description: Note that replaces "Opening…" on the cover shown while an app opens, once it has taken unusually long.

appStatus.sample.text: Preview sample app. You can try its discussion, favorites, reporting and blocking. No live app is deployed here.
appStatus.sample.description: Message shown in place of an app on a test build of Homeroom, for a made-up sample app that has no running version.

appStatus.spinningUp.description: Message shown in place of an app while its first deployment is still starting.

appStatus.awaitingSecrets.text: Awaiting required secrets. Deploy is blocked.
appStatus.awaitingSecrets.description: Message shown in place of an app that cannot be deployed until its required secrets (private configuration values such as API keys) are entered. The names of the missing secrets are listed under it.

appStatus.configureSecrets.description: Button under the message that an app is waiting for its secrets: opens the dialog where the secrets (private configuration values such as API keys) are entered.

appStatus.failed.description: Message shown in place of an app whose deployment failed. The reason, when known, is shown under it.

appStatus.viewBuildLog.description: Button under the message that an app failed to start: opens the log of the failed build. "Build" is a noun here.

appStatus.notAvailable.description: Message shown in place of an app that is not running and has no more specific state to report.

appStatus.checking.description: The only line shown in place of an app while Homeroom asks the server whether the project's first version is live yet.

appStatus.needsConnection.text: This app needs a connection. Reconnect to open it.
appStatus.needsConnection.description: Message shown in place of an app when the device is offline and the app has not been saved for offline use.

appStatus.unsafe.description: Message shown in place of an app whose address would not keep it separated from Homeroom, so Homeroom refuses to open it.

appStatus.unsafeDetail.text: Its address is not isolated from Homeroom.
appStatus.unsafeDetail.description: Smaller line under "This app cannot open safely." giving the reason. "Homeroom" is the product's name.

firstVersion.reviewPlan.description: Button on a new project's App tab while Homeroom bot waits for its maker to agree to the plan for the first version: opens the chat with Homeroom bot where the plan is.

firstVersion.openBot.description: Quiet link on a new project's App tab while its first version is being built: opens this person's chat with Homeroom bot. "Open" is a verb; "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant.

firstVersion.opensWhenReady.text: It opens here when it’s ready.
firstVersion.opensWhenReady.description: Line under a new project's card on its App tab while the first version is being built, for everyone but the person who started the project. "It" is the app.

firstVersion.notifyWhenLive.text: We’ll notify you when it’s live
firstVersion.notifyWhenLive.description: Line beside a small check under a new project's card on its App tab while its first version is being made, for the person who started the project and for its other members: a promise that Homeroom will send them a notification once the app is live. "It" is the app; "live" means published and running for everyone.

firstVersion.tryAgain.description: Button under a new project's card on its App tab, for the person who started the project, when Homeroom bot's build of its first version stopped before the app went live: opens the build's conversation in their chat with Homeroom bot, where they can start it again.

firstVersion.tryFromChat.description: Line on a new project's App tab, for its maker, when the first version is built and can be tried from their chat with Homeroom bot. "It" is the first version of the app.

firstVersion.waitingForApproval.description: Line on a new project's App tab, for someone who is not its maker, when the first version is built and has not been approved yet.

firstVersion.openMyBotChat.text: Open my chat with Homeroom bot
firstVersion.openMyBotChat.description: Button on a new project's App tab, for its maker, when the first version is ready to try: opens their own chat with Homeroom bot. "Open" is a verb; "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant.

firstVersion.tryIt.description: Button on a new project's App tab when its first version is waiting for approval: opens a preview of that version so the person can use it.

firstVersion.seeChange.description: Button on a new project's App tab when its first version is waiting for approval: opens the page of the change that holds the first version, where people vote. "Change" is a noun.

firstVersion.waitingForYourApproval.description: Line on a new project's App tab when the first version cannot go live until the person reading approves it.

firstVersion.noVote.soon.text: No vote needed. It goes live in a minute or two.
firstVersion.noVote.soon.description: Line on a new project's App tab when its first version is ready: a project's first version goes live without a vote once it passes its checks, and it has, so it is about to be released. "It" is the first version of the app.

firstVersion.noVote.onceTested.text: No vote needed. It goes live once it passes its checks.
firstVersion.noVote.onceTested.description: Line on a new project's App tab when its first version is ready to try: a project's first version goes live without a vote, and it is released as soon as its automated checks pass. "It" is the first version of the app.

firstVersion.wait.soon.text: It goes live in a minute or two.
firstVersion.wait.soon.description: Line on a new project's App tab when its first version has been approved and is about to be released. "It" is the first version of the app.

firstVersion.wait.liveToday.text: It goes live later today if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.liveToday.description: Line on a new project's App tab when nothing more is needed for its first version except time: it is released automatically unless somebody votes against it. "It" is the first version of the app. Used when the release is later the same day.

firstVersion.wait.liveTomorrow.text: It goes live tomorrow if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.liveTomorrow.description: Line on a new project's App tab when nothing more is needed for its first version except time: it is released automatically unless somebody votes against it. "It" is the first version of the app. Used when the release is the next day.

firstVersion.wait.liveWeekday.text: It goes live on {{weekday}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.liveWeekday.description: Line on a new project's App tab when nothing more is needed for its first version except time: it is released automatically unless somebody votes against it. "It" is the first version of the app. {{weekday}} is the name of a day within the coming week, already in the reader's language, for example Wednesday.

firstVersion.wait.liveDate.text: It goes live on {{date}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.liveDate.description: Line on a new project's App tab when nothing more is needed for its first version except time: it is released automatically unless somebody votes against it. "It" is the first version of the app. {{date}} is a month and day already in the reader's language, for example October 12.

firstVersion.wait.forApproval.description: Line on a new project's App tab, for someone whose own approval is not asked for, while the first version still needs other people's approval.

firstVersion.wait.people.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", naming the people whose approval the first version still needs. {{people}} is a list of @usernames already joined, for example "@sam and @ada" or "@sam, @ada and 2 more".

firstVersion.wait.peopleOrToday.text: Waiting for {{people}}, or it goes live later today if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.peopleOrToday.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", naming the people whose approval the first version still needs. {{people}} is a list of @usernames already joined, for example "@sam and @ada" or "@sam, @ada and 2 more". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it.

firstVersion.wait.peopleOrTomorrow.text: Waiting for {{people}}, or it goes live tomorrow if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.peopleOrTomorrow.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", naming the people whose approval the first version still needs. {{people}} is a list of @usernames already joined, for example "@sam and @ada" or "@sam, @ada and 2 more". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it.

firstVersion.wait.peopleOrWeekday.text: Waiting for {{people}}, or it goes live on {{weekday}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.peopleOrWeekday.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", naming the people whose approval the first version still needs. {{people}} is a list of @usernames already joined, for example "@sam and @ada" or "@sam, @ada and 2 more". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{weekday}} is the name of a day within the coming week, for example Wednesday.

firstVersion.wait.peopleOrDate.text: Waiting for {{people}}, or it goes live on {{date}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.peopleOrDate.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", naming the people whose approval the first version still needs. {{people}} is a list of @usernames already joined, for example "@sam and @ada" or "@sam, @ada and 2 more". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{date}} is a month and day, for example October 12.

firstVersion.wait.more_one.text: Waiting for one more person to approve.
firstVersion.wait.more_one.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

firstVersion.wait.more_other.text: Waiting for {{count}} more people to approve.
firstVersion.wait.more_other.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one".

firstVersion.wait.moreOrToday_one.text: Waiting for one more person to approve, or it goes live later today if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrToday_one.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrToday_other.text: Waiting for {{count}} more people to approve, or it goes live later today if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrToday_other.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrTomorrow_one.text: Waiting for one more person to approve, or it goes live tomorrow if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrTomorrow_one.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrTomorrow_other.text: Waiting for {{count}} more people to approve, or it goes live tomorrow if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrTomorrow_other.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrWeekday_one.text: Waiting for one more person to approve, or it goes live on {{weekday}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrWeekday_one.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{weekday}} is the name of a day within the coming week, for example Wednesday. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrWeekday_other.text: Waiting for {{count}} more people to approve, or it goes live on {{weekday}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrWeekday_other.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{weekday}} is the name of a day within the coming week, for example Wednesday.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrDate_one.text: Waiting for one more person to approve, or it goes live on {{date}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrDate_one.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{date}} is a month and day, for example October 12. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

firstVersion.wait.moreOrDate_other.text: Waiting for {{count}} more people to approve, or it goes live on {{date}} if nobody objects.
firstVersion.wait.moreOrDate_other.description: Line on a new project's App tab, after "You approved it.", saying how many more approvals the first version still needs when the people cannot be named. {{count}} is that number; the singular form spells it out as "one". The second half says it is released automatically at that time unless somebody votes against it. {{date}} is a month and day, for example October 12.

firstVersion.wait.approved.description: Line on a new project's App tab for someone who has approved the first version, when there is nothing else to say. "It" is the first version of the app.

firstVersion.wait.approvedThen.description: Line on a new project's App tab for someone who has approved the first version. {{next}} is one more complete sentence saying what it still waits for, for example "It goes live tomorrow if nobody objects."; keep it after the first sentence.

firstVersion.people.lastTwo.description: Ends a list of @usernames whose approval a first version is waiting for, as in "@sam, @ada and @kim". {{first}} is the name or comma-joined names before the last one, and {{last}} the last name. The result is placed in "Waiting for …".

firstVersion.people.andMore_one.description: A list of @usernames whose approval a first version is waiting for, followed by how many further people are not named, as in "@sam, @ada and 2 more". {{people}} is the comma-joined names and {{count}} the number of unnamed people. The result is placed in "Waiting for …".

firstVersion.people.andMore_other.description: A list of @usernames whose approval a first version is waiting for, followed by how many further people are not named, as in "@sam, @ada and 2 more". {{people}} is the comma-joined names and {{count}} the number of unnamed people. The result is placed in "Waiting for …".

versionPill.redeploying.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. Nothing more is known.

versionPill.redeployingFrom.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. {{sha}} is the short code of the version being replaced, for example 3f9a2c1.

versionPill.redeployingElapsed_one.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. {{count}} is how many seconds it has taken so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

versionPill.redeployingElapsed_other.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. {{count}} is how many seconds it has taken so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

versionPill.redeployingFromElapsed_one.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. {{sha}} is the short code of the version being replaced, for example 3f9a2c1, and {{count}} how many seconds it has taken so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

versionPill.redeployingFromElapsed_other.description: Tooltip on the small version pill of an app while a new version is being deployed. {{sha}} is the short code of the version being replaced, for example 3f9a2c1, and {{count}} how many seconds it has taken so far; "s" abbreviates seconds.

versionPill.deploying.description: Lower-case label inside the small version pill of an app, beside a spinner, while a new version is being deployed. It stands where the version code normally is.

versionPill.dev.description: Lower-case label inside the small version pill of an app that has no deployed version on record. Short for "development"; it stands where the version code normally is.

versionPill.noVersion.description: Tooltip on the version pill of an app that has no deployed version on record.

versionPill.mergedBy.description: One whole fact in the tooltip of an app's version pill: who merged the change that produced this version. The tooltip lists independent facts separated by middle dots (the change's title, this, how long ago), so it is not part of a sentence and starts in lower case. {{username}} is that person's username; keep the @ before it.

versionPill.commit.description: Tooltip on an app's version pill when nothing is known about the version except its commit. "Commit" is a noun, the saved revision of the code; {{sha}} is its short code, for example 3f9a2c1.

header.appFallback.description: Title in the header bar over a project's old discussion channel when the project's name is not known. A noun.

header.channel.description: Subtitle in the header bar, under the project's name, when its old discussion channel is open. A noun: a chat room.

header.communities.description: Title in the header bar while a project's page is open: the name of the Communities section of Homeroom, which the page belongs to.

discussion.openFailed.description: Brief notice shown when the link to the discussion of a proposal (here a proposed change to a project's settings or rules) could not be followed; the person is taken to the project's board instead.

discussion.readOnlyNotice.text: You're viewing this app's dev space read-only. Only collaborators can post.
discussion.readOnlyNotice.description: Notice in place of the message box of a project's discussion, and of the replies on a change's page, for a person who may read and may not write. "Dev space" is the project's build area; "post" is a verb, to send a message.

discussion.archivedNotice.text: This was Homeroom’s project discussion. It is read-only now: Homeroom’s channel is #general.
discussion.archivedNotice.description: Notice above the old discussion channel of the Homeroom project itself, which can still be read and no longer written in. "Homeroom" is the product's name and "#general" the name of a channel; keep both.

discussion.door.empty.text: Talk with everyone building this app
discussion.door.empty.description: Line under the door to a project's discussion on its page, shown when there is no latest message to preview.

discussion.door.said.description: Preview of the latest message under the door to a project's discussion. {{author}} is the username of the person who wrote it, or the word for the system, and {{message}} the start of what they wrote.

discussion.door.system.description: Stands in for the author's name in the preview of a project's latest discussion message when the message was written by the platform and not by a person. A noun.

discussion.card.empty.text: Talk with everyone building this app
discussion.card.empty.description: Line on the General discussion card at the top of a project's board, shown when there is no latest message to preview.

discussion.card.said.description: Preview of the latest message on the General discussion card of a project's board. {{author}} is the username of the person who wrote it and {{message}} the start of what they wrote.

discussion.card.tooltip.description: Tooltip on the General discussion card of a project's board. "Open" is a verb.

discussion.card.titleFor.description: Title of the card at the top of a project's board that leads to its discussion. {{app}} is the project's name.

discussion.card.title.description: Title of the card at the top of a project's board that leads to its discussion, when the project's name is not known.

card.meta.visibleToGroup.description: Status at the end of the small line on the card of a change that is still being built, when its owner has shared it with the project's members.

card.meta.notShared.description: Status at the end of the small line on the card of a change that is still being built, when only its owner can see it.

card.actions.explore.description: Button on a proposal's card: opens the viewer's own conversation with Homeroom bot (Homeroom's building assistant) about this proposal, so the person can ask what it does or ask for changes.

card.actions.moveBack.description: Button on the card of a person's own proposal that is up for a vote: takes it out of the vote so they can keep working. "Underway" is the name of the board's column for work in progress.

card.actions.moveBackTitle.text: Take this proposal out of review to keep working on it (clears its votes, keeps the PR open)
card.actions.moveBackTitle.description: Tooltip on the Move back to Underway button. A proposal is a change put up for a vote; "PR" is the pull request on GitHub.

card.actions.withdraw.description: Button on the card of a person's own proposal that is up for a vote: takes the proposal back for good. A verb.

card.actions.withdrawTitle.text: Withdraw this proposal (closes the PR, removes it from the vote panel)
card.actions.withdrawTitle.description: Tooltip on the Withdraw button of a proposal's card. "PR" is the pull request on GitHub.

card.actions.askForApproval.description: Button on the card of a change imported from GitHub that its owner has not put up for a vote yet: puts it up for the group's vote.

card.actions.askForApprovalTitle.text: Ask the group to approve this imported change
card.actions.askForApprovalTitle.description: Tooltip on the Ask for approval button of an imported change. "The group" is the project's members; "change" is a noun.

card.reasons.attention.description: Heading over the list of problems on the card of an imported change that is not up for a vote yet.

card.reasons.cantMerge.description: Heading over the list of problems on a proposal's card when at least one of them stops the change from being merged into the project.

card.reasons.worthKnowing.description: Heading over the list of notes on a proposal's card when none of them stops the change from being merged.

card.menu.retractKudos.description: Row in a card's ⋯ menu: takes back the kudos (a thank-you point) this person gave for the change. "Retract" is a verb.

card.menu.giveKudos.description: Row in a card's ⋯ menu: gives kudos (a thank-you point) to the author of the change.

card.menu.openCard.description: First row in a card's ⋯ menu on the board: opens the card on a page of its own. "Open" is a verb.

card.menu.openCardTitle.text: The card on its own page
card.menu.openCardTitle.description: Tooltip on the Open card row of a card's ⋯ menu.

card.proposal.fallbackTitle.description: Title shown on a proposal's card when the change has no title of its own. {{username}} is the account name of the person who made the change. "Change" is a noun here: a set of edits to the project.

card.proposal.revertLead.description: Coloured label at the start of the title of a proposal that undoes an earlier change. The title of the change being undone follows it in its own element. Keep the arrow.

card.proposal.revertedPr.description: Stands in for the title of the change being undone, after "↩ Revert of" on a proposal's card, when that change has no title. {{number}} is its pull request number. "PR" abbreviates pull request.

card.proposal.openTitle.description: Tooltip of a proposal's card on the Workshop board: pressing the card opens the proposal's page with its discussion. "Open" is a verb.

card.proposal.mineIconTitle.text: This is your PR. Its session is under ⋯.
card.proposal.mineIconTitle.description: Tooltip of the icon on a proposal's card that the viewer made. "PR" abbreviates pull request; "session" is the viewer's own work on the change, whose actions are in the card's menu; ⋯ is the card's menu button and stays as it is.

card.provenance.importedBy.description: Fact on a proposal card's line of details, saying the change came from a GitHub pull request. {{author}} is the GitHub name of its author. Lower case: it sits among other facts separated by dots.

card.provenance.imported.description: Fact on a proposal card's line of details, saying the change came from a GitHub pull request whose author is not known. Lower case: it sits among other facts separated by dots.

card.provenance.builtWith.description: Fact on a proposal card's line of details. {{agent}} is the name of the coding agent that made the change, for example Claude Code. Lower case: it sits among other facts separated by dots.

card.provenance.maintenance.description: Fact on a proposal card's line of details, marking a change Homeroom itself opened to keep the project up to date. Lower case: it sits among other facts separated by dots.

card.provenance.autoTitle.description: Fact on a proposal card's line of details: the title shown is a placeholder and an automatically written one is on its way. Lower case: it sits among other facts separated by dots.

card.waiting.yourApproval.description: Status of a proposal on a project that is just the viewer, where their own Yes is the only approval needed.

card.waiting.approval.description: Status of a proposal that has been put up for the group's vote and is not approved yet.

card.waiting.noVote.description: Status of a proposal that is a project's first version: it is not put to a vote, and goes live once its automated checks pass.

board.plusMenu.settingsTitle.description: Title of the sheet, on a phone, listing a project's settings and rules, opened from the board's + menu.

board.filterChip.search.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that the cards are filtered by a search. {{query}} is what the person typed. Pressing the chip removes the filter.

board.filterChip.stageOpen.description: Chip above All items showing that only the work still open (requests, work underway and changes up for a vote) is shown, set by tapping the open items figure on the Workshop. Pressing the chip removes the filter.

board.filterChip.stageUnclaimed.description: Chip above All items showing that only the open requests nobody has picked up yet are shown, set by tapping that figure on the Workshop. Pressing the chip removes the filter.

board.filterChip.stageShipped.description: Chip above All items showing that only the changes that went live this week are shown, set by tapping that figure on the Workshop. Pressing the chip removes the filter.

board.filterChip.priorityLow.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only cards the group marked as low priority are shown. Pressing it removes the filter.

board.filterChip.priorityMedium.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only cards the group marked as medium priority are shown. Pressing it removes the filter.

board.filterChip.priorityHigh.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only cards the group marked as high priority are shown. Pressing it removes the filter.

board.filterChip.nobodyYet.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only cards with no person assigned to them are shown. It answers "who is on this?".

board.filterChip.needsVote.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only the proposals the viewer has not voted on yet are shown.

board.filterChip.assignedToYou.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only the cards assigned to the viewer are shown.

board.filterChip.yours.description: Chip above the Workshop board (All items) showing that only the person's own work as the Homeroom bot tab reads it: everything they filed, built, claimed, voted on, wrote in or chose Notify me on. It is dismissable.

board.filterChip.category.description: Chip above the Workshop board showing that only the cards in one category are shown. {{category}} is that category's name.

board.column.emptyFiltered.description: Shown inside a column of the Workshop board when filters or a search are on and no card in that column matches.

board.column.empty.description: Shown inside a column of the Workshop board that has no cards at all.

board.column.requests.description: Title of the first column of the Workshop board: requests people have filed that nobody has started on. A plural noun.

board.column.underway.description: Title of the second column of the Workshop board: requests and changes somebody is working on now.

board.column.underwayHint.text: A person or an agent is on each of these. The chip on each card says how.
board.column.underwayHint.description: Explanation shown with the "Underway" column of the Workshop board: each card there is being handled by a person or an AI agent. The "chip" is the small status label on each card (worked on, auto-solving, paused, waiting on an answer, claimed). Keep it short.

board.column.review.description: Title of the third column of the Workshop board: changes that have been put up for a vote and are not approved yet.

board.column.done.description: Title of the last column of the Workshop board: changes that were merged and requests that were closed.

board.deploy.childFailed.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when putting the newest merged change into production failed.

board.deploy.childFailedTitle.text: The latest merged change has not been confirmed in production.
board.deploy.childFailedTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Latest merged change · deploy failed" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column. "Production" is the live, running project.

board.deploy.childPending.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when the newest merged change is not running in production yet.

board.deploy.childPendingTitle.text: Production is still serving an earlier revision.
board.deploy.childPendingTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Latest merged change · awaiting deployment" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column. A "revision" is one version of the project's code.

board.deploy.childLive.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when the newest merged change is running and no pull request number is known for it. {{sha}} is the short code that identifies the running version, for example 3fa9c21.

board.deploy.childLiveTitle.text: The latest merged change is included in the observed production revision.
board.deploy.childLiveTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Live in production …" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column when the newest merged change is running.

board.deploy.stalled_one.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when merged changes are not live and the release has stopped making progress. {{count}} is how many merged changes are waiting.

board.deploy.stalled_other.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when merged changes are not live and the release has stopped making progress. {{count}} is how many merged changes are waiting.

board.deploy.stalledTitle.text: Production is still running an earlier revision. The release watcher has detected a stalled deployment.
board.deploy.stalledTitle.description: Tooltip of the "deployment stalled" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column. The "release watcher" is the automatic process that monitors releases.

board.deploy.waiting_one.text: {{count}} merged change waiting to go live
board.deploy.waiting_one.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when merged changes are not running in production yet. {{count}} is how many.

board.deploy.waiting_other.text: {{count}} merged changes waiting to go live
board.deploy.waiting_other.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when merged changes are not running in production yet. {{count}} is how many.

board.deploy.waitingTitle.text: Production is still running an earlier revision.
board.deploy.waitingTitle.description: Tooltip of the "merged changes waiting to go live" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column.

board.deploy.liveThroughPrSha.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column: every merged change up to and including this pull request is running. {{number}} is the pull request's number and {{sha}} the short code of the running version.

board.deploy.liveThroughPr.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column: every merged change up to and including this pull request is running. {{number}} is the pull request's number.

board.deploy.liveThroughSha.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column: every merged change up to this version is running. {{sha}} is the short code of the running version.

board.deploy.liveThroughLatest.text: Live in production through the latest merged change
board.deploy.liveThroughLatest.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when every merged change is running and no version code is known.

board.deploy.liveThroughTitle.text: Every merged change through this point is live in production.
board.deploy.liveThroughTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Live in production through …" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column.

board.deploy.unmatched.text: Production deployment could not be matched to completed history
board.deploy.unmatched.description: Status line at the top of the Workshop board's "Done" column when the running version does not correspond to any merged change on record.

board.deploy.unmatchedTitle.text: Production is running {{sha}}, but no completed proposal records that merge commit.
board.deploy.unmatchedTitle.description: Tooltip of the "could not be matched" status line on the Workshop board's "Done" column. {{sha}} is the short code of the running version.

board.divider.private.description: Label of a divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column, above the viewer's own changes in progress that nobody else can see.

board.divider.privateTitle.text: Only you can see your active sessions here. Their code is public.
board.divider.privateTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Yours · not shared" divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column.

board.divider.visible.description: Label of a divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column, above the viewer's own changes in progress that everyone can see.

board.divider.visibleTitle.text: Visible to everyone, including a live preview of your changes.
board.divider.visibleTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Yours · visible" divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column.

board.divider.others.description: Label of a divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column, above changes in progress that belong to other people.

board.divider.othersTitle.text: Changes in progress that other people have made visible.
board.divider.othersTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Others" divider in the Workshop board's "Underway" column.

board.sessionNote.priority_one.text: Changes in progress don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} such card below is not filtered by priority.
board.sessionNote.priority_one.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by priority and the cards of changes in progress are shown anyway, because those have none of them. {{count}} is how many such cards are below.

board.sessionNote.priority_other.text: Changes in progress don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} such cards below are not filtered by priority.
board.sessionNote.priority_other.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by priority and the cards of changes in progress are shown anyway, because those have none of them. {{count}} is how many such cards are below.

board.sessionNote.category_one.text: Changes in progress don't carry priority, category or assignee. The {{count}} such card below is not filtered by category.
board.sessionNote.category_one.description: Note at the top of the Workshop board's "Underway" column when the board is filtered by category and the cards of changes in progress are shown anyway, because those have none of them. {{count}} is how many such cards are below.
