step.checks.somePassedOlder_other.text: {{passed}} of {{count}} passed · on an older main
step.checks.somePassedOlder_other.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps, when the checks ran against an earlier version of the main branch. {{passed}} is how many automated checks passed and {{count}} how many ran.

step.checks.allPassed_one.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when every automated check passed. {{count}} is how many ran.

step.checks.allPassed_other.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when every automated check passed. {{count}} is how many ran.

step.checks.allPassedOlder_one.text: All {{count}} passed · on an older main
step.checks.allPassedOlder_one.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when every automated check passed, but against an earlier version of the main branch. {{count}} is how many ran.

step.checks.allPassedOlder_other.text: All {{count}} passed · on an older main
step.checks.allPassedOlder_other.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when every automated check passed, but against an earlier version of the main branch. {{count}} is how many ran.

step.checks.couldNotRun.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when the automated checks could not be run at all.

step.checks.failing.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when automated checks are failing and no count is available.

step.checks.someFailed_one.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps. {{failed}} is how many automated checks failed and {{count}} how many ran.

step.checks.someFailed_other.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps. {{failed}} is how many automated checks failed and {{count}} how many ran.

step.checks.starting.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps just before the automated checks begin.

step.checks.willRunAgain.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps when the last run broke and the automated checks are about to be retried.

step.checks.buildingStep.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the preview copy of the app is being built. {{step}} is the build stage it is on and {{steps}} the number of stages.

step.checks.waiting.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks wait their turn to run; only a few proposals are checked at a time.

step.checks.waitingNext.text: Waiting for a slot · next in line
step.checks.waitingNext.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks wait their turn and this proposal is the next to run.

step.checks.waitingAhead_one.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks wait their turn. {{count}} is how many other proposals run before this one.

step.checks.waitingAhead_other.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks wait their turn. {{count}} is how many other proposals run before this one.

step.checks.runningOf.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks run. {{ran}} is how many have finished and {{expected}} how many there are.

step.checks.runningSoFar.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks run and the total is not known. {{ran}} is how many have finished.

step.checks.building.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the preview copy of the app is being built, before the checks run.

step.checks.running.description: Line under the "Checks" step in a proposal's list of steps while the automated checks are running and no progress is known.

step.resume.label.description: Button beside the "Main is healthy" step in a proposal's list of steps, shown to administrators when merges are paused because the main branch's tests fail: lets merges continue anyway.

step.resume.title.text: Main’s unit suite is failing at this commit. Resume merges on the app anyway; the pause returns if a later merge fails the suite again.
step.resume.title.description: Tooltip of the "Resume merges" button. The "unit suite" is the project's automated tests.

step.resume.resuming.description: Label of the "Resume merges" button while the request is being sent.

step.resume.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when the server refused to resume merges and gave no explanation. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

step.resume.failedWith.description: Toast shown when the request to resume merges could not be sent. {{error}} is the technical error message.

step.resume.done.text: Merges resumed. Anything ready merges on the next pass.
step.resume.done.description: Toast shown after an administrator resumed merges on a project. "The next pass" is the next time Homeroom looks for approved changes to merge, usually within a minute.

step.resume.pending.text: Resuming merges. Homeroom has the request and lifts the pause shortly.
step.resume.pending.description: Toast shown after an administrator asked to resume merges on a project and Homeroom accepted the request but has not applied it yet; the pause shows until it does.

step.headline.live.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when every step is done: the change is merged and running.

step.headline.checking.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps while Homeroom is still working out which steps the change has to pass.

step.headline.merging.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps while the change is being merged right now.

step.headline.blocked.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when an automatic step has failed and the change cannot move on by itself.

step.headline.nothingNeedsYou.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is automatic or already in progress, so the viewer has nothing to do.

step.headline.waitingAuthor.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is something the change's author must do, shown to other people.

step.headline.waitingYouAuthor.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is something the change's author must do, shown to the author.

step.headline.waitingAdmin.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is something an administrator must do, shown to people who are not administrators.

step.headline.waitingYouAdmin.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is something an administrator must do, shown to an administrator.

step.headline.waitingGroup.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is the group's vote and the viewer has already voted.

step.headline.waitingYourApproval.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step is the group's vote and the viewer has not voted yet.

step.headline.waiting.description: Headline of a proposal's list of steps when the current step waits on somebody Homeroom cannot name.

step.integration.manualSyncFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · needs a manual sync
step.integration.manualSyncFiles_one.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and it could not be resolved automatically, so a person has to bring the change up to date with main by hand.

step.integration.manualSyncFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · needs a manual sync
step.integration.manualSyncFiles_other.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and it could not be resolved automatically, so a person has to bring the change up to date with main by hand.

step.integration.manualSyncMain.text: Conflict with main · needs a manual sync
step.integration.manualSyncMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch, and it could not be resolved automatically, so a person has to bring the change up to date with main by hand.

step.integration.mergeForkFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · merge main into your fork
step.integration.mergeForkFiles_one.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and the viewer wrote the change in their own fork (copy) of the repository and has to merge main into it themselves.

step.integration.mergeForkFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · merge main into your fork
step.integration.mergeForkFiles_other.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and the viewer wrote the change in their own fork (copy) of the repository and has to merge main into it themselves.

step.integration.mergeForkMain.text: Conflict with main · merge main into your fork
step.integration.mergeForkMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch, and the viewer wrote the change in their own fork (copy) of the repository and has to merge main into it themselves.

step.integration.authorForkFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · the author updates their fork
step.integration.authorForkFiles_one.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and the change lives in its author's own fork (copy) of the repository, and the author has to update it.

step.integration.authorForkFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · the author updates their fork
step.integration.authorForkFiles_other.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and the change lives in its author's own fork (copy) of the repository, and the author has to update it.

step.integration.authorForkMain.text: Conflict with main · the author updates their fork
step.integration.authorForkMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch, and the change lives in its author's own fork (copy) of the repository, and the author has to update it.

step.integration.afterVoteFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · fixed after the vote
step.integration.afterVoteFiles_one.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and it will be resolved automatically once the group has approved the change.

step.integration.afterVoteFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · fixed after the vote
step.integration.afterVoteFiles_other.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and it will be resolved automatically once the group has approved the change.

step.integration.afterVoteMain.text: Conflict with main · fixed after the vote
step.integration.afterVoteMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch, and it will be resolved automatically once the group has approved the change.

step.integration.budgetFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · resumes after the daily budget reset
step.integration.budgetFiles_one.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and automatic resolving is paused until the project's daily AI budget resets.

step.integration.budgetFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · resumes after the daily budget reset
step.integration.budgetFiles_other.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and automatic resolving is paused until the project's daily AI budget resets.

step.integration.budgetMain.text: Conflict with main · resumes after the daily budget reset
step.integration.budgetMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch, and automatic resolving is paused until the project's daily AI budget resets.

step.integration.checksFirstFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · fix the checks first
step.integration.checksFirstFiles_one.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} file, and its automated checks are failing, so it will not be resolved automatically until its author fixes the checks.

step.integration.checksFirstFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · fix the checks first
step.integration.checksFirstFiles_other.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and its automated checks are failing, so it will not be resolved automatically until its author fixes the checks.

step.integration.checksFirstMain.text: Conflict with main · fix the checks first
step.integration.checksFirstMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch, and its automated checks are failing, so it will not be resolved automatically until its author fixes the checks.

step.integration.checksRerunFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · re-run the checks first
step.integration.checksRerunFiles_one.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} file, and its automated checks could not run, so it will not be resolved automatically until they are re-run and pass.

step.integration.checksRerunFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · re-run the checks first
step.integration.checksRerunFiles_other.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and its automated checks could not run, so it will not be resolved automatically until they are re-run and pass.

step.integration.checksRerunMain.text: Conflict with main · re-run the checks first
step.integration.checksRerunMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch, and its automated checks could not run, so it will not be resolved automatically until they are re-run and pass.

step.integration.queuedFiles_one.text: Conflict in {{count}} file · queued to fix
step.integration.queuedFiles_one.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and it is waiting its turn to be resolved automatically.

step.integration.queuedFiles_other.text: Conflict in {{count}} files · queued to fix
step.integration.queuedFiles_other.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch in {{count}} files, and it is waiting its turn to be resolved automatically.

step.integration.queuedMain.text: Conflict with main · queued to fix
step.integration.queuedMain.description: Line under the "No conflicts with main" step in a proposal's list of steps: the change conflicts with the main branch, and it is waiting its turn to be resolved automatically.

proposal.menu.adminMerge.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu, shown to administrators: merges the change immediately without waiting for the vote.

proposal.menu.moveBack.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own proposal: takes it out of the vote and returns it to the "Underway" column so they can keep working on it.

proposal.menu.moveBackTitle.text: Take this proposal out of review to keep working on it (clears its votes, keeps the PR open)
proposal.menu.moveBackTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Move back to Underway" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu. "PR" abbreviates pull request.

proposal.menu.withdraw.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own proposal: withdraws the proposal entirely. A verb.

proposal.menu.withdrawTitle.text: Withdraw this proposal (closes the PR, removes it from the vote panel)
proposal.menu.withdrawTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Withdraw" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu. "PR" abbreviates pull request.

proposal.menu.undo.description: Item in the ⋯ menu of a merged change: opens a new proposal that reverses it. A verb.

proposal.menu.undoTitle.text: Open a revert PR for this merge. It still needs a merge vote to land.
proposal.menu.undoTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Undo" item in a merged change's ⋯ menu. A "revert PR" is a pull request that reverses the change; "to land" means to be merged.

proposal.menu.kudosOwnChange.text: You can’t give kudos to your own change
proposal.menu.kudosOwnChange.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Give kudos" item in the ⋯ menu of the viewer's own proposal. "Kudos" is Homeroom's way of thanking an author.

proposal.menu.kudosViaBounty.text: Credited via a bounty award, so it can’t be retracted
proposal.menu.kudosViaBounty.description: Tooltip of the disabled kudos item in a proposal's ⋯ menu when the viewer's kudos went to the author automatically as a bounty they had pledged.

proposal.menu.retractKudos.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu when the viewer has given kudos to the change and nobody else has: takes their kudos back.

proposal.menu.retractKudosCount_one.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu when the viewer has given kudos to the change: takes their kudos back. {{count}} is how many kudos the change has.

proposal.menu.retractKudosCount_other.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu when the viewer has given kudos to the change: takes their kudos back. {{count}} is how many kudos the change has.

proposal.menu.giveKudos.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: thanks the author of the change, when it has no kudos yet.

proposal.menu.giveKudosCount_one.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: thanks the author of the change. {{count}} is how many kudos the change has.

proposal.menu.giveKudosCount_other.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: thanks the author of the change. {{count}} is how many kudos the change has.

proposal.menu.retractKudosTitle.text: You gave kudos to this change. This retracts it
proposal.menu.retractKudosTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Retract kudos" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu.

proposal.menu.giveKudosTitle.text: Thank the author of this change
proposal.menu.giveKudosTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Give kudos" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu.

proposal.menu.explore.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: opens the viewer's own conversation with Homeroom bot (Homeroom's building assistant) about this change, so the viewer can ask it to explain the change.

proposal.menu.retryPreview.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu when building its preview copy of the app failed: tries the build again.

proposal.menu.retryPreviewTitle.text: Try building this proposal's staging preview again
proposal.menu.retryPreviewTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Retry preview" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu. The "staging preview" is the trial copy of the app with the change applied.

proposal.menu.beforeAfter.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: opens the proposal with its before-and-after screenshots shown.

proposal.menu.beforeAfterTitle.text: Open the declared changes and their before & after screenshots
proposal.menu.beforeAfterTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Before & after" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu. "Declared changes" are the visible changes the author listed; "screenshots" are the pictures Homeroom takes of what a proposal changes.

proposal.menu.screenshots.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu, for an older proposal whose screenshots were captured the earlier way: opens the proposal with them expanded.

proposal.menu.screenshotsTitle.text: Open this proposal and expand its before/after captures
proposal.menu.screenshotsTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Before/after screenshots" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu.

proposal.menu.copyLink.description: Row in a change's ⋯ menu: copies the address of the change's page to the clipboard.

proposal.menu.copyLinkDone.description: Brief notice after pressing Copy link in a change's ⋯ menu: the link is on the clipboard.

proposal.menu.share.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu: opens a picker to send the proposal's card to a chat or a discussion. "Share" is a verb.

proposal.menu.shareTitle.text: Share this proposal card to a chat or a discussion
proposal.menu.shareTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Share to…" item in a proposal's ⋯ menu.

proposal.menu.viewPr.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu, for a proposal whose pull request is on GitHub: opens it on GitHub in a new tab.

proposal.menu.viewCode.description: Item in a proposal's ⋯ menu, for a proposal whose code is on Homeroom's own git host rather than GitHub: opens that code in a new tab. "View" is a verb.

proposal.details.viewPr.description: Link in the details section of a proposal's page, for a proposal whose pull request is on GitHub: opens it on GitHub.

proposal.details.viewCode.description: Link in the details section of a proposal's page, for a proposal whose code is on Homeroom's own git host rather than GitHub: opens that code. "View" is a verb.

proposal.details.importedBy.description: Fact in the details section of a proposal's page for a change imported from GitHub. {{username}} is the account name of the person who imported it, shown in bold.

proposal.details.proposedBy.description: Fact in the details section of a proposal's page. {{username}} is the account name of the person who put the change up for a vote, shown in bold.

proposal.details.previewBuilding.text: A staging preview is being built for this proposal. It usually takes a few minutes, and a Preview button appears as soon as it's ready. Automated checks run against that preview, so they'll still be pending until then.
proposal.details.previewBuilding.description: Note in the details section of a proposal's page while the trial copy of the app is being built. "Preview" is the name of a button.

proposal.details.previewFailed.text: The staging preview couldn't be built, so there's nothing to preview and the automated checks can't run: {{error}}
proposal.details.previewFailed.description: Warning in the details section of a proposal's page when building the trial copy of the app failed. {{error}} is the technical error message.

proposal.details.lockedNote.text: App is locked, so it also needs at least one admin yes before it merges.
proposal.details.lockedNote.description: Note in the details section of a proposal's page on a project whose administrators have locked it: besides the vote, an administrator must vote Yes.

ledger.label.conflict.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page that says whether the change conflicts with the project's main branch.

ledger.label.checks.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page that reports the automated checks run on the change. A plural noun.

ledger.label.env.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page about configuration values an administrator has to set before the change can merge.

ledger.label.console.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page that reports errors the app logged in the browser console during the automated checks.

ledger.label.preview.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page about the trial copy of the app built with the change. A noun.

ledger.label.note.description: Label of a row on a proposal's page that carries a general remark with no more specific label. A noun.

ledger.label.votes.description: Label of the row on a proposal's page that shows who has voted and how many Yes votes are needed. A plural noun.

ledger.checks.lastRun.description: Small text beside the "Checks" label on a proposal's page. {{when}} is how long ago the automated checks last ran, for example "3h ago".

ledger.checks.passingOne.text: <0>Passing.</0> The one check passed on this build.
ledger.checks.passingOne.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when the change has a single automated check and it passed. The verdict inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.checks.passingAll_one.text: <0>Passing.</0> All {{count}} check passed on this build.
ledger.checks.passingAll_one.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when every automated check passed. {{count}} is how many there are. The verdict inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.checks.passingAll_other.text: <0>Passing.</0> All {{count}} checks passed on this build.
ledger.checks.passingAll_other.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when every automated check passed. {{count}} is how many there are. The verdict inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.checks.passingAdvisory_one.text: <0>Passing.</0> Every merge-blocking check passed on this build. {{count}} check that only advise did not.
ledger.checks.passingAdvisory_one.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when all checks that can block a merge passed but some advisory ones failed. {{count}} is how many advisory checks failed. The verdict inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.checks.passingAdvisory_other.text: <0>Passing.</0> Every merge-blocking check passed on this build. {{count}} checks that only advise did not.
ledger.checks.passingAdvisory_other.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when all checks that can block a merge passed but some advisory ones failed. {{count}} is how many advisory checks failed. The verdict inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.checks.waiting.text: <0>Waiting.</0> They run again by themselves once the branch is up to date. Nothing to do here.
ledger.checks.waiting.description: Text of the "Checks" row on a proposal's page when failing checks are out of date because the change must first be brought up to date with main. "They" are the checks. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.behind.commits_one.description: Small text beside the label of the row on a proposal's page that says the change is behind the main branch. {{count}} is how many commits (saved code changes) behind it is.

ledger.behind.commits_other.description: Small text beside the label of the row on a proposal's page that says the change is behind the main branch. {{count}} is how many commits (saved code changes) behind it is.

ledger.votes.needed_one.description: Small text beside the "Votes" label on a proposal's page. {{count}} is the number of Yes votes so far (one) and {{required}} the number needed to approve the change.

ledger.votes.needed_other.description: Small text beside the "Votes" label on a proposal's page. {{count}} is the number of Yes votes so far and {{required}} the number needed to approve the change.

ledger.sync.label.description: Label of the first step on a proposal's page when the change has to be brought up to date with the project's main branch before it can merge.

ledger.sync.subNamed.description: Small text beside "Sync with main" on a proposal's page when a person has to do the sync by hand: it names who, and that it is needed now. {{username}} is the author's account name.

ledger.sync.subAuthor.description: Small text beside "Sync with main" on a proposal's page when the change's author has to do the sync by hand and their name is not known.

ledger.sync.fact.moved_one.description: A complete counted fact used inside the sentences of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page, where the sentence has {{moved}} (for example "Main has moved 3 commits ahead, and 2 files changed on both sides, so …"). It has its own plural forms because the sentence holds two different counts. {{count}} is how many commits the project's main branch has gained since this change was started. No full stop: the sentence around it supplies the punctuation.

ledger.sync.fact.moved_other.description: A complete counted fact used inside the sentences of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page, where the sentence has {{moved}} (for example "Main has moved 3 commits ahead, and 2 files changed on both sides, so …"). It has its own plural forms because the sentence holds two different counts. {{count}} is how many commits the project's main branch has gained since this change was started. No full stop: the sentence around it supplies the punctuation.

ledger.sync.fact.overlap_one.description: A complete counted fact used inside the sentences of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page, where the sentence has {{overlap}} (for example "Main has moved 3 commits ahead, and 2 files changed on both sides, so …"). It has its own plural forms because the sentence holds two different counts. {{count}} is how many files were edited both in this change and on main. It follows other words in the sentence, so it does not start with a capital unless your language requires one. No full stop.

ledger.sync.fact.overlap_other.description: A complete counted fact used inside the sentences of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page, where the sentence has {{overlap}} (for example "Main has moved 3 commits ahead, and 2 files changed on both sides, so …"). It has its own plural forms because the sentence holds two different counts. {{count}} is how many files were edited both in this change and on main. It follows other words in the sentence, so it does not start with a capital unless your language requires one. No full stop.

ledger.sync.blocked.commitsAndFiles.text: <0>Blocked.</0> {{moved}}, and {{overlap}}, so the automatic sync cannot finish this one.
ledger.sync.blocked.commitsAndFiles.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page when a person has to resolve the conflict by hand. {{moved}} is the complete fact about how far the main branch has moved (changes:ledger.sync.fact.moved, for example "Main has moved 3 commits ahead") and {{overlap}} the complete fact about the files edited on both sides (changes:ledger.sync.fact.overlap, for example "2 files changed on both sides"); each already carries its own number in the right plural form. Place the two wherever your language needs them. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.sync.blocked.commitsLines_one.text: <0>Blocked.</0> Main has moved {{count}} commit ahead, and the two changes touch the same lines, so the automatic sync cannot finish this one.
ledger.sync.blocked.commitsLines_one.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page when a person has to resolve the conflict by hand. {{count}} is how many commits the project's main branch has gained since this change was started. Used when the conflicting files are not known. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.sync.blocked.commitsLines_other.text: <0>Blocked.</0> Main has moved {{count}} commits ahead, and the two changes touch the same lines, so the automatic sync cannot finish this one.
ledger.sync.blocked.commitsLines_other.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page when a person has to resolve the conflict by hand. {{count}} is how many commits the project's main branch has gained since this change was started. Used when the conflicting files are not known. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.sync.blocked.aheadFiles_one.text: <0>Blocked.</0> Main has moved ahead, and {{count}} file changed on both sides, so the automatic sync cannot finish this one.
ledger.sync.blocked.aheadFiles_one.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page when a person has to resolve the conflict by hand. Used when the number of new commits on the main branch is not known. {{count}} is how many files were edited both in this change and on main. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.sync.blocked.aheadFiles_other.text: <0>Blocked.</0> Main has moved ahead, and {{count}} files changed on both sides, so the automatic sync cannot finish this one.
ledger.sync.blocked.aheadFiles_other.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page when a person has to resolve the conflict by hand. Used when the number of new commits on the main branch is not known. {{count}} is how many files were edited both in this change and on main. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.sync.blocked.aheadLines.text: <0>Blocked.</0> Main has moved ahead, and the two changes touch the same lines, so the automatic sync cannot finish this one.
ledger.sync.blocked.aheadLines.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page when a person has to resolve the conflict by hand. Used when the number of new commits on the main branch is not known. Used when the conflicting files are not known. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.sync.resolvingNow.commitsAndFiles.text: <0>Syncing.</0> {{moved}}, and {{overlap}}. Homeroom is resolving it now, then it tries the merge again.
ledger.sync.resolvingNow.commitsAndFiles.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page while Homeroom is resolving the conflict automatically. {{moved}} is the complete fact about how far the main branch has moved (changes:ledger.sync.fact.moved, for example "Main has moved 3 commits ahead") and {{overlap}} the complete fact about the files edited on both sides (changes:ledger.sync.fact.overlap, for example "2 files changed on both sides"); each already carries its own number in the right plural form. Place the two wherever your language needs them. The word inside <0></0> is shown in bold.

ledger.sync.resolvingNow.commitsLines_on.text: <0>Syncing.</0> Main has moved {{count}} commit ahead, and the two changes touch the same lines. Homeroom is resolving it now, then it tries the merge again.
ledger.sync.resolvingNow.commitsLines_on.description: Text of the "Sync with main" row on a proposal's page while Homeroom is resolving the conflict automatically. {{count}} is how many commits the project's main branch has gained since this change was started. votingHelp.dialogLabel.description: Accessible name of the small pop-up that explains how a proposal is voted on and merged, opened from the help mark on a proposal's page.

votingHelp.sentences.description: Joins two whole sentences into the paragraph shown in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page. {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next sentence. Only the space between sentences is translated.

votingHelp.tally.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page giving the current vote count. {{yes}} and {{no}} are numbers; "Yes" and "No" are the names of the two votes.

votingHelp.merged.text: This proposal has already merged into the app.
votingHelp.merged.description: The whole text of the voting help pop-up on the page of a proposal that has been merged.

votingHelp.merging.text: This passed and is being merged into the app right now.
votingHelp.merging.description: The whole text of the voting help pop-up on the page of a proposal that was approved and is being merged at this moment.

votingHelp.noTimer_one.text: It won’t merge on a timer: it needs {{count}} actual Yes vote.
votingHelp.noTimer_one.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up for a proposal that needs explicit approval: it is not approved automatically when a waiting period ends. {{count}} is how many Yes votes it needs.

votingHelp.noTimer_other.text: It won’t merge on a timer: it needs {{count}} actual Yes votes.
votingHelp.noTimer_other.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up for a proposal that needs explicit approval: it is not approved automatically when a waiting period ends. {{count}} is how many Yes votes it needs.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.conflictFail.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: automatic conflict resolution failed, so the proposer must resolve it before it can merge.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.conflictFail.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because Homeroom tried to resolve the conflict with the project's main version and could not, so the person who proposed the change has to. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.resolving.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: conflicts with the main app are being reconciled automatically before it can merge.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.resolving.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because Homeroom is resolving the conflict with the project's main version by itself right now. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.conflict.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: it conflicts with the main app, so its creator has to sync with main and resolve them before it can merge.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.conflict.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because the change conflicts with the project's main version and its author has to bring it up to date ("sync with main") and resolve the conflicts. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.checksFailin.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: its automated checks are failing, so it can’t merge until they pass.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.checksFailin.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because the proposal's automated checks (tests) are failing. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.checksPendin.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: its automated checks are still running, so it can’t merge until they finish.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.checksPendin.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because the proposal's automated checks (tests) have not finished. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.checksError.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: its automated checks couldn’t run, so it can’t merge until they pass.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.checksError.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because the proposal's automated checks (tests) could not be run at all. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.behind.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: it’s behind the main app and will sync automatically before merging.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.behind.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because the project's main version has moved on, and Homeroom will bring the change up to date by itself. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.locked.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: the app is locked, so it also needs an admin’s Yes.
votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.locked.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them but cannot merge because the project is locked by its administrators, so one of them must also vote Yes. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed. votingHelp.approvalsBlocked.noOtherMembe.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}), but it can’t merge yet: none of its Yes votes is from another member yet.

"It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.note.locked.text: Note: the app is locked, so it also needs an admin’s Yes.
votingHelp.note.locked.description: Sentence added at the end of the voting help pop-up on a proposal's page, after the sentences about its votes, to say what else holds the merge back: the project is locked by its administrators, so one of them must also vote Yes. "It" is the proposal.

votingHelp.approvalsQueued.text: It has the approvals it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}). Queued to merge shortly.
votingHelp.approvalsQueued.description: Text in the voting help pop-up on a project with a fixed number of required approvals, when the proposal has them and nothing holds it back. {{yes}} is the number of approvals it has and {{required}} the number needed.

votingHelp.requiresInvited_one.text: This app requires at least {{count}} approval from its invited approvers. Currently {{yes}} of {{count}}.
votingHelp.requiresInvited_one.description: Text in the voting help pop-up on a project where only invited approvers' votes count. {{count}} is how many approvals are required and {{yes}} how many the proposal has.

votingHelp.requiresInvited_other.text: This app requires at least {{count}} approvals from its invited approvers. Currently {{yes}} of {{count}}.
votingHelp.requiresInvited_other.description: Text in the voting help pop-up on a project where only invited approvers' votes count. {{count}} is how many approvals are required and {{yes}} how many the proposal has.

votingHelp.requiresAnyone_one.text: This app requires at least {{count}} approval from any user. Currently {{yes}} of {{count}}.
votingHelp.requiresAnyone_one.description: Text in the voting help pop-up on a project where anyone's vote counts toward a fixed number of approvals. {{count}} is how many approvals are required and {{yes}} how many the proposal has.

votingHelp.requiresAnyone_other.text: This app requires at least {{count}} approvals from any user. Currently {{yes}} of {{count}}.
votingHelp.requiresAnyone_other.description: Text in the voting help pop-up on a project where anyone's vote counts toward a fixed number of approvals. {{count}} is how many approvals are required and {{yes}} how many the proposal has.

votingHelp.approversOnly.text: Everyone can still vote, but only approvers’ votes count toward the target.
votingHelp.approversOnly.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a project where only invited approvers' votes count.

votingHelp.votesQueued.text: It has the votes it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}). Queued to merge shortly.
votingHelp.votesQueued.description: Text in the voting help pop-up for a proposal needing explicit approval that has its votes and nothing holding it back. {{yes}} is the number of Yes votes and {{required}} the number needed.

votingHelp.votesGreenQueued.text: It has the votes it needs ({{yes}} of {{required}}) and green checks. Queued to merge shortly.
votingHelp.votesGreenQueued.description: Text in the voting help pop-up when the proposal has its votes and its automated checks passed ("green"). {{yes}} is the number of Yes votes and {{required}} the number needed.

votingHelp.setAside.text: More No than Yes, and not enough support yet. It will be set aside in {{time}} unless support arrives.
votingHelp.setAside.description: Text in the voting help pop-up when a proposal is losing the vote. {{time}} is a short countdown such as "~2d 5h". "Set aside" means the proposal is closed without merging.

votingHelp.needs.text: It needs {{required}} of {{active}} active testers to vote Yes.
votingHelp.needs.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up. {{required}} is how many Yes votes the proposal needs and {{active}} how many active members the project has. "Testers" are the project's members.

votingHelp.enoughGoesLive.text: There are enough Yes votes ({{yes}} of {{required}}). It goes live in {{time}} unless someone objects.
votingHelp.enoughGoesLive.description: Text in the voting help pop-up when the proposal has its votes and is waiting out the objection period. {{yes}} is the number of Yes votes, {{required}} the number needed and {{time}} a short countdown such as "~3h 20m".

votingHelp.supportGoesLive.text: It has support ({{yes}} of {{required}} needed) and nobody has objected. It goes live in {{time}} unless the vote changes. Quiet is taken as a nod, so speak up if something bothers you.
votingHelp.supportGoesLive.description: Text in the voting help pop-up when a proposal has some Yes votes, no objections, and will be approved when the waiting period ends. {{yes}} is the number of Yes votes, {{required}} the number that would approve it outright and {{time}} a short countdown such as "~3h 20m".

votingHelp.contested.text: It needs a conversation. Enough people have objected that the timer is off, so it now needs a clear majority of Yes votes to pass.
votingHelp.contested.description: Text in the voting help pop-up when enough members voted No that the proposal will no longer be approved automatically.

votingHelp.advisory_one.text: {{count}} advisory vote from a non-approver is recorded but doesn’t count.
votingHelp.advisory_one.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a project where only invited approvers' votes count. {{count}} is how many votes came from people who are not approvers.

votingHelp.advisory_other.text: {{count}} advisory votes from non-approvers are recorded but don’t count.
votingHelp.advisory_other.description: Sentence in the voting help pop-up on a project where only invited approvers' votes count. {{count}} is how many votes came from people who are not approvers.

remedy.leadThenRest.description: How the two sentences of a proposal's conflict note are put together. {{lead}} is a complete sentence about what Homeroom does on its own, and {{rest}} is a complete sentence about what a person can do (it may contain words in bold). Both are placed exactly where they stand here, so a language may reorder them or change what stands between them.

remedy.lead.mayNotRun.text: Automatic resolution may not run for this proposal.
remedy.lead.mayNotRun.description: First sentence of the note on a proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch, when Homeroom may not be able to resolve it by itself.

remedy.lead.resolvingNow.text: The platform is resolving it now.
remedy.lead.resolvingNow.description: First sentence of the note on a proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch, while Homeroom is resolving it. "It" is the conflict.

remedy.lead.triedAndFailed.text: The platform tried to resolve it and could not.
remedy.lead.triedAndFailed.description: First sentence of the note on a proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch that Homeroom failed to resolve. "It" is the conflict.

remedy.lead.afterVote.text: The platform resolves it once the vote passes.
remedy.lead.afterVote.description: First sentence of the note on a proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch that Homeroom will resolve after the group approves the change. "It" is the conflict.

remedy.lead.automatic.description: First sentence of the note on a proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch that Homeroom will resolve by itself. "It" is the conflict.

remedy.lead.nextMerge.text: Homeroom keeps this branch itself and will try to resolve it automatically at the next merge attempt.
remedy.lead.nextMerge.description: First sentence of the note on an imported proposal's page about a conflict with the main branch, when the code lives in the project's own repository. "It" is the conflict.

remedy.rest.resolveInChat.text: <0>{{creator}}</0> needs to resolve it: run "Sync with main" on the change's page.
remedy.rest.resolveInChat.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page after automatic resolution failed. "Sync with main" is the name of a button on the change's page. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.resolveInChatUnnamed.text: <0>the proposal’s creator</0> needs to resolve it: run "Sync with main" on the change's page.
remedy.rest.resolveInChatUnnamed.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page after automatic resolution failed. "Sync with main" is the name of a button on the change's page. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.needsSync.text: <0>{{creator}}</0> needs to bring it up to date: run "Sync with main" on the change's page.
remedy.rest.needsSync.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when the author must bring the change up to date with main. "Sync with main" is the name of a button on the change's page. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.needsSyncUnnamed.text: <0>the proposal’s creator</0> needs to bring it up to date: run "Sync with main" on the change's page.
remedy.rest.needsSyncUnnamed.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when the author must bring the change up to date with main. "Sync with main" is the name of a button on the change's page. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.nobody.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page while Homeroom is resolving the conflict by itself.

remedy.rest.canSyncSooner.text: <0>{{creator}}</0> can bring it up to date sooner: run "Sync with main" on the change's page.
remedy.rest.canSyncSooner.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when Homeroom will resolve the conflict after the vote, but the author may do it earlier. "Sync with main" is the name of a button on the change's page. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.canSyncSoonerUnnamed.text: <0>the proposal’s creator</0> can bring it up to date sooner: run "Sync with main" on the change's page.
remedy.rest.canSyncSoonerUnnamed.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when Homeroom will resolve the conflict after the vote, but the author may do it earlier. "Sync with main" is the name of a button on the change's page. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.canAlsoSyncSooner.text: <0>{{creator}}</0> can also bring it up to date sooner: run "Sync with main" on the change's page.
remedy.rest.canAlsoSyncSooner.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when Homeroom will resolve the conflict automatically, but the author may do it earlier. "Sync with main" is the name of a button on the change's page. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.canAlsoSyncSoonerUnnamed.text: <0>the proposal’s creator</0> can also bring it up to date sooner: run "Sync with main" on the change's page.
remedy.rest.canAlsoSyncSoonerUnnamed.description: Sentence in the conflict note on a proposal's page when Homeroom will resolve the conflict automatically, but the author may do it earlier. "Sync with main" is the name of a button on the change's page. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.resubmit.text: <0>{{creator}}</0> needs to bring the branch up to date with main in the coding agent that wrote it, then submit it again as an update to this proposal. Homeroom keeps this branch itself, so the merge is retried once the update lands.
remedy.rest.resubmit.description: Text of the conflict note on an imported proposal's page after automatic resolution failed, when the code lives in the project's own repository. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.resubmitUnnamed.text: <0>the proposal’s creator</0> needs to bring the branch up to date with main in the coding agent that wrote it, then submit it again as an update to this proposal. Homeroom keeps this branch itself, so the merge is retried once the update lands.
remedy.rest.resubmitUnnamed.description: Text of the conflict note on an imported proposal's page after automatic resolution failed, when the code lives in the project's own repository. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.resubmitIfFails.text: If that fails, <0>{{creator}}</0> needs to bring the branch up to date with main in the coding agent that wrote it and submit it again as an update to this proposal.
remedy.rest.resubmitIfFails.description: Sentence in the conflict note on an imported proposal's page, after the sentence saying Homeroom will try to resolve the conflict at the next merge attempt. <0>{{creator}}</0> is the account name of the change's author, shown in bold.

remedy.rest.resubmitIfFailsUnnamed.text: If that fails, <0>the proposal’s creator</0> needs to bring the branch up to date with main in the coding agent that wrote it and submit it again as an update to this proposal.
remedy.rest.resubmitIfFailsUnnamed.description: Sentence in the conflict note on an imported proposal's page, after the sentence saying Homeroom will try to resolve the conflict at the next merge attempt. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.rest.fork.text: This branch lives in <0>{{creator}}</0>’s own fork, which Homeroom cannot write to, so it cannot sync it itself. <1>{{creator}}</1> needs to merge main into the branch and push it; the proposal follows the push.
remedy.rest.fork.description: Text of the conflict note on an imported proposal's page when the code lives in its author's own copy (fork) of the repository. {{creator}} is the author's account name, shown in bold both times.

remedy.rest.forkUnnamed.text: This branch lives in <0>the proposal’s creator</0>’s own fork, which Homeroom cannot write to, so it cannot sync it itself. <1>the proposal’s creator</1> needs to merge main into the branch and push it; the proposal follows the push.
remedy.rest.forkUnnamed.description: Text of the conflict note on an imported proposal's page when the code lives in its author's own copy (fork) of the repository. Used when the author's account name is not known: the words in the tags, which name the author instead, are shown in bold both times and stay in lower case in English.

remedy.detail.failed.text: The change’s owner needs to resolve it from the change’s page.
remedy.detail.failed.description: Short explanation, in a tooltip, of why a proposal is blocked after automatic conflict resolution failed. "It" is the conflict with the main branch.

remedy.detail.conflict.text: Its creator needs to bring it up to date from the change’s page ("Sync with main").
remedy.detail.conflict.description: Short explanation, in a tooltip, of why a proposal that conflicts with the main branch is blocked. "Sync with main" is the name of a button on the change's page.

remedy.label.text: Needs author to sync with main
remedy.label.description: Short status label on a proposal that conflicts with the main branch when its author has to bring it up to date by hand.

conflictNote.files.description: Line above the list of file names in the conflict note on a proposal's page.

conflictNote.lastAttempt.description: Line in the conflict note on a proposal's page. {{when}} is how long ago Homeroom last tried to merge or resolve it, for example "3h ago".

conflictNote.headingFailed.description: Heading of the conflict note on a proposal's page when Homeroom tried to resolve a conflict with the main branch and could not.

conflictNote.headingConflict.text: A merge was attempted, but this proposal conflicts with main.
conflictNote.headingConflict.description: Heading of the conflict note on a proposal's page when a merge was tried and the change conflicts with the main branch.

mergeability.explanation.text: Main has moved on since this was written, and the two changes touch the same lines. It cannot merge until somebody reconciles them.
mergeability.explanation.description: First line of the note on a proposal's page that warns, before any merge is tried, that the change would conflict with the main branch.

mergeability.files.description: Line above the list of files that were edited both in the proposal and on the main branch, in the conflict warning on a proposal's page.

mergeability.filesSample.text: That is a sample of the files, and some of them may merge cleanly.
mergeability.filesSample.description: Line under the list of files in the conflict warning on a proposal's page, when the list is incomplete.

mergeability.filesHint.text: Some of those may still merge cleanly. They are where to look first.
mergeability.filesHint.description: Line under the list of files in the conflict warning on a proposal's page, when the list is complete.

mergeability.checked.description: Line in the conflict warning on a proposal's page. {{when}} is how long ago Homeroom checked whether the change merges, for example "3h ago".

mergeability.heading.text: This proposal no longer merges into main on its own.
mergeability.heading.description: Heading of the note on a proposal's page that warns the change would conflict with the main branch.

envNote.errorHeading.description: Heading of a note on a proposal's page when Homeroom could not verify that the configuration values the change needs are set.

envNote.errorBody.text: This does not block the merge. The check is re-run when votes reach the threshold.
envNote.errorBody.description: Body of the note on a proposal's page shown when the platform variables could not be checked.

envNote.missingHeading.text: ⚠ New platform variables have no value set. Merge is blocked.
envNote.missingHeading.description: Heading of a warning on a proposal's page when the change adds configuration values that nobody has set. Keep the leading ⚠ and the space after it.

envNote.deployWithout_one.text: Deploying without it would restart the platform missing configuration it now expects.
envNote.deployWithout_one.description: Line in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page. {{count}} is how many variables are missing; "it" (or "them") refers to those values.

envNote.deployWithout_other.text: Deploying without them would restart the platform missing configuration it now expects.
envNote.deployWithout_other.description: Line in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page. {{count}} is how many variables are missing; "it" (or "them") refers to those values.

envNote.setAndVote_one.text: No rebuild needed. Set the value and vote again.
envNote.setAndVote_one.description: Line in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page, telling an administrator what to do. {{count}} is how many values are missing.

envNote.setAndVote_other.text: No rebuild needed. Set the values and vote again.
envNote.setAndVote_other.description: Line in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page, telling an administrator what to do. {{count}} is how many values are missing.

envNote.setNow.description: Button in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page, shown to administrators: opens the panel where the values are set.

envNote.proposeValue.description: Button in the warning about unset platform variables on a proposal's page, shown to people who are not administrators: opens the panel where they can suggest a value.

envNote.added.text: This proposal adds {{names}}, already set and ready for the deploy.
envNote.added.description: Line on a proposal's page when the change adds configuration values and all of them are set. {{names}} is a comma-separated list of the variables' names.

envNote.carried_one.text: {{names}} carries its value with this proposal, applied when it merges.
envNote.carried_one.description: Line on a proposal's page about configuration values whose values travel with the proposal. {{names}} is a comma-separated list of {{count}} variable names.

envNote.carried_other.text: {{names}} carry their values with this proposal, applied when it merges.
envNote.carried_other.description: Line on a proposal's page about configuration values whose values travel with the proposal. {{names}} is a comma-separated list of {{count}} variable names.

envNote.okHeading.description: Heading of a note on a proposal's page when the configuration values the change adds are all set. Keep the leading ✓ and the space after it.

consoleNote.intro.text: The staging preview logged these console errors when it loaded:
consoleNote.intro.description: Line above the list of errors in the warning on a proposal's page that the trial copy of the app reported errors in the browser console.

consoleNote.detected.text: Console errors were detected on the staging preview.
consoleNote.detected.description: Line in the console-errors warning on a proposal's page when the errors themselves are not available to list.

consoleNote.lastChecked.description: Line in the console-errors warning on a proposal's page. {{when}} is how long ago the check ran, for example "3h ago".

consoleNote.fix.text: Pushing a fix rebuilds the preview and re-runs the check. The warning clears if the errors are gone.
consoleNote.fix.description: Last line of the console-errors warning on a proposal's page, telling the author how to clear it.

consoleNote.heading.text: ⚠ This change may break the app.
consoleNote.heading.description: Heading of the warning on a proposal's page that the trial copy of the app reported errors in the browser console. Keep the leading ⚠ and the space after it.

recheck.running.description: Label of the "Re-run checks" button on a proposal or session while the request to run the automated checks again is in progress.

recheck.label.description: Button on a change whose automated checks did not pass: runs them again.

recheck.title.text: Rebuild the staging preview if needed and re-run the automated tests
recheck.title.description: Tooltip of the "Re-run checks" button on a change.

recheck.botFixing.text: Homeroom bot is fixing this. Re-running now would restart its fix.
recheck.botFixing.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Re-run checks" button on a change's page while Homeroom bot, the change's author, is fixing the checks that failed on it.

progress.checks.sub.ofExpected_one.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{expected}} how many there are in all. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.ofExpected_other.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{expected}} how many there are in all. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.ofExpectedFailed_one.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed, {{failed}} how many failed and {{expected}} how many there are in all. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.ofExpectedFailed_oth.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed, {{failed}} how many failed and {{expected}} how many there are in all. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.soFar_one.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.soFar_other.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.soFarFailed_one.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{failed}} how many failed. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sub.soFarFailed_other.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{failed}} how many failed. "run" means "have been run".

progress.checks.sentence.ofExpected_one.text: {{count}} of {{expected}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed.
progress.checks.sentence.ofExpected_one.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{expected}} how many checks there are in all.

progress.checks.sentence.ofExpected_othe.text: {{count}} of {{expected}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed.
progress.checks.sentence.ofExpected_othe.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{expected}} how many checks there are in all.

progress.checks.sentence.ofExpectedFaile.text: {{count}} of {{expected}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed, {{failed}} failed.
progress.checks.sentence.ofExpectedFaile.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed, {{failed}} how many failed and {{expected}} how many checks there are in all.

progress.checks.sentence.ofExpectedFaile.text: {{count}} of {{expected}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed, {{failed}} failed.
progress.checks.sentence.ofExpectedFaile.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed, {{failed}} how many failed and {{expected}} how many checks there are in all.

progress.checks.sentence.soFar_one.text: {{count}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed.
progress.checks.sentence.soFar_one.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed.

progress.checks.sentence.soFar_other.text: {{count}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed.
progress.checks.sentence.soFar_other.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed.

progress.checks.sentence.soFarFailed_one.text: {{count}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed, {{failed}} failed.
progress.checks.sentence.soFarFailed_one.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{failed}} how many failed.

progress.checks.sentence.soFarFailed_oth.text: {{count}} checks have run so far: {{passed}} passed, {{failed}} failed.
progress.checks.sentence.soFarFailed_oth.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are still running. Used when the total is not known yet. {{count}} is how many checks have run so far, {{passed}} how many of those passed and {{failed}} how many failed.

progress.duration.seconds.description: A short length of time under one minute, for example "20s", used inside the lines that say how long a step of building a proposal's preview took. {{seconds}} is a whole number; "s" abbreviates seconds.

progress.duration.minutesSeconds.description: A length of time of a minute or more, for example "9m 40s", used inside the lines that say how long a step of building a proposal's preview took. {{minutes}} and {{seconds}} are whole numbers; "m" and "s" abbreviate minutes and seconds.

progress.build.label.fetch.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. This step is fetching the proposal's branch of code. It is an imperative-style step name, all lower case.

progress.build.label.fetchTemplate.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. This step is fetching the proposal's branch of code. It is an imperative-style step name, all lower case. "(from template)" says the step was quick because it reused a ready-made template instead of starting from nothing.

progress.build.label.fetchWaited.text: fetch branch (waited for an earlier run)
progress.build.label.fetchWaited.description: Name of one of the five steps in the row that shows a proposal's preview being built, on the proposal's page. This step is fetching the proposal's branch of code. It is an imperative-style step name, all lower case. "(waited for an earlier run)" says the step is finished and took long because it waited for an earlier run of the same proposal's checks.

progress.build.done.fetch.description: One item in the list of finished steps after "Preview build:" or "Preview built in 20s:" in the checks note on a proposal's page: the step of fetching the proposal's branch of code is finished. {{duration}} is how long it took, for example "3s". Items are joined with commas, so it starts in lower case.

progress.build.done.fetchTemplate.description: One item in the list of finished steps after "Preview build:" or "Preview built in 20s:" in the checks note on a proposal's page: the step of fetching the proposal's branch of code is finished. {{duration}} is how long it took, for example "3s". Items are joined with commas, so it starts in lower case. "from template" says it reused a ready-made template.

progress.build.now.fetch.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its preview is being built: the step running now is fetching the proposal's branch of code. No step has finished yet.

progress.build.nowAfter.fetch.text: Preview build: {{steps}}, now fetching the branch.
progress.build.nowAfter.fetch.description: Sentence in the checks note on a proposal's page while its preview is being built: the step running now is fetching the proposal's branch of code. {{steps}} is the list of finished steps with their times, for example "branch fetched (3s), image built (40s)".

progress.build.sub.fetch.description: One short line under the "Checks" label on a proposal's page while its preview is being built: the step running now is fetching the proposal's branch of code. "build" is a noun here, the building of the preview; the line starts in lower case.
