checks.none.heading.description: Heading of the checks note on a change's page when the change is still being worked on and its automated checks have never run.

checks.none.body.text: Checks run once the agent commits a change: a staging preview is built, then the automated tests run against it.
checks.none.body.description: Body of the checks note on a change's page under "No checks yet": says when the automated checks will first run. "Checks run" is a statement (the checks will run), not a command; "the agent" is the AI coding agent working on the change.

checks.starting.heading.description: Heading of the checks note on a change's page, beside a spinner, when a first run of the automated checks is about to begin.

checks.starting.body.text: The staging preview is being prepared, then automated tests run against it. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.starting.body.description: Body of the checks note on a change's page under "Checks are starting…". "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app.

checks.starting.stuck.text: If this has been stuck for a while, the platform re-runs the checks automatically, or re-run them now.
checks.starting.stuck.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page when the checks have been "starting" for over ten minutes; a "Re-run checks" button follows it. "re-run them now" addresses the reader.

checks.deferred.heading.text: Checks deferred until this merges cleanly.
checks.deferred.heading.description: Heading of the checks note on a change's page when the preview was built but the tests were put off because the proposal conflicts with the main line of code. "this" is the proposal.

checks.deferred.body.text: This proposal conflicts with main, so its preview was built but the automated tests were not run: they would judge a tree that cannot merge. They run automatically once it merges cleanly, and the merge waits for them.
checks.deferred.body.description: Body of the checks note on a change's page when the tests were put off. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is; "a tree" is a version of the code.

checks.deferred.builtWhen.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page when the tests were put off: when the preview was built. {{when}} is a relative time such as "5 minutes ago".

checks.deferred.rerun.text: To test this head as it stands anyway, re-run the checks.
checks.deferred.rerun.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page when the tests were put off; a "Re-run checks" button follows it. "this head" is the proposal's latest commit.

checks.pending.waitingSince.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page while the run waits its turn for a free slot. {{when}} is a relative time such as "4 minutes ago".

checks.pending.started.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page while the automated checks are running: when this run began. {{when}} is a relative time such as "4 minutes ago".

checks.pending.movedConflict_one.text: Main has moved {{count}} commit ahead and this proposal conflicts with it. This run is judged against the commit before that, so when the platform resolves the conflict the run starts again on the resolved commit.
checks.pending.movedConflict_one.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page while the checks are running and the project's main line of code ("main", kept as it is) has gained {{count}} commits that this proposal conflicts with. "run" is a noun: this run of the checks.

checks.pending.movedConflict_other.text: Main has moved {{count}} commits ahead and this proposal conflicts with it. This run is judged against the commit before that, so when the platform resolves the conflict the run starts again on the resolved commit.
checks.pending.movedConflict_other.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page while the checks are running and the project's main line of code ("main", kept as it is) has gained {{count}} commits that this proposal conflicts with. "run" is a noun: this run of the checks.

checks.pending.movedClean_one.text: Main has moved {{count}} commit ahead. That does not restart this run: a proposal that still merges cleanly merges as it stands.
checks.pending.movedClean_one.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page while the checks are running and the project's main line of code ("main", kept as it is) has gained {{count}} commits that this proposal does not conflict with. "run" is a noun: this run of the checks.

checks.pending.movedClean_other.text: Main has moved {{count}} commits ahead. That does not restart this run: a proposal that still merges cleanly merges as it stands.
checks.pending.movedClean_other.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page while the checks are running and the project's main line of code ("main", kept as it is) has gained {{count}} commits that this proposal does not conflict with. "run" is a noun: this run of the checks.

checks.pending.stuck.text: If this has been running for a while, the platform re-runs the checks automatically, or re-run them now.
checks.pending.stuck.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page when a run of the checks has been going for over ten minutes; a "Re-run checks" button follows it. "re-run them now" addresses the reader.

checks.pending.left_one.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page while the automated checks run: how much longer they should take, from this project's usual time. {{count}} is the estimated number of minutes.

checks.pending.left_other.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page while the automated checks run: how much longer they should take, from this project's usual time. {{count}} is the estimated number of minutes.

checks.pending.leftUnder.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page while the automated checks run: under a minute should remain.

checks.pending.longer_one.text: This is taking longer than usual (usually about {{count}} minute).
checks.pending.longer_one.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page when a run has gone past its usual total time. {{count}} is how many minutes a whole run usually takes here.

checks.pending.longer_other.text: This is taking longer than usual (usually about {{count}} minutes).
checks.pending.longer_other.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page when a run has gone past its usual total time. {{count}} is how many minutes a whole run usually takes here.

checks.pending.wait_one.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page while a run waits for a free slot: how long its wait should be. {{count}} is the estimated number of minutes.

checks.pending.wait_other.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page while a run waits for a free slot: how long its wait should be. {{count}} is the estimated number of minutes.

checks.pending.waitLonger.text: This wait is longer than usual.
checks.pending.waitLonger.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page when a run has waited for a free slot longer than its rough wait suggested.

checks.pending.rough.text: A rough estimate from other projects, since this one has few finished runs.
checks.pending.rough.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page when the time shown is borrowed from recent runs across Homeroom: the project has too few finished runs of its own.

checks.error.heading.description: Heading of the checks note on a change's page when the automated checks could not be run at all (the build or the test run broke). Keep the warning sign.

checks.error.generic.text: The staging build or the test run itself broke, so the platform can't confirm the app works.
checks.error.generic.description: Body of the checks note on a change's page under "Checks couldn't run." when no more specific reason was recorded.

checks.error.blocked.text: Merge is blocked until checks pass. Pushing a fix rebuilds the preview and re-runs the checks.
checks.error.blocked.description: Small print in the checks note on a change's page under "Checks couldn't run.". "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app. "Pushing a fix" is uploading a corrected commit.

checks.skipped.heading.description: Heading of the checks note on a change's page when the automated checks were left out on purpose because there was nothing for them to test.

checks.skipped.withReason.text: Checks were skipped: {{reason}}. It can still go live.
checks.skipped.withReason.description: Body of the checks note on a change's page under "Checks skipped.". {{reason}} is the reason the platform recorded, in its own words, without a full stop. "It" is the change; "go live" means be merged and running.

checks.skipped.nothingToTest.text: Checks were skipped: there was nothing to test. It can still go live.
checks.skipped.nothingToTest.description: Body of the checks note on a change's page under "Checks skipped." when no reason was recorded. "It" is the change; "go live" means be merged and running.

checks.reason.failedRuns_one.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build.
checks.reason.failedRuns_one.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more).

checks.reason.failedRuns_other.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build.
checks.reason.failedRuns_other.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more).

checks.reason.failedThenPassed_one.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build, then passed when re-run.
checks.reason.failedThenPassed_one.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). The check passed in the end.

checks.reason.failedThenPassed_other.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build, then passed when re-run.
checks.reason.failedThenPassed_other.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). The check passed in the end.

checks.reason.failedRunsWith_one.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build. {{reason}}
checks.reason.failedRunsWith_one.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). {{reason}} is the failure message the check itself wrote, shown as it is.

checks.reason.failedRunsWith_other.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build. {{reason}}
checks.reason.failedRunsWith_other.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). {{reason}} is the failure message the check itself wrote, shown as it is.

checks.reason.failedThenPassedWith_one.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build, then passed when re-run. {{reason}}
checks.reason.failedThenPassedWith_one.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). The check passed in the end. {{reason}} is the failure message the check itself wrote, shown as it is.

checks.reason.failedThenPassedWith_other.text: Failed {{fails}} of {{count}} runs on this build, then passed when re-run. {{reason}}
checks.reason.failedThenPassedWith_other.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that was run several times on the same build. {{fails}} is how many of those runs failed and {{count}} how many runs there were (always two or more). The check passed in the end. {{reason}} is the failure message the check itself wrote, shown as it is.

checks.reason.earlyBurst.text: Failed early in the run together with other checks, then passed every re-run. This often means the test environment was not ready yet, but check that this change does not break the screen this check opens.
checks.reason.earlyBurst.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that failed in a burst of failures in the first seconds of the test run and then passed every time it was run again on a fresh page. Says the environment is a likely cause but not a proven one, and asks the author to check the screen anyway.

checks.reason.earlyBurstWith.text: Failed early in the run together with other checks, then passed every re-run. This often means the test environment was not ready yet, but check that this change does not break the screen this check opens. {{reason}}
checks.reason.earlyBurstWith.description: Reason line under one check in the list of a proposal's check results, for a check that failed in a burst of failures in the first seconds of the test run and then passed every time it was run again on a fresh page. Says the environment is a likely cause but not a proven one, and asks the author to check the screen anyway. {{reason}} is the failure message the check itself wrote, shown as it is.

checks.note.freshLoad.text: This check needed a fresh load after an address change: fix the navigation (an address change must draw what a fresh load of that address draws).
checks.note.freshLoad.description: Advice under one automated check that this proposal adds or changes, in its opened details. The checks reach several screens of one page by changing the address after the # sign; this check only passed after the page was loaded again from scratch. Tells the author to fix the app's navigation so that changing the address shows the same screen a fresh load of that address shows. Advisory: the check's result is unchanged.

verdict.summary.checks_one.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many automated checks ran.

verdict.summary.checks_other.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many automated checks ran.

verdict.summary.passed_one.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many checks passed.

verdict.summary.passed_other.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many checks passed.

verdict.summary.blocking_one.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many failed checks stop the change from being merged.

verdict.summary.blocking_other.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many failed checks stop the change from being merged.

verdict.summary.advisory_one.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many failed checks are advisory: they are reported but do not stop the merge.

verdict.summary.advisory_other.description: One fact in the summary line above a proposal's list of check results, for example "523 checks · 520 passed · 1 blocking failure · 2 advisory failures". {{count}} is how many failed checks are advisory: they are reported but do not stop the merge.

verdict.heading.failed.text: ⚠ Some checks failed. Merge is blocked until they pass.
verdict.heading.failed.description: Heading of the check results on a proposal's page when at least one check that gates the merge failed. Keep the warning sign. "Merge" is the noun.

verdict.heading.blockingPassed.text: ✓ Every merge-blocking check passed on the staging build.
verdict.heading.blockingPassed.description: Heading of the check results on a proposal's page when every check that gates the merge passed and only advisory checks failed. Keep the check mark. "the staging build" is the preview built from the proposal.

verdict.heading.allPassed.text: ✓ All checks passed on the staging build.
verdict.heading.allPassed.description: Heading of the check results on a proposal's page when every check passed. Keep the check mark. "the staging build" is the preview built from the proposal.

verdict.advisoryNote.text: Advisory checks have not yet passed on a change that merged, so they report without blocking. Fix one, and once the fix merges it guards every change after it.
verdict.advisoryNote.description: Note under a proposal's check results explaining what an advisory check is: a check that has never passed on a merged change, so its failures do not block. Once a change that makes it pass merges, it blocks every later change that fails it.

verdict.lastChecked.description: Small print under a proposal's check results: when the checks last ran. {{when}} is a relative time such as "3 hours ago".

verdict.fixNote.text: Pushing a fix rebuilds the preview and re-runs the checks. The block clears when they pass.
verdict.fixNote.description: Small print under a proposal's failed check results. "Pushing a fix" is uploading a corrected commit; "The block" is the block on merging.

verdict.row.unnamedCheck.description: Stands in for a check's name in a proposal's list of check results when the check has no name. A noun, lower case.

verdict.row.unnamedTest.description: Stands in for a unit test's name above its captured error text in a proposal's check results, when the test has no name. A noun, lower case.

checks.baseNote.these.agoConflict_one.text: These ran against main as it was {{count}} commit ago, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. It now conflicts with main; resolving the conflict re-runs them on the resolved commit.
checks.baseNote.these.agoConflict_one.description: Note under a proposal's check results when they were earned against an older state of the main line of code. "These" and "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. The proposal now conflicts with main.

checks.baseNote.these.agoConflict_other.text: These ran against main as it was {{count}} commits ago, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. It now conflicts with main; resolving the conflict re-runs them on the resolved commit.
checks.baseNote.these.agoConflict_other.description: Note under a proposal's check results when they were earned against an older state of the main line of code. "These" and "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. The proposal now conflicts with main.

checks.baseNote.these.movedConflict.text: These ran against a version of main that has since moved on, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. It now conflicts with main; resolving the conflict re-runs them on the resolved commit.
checks.baseNote.these.movedConflict.description: Note under a proposal's check results when they were earned against an older state of the main line of code. "These" and "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. Used when it is not known how far main has moved. The proposal now conflicts with main.

checks.baseNote.these.agoClean_one.text: These ran against main as it was {{count}} commit ago, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. That does not hold the merge: a proposal that still merges cleanly merges as it stands, and the platform runs the app’s tests on main again straight after.
checks.baseNote.these.agoClean_one.description: Note under a proposal's check results when they were earned against an older state of the main line of code. "These" and "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. The proposal still merges cleanly, so nothing holds it.

checks.baseNote.these.agoClean_other.text: These ran against main as it was {{count}} commits ago, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. The proposal still merges cleanly, so nothing holds it.

checks.baseNote.these.movedClean.description: Note under a proposal's check results when they were earned against an older state of the main line of code. "These" and "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. Used when it is not known how far main has moved. The proposal still merges cleanly, so nothing holds it.

checks.baseNote.passedBut.agoConflict_on.text: The checks passed, but ran against main as it was {{count}} commit ago, so they describe code this proposal would no longer merge into. It now conflicts with main; resolving the conflict re-runs them on the resolved commit.
checks.baseNote.passedBut.agoConflict_on.description: Tooltip of the "older main" tag on a proposal's card when its checks passed against an older state of the main line of code. "they" are the check results. "main" is the name of the project's main line of code and stays as it is. {{count}} is how many commits main has gained since. The proposal now conflicts with main.

checks.phase.building.title.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note, on its card's status chip and in the "Tested" line of its page: the proposal's preview is still being built.

checks.phase.building.detail.text: The change is being built and a preview copy of the app’s data is being made.
checks.phase.building.detail.description: Tooltip of the checks status chip on a proposal's or session's card, explaining the status: the proposal's preview is still being built.

checks.phase.building.blocked.text: The change is being built and a preview copy of the app’s data is being made. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.phase.building.blocked.description: First line of the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are in progress: the proposal's preview is still being built. "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app.

checks.phase.testing.title.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note, on its card's status chip and in the "Tested" line of its page: the preview is built and the tests are running.

checks.phase.testing.detail.text: The preview is up and the automated tests are running against it.
checks.phase.testing.detail.description: Tooltip of the checks status chip on a proposal's or session's card, explaining the status: the preview is built and the tests are running.

checks.phase.testing.blocked.text: The preview is up and the automated tests are running against it. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.phase.testing.blocked.description: First line of the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are in progress: the preview is built and the tests are running. "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app.

checks.phase.queued.title.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note, on its card's status chip and in the "Tested" line of its page: the preview is built and the run waits its turn, because only a few proposals' checks run at once. "slot" is a free place to run.

checks.phase.queued.detail.text: The preview is up. Homeroom runs a few proposals’ checks at a time so they don’t slow each other down, and these start on their own when a slot frees up.
checks.phase.queued.detail.description: Tooltip of the checks status chip on a proposal's or session's card, explaining the status: the preview is built and the run waits its turn, because only a few proposals' checks run at once. "Homeroom" is the product's name; "these" are the checks.

checks.phase.queued.blocked.text: The preview is up. Homeroom runs a few proposals’ checks at a time so they don’t slow each other down, and these start on their own when a slot frees up. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.phase.queued.blocked.description: First line of the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are in progress: the preview is built and the run waits its turn, because only a few proposals' checks run at once. "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app. "Homeroom" is the product's name; "these" are the checks.

checks.phase.deferred.title.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note, on its card's status chip and in the "Tested" line of its page: the preview is built but the tests were put off because the proposal conflicts with the main line of code ("main", kept as it is).

checks.phase.deferred.detail.text: The preview is up, but the tests were not run: this proposal conflicts with main, and they would judge a tree that cannot merge. They run once it merges cleanly.
checks.phase.deferred.detail.description: Tooltip of the checks status chip on a proposal's or session's card, explaining the status: the preview is built but the tests were put off because the proposal conflicts with the main line of code ("main", kept as it is).

checks.phase.deferred.blocked.text: The preview is up, but the tests were not run: this proposal conflicts with main, and they would judge a tree that cannot merge. They run once it merges cleanly. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.phase.deferred.blocked.description: First line of the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are in progress: the preview is built but the tests were put off because the proposal conflicts with the main line of code ("main", kept as it is). "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app.

checks.phase.other.title.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note, on its card's status chip and in the "Tested" line of its page: the checks are running and the stage is not known.

checks.phase.other.detail.text: The staging build is being tested.
checks.phase.other.detail.description: Tooltip of the checks status chip on a proposal's or session's card, explaining the status: the checks are running and the stage is not known.

checks.phase.other.blocked.text: The staging build is being tested. Merge is blocked until all tests pass.
checks.phase.other.blocked.description: First line of the checks note on a proposal's page while its automated checks are in progress: the checks are running and the stage is not known. "Merge" is the noun: putting the change into the live app.

checks.phase.queued.titleNext.text: Waiting for a checks slot (next in line)
checks.phase.queued.titleNext.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note and on its card: the run waits its turn for a free slot and no other run is ahead of it.

checks.phase.queued.titleAhead_one.text: Waiting for a checks slot ({{count}} ahead)
checks.phase.queued.titleAhead_one.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note and on its card: the run waits its turn for a free slot. {{count}} is how many other runs are ahead of it in line.

checks.phase.queued.titleAhead_other.text: Waiting for a checks slot ({{count}} ahead)
checks.phase.queued.titleAhead_other.description: Status of a proposal's automated checks, shown as the heading of its checks note and on its card: the run waits its turn for a free slot. {{count}} is how many other runs are ahead of it in line.

checks.trigger.proposalOpen.text: Triggered by this proposal being opened.
checks.trigger.proposalOpen.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: the proposal was opened (created).

checks.trigger.commitPush.text: Triggered by a new commit on this proposal.
checks.trigger.commitPush.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: new code was added to the proposal.

checks.trigger.syncMain.text: Triggered by this proposal being updated from main.
checks.trigger.syncMain.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: the proposal was brought up to date with the main line of code ("main", kept as it is).

checks.trigger.prImport.text: Triggered by a new commit on the imported pull request.
checks.trigger.prImport.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: new code arrived on the GitHub pull request this proposal was imported from.

checks.trigger.manualRecheck.text: Triggered by someone asking for a re-run.
checks.trigger.manualRecheck.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: a person pressed "Re-run checks".

checks.trigger.promoteKick.text: Triggered by this proposal being put to a vote.
checks.trigger.promoteKick.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: the proposal was put up for a vote.

checks.trigger.bootReconcile.text: Restarted by the platform after it came back up.
checks.trigger.bootReconcile.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: the platform restarted and picked the run up again.

checks.trigger.stuckSweep.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: the platform noticed the earlier run was stuck and started it again.

checks.trigger.fleetMaintenance.description: Small print in the checks note on a proposal's page saying why the run of checks now in progress began: routine maintenance of the platform.

checks.recheck.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when asking to run a proposal's automated checks again failed and the server gave no message. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

checks.recheck.failedWith.description: Toast shown when asking to run a proposal's automated checks again failed. {{error}} is the error's own message, shown as it is.

checks.recheck.unavailable.text: Re-running checks is unavailable in this preview.
checks.recheck.unavailable.description: Toast shown when "Re-run checks" is pressed inside a staging preview of Homeroom itself, where checks cannot be run.

checks.recheck.stillRunning.text: These checks are still running, so they were not started again. The result will show here when they finish.
checks.recheck.stillRunning.description: Toast shown after "Re-run checks" is pressed while a run of the same commit's checks has not finished yet.

governance.apply.closingIssue.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) is being closed. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.closingIssueSlow.text: Closing issue, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.closingIssueSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) is being closed. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.reopeningIssue.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on reopening a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) is being reopened. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.reopeningIssueSlow.text: Reopening the issue, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.reopeningIssueSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on reopening a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) is being reopened. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.envVar.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: a change to one of the app's environment variables is being applied. "env-var" is short for environment variable. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.envVarSlow.text: Applying env-var change, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.envVarSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: a change to one of the app's environment variables is being applied. "env-var" is short for environment variable. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.rename.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the app is being renamed. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.renameSlow.text: Renaming app, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.renameSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the app is being renamed. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.campaign.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: a maintenance campaign (one change rolled out to many apps) is being started. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.campaignSlow.text: Starting campaign, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.campaignSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: a maintenance campaign (one change rolled out to many apps) is being started. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.illustration.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the app's featured illustration is being replaced. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.illustrationSlow.text: Updating illustration, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.illustrationSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the app's featured illustration is being replaced. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.other.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the decision is being applied; used when the kind of proposal is not known. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.otherSlow.text: Applying, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.otherSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the decision is being applied; used when the kind of proposal is not known. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.closingIssueNumber.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) with number {{number}} is being closed. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.apply.closingIssueNumberSlow.text: Closing issue #{{number}}, still working, GitHub may be slow…
governance.apply.closingIssueNumberSlow.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request, not on code) once the vote has passed and the decision is being carried out: the request (issue) with number {{number}} is being closed. Shown once it has taken more than a few seconds. "GitHub" is the service's name. Keep the ellipsis.

governance.failed.closeLabel.text: Close didn't complete. Try voting again
governance.failed.closeLabel.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when the vote passed but closing the request failed. "Close" is a noun here: the act of closing the request.

governance.failed.label.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when the vote passed but carrying out the decision failed.

governance.failed.titleWith.description: Tooltip of the "Didn't complete" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request). "The apply" is a noun: carrying out the decision. {{error}} is the server's own error message.

governance.failed.title.text: The apply didn't finish. Voting again re-drives it.
governance.failed.title.description: Tooltip of the "Didn't complete" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request), when no error message came back. "The apply" is a noun: carrying out the decision; "re-drives it" means starts it again.

governance.stalled.closeLabel.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when closing the request has run for over a minute with no answer. "Refresh" tells the reader to reload the page.

governance.stalled.label.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when carrying out the decision has run for over a minute with no answer. "Refresh" tells the reader to reload the page.

governance.stalled.title.text: This is taking much longer than usual. The apply may still be running on the server. Refresh to see where it landed.
governance.stalled.title.description: Tooltip of the "Still closing" / "Still applying" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request). "The apply" is a noun: carrying out the decision.

governance.slow.title.text: Still working. GitHub can be slow to accept the close; nothing is lost while this runs.
governance.slow.title.description: Tooltip of the status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) once carrying out the decision has taken more than a few seconds. "the close" is a noun: closing the request. "GitHub" is the service's name.

governance.applying.closeTitle.text: The vote passed. The issue is being closed here and on GitHub.
governance.applying.closeTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Closing issue…" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request). "here" is Homeroom; "GitHub" is the service's name.

governance.applying.title.text: The vote passed. This change is being applied.
governance.applying.title.description: Tooltip of the "Applying…" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request). "This change" is the change to a setting that was voted on.

governance.pending.closeLabel.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when the vote passed but the request has not been closed yet, some minutes later. "Close" is a noun: the closing of the request.

governance.pending.label.description: Status chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request) when the vote passed but the decision has not been carried out yet, some minutes later. "Apply" is a noun: the carrying out.

governance.pending.title.text: The vote passed, but the change hasn't gone through yet. The platform retries automatically.
governance.pending.title.description: Tooltip of the "Close pending" / "Apply pending" chip on a governance proposal's card (a vote on a setting or on closing a request).

governance.title.rename.description: Title of a governance proposal's card that asks the group to rename the app. {{name}} is the proposed new name.

governance.title.closeIssue.description: Title of a governance proposal's card that asks the group to close a request. "Close" is a verb. {{number}} is the request's number (or "?" when unknown) and {{title}} its title.

governance.title.reopenIssue.description: Title of a governance proposal's card that asks the group to reopen a closed request. "Reopen" is a verb. {{number}} is the request's number (or "?" when unknown) and {{title}} its title.

governance.meta.kind.description: First item on the small line under a governance proposal's title on its card: says what kind of thing the card is, a vote on a setting or on closing a request and not on code.

governance.meta.closedByAdminWhen.description: Item on the small line under a settled governance proposal's title: an admin closed it. {{when}} is a relative time such as "3h ago". Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.meta.closedByVoteWhen.description: Item on the small line under a settled governance proposal's title: the group's vote closed it. {{when}} is a relative time such as "3h ago". Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.meta.closedByAdmin.description: Item on the small line under a settled governance proposal's title, when the time is not known: an admin closed it. Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.meta.closedByVote.description: Item on the small line under a settled governance proposal's title, when the time is not known: the group's vote closed it. Lower case, it follows other items.

governance.vote.yes.description: Button on a governance proposal's card: votes in favour. {{tally}} is the number of Yes votes so far, sometimes with a mark such as "2✓".

governance.vote.no.description: Button on a governance proposal's card: votes against. {{tally}} is the number of No votes so far, sometimes with a mark such as "2✓".

governance.menu.adminMerge.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a governance proposal's card, shown to admins: carries out the decision now without waiting for the vote. "merge" is the verb used across Homeroom for an admin forcing a decision through.

governance.menu.adminMergeTitle.text: Admin: apply this change right now, bypassing the vote majority
governance.menu.adminMergeTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Admin merge" row in a governance proposal's ⋯ menu. "Admin:" marks it as an admin-only action.

governance.menu.viewCampaign.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a maintenance-campaign proposal's card, shown to admins: opens the campaign's dashboard. A campaign is one change rolled out to many apps.

governance.menu.viewCampaignTitle.description: Tooltip of the "View campaign" row in a governance proposal's ⋯ menu. "Open" is a verb.

governance.menu.withdraw.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a governance proposal's card, shown to the person who made it: takes the proposal back so it is no longer voted on. A verb.

governance.menu.edit.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a card-picture proposal's card, shown to the person who proposed it while the vote waits: opens the picture editor to replace the waiting picture.

governance.menu.editTitle.text: Replace the picture this waiting proposal carries
governance.menu.editTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Edit proposal" row in a card-picture proposal's ⋯ menu. "Replace" is a verb.

governance.menu.withdrawTitle.text: Withdraw this proposal (removes it from the vote panel)
governance.menu.withdrawTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Withdraw" row in a governance proposal's ⋯ menu.

governance.card.openTitle.description: Tooltip of a governance proposal's card in the Workshop list; pressing the card opens its page. "Open" is a verb.

governance.closes.title.description: Small heading inside About this proposal on a proposal to close a request, over the closed request's title, who asked and its words.

governance.roster.yes_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a governance proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

governance.roster.yes_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a governance proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

governance.roster.no_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a governance proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

governance.roster.no_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a governance proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

governance.withdraw.title.description: Title of the dialog confirming that the person wants to take back a governance proposal they made.

governance.withdraw.message.text: This removes it from the vote panel and stops the vote. You can propose it again later.
governance.withdraw.message.description: Body of the dialog confirming the withdrawal of a governance proposal.

governance.withdraw.confirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog that withdraws a governance proposal. A verb.

governance.withdraw.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when withdrawing a governance proposal failed and the server gave no message. "Withdraw" is a noun here: the withdrawal. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

governance.withdraw.failedWith.description: Toast shown when withdrawing a governance proposal failed. "Withdraw" is a noun here: the withdrawal. {{error}} is the error's own message.

vote.roster.yes.all_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

vote.roster.yes.all_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

vote.roster.yes.approvers_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{count}} is how many approvers voted this way, and the check mark means "approver". Keep the check mark.

vote.roster.yes.approvers_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{count}} is how many approvers voted this way, and the check mark means "approver". Keep the check mark.

vote.roster.yes.approversAdvisory_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{approvers}} is how many approvers voted this way (the check mark means "approver", keep it) and {{count}} how many other people did, whose votes are advisory and do not count.

vote.roster.yes.approversAdvisory_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted Yes on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{approvers}} is how many approvers voted this way (the check mark means "approver", keep it) and {{count}} how many other people did, whose votes are advisory and do not count.

vote.roster.no.all_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

vote.roster.no.all_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. {{count}} is how many people.

vote.roster.no.approvers_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{count}} is how many approvers voted this way, and the check mark means "approver". Keep the check mark.

vote.roster.no.approvers_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{count}} is how many approvers voted this way, and the check mark means "approver". Keep the check mark.

vote.roster.no.approversAdvisory_one.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{approvers}} is how many approvers voted this way (the check mark means "approver", keep it) and {{count}} how many other people did, whose votes are advisory and do not count.

vote.roster.no.approversAdvisory_other.description: Lead of the list of people who voted No on a proposal, on its page; the names follow after a colon. Used where only invited approvers' votes count: {{approvers}} is how many approvers voted this way (the check mark means "approver", keep it) and {{count}} how many other people did, whose votes are advisory and do not count.

vote.roster.earlier.yes_one.text: Earlier version: {{yes}} said yes. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.yes_one.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{yes}} lists them by @username.

vote.roster.earlier.yes_other.text: Earlier version: {{yes}} said yes. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.yes_other.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{yes}} lists them by @username.

vote.roster.earlier.no_one.text: Earlier version: {{no}} said no. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.no_one.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{no}} lists them by @username.

vote.roster.earlier.no_other.text: Earlier version: {{no}} said no. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.no_other.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{no}} lists them by @username.

vote.roster.earlier.both_one.text: Earlier version: {{yes}} said yes; {{no}} said no. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.both_one.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{yes}} lists by @username those who had voted Yes and {{no}} those who had voted No.

vote.roster.earlier.both_other.text: Earlier version: {{yes}} said yes; {{no}} said no. Not counted until they take another look.
vote.roster.earlier.both_other.description: Line under the list of voters on a proposal's page, about people who voted before the proposal was changed. Their votes are set aside until they vote again on the new version. {{count}} is how many such people there are in all. {{yes}} lists by @username those who had voted Yes and {{no}} those who had voted No.

proposal.askApproval.sharing.description: Label of the "Ask for approval" button on an imported pull request's card while the request to put it up for a vote is being sent.

proposal.askApproval.failedHttp.text: Could not ask for approval on this change (HTTP {{status}}).
proposal.askApproval.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when putting an imported change up for a vote failed and the server gave no message. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

proposal.askApproval.failedWith.text: Could not ask for approval on this change: {{error}}
proposal.askApproval.failedWith.description: Toast shown when putting an imported change up for a vote failed. {{error}} is the error's own message.

proposal.withdraw.title.description: Title of the dialog confirming that the person wants to take back their own proposal (a change put up for a vote).

proposal.withdraw.message.text: This closes PR {{number}} and removes it from the vote panel. You can propose it again later.
proposal.withdraw.message.description: Body of the dialog confirming the withdrawal of a proposal. "PR" is a GitHub pull request; {{number}} is its number.

proposal.withdraw.confirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog that withdraws the person's own proposal. A verb.

proposal.withdraw.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when withdrawing a proposal failed and the server gave no message. "Withdraw" is a noun here: the withdrawal. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

proposal.withdraw.failedWith.description: Toast shown when withdrawing a proposal failed. "Withdraw" is a noun here: the withdrawal. {{error}} is the error's own message.

proposal.moveBack.title.description: Title of the dialog confirming that the person wants to take their own proposal out of the vote and keep working on it. "Underway" is the name of the board column for changes still being worked on.

proposal.moveBack.message.text: This takes PR {{number}} out of review so you can keep working on it. Its votes are cleared and it cannot be merged until you propose it again. The pull request stays open.
proposal.moveBack.message.description: Body of the dialog confirming that a proposal goes back to Underway. "PR" is a GitHub pull request; {{number}} is its number.

proposal.moveBack.confirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog that takes a proposal out of the vote and back to the Underway column.

proposal.moveBack.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when taking a proposal back to Underway failed and the server gave no message. "it" is the proposal. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

proposal.moveBack.failedWith.description: Toast shown when taking a proposal back to Underway failed. "it" is the proposal. {{error}} is the error's own message.

attributes.priority.high.description: One of the three priorities people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's priority chip (after a flag glyph) and as an option in the priority picker. The most urgent.

attributes.priority.medium.description: One of the three priorities people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's priority chip (after a flag glyph) and as an option in the priority picker. The middle one.

attributes.priority.low.description: One of the three priorities people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's priority chip (after a flag glyph) and as an option in the priority picker. The least urgent.

attributes.category.feature.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. Something new the app would do.

attributes.category.bug.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. Something that is broken.

attributes.category.improvement.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. Making something that exists better.

attributes.category.design.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. How the app looks and feels.

attributes.category.docs.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. Documentation; short for "documents".

attributes.category.chore.description: One of the six built-in categories of work people can vote onto a request's or proposal's card; shown on the card's category chip, in the category picker and in the board's category filter. Routine upkeep that changes nothing people see.

attributes.chip.setPriority.description: Chip on a request's or proposal's page, after a flag glyph, when nobody has voted a priority for it yet; pressing it opens the priority picker.

attributes.chip.setCategory.description: Chip on a request's or proposal's page when it has no category yet; pressing it opens the category picker.

attributes.chip.unassigned.description: Chip on a request's or proposal's page when nobody has been suggested to take the work; pressing it opens the picker of people.

attributes.chip.priorityTitle.description: Tooltip of the priority chip on a request's or proposal's card.

attributes.chip.categoryTitle.description: Tooltip of the category chip on a request's or proposal's card.

attributes.chip.categoryPlacedTitle.text: Placed automatically. Tap to vote for a different category
attributes.chip.categoryPlacedTitle.description: Tooltip of the category chip on a card whose category was chosen by Homeroom's AI and not by a vote.

attributes.chip.assigneeTitle.text: Suggest or vote on who should take this
attributes.chip.assigneeTitle.description: Tooltip of the chip that shows who a request or proposal is assigned to. "take this" means take on the work.

attributes.chip.assignTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Unassigned" chip on a request's or proposal's page.

attributes.menu.setPriority.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of priorities. Shown when the card has no priority yet. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.changePriority.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of priorities. Shown when the card already has one. "Change" is a verb. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.priorityTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Set priority…" / "Change priority…" row in a card's ⋯ menu.

attributes.menu.setCategory.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of categories. Shown when the card has no category yet. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.changeCategory.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of categories. Shown when the card already has one. "Change" is a verb. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.categoryTitle.text: Vote on which category this card belongs to
attributes.menu.categoryTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Set category…" / "Change category…" row in a card's ⋯ menu.

attributes.menu.assign.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of people. Shown when nobody is assigned to the work yet. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.changeAssignee.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's or proposal's card: opens the picker of people. Shown when somebody is already assigned. "Change" is a verb; the assignee is the person who takes the work. Keep the ellipsis.

attributes.menu.assigneeTitle.text: Suggest or vote on who should take this
attributes.menu.assigneeTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Assign someone…" / "Change assignee…" row in a card's ⋯ menu. "take this" means take on the work.

attributes.picker.priorityHead.description: Heading of the small picker that opens from a card's priority chip, above the three priorities to vote for.

attributes.picker.categoryHead.description: Heading of the small picker that opens from a card's category chip, above the built-in categories to vote for.

attributes.picker.customHead.description: Heading in the category picker above the categories this project's members typed themselves, under the built-in ones.

attributes.picker.categoryPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the text box at the bottom of the category picker, where a person types a new category name.

attributes.picker.assigneeHead.description: Heading of the small picker that opens from a card's assignee chip, above the people suggested for the work.

attributes.picker.noSuggestions.description: Line in the assignee picker when nobody has been suggested for the work yet.

attributes.picker.namePlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the text box at the bottom of the assignee picker, where a person types a username.

attributes.vote.saveFailed.description: Toast shown when a vote for a card's priority, category or assignee could not be saved and the server gave no message.

attributes.vote.saveFailedWith.description: Toast shown when a vote for a card's priority, category or assignee could not be saved. {{error}} is the error's own message.

attributes.vote.removeFailed.description: Toast shown when taking back a vote for a card's priority, category or assignee failed and the server gave no message.

attributes.vote.removeFailedWith.description: Toast shown when taking back a vote for a card's priority, category or assignee failed. {{error}} is the error's own message.

proposal.undo.title.description: Title of the dialog confirming that the person wants to undo a change that is already merged and live.

proposal.undo.message.text:
This opens a revert PR that backs out this merged change.

It still needs a merge vote to land. Undoing is a proposal the group votes on, just like any other change.
proposal.undo.message.description: Body of the dialog confirming an undo of a merged change, two paragraphs: keep the blank line between them. "revert PR" is a GitHub pull request that reverses the change; "to land" means to be merged.

proposal.undo.confirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog that undoes a merged change. "Open" is a verb: create the pull request that reverses the change.

proposal.undo.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when undoing a merged change failed and the server gave no message. "Undo" is a noun here. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

proposal.undo.failedWith.description: Toast shown when undoing a merged change failed. "Undo" is a noun here. {{error}} is the error's own message.

governance.adminApply.closeTitleNumber.description: Title of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote; the proposal is to close a request. "Close" is a verb. {{number}} is the request's number.

governance.adminApply.closeTitle.description: Title of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote; the proposal is to close a request whose number is not known. "Close" is a verb.

governance.adminApply.campaignTitle.description: Title of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote; the proposal is a maintenance campaign, one change rolled out to many apps.

governance.adminApply.illustrationTitle.description: Title of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote; the proposal replaces the app's featured illustration.

governance.adminApply.envVarTitle.description: Title of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote; the proposal changes one of the app's environment variables ("env-var").

governance.adminApply.closeMessage.text:
This bypasses the active-user vote majority and closes the issue right now, here and on GitHub.

Use only when you're confident the change should ship. The override is announced in group chat with your username.
governance.adminApply.closeMessage.description: Body of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, two paragraphs (keep the blank line); the proposal is to close a request. "here" is Homeroom; "GitHub" is the service's name; "should ship" means should take effect.

governance.adminApply.campaignMessage.text:
This bypasses the platform vote and starts the campaign right now: an AI will open one maintenance PR per app across the fleet.

Use only when you're confident the change should ship. The override is announced in group chat with your username.
governance.adminApply.campaignMessage.description: Body of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, two paragraphs (keep the blank line); the proposal is a maintenance campaign. "PR" is a pull request; "the fleet" is all the apps on the platform.

governance.adminApply.illustrationMessag.text:
This bypasses the active-user vote majority and changes the featured illustration on Discover right now.

Use only when you're confident the change should ship. The override is announced in group chat with your username.
governance.adminApply.illustrationMessag.description: Body of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, two paragraphs (keep the blank line); the proposal replaces the app's featured illustration. "Discover" is the name of the screen where apps are found.

governance.adminApply.envVarMessage.text:
This bypasses the active-user vote majority and applies the proposed secret change right now (the app redeploys with the new value).

Use only when you're confident the change should ship. The override is announced in group chat with your username.
governance.adminApply.envVarMessage.description: Body of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, two paragraphs (keep the blank line); the proposal changes a secret environment variable of the app.

governance.adminApply.closeConfirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, for a proposal to close a request. "Close" is a verb: close the request.

governance.adminApply.campaignConfirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, for a maintenance campaign: starts the campaign.

governance.adminApply.applyConfirm.description: Confirm button of the dialog an admin sees before carrying out a governance proposal at once, without waiting for the vote, for a change to a setting or illustration: applies the change.

governance.adminApply.failedHttp.description: Toast shown when an admin's attempt to carry out a governance proposal at once failed and the server gave no message. "Admin apply" is a noun: the admin's forced apply. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

governance.adminApply.failedWith.description: Toast shown when an admin's attempt to carry out a governance proposal at once failed. "Admin apply" is a noun. {{error}} is the error's own message.

issue.card.kudosTitle.description: Tooltip of the star and number on a request's card: how many kudos (the platform's thanks points) people have promised to whoever makes the request happen.

issue.card.autoTitlePending.description: Item on the small line under a request's title on its card: the title shown is a stand-in and an AI-written one is on its way. Lower case, it follows other items.

issue.card.closing.description: Status chip, beside a spinner, on a request's card once the vote to close it has passed and it is being closed. Keep the ellipsis.

issue.card.closeProposed.description: Status chip on a request's card while a proposal to close it is being voted on. "Close" is a noun: closing the request has been proposed.

issue.card.closeProposedTitle.text: Closing this request is waiting for approval
issue.card.closeProposedTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Close proposed" chip on a request's card.

issue.card.closed.description: Status chip on the card of a request that is closed (finished or dismissed). Describes the request.

issue.card.closedWhen.description: Tooltip of the "Closed" chip on a request's card. {{when}} is a relative time such as "3 days ago".

issue.card.closedTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Closed" chip on a request's card when the time it was closed is not known.

issue.card.openTitle.description: Tooltip of a request's card in the Workshop list; pressing the card opens the request's page. "Open" is a verb.

issue.action.seeProgress.description: Main button on a request's card in the Workshop list, shown to the person Homeroom bot is building the request for: opens the request's page at the bot's progress card.

issue.action.seePlan.description: Main button on a request's card in the Workshop list while Homeroom bot's plan for it waits for Build it: opens the request's page at the plan, where its Build it button is. Any member may press Build it there.

issue.action.seePlanTitle.text: Open the plan on this request, where you can build it
issue.action.seePlanTitle.description: Tooltip of the "See the plan" button on a request's card in the Workshop list.

issue.action.seeProgressTitle.text: Open this request, where its progress is
issue.action.seeProgressTitle.description: Tooltip of the "See progress" button on a request's card in the Workshop list. "Open" is a verb.

issue.action.botOnIt.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): disabled, shown to other people while the request waits in Homeroom bot's queue. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's builder bot; "is on it" means it has taken the job.

issue.action.botHeld.description: Main button on a request's card: disabled, shown while Homeroom bot waits to build the request because it already has as many changes up for a vote on this project as it may.

issue.action.botHeldTitle.text: Homeroom bot starts when one of its changes here is voted in or closed
issue.action.botHeldTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Homeroom bot will build this" button on a request's card. "Here" is the project.

issue.action.botReading.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): disabled, shown while Homeroom bot is reading the request before building. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's builder bot. Keep the ellipsis.

issue.action.botBuilding.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): disabled, shown while Homeroom bot is building what the request asks for. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's builder bot. Keep the ellipsis.

issue.action.botReadingTitle.text: The Homeroom bot is reading this request now
issue.action.botReadingTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Homeroom bot is reading…" button on a request's card.

issue.action.botBuildingTitle.text: The Homeroom bot is building this request now
issue.action.botBuildingTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Homeroom bot is on it" / "Homeroom bot is building…" button on a request's card.

issue.action.askBot.text: Ask Homeroom bot to build this
issue.action.askBot.description: Main button on a request's card (a request is a filed issue): asks the platform's builder bot, named Homeroom bot, to build what the request asks for.

issue.action.workWithBot.text: Work on this with Homeroom bot
issue.action.workWithBot.description: Main button on a request's card and page (a request is a filed issue), where nobody is building it yet: opens a thread only the viewer can see, in their chat with Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant), about this request, to talk it through and plan it. "Work on" is a verb.

issue.action.workWithBotTitle.text: Talk it through and plan it with Homeroom bot, in a thread only you can see
issue.action.workWithBotTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Work on this with Homeroom bot" button on a request's card and page. Homeroom bot is the platform's assistant.

issue.action.letBotBuild.text: Let the bot build it now
issue.action.letBotBuild.description: Main button on a request's card and page while Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) waits for the viewer's plan, because they are working on their own request with it in a private thread: tells the bot to go ahead without a plan. "Build" is a verb.

issue.action.letBotBuildTitle.text: Homeroom bot starts on it without waiting for your plan
issue.action.letBotBuildTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Let the bot build it now" button on a request's card and page. Homeroom bot is the platform's assistant.

issue.action.stopWorking.description: Second button on a request's card in the Workshop list, shown to someone who said they are working on it: takes their name off it.

issue.action.stopWorkingTitle.text: Stop working on this so somebody else can pick it up
issue.action.stopWorkingTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Stop working on this" button on a request's card.

issue.action.claim.description: Second button on a request's card in the Workshop list: tells everyone the viewer will work on the request. "It" is the request.

issue.action.claimTitle.text: Let everyone know you'll work on this. It's not a promise of progress. It clears itself after about 7 days with no activity; talking about it in the request's thread keeps it going.
issue.action.claimTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Claim it" button on a request's card. "It" is the mark that says the viewer is working on the request.

issue.bot.hint_one.text: Usually ready to try in about {{count}} minutes.
issue.bot.hint_one.description: Line under (and tooltip of) the "Ask Homeroom bot to build this" button on a request: how long the bot usually takes before there is something to try. {{count}} is a number of minutes.

issue.bot.hint_other.text: Usually ready to try in about {{count}} minutes.
issue.bot.hint_other.description: Line under (and tooltip of) the "Ask Homeroom bot to build this" button on a request: how long the bot usually takes before there is something to try. {{count}} is a number of minutes.

issue.bot.askFailedHttp.text: Couldn't ask Homeroom bot just now (HTTP {{status}}).
issue.bot.askFailedHttp.description: Toast shown when asking Homeroom bot to build a request failed and the server gave no message. "Homeroom bot" is the bot's name. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

issue.bot.askFailedWith.text: Couldn't ask Homeroom bot just now: {{error}}
issue.bot.askFailedWith.description: Toast shown when asking Homeroom bot to build a request failed. "Homeroom bot" is the bot's name. {{error}} is the error's own message.

issue.bot.threadFailed.text: The thread with Homeroom bot could not be started just now. Try again in a minute.
issue.bot.threadFailed.description: Toast when "Work on this with Homeroom bot" on a request could not open its private thread with Homeroom bot, the platform's assistant.

issue.bot.letBuildDone.text: Homeroom bot no longer waits for your plan.
issue.bot.letBuildDone.description: Toast after "Let the bot build it now" on a request: Homeroom bot, the platform's assistant, may now pick the request up without a plan.

issue.bot.letBuildFailed.text: That did not go through. Try again in a minute.
issue.bot.letBuildFailed.description: Toast when "Let the bot build it now" on a request failed.

issue.bot.onItMine.text: Homeroom bot is on it. Its card is in your chat with it.
issue.bot.onItMine.description: Toast shown after the viewer asked Homeroom bot to build a request for them. "is on it" means it has taken the job; "Its card" is the request's card, and "it" at the end is the bot.

issue.bot.onIt.description: Toast shown after Homeroom bot was asked to build a request. "is on it" means it has taken the job.

issue.menu.alreadyBountied.text: You already placed a bounty on this issue
issue.menu.alreadyBountied.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Bountied" row in a request's ⋯ menu. A bounty is kudos (thanks points) promised to whoever makes the request happen.

issue.menu.allowanceSpent.description: Tooltip of the disabled "Pledge kudos" row in a request's ⋯ menu, when the viewer has no kudos left to promise this week.

issue.menu.bountied.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: disabled, shown when the viewer has already promised kudos on this request.

issue.menu.pledgeKudos.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: promises kudos (thanks points) to whoever makes the request happen. "Pledge" is a verb.

issue.menu.pledgeKudosTitle.text: Pledge kudos to whoever’s change makes this happen
issue.menu.pledgeKudosTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Pledge kudos" row in a request's ⋯ menu. "change" is a noun: the change that fulfils the request.

issue.menu.stopWorking.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: shown to someone who said they are working on the request; takes their name off it.

issue.menu.stopWorkingTitle.text: Stop working on this so somebody else can pick it up
issue.menu.stopWorkingTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Stop working on this" row in a request's ⋯ menu.

issue.menu.claim.description: Row in the ⋯ menu of a request's card: tells everyone the viewer will work on the request. "It" is the request.

issue.menu.claimTitle.text: Let everyone know you’ll work on this. It’s not a promise of progress. It clears itself after about 7 days with no activity; talking about it in the request’s thread keeps it going.
