menu.myApps.showAgainTip.description: Tooltip of "Pin to Home" in an app's menu, for someone who builds the app and had hidden its tile.

menu.myApps.hideTip.text: Hide this app from Pinned apps. It stays live and you keep your builder access.
menu.myApps.hideTip.description: Tooltip of "Unpin from Home" in an app's menu, for someone who builds the app. "Live" means still running for its users.

menu.notifications.label.description: Item in an app's menu: opens the choices of what this app may notify the viewer about.

menu.notifications.tip.text: Choose what this app can notify you about, here and on your phone.
menu.notifications.tip.description: Tooltip of the "Notifications" item in an app's menu.

menu.widget.edit.description: Item in an app's menu in the iPhone app, when the app is already on the Homeroom widget: reveals the strip on Home where the widget's apps are arranged. Homeroom is the product's name.

menu.widget.add.description: Item in an app's menu in the iPhone app: adds the app to the Homeroom widget on the phone's home screen. Homeroom is the product's name.

menu.phoneHome.add.description: Item in an app's menu in the Android app: puts a shortcut to the app on the phone's home screen.

menu.phoneHome.addFailed.description: Brief notice when putting an app on the phone's home screen, or on the Homeroom widget, failed. {{reason}} is the error the phone reported.

menu.install.label.description: Item in an app's menu in a phone browser: opens the page that explains how to install the app on the phone's home screen with its own icon.

menu.install.tip.text: Put this app on your phone’s home screen with its own icon
menu.install.tip.description: Tooltip of the "Add to Home Screen" item in an app's menu.

menu.retry.description: Item in the menu of an app that failed to build, shown to its creator: tries building and starting the app again.

menu.buildLog.label.description: Item in the menu of an app whose last build failed: opens the log of that build. "Build" is a noun.

menu.buildLog.tip.text: See why the last build/deploy failed
menu.buildLog.tip.description: Tooltip of "View build log" in an app's menu when the server gave no failure reason of its own.

menu.checkUpdates.label.description: Item in an app's menu, for administrators: checks whether the app's repository has a newer version to deploy.

menu.checkUpdates.checking.description: Replaces the label of "Check for updates" in an app's menu while the check is running.

menu.checkUpdates.failedHttp.description: Brief notice when "Check for updates" failed and the server gave no message. {{status}} is the HTTP status number, such as 500.

menu.checkUpdates.failed.description: Brief notice when "Check for updates" could not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own error message.

menu.remix.label.description: Item in an app's menu: makes the viewer their own version of the app, a project of their own made from it, to change freely.

menu.remix.sub.description: Second line, and tooltip, of the "Make your own" item in an app's menu.

menu.lock.lock.description: Item in an app's menu, for administrators: from then on a change to the app also needs an administrator's yes vote. "Lock" is a verb.

menu.lock.unlock.description: Item in an app's menu, for administrators, when the app is locked: lifts the extra administrator vote. A verb.

menu.lock.lockTip.text: Lock this app. An admin yes vote will also be required to merge changes.
menu.lock.lockTip.description: Tooltip of "Lock app" in an app's menu. To merge a change is to accept it into the app.

menu.lock.unlockTip.text: App locked: merges also need an admin yes vote. Click to unlock.
menu.lock.unlockTip.description: Tooltip of "Unlock app" in an app's menu. A merge is the acceptance of a change into the app.

menu.lock.failedHttp.description: Brief notice when locking or unlocking an app failed and the server gave no message. {{status}} is the HTTP status number.

menu.lock.failed.description: Brief notice when locking or unlocking an app could not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own error message.

menu.settings.description: Item in an app's menu, for people who manage the app: opens the app's settings dialog.

menu.report.description: Item in an app's menu: reports the app to Homeroom's moderators as breaking the rules. "Report" is a verb.

check.noDetails.description: Brief notice after "Check for updates" when the server's answer said nothing about the outcome.

check.noDrift.title.description: Title of the question asked after "Check for updates" found the app already runs its repository's newest version (commit).

check.noDrift.message.text: Force a rebuild anyway? (Useful if env vars or platform code changed.)
check.noDrift.message.description: Body of the question asked after "Check for updates" found nothing new. "Env vars" are the app's environment variables.

check.noDrift.confirm.description: Confirming button of the "Force a rebuild anyway?" question: builds and deploys the app again. A verb.

check.rebuild.started.text: Rebuild started. Watch the version pill.
check.rebuild.started.description: Brief notice after a forced rebuild of an app began. The version pill is the small chip showing the app's version, where progress appears.

check.rebuild.failed.description: Brief notice when a forced rebuild of an app could not be started. {{reason}} is the server's own error message.

check.deployRequested.text: Main has a newer version ({{sha}}). Deploying it now: watch the version pill.
check.deployRequested.description: Brief notice after "Check for updates" found a newer version and asked for it to be deployed; the deploy runs in the background. {{sha}} is the first seven characters of that version's commit id. The version pill is the small chip showing the app's version, where progress appears.

check.inFlight.text: A redeploy is already in progress for this app.
check.inFlight.description: Brief notice after "Check for updates" when the app is already being deployed again.

check.firstSeen.text: Recorded current SHA ({{sha}}). Future drift will trigger a redeploy.
check.firstSeen.description: Brief notice after the first "Check for updates" on an app. {{sha}} is the first seven characters of the current commit id. Drift means the repository moving ahead of what is deployed.

check.fetchFailed.description: Brief notice when "Check for updates" could not read the app's repository. {{reason}} is the server's own error message.

check.fetchFailedUnknown.description: Brief notice when "Check for updates" could not read the app's repository and the server gave no reason.

check.invalidRepo.text: This app has an invalid repo URL.
check.invalidRepo.description: Brief notice after "Check for updates" when the address of the app's repository is not usable.

check.finished.description: Brief notice after "Check for updates" ended with an outcome this screen has no sentence for. {{status}} is the server's own status code, such as no_change.

time.justNow.description: A relative time inside "Updated …" in an app tile's menu: less than a minute ago. Lower case because it follows another word.

time.minutesAgo_one.description: A compact relative time inside "Updated …" in an app tile's menu. {{count}} is a number of minutes; "m" abbreviates minutes.

time.minutesAgo_other.description: A compact relative time inside "Updated …" in an app tile's menu. {{count}} is a number of minutes; "m" abbreviates minutes.

time.hoursAgo_one.description: A compact relative time inside "Updated …" in an app tile's menu. {{count}} is a number of hours; "h" abbreviates hours.

time.hoursAgo_other.description: A compact relative time inside "Updated …" in an app tile's menu. {{count}} is a number of hours; "h" abbreviates hours.

time.daysAgo_one.description: A compact relative time inside "Updated …" in an app tile's menu. {{count}} is a number of days; "d" abbreviates days.

time.daysAgo_other.description: A compact relative time inside "Updated …" in an app tile's menu. {{count}} is a number of days; "d" abbreviates days.

time.monthsAgo_one.description: A compact relative time inside "Updated …" in an app tile's menu. {{count}} is a number of months; "mo" abbreviates months.

time.monthsAgo_other.description: A compact relative time inside "Updated …" in an app tile's menu. {{count}} is a number of months; "mo" abbreviates months.

time.yearsAgo_one.description: A compact relative time inside "Updated …" in an app tile's menu. {{count}} is a number of years; "y" abbreviates years.

time.yearsAgo_other.description: A compact relative time inside "Updated …" in an app tile's menu. {{count}} is a number of years; "y" abbreviates years.

widget.heading.description: Heading of the strip on Home, in the iPhone app, where the apps shown on the Homeroom home-screen widget are arranged. Homeroom is the product's name.

widget.help.toggle.text: How to add the widget to your home screen
widget.help.toggle.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the small ⓘ button beside the "Homeroom widget" heading: shows or hides the instructions.

widget.help.steps.text: <0>Add the widget to your home screen:</0> touch and hold an empty area of your iPhone home screen, tap <1>Edit</1> → <2>Add Widget</2> (or the <3>+</3>), search for <4>Homeroom</4>, pick a size and tap <5>Add Widget</5>. The apps below appear on it automatically.
widget.help.steps.description: Instructions shown in the widget strip on Home in the iPhone app. Every numbered tag is emphasis. "Edit" and "Add Widget" are the names of buttons in iOS: use the names iOS shows in your language. Homeroom is the product's name; keep it.

widget.close.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the "Done" button on the widget strip on Home: hides the strip.

widget.hint.withTiles.text: Drag tiles to reorder. Drag cards from Pinned apps here to add them.
widget.hint.withTiles.description: Hint under the app tiles in the widget strip on Home. "Pinned apps" is the name of the grid below it.

widget.hint.empty.text: Drag a card from Pinned apps here (or use its menu) to add it to the Homeroom widget on your home screen.
widget.hint.empty.description: Hint in the widget strip on Home while it holds no apps. "Pinned apps" is the name of the grid below; Homeroom is the product's name.

widget.tile.remove.description: Tooltip of the ✕ button on an app's tile in the widget strip on Home: takes that app off the Homeroom widget.

widget.tile.removeNamed.description: Accessible name of the ✕ button on an app's tile in the widget strip on Home. {{app}} is the app's name.

widget.removeFailed.description: Brief notice when taking an app off the Homeroom widget failed. {{reason}} is the error the phone reported.

widget.reorderFailed.description: Brief notice when saving the new order of apps on the Homeroom widget failed. {{reason}} is the error the phone reported.

waitlist.regionLabel.description: Accessible name of the card on Home where someone invited into a private community can join the waiting list to make their own apps.

waitlist.title.description: Heading of the waitlist card on the Home screen, shown to someone not yet let in: an invitation to build apps of their own. "Make" is a verb; keep it short, it is one line on a phone.

waitlist.join.button.description: Main button of the waitlist card on Home: starts joining the waiting list for creating apps.

waitlist.join.note.text: We're letting people in a few at a time.
waitlist.join.note.description: Small note under the "Join the waitlist" button on Home.

waitlist.listed.byText.text: We’ll text you when your spot is ready.
waitlist.listed.byText.description: Shown on the waitlist card once the viewer is on the list with a phone number only: they will get a text message.

waitlist.listed.byEmail.text: We’ll email you when your spot is ready.
waitlist.listed.byEmail.description: Shown on the waitlist card once the viewer is on the list with an email address.

waitlist.addEmail.link.description: Link on the waitlist card for someone listed by phone only: opens the form to add an email address as well.

waitlist.sooner.title.description: Line at the foot of the waitlist card, beside a link to a short survey that can move the viewer up the list.

waitlist.sooner.answer.description: Link beside "Want in sooner?" on the waitlist card: opens the four-question survey.

waitlist.sooner.edit.description: Link beside "Want in sooner?" on the waitlist card once the survey was answered: reopens it.

waitlist.email.titleJoin.description: Title of the email step of the waitlist card on Home, for someone not on the list yet.

waitlist.email.titleAdd.description: Title of the email step of the waitlist card on Home, for someone already listed by phone.

waitlist.email.leadOwn.text: With your email, or another one.
waitlist.email.leadOwn.description: Line under the title of the waitlist card's email step when the account already has an email address, which is filled in below. It completes the title "Join the waitlist".

waitlist.email.leadAdd.text: Add your email. We’ll email you a 6-digit code.
waitlist.email.leadAdd.description: Line under the title of the waitlist card's email step when the account has no email address.

waitlist.email.label.description: Label of the email address field on the waitlist card.

waitlist.email.placeholder.description: Placeholder inside the email address field on the waitlist card: an example of an address. Keep it a valid-looking address.

waitlist.email.submitJoin.description: Submit button of the waitlist card's email step when the address is the account's own, so no code is needed.

waitlist.email.submitCode.description: Submit button of the waitlist card's email step when the address must be confirmed: sends a 6-digit code to it.

waitlist.email.privacy.text: We use it to tell you when your spot is ready, and you can sign in with it. Nobody else sees it.
waitlist.email.privacy.description: Small note under the email field on the waitlist card. "It" is the email address.

waitlist.email.notNow.description: Link under the waitlist card's email step: goes back without adding an address.

waitlist.code.title.description: Title of the waitlist card's step where the emailed code is typed in.

waitlist.code.sent.text: We sent a 6-digit code to {{email}}. It expires in 15 minutes.
waitlist.code.sent.description: Line under "Check your email" on the waitlist card. {{email}} is the address the code went to.

waitlist.code.label.description: Label of the field for the 6-digit emailed code on the waitlist card. A noun.

waitlist.code.submit.description: Submit button of the waitlist card's code step: confirms the code and joins the list.

waitlist.code.otherEmail.description: Link under the code field on the waitlist card: goes back to enter a different address.

waitlist.code.resend.description: Link under the code field on the waitlist card: emails a fresh code to the same address.

waitlist.error.join.text: Could not join the waitlist. Try again.
waitlist.error.join.description: Error on the waitlist card when joining failed and the server gave no message of its own.

waitlist.error.code.text: Could not check that code. Try again.
waitlist.error.code.description: Error on the waitlist card when the emailed code could not be checked and the server gave no message of its own.

verify.regionLabel.description: Accessible name of the card on Home that asks a member to verify their identity.

verify.title.description: Title of the card on Home that asks a member to verify their identity.

verify.lead.text: Add your phone number to vote on public apps and get the full AI budget. Nobody sees your number.
verify.lead.description: Text under "Verify your account" on Home when verifying by phone number is offered. The AI budget is the allowance of AI use each account gets.

verify.reason.text: Verified accounts vote on public apps and get the full AI budget.
verify.reason.description: Text under "Verify your account" on Home when phone verification is not offered; instructions to link other accounts follow it.

discover.heading.description: Heading of the section of Home that shows a rail of app cards to try.

discover.fallbackTitle.description: Title of Home's Discover block when the server sent none. Not shown as a heading today; kept with the block's data.

discover.browseAll.text.description: Link at the right end of the "Discover communities" heading on Home: opens the Discover screen, which lists every community the person can join. The Challenges heading's link says the same.

discover.browseAll.label.description: Accessible name of the "See all" link beside the "Discover communities" heading on Home: opens the Discover screen, which lists every community the person can join.

discover.browseAll.tip.text: See every community you can join in Discover
discover.browseAll.tip.description: Tooltip of the "See all" link beside the "Discover communities" heading on Home. Discover is the name of the screen it opens.

discover.empty.title.text: No communities to suggest right now
discover.empty.title.description: First line of the card shown in Home's Discover communities section when there is no community to suggest: none the person can join that they have not. The whole card links to the Discover screen.

discover.empty.detail.text: Discover lists every community you can join.
discover.empty.detail.description: Second line of the card shown in Home's Discover communities section when there is no community to suggest. Discover is the name of the screen the card opens.

discover.card.addTip.description: Tooltip of the labelled pill in the corner of an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail, shown when the viewer is already a member but the app is not in Pinned apps: puts a tile for the app in Pinned apps.

discover.card.addedTip.text: Added. Tap to remove from Pinned apps
discover.card.addedTip.description: Tooltip of the round check button on an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail when the app is already in Pinned apps.

discover.card.removeNamed.description: Accessible name of the round check button on an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail when the app is already in Pinned apps. {{app}} is the app's name.

discover.card.join.description: Label of the pill in the corner of an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail, shown when the viewer has not joined the app's community. Tapping it joins that community and puts a tile for the app in Pinned apps.

discover.card.joined.description: Label of the pill in the corner of an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail, shown when the viewer is a member and the app is in Pinned apps. Tapping it asks whether to leave the community.

discover.card.add.description: Label of the pill in the corner of an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail, shown when the viewer is already a member but the app is not in Pinned apps. Tapping it puts a tile for the app in Pinned apps.

discover.card.joinNamed.description: Accessible name of the Join pill on an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail. {{app}} is the app's name.

discover.card.joinedNamed.description: Accessible name of the pill on an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail when the viewer is a member and the app is in Pinned apps; tapping it asks whether to leave. {{app}} is the app's name.

discover.card.joinTip.text: Join this community. It also goes on Pinned apps
discover.card.joinTip.description: Tooltip of the Join pill in the corner of an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail. "Pinned apps" is the name of the grid on Home.

discover.card.joinedTip.text: You're a member. Tap to leave
discover.card.joinedTip.description: Tooltip of the Joined pill in the corner of an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail; tapping it opens the leave confirmation.

discover.card.addNamed.description: Accessible name of the Add pill in the corner of an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail, shown when the viewer is already a member. {{app}} is the app's name; "Pinned apps" is the name of the grid on Home.

grid.tile.members_one.description: First small line under a project's name on its tile in Pinned projects on Home (the Standard (WIP) look, wide screens), after a people glyph: how many people are in the project's community. {{formatted}} is that number written with digit grouping, for example 1,284; {{count}} is the same number and only selects the plural form.

grid.tile.members_other.description: First small line under a project's name on its tile in Pinned projects on Home (the Standard (WIP) look, wide screens), after a people glyph: how many people are in the project's community. {{formatted}} is that number written with digit grouping, for example 1,284; {{count}} is the same number and only selects the plural form.

discover.card.contributors_one.description: Small line at the bottom of an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail. {{count}} is how many people have contributed to the app.

discover.card.contributors_other.description: Small line at the bottom of an app's card in Home's Discover communities rail. {{count}} is how many people have contributed to the app.

challenges.scrollOn.description: Accessible name of the arrow button at the end of the row of challenges on Home (the Standard (WIP) look), shown when the row holds more than fit: scrolls the row on to the next ones.

challenges.scrollBack.description: Accessible name of the arrow button at the start of the row of challenges on Home (the Standard (WIP) look), shown once the row has been scrolled: scrolls it back toward the first ones.

challenges.heading.description: Heading of the section of Home about challenges (tasks that earn points), while it loads and when it shows one line because no challenge is open.

challenges.headingFirst.description: Heading of Home's Challenges section while the viewer still has a first challenge to finish: the section then lists those first challenges.

challenges.headingNext.description: Heading of Home's Challenges section once the viewer's first challenges are done: the section then lists up to 3 open challenges, the ones the viewer is furthest along first.

challenges.seeAll.text.description: Link at the right end of the Challenges heading on Home: goes to the Challenges tab, which lists every challenge.

challenges.seeAll.label.description: Accessible name of the "See all" link beside the Challenges heading on Home: goes to the Challenges tab, which lists every challenge.

challenges.allDone.title.description: Title of the one card in Home's Challenges section when nothing is open because the viewer finished every challenge of this week.

challenges.allDone.text_one.description: Line under "All done for this week" on Home. {{count}} is how many weekly challenges there are; their counts start again on Monday.

challenges.allDone.text_other.description: Line under "All done for this week" on Home. {{count}} is how many weekly challenges there are; their counts start again on Monday.

challenges.none.title.description: Title of the one card in Home's Challenges section when no challenge is open.

challenges.none.text.text: New ones will show up here.
challenges.none.text.description: Line under "No challenges right now" on Home: new challenges will appear in this section.

challenges.fallbackTitle.description: Title of Home's Challenges block when the server sent none. Kept with the block's data.

panels.fallbackTitle.description: Title of a block on the Home screen whose own title is missing. A block of Home, not the phone's home-screen widget.

challenges.row.done.description: State shown on a challenge's card on Home: the viewer has completed it.

challenges.row.started.description: State shown on a challenge's card on Home: the viewer has earned something from it but not completed it.

challenges.row.notStarted.description: State shown on a challenge's card on Home: the viewer has made no progress on it.

challenges.row.countOf.description: Progress shown on a challenge's card on Home: {{current}} done out of the {{target}} needed.

challenges.row.countOfUnit.description: Progress shown on a challenge's card on Home: {{current}} done out of the {{target}} needed. {{unit}} is the organisers' own word for what is counted, such as "apps".

challenges.row.countOfThisWeek.description: Progress shown on a weekly challenge's card on Home: {{current}} done this week out of the {{target}} needed. The count starts again every Monday.

challenges.row.countOfUnitThisWeek.description: Progress shown on a weekly challenge's card on Home: {{current}} done this week out of the {{target}} needed. {{unit}} is the organisers' own word for what is counted, such as "apps tried". The count starts again every Monday.

challenges.row.earned_one.description: Points a completed challenge paid, at the right of its title on its card on Home, in green. {{points}} is the points it paid, already formatted ("1,500"); "pts" abbreviates points. {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

challenges.row.earned_other.description: Points a completed challenge paid, at the right of its title on its card on Home, in green. {{points}} is the points it paid, already formatted ("1,500"); "pts" abbreviates points. {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

challenges.reward.points_one.description: A challenge's reward on its card on Home. {{points}} is the number of points as the organisers wrote it; "pts" abbreviates points. {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

challenges.reward.points_other.description: A challenge's reward on its card on Home. {{points}} is the number of points as the organisers wrote it; "pts" abbreviates points. {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

tone.cream.description: Name of a card colour, a pale warm off-white: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

tone.yellow.description: Name of a card colour, a soft yellow: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

tone.orange.description: Name of a card colour, a soft orange: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

tone.coral.description: Name of a card colour, a pinkish orange: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

tone.pink.description: Name of a card colour, a soft pink: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

tone.purple.description: Name of a card colour, a soft purple: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

tone.indigo.description: Name of a card colour, a blue-violet: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

tone.blue.description: Name of a card colour, a soft blue: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

tone.teal.description: Name of a card colour, a blue-green: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

tone.mint.description: Name of a card colour, a pale green: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

tone.sage.description: Name of a card colour, a greyish green: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

tone.gray.description: Name of a card colour, a neutral grey: tooltip and accessible name of its swatch in the featured illustration editor.

edit.start.description: Button beside the Pinned apps heading on Home: puts the grid into edit mode, where tiles can be moved and removed. "Edit" is a verb.

edit.startLabel.description: Accessible name of the Edit button beside the Pinned apps heading on Home. "Edit" is a verb; "Pinned apps" is the name of the section.

edit.done.description: Button beside the Pinned apps heading on Home while the grid is in edit mode: ends edit mode.

edit.removeNamed.description: Accessible name of the small round remove button on an app tile while the Pinned apps grid on Home is in edit mode. {{app}} is the app's name.

edit.addTile.description: Button beside the Pinned apps heading on Home while the grid is in edit mode, next to Done: it opens the sheet of apps not yet in Pinned apps, to add some.

addSheet.title.description: Title of the sheet that lists apps to put on Pinned apps, opened from the Add apps button beside the Pinned apps heading in edit mode. The same words as the tile menu's add action.

addSheet.yours.description: Small-caps section label in the Pin to Home sheet, over the apps this person belongs to that have no tile on Pinned apps.

addSheet.popular.description: Small-caps section label in the Pin to Home sheet, over the popular public communities the person has not joined.

addSheet.add.description: Button on a row of the Pin to Home sheet: puts that app at the end of Pinned apps.

addSheet.added.description: What a row of the Pin to Home sheet reads once its app is on Pinned apps.

addSheet.empty.description: Shown in the Pin to Home sheet when there is no app to offer: everything the person can reach is already on Pinned apps.

addSheet.browse.description: Link under the empty line in the Pin to Home sheet, to the full app directory. The same words as the link beside the Discover heading.

communities.heading.description: Heading over the grid of pinned community tiles: on Home for a visitor who is not signed in (the communities pinned on this device), and on Home under a look of the frame. A community's tile opens its hub.

communities.matches.description: Heading on Home over the person's own communities that match what they typed in Home's search field. Shown only while searching: the communities themselves are listed on the Communities page. A community's tile opens its hub.

communities.editLabel.description: Accessible name of the Edit button beside the Pinned communities heading on Home under a look of the frame. "Edit" is a verb.

communities.all.description: Tile at the end of Pinned communities on Home under a look of the frame. Pressing it also shows the communities the viewer is in but has not pinned; pressing it again hides them.

communities.new.description: The control that starts making a new project and its community: the last tile of Joined on the Communities page, and the filled button beside that page's search field on a wide screen.

communities.newTip.text: Start a community and its app
communities.newTip.description: Tooltip of the New community control on the Communities page.

communities.newLocked.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the New community control on the Communities page when the viewer cannot make another project right now. {{hint}} is one whole sentence saying what pressing it does ('View your app allowance or request more slots.').

communities.pinNamed.description: Accessible name of the + on a joined community's tile while the Communities page is being edited: pins it, which moves it to the page's Pinned group. {{community}} is the project's name. "Pin" is a verb.

communities.unpinNamed.description: Accessible name of the remove badge on a pinned community's tile while the Communities page is being edited. {{community}} is the project's name. "Unpin" is a verb.

communities.pinned.description: Brief notice after the viewer pinned a community: it is now in the Pinned group of the Communities page. {{community}} is the project's name; Communities is that page's name.

communities.unpinned.text: Unpinned {{community}}. You're still a member if you were.
communities.unpinned.description: Brief notice after the viewer unpinned a community from the Communities page; it does not leave the community. {{community}} is the project's name.

communities.failed.description: Brief notice when pinning or unpinning a community failed. {{reason}} is the server's explanation.

communities.needs.description: Name under the tile on the Communities page that opens Needs you, the page of every vote and decision waiting on the viewer across their projects. Shown only while something waits.

communities.needsNamed_one.text: Needs you: {{count}} vote waiting on you
communities.needsNamed_one.description: Accessible name of the Needs you tile on the Communities page, with how many votes wait on the viewer across their projects. Singular.

communities.needsNamed_other.text: Needs you: {{count}} votes waiting on you
communities.needsNamed_other.description: Accessible name of the Needs you tile on the Communities page, with how many votes wait on the viewer across their projects. Plural.

communities.members_one.description: Line under a community's name on its card on the Communities page (wide screens, in the brand look), after a people glyph: how many people are in the community. {{formatted}} is that number written with digit grouping, for example 1,284; {{count}} is the same number and only selects the plural form.

communities.members_other.description: Line under a community's name on its card on the Communities page (wide screens, in the brand look), after a people glyph: how many people are in the community. {{formatted}} is that number written with digit grouping, for example 1,284; {{count}} is the same number and only selects the plural form.

communities.liveWeek_one.description: Line at the foot of a community's card on the Communities page (wide screens, in the brand look), after a check mark: how many changes to the community's project were voted in and went live in the last seven days. Shown only when there is at least one.

communities.liveWeek_other.description: Line at the foot of a community's card on the Communities page (wide screens, in the brand look), after a check mark: how many changes to the community's project were voted in and went live in the last seven days. Shown only when there is at least one.

communities.activeWeek_one.description: Line at the foot of a community's card on the Communities page (wide screens, in the brand look), beside the faces of a few of them: how many people took part in the community in the last seven days (talked in its channel, started a change or voted). {{formatted}} is the number with digit grouping; {{count}} selects the plural form.

communities.activeWeek_other.description: Line at the foot of a community's card on the Communities page (wide screens, in the brand look), beside the faces of a few of them: how many people took part in the community in the last seven days (talked in its channel, started a change or voted). {{formatted}} is the number with digit grouping; {{count}} selects the plural form.

communities.quietWeek.description: Line at the foot of a community's card on the Communities page (wide screens, in the brand look), in place of how many were active and how many changes went live, when in the last seven days nobody took part in the community and no change went live.

join.heading.description: Heading over the cards of public communities at the bottom of Home that the viewer has not joined.

join.headingSignedOut.description: Heading over the cards of public communities at the bottom of Home for a visitor who is not signed in.

join.featuredAppsCommunities.description: Small label over the row of featured cards on the Home screen under the Standard (WIP) look, where that row stands apart from Communities to join. Each card is an app and the community that builds it.

join.featured.description: Small heading over the communities the platform features, the first group of cards in Communities to join on Home (signed in or out).

join.featuredKind.description: Small heading over the communities the platform features, in Communities to join on Home (signed in or out), when a kind is chosen from the chips above. {{kind}} is the chosen chip's name, such as Games or Tools.

join.more.description: Small heading over the community cards after Featured in Communities to join on Home (signed in or out): every community of the chosen kind that Featured does not show, in the chosen order. Not shown while searching, with nothing featured, or when every community of the kind is featured.

join.sort.label.description: Accessible name of the small menu beside the More communities heading in Communities to join on Home: orders the community cards there. It offers New, Popular and Most active.

join.sort.new.description: One choice of the sort menu in Communities to join on Home: the most recently made communities first.

join.sort.popular.description: One choice of the sort menu in Communities to join on Home: the communities with the most members first.

join.sort.active.description: One choice of the sort menu in Communities to join on Home: the communities with the most people active lately first. It is the starting order.

join.members_one.description: Line on a community's row under a frame look (Home's Featured and Communities to join, and the signed-out landing's lists): how many people are in it. It has no line when the community has no members. Singular.

join.members_other.description: Line on a community's row under a frame look (Home's Featured and Communities to join, and the signed-out landing's lists): how many people are in it. It has no line when the community has no members. Plural.

join.allJoined.text: You're in every community of this kind.
join.allJoined.description: Line in Communities to join when the chosen kind has no community the viewer is not already in.

join.empty.description: Line in Communities to join when there are no public communities at all to list, signed in or out.

join.failed.description: Line in Communities to join when the public directory could not be read.

join.retry.description: Button under the line that says the communities could not be loaded. Reads the directory once more.

join.loadingMore.description: Accessible name of the placeholder cards shown while the next communities load at the end of the list.

join.end.description: Line under the last card in Communities to join.

join.endKind.text: That's every public community of this kind.
join.endKind.description: Line under the last card in Communities to join when a kind is chosen.

membership.joinedPinned.description: Brief notice after the viewer joined a community; joining also pins the community, so it is in the Pinned group of the Communities page. {{community}} is the project's name; Communities is that page's name.

membership.pinAppToo.description: Button in the notice after joining a community: also pins the community's app to Home, where its tile opens the app.

devicePins.moved_one.text: {{count}} pin from this device moved to your account
devicePins.moved_one.description: Brief notice after signing in, when an app or community pinned on this device while signed out was moved to the account. Singular.

devicePins.moved_other.text: {{count}} pins from this device moved to your account
devicePins.moved_other.description: Brief notice after signing in, when apps or communities pinned on this device while signed out were moved to the account. Plural.

guest.unpinApp.description: Accessible name of the remove badge on an app a visitor pinned on this device. {{app}} is the app's name.

guest.pinCommunity.description: Button on a project's page for a visitor who is not signed in: keeps the community on this device's Home.

guest.pinnedCommunity.description: The same button once the community is on this device's Home; pressing it again unpins it.

frame.title.description: Home drawn in the one frame, under any of its looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). The page title.

frame.purpose.description: Home drawn in the one frame, under any of its looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). The one sentence under the page title, saying what Home holds.

tabs.challenges.description: Tab at the top of the Leaderboard screen: the challenges running now, tasks that earn points.

tabs.kudos.description: Tab at the top of the Leaderboard screen: the rankings by kudos, the thank-yous members give for changes. "Kudos" is the feature's name.

tabs.standings.description: Tab at the top of the Leaderboard screen: the ranking of participants by points.

eventBar.label.description: Accessible name of the drop-down on the Leaderboard screen that chooses which event (a season or a competition within it) is shown.

eventBar.loading.description: Only option in the event drop-down on the Leaderboard screen while the list of events is being fetched.

eventBar.noEvents.description: Only option in the event drop-down on the Leaderboard screen when there is no event to choose.

eventBar.option.season.description: Option in the event drop-down on the Leaderboard screen: {{event}} is a season's name, and choosing it shows the whole season combined.

eventBar.option.current.description: Option in the event drop-down on the Leaderboard screen: {{event}} is the name of the event running now.

eventBar.option.past.description: Option in the event drop-down on the Leaderboard screen: {{event}} is the name of an event that has ended.

eventBar.noneSelected.description: Shown under the event drop-down on the Leaderboard screen when no event is chosen.

eventBar.loadFailed.description: Error shown under the event drop-down on the Leaderboard screen when the chosen event's details could not be fetched and the server gave no reason.

eventBar.status.season.description: Small label beside the event's name on the Standings tab: the whole season is shown, not one event. Lower case.

eventBar.status.activeNow.description: Small label beside the event's name on the Standings tab: the event is running at this moment. Lower case.

eventBar.status.active.description: Small label beside the event's name on the Standings tab: the event is open but is not the one running now. Lower case.

eventBar.status.past.description: Small label beside the event's name on the Standings tab: the event has ended. Lower case.

eventBar.dates.description: Under the event's name on the Standings tab: the dates it runs from and to. {{start}} and {{end}} are dates such as "Mar 4, 2026", or a dash when unknown. Only the separator is translated.

eventBar.datesTakingPart_one.description: Under the event's name on the Standings tab: the dates it runs from and to, then how many people take part. {{start}} and {{end}} are dates such as "Mar 4, 2026", or a dash when unknown.

eventBar.datesTakingPart_other.description: Under the event's name on the Standings tab: the dates it runs from and to, then how many people take part. {{start}} and {{end}} are dates such as "Mar 4, 2026", or a dash when unknown.

eventBar.seasonNote.text: Whole-season standings: every public event in this season, combined. Pick a single event above to see just its results.
eventBar.seasonNote.description: Note on the Standings tab when the whole season is chosen in the event drop-down. "Above" is that drop-down.

eventBar.fallbackNote.text: Nothing is running right now, so this shows the most recent event.
eventBar.fallbackNote.description: Note on the Standings tab when no event is running and the last one that ended is shown instead.

challenges.loading.description: Accessible name of the grey placeholder shown on the Challenges tab while the challenges are being fetched.

challenges.empty.description: Title of the one card on the Challenges tab when no challenge is running.

challenges.emptyHint.text: New ones will show up here.
challenges.emptyHint.description: Line under "No challenges right now" on the Challenges tab: new challenges will appear on this tab.

challenges.loadFailed.description: Error shown on the Challenges tab when the challenges could not be fetched and the server gave no reason.

challenges.toFirst.description: Link on the Challenges tab for a new member looking at another event: switches to the event that holds their first challenges. "First challenges" is that group's name.

challenges.locked.notice.text: Finish Getting started to unlock the rest of the season.
challenges.locked.notice.description: Note under the list on the Challenges tab while the member's first challenges are unfinished. "Getting started" is the title of the card of first steps on Home.

challenges.points_one.description: What a challenge pays, on its card and page, and what a participant has earned in it. {{points}} is a number of points, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural; "pts" abbreviates points.

challenges.points_other.description: What a challenge pays, on its card and page, and what a participant has earned in it. {{points}} is a number of points, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural; "pts" abbreviates points.

challenges.soFar_one.description: On an unfinished challenge's page. {{points}} is the points the viewer has earned in it up to now, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural; "pts" abbreviates points.

challenges.soFar_other.description: On an unfinished challenge's page. {{points}} is the points the viewer has earned in it up to now, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural; "pts" abbreviates points.

challenges.state.done.description: Label in the progress bar of a challenge the viewer has finished.

challenges.state.started.description: Label in the progress bar of a challenge the viewer has begun, where no count can be shown.

challenges.state.notStarted.description: Label in the progress bar of a challenge the viewer has not begun.

challenges.state.named.description: Accessible name of a challenge's progress bar. {{challenge}} is the challenge's title and {{state}} what the bar shows ("Done", "3/5 changes").

challenges.rail.count.description: Label in the progress bar of a challenge counted in steps, e.g. "1/3 apps tried". {{current}} is how many the viewer has, {{target}} how many it takes, {{unit}} the organiser's own word for what is counted, shown as written.

challenges.rail.countThisWeek.description: Label in the progress bar of a weekly challenge counted in steps, e.g. "0/2 accepted this week"; the count starts again each Monday. {{current}} is how many the viewer has this week, {{target}} how many it takes, {{unit}} the organiser's own word for what is counted, shown as written.

challenges.rail.fraction.description: Label in the progress bar of a challenge counted in steps when the organiser named no unit, e.g. "1/3". {{current}} is how many the viewer has, {{target}} how many it takes.

challenges.rail.fractionThisWeek.description: Label in the progress bar of a weekly challenge counted in steps when the organiser named no unit, e.g. "0/2 this week"; the count starts again each Monday. {{current}} is how many the viewer has this week, {{target}} how many it takes.

challenges.heading.first.description: Heading over the Challenges tab's first group: the challenges a newcomer does first.

challenges.heading.next.description: Heading over the Challenges tab's group of every other challenge still open.

challenges.heading.done.description: Heading over the Challenges tab's last group: the challenges the viewer has finished.

challenges.locked.title_one.description: Title of the dashed card at the foot of the challenges list while the member's first steps are unfinished. {{count}} is how many challenges are still hidden. "Getting started" is the title of the card of first steps on Home.

challenges.locked.title_other.description: Title of the dashed card at the foot of the challenges list while the member's first steps are unfinished. {{count}} is how many challenges are still hidden. "Getting started" is the title of the card of first steps on Home.

challenges.locked.hint.text: Finish Getting started on Home to see them
challenges.locked.hint.description: Under the title of the locked-challenges card when the hidden challenges' names are not known. "Getting started" is the title of the card of first steps; "Home" is the Home screen.

challenges.locked.namesAnd.description: Under the title of the locked-challenges card: the names of the hidden challenges. {{names}} is all but the last name, already joined with commas, and {{last}} the last one.

challenges.locked.namesAndMore_one.description: Under the title of the locked-challenges card: the names of some hidden challenges, then how many more there are. {{names}} is the names, already joined with commas.

challenges.locked.namesAndMore_other.description: Under the title of the locked-challenges card: the names of some hidden challenges, then how many more there are. {{names}} is the names, already joined with commas.

progress.plainLabel_one.description: The summary over the Challenges tab's grid when the viewer's points are not known, and the accessible name of its progress bar. {{done}} is the number finished and {{count}} how many there are.

progress.plainLabel_other.description: The summary over the Challenges tab's grid when the viewer's points are not known, and the accessible name of its progress bar. {{done}} is the number finished and {{count}} how many there are.

progress.summary_one.description: The summary line over the Challenges tab's grid, e.g. "3,500 pts · 4 of 11 done". <0> wraps the points, drawn in bold. {{points}} is the viewer's points, already written out ("3,500 pts"); {{done}} is how many challenges they finished and {{count}} how many there are.

progress.summary_other.description: The summary line over the Challenges tab's grid, e.g. "3,500 pts · 4 of 11 done". <0> wraps the points, drawn in bold. {{points}} is the viewer's points, already written out ("3,500 pts"); {{done}} is how many challenges they finished and {{count}} how many there are.

challenges.detail.header.description: Title in the app's header while one challenge's page is open. A noun.

challenges.detail.headerFallback.description: Title in the app's header after a challenge's page is closed, when the screen's own title is not available.

challenges.detail.go.description: Button on a challenge's page that leads to where the challenge is done, when the challenge supplies no label of its own.

challenges.detail.openLinkedAccounts.description: Button on the Connect X and GitHub challenge's page: opens Settings, Linked accounts, where an X or GitHub account is linked. X and GitHub are product names.

challenges.detail.linkUnavailable.description: On a challenge's page, in place of its button when the challenge's link cannot be used. {{label}} is the button's text; the note in the tag is shown in italics.

challenges.detail.seeFeedback.description: Link on the page of the feedback challenge: opens the list of feedback the viewer has sent.

challenges.detail.counted.description: Heading on a challenge's page over the list of the viewer's own credits that make up its count.

challenges.detail.countedWeek.description: The same heading on a weekly challenge's page, whose count starts again every Monday: the list holds this week's credits only.

challenges.detail.requirements.description: Heading on a challenge's page over the organiser's words on what counts towards it and how.

challenges.invites.note.text: An invite counts when the person joins your community through your invite link, or accepts your invite, while this challenge is open. Each person counts once, for the first invite they took. Counts run on a schedule, so a new join shows here a little later.
challenges.invites.note.description: Under the progress rail on the Invite 3 people challenge's page: the plain-language rule the scorer pays by.

challenges.feedback.note.text: A report counts when you send it while this challenge is open, about Homeroom or a project somebody else made. Feedback on a project you made, or on one only you are in, doesn't count here, and nor does a report too short to act on or a copy of one you already sent. Counts run on a schedule and each report is graded, so a new one shows here a little later.
challenges.feedback.note.description: Under the progress rail on the feedback challenge's page (Send useful feedback): the plain-language rule the scorer pays by.

challenges.invites.heading.description: Heading of the per-person invite list on the Invite 3 people challenge's page, before What counts.

challenges.invites.empty.description: The invite list on the Invite 3 people challenge's page when the viewer has no invite records at all.

challenges.invites.error.description: The invite list on the Invite 3 people challenge's page when the read failed; the pane offers a retry.

challenges.invites.someone.description: A row in the invite list for a person whose name cannot be shown yet (a claimed email invite with no handle).

challenges.invites.status.counted.description: The word on a row of the invite list: the person's join is in the ledger and the points are paid.

challenges.invites.status.soon.description: The word on a row of the invite list: they joined through the viewer's invite and the next scheduled count pays for them.

challenges.invites.status.over.description: The word on a row of the invite list: they joined through the viewer's invite but the challenge has paid for its full number of people already.

challenges.invites.status.notCounted.description: The word on a row of the invite list: they joined, but someone else's invite was first, or outside the challenge's dates.

challenges.invites.status.waiting.description: The word on a row of the invite list: they followed the link but haven't joined yet, or haven't accepted the invite.

challenges.invites.status.wontJoin.description: The word on a row of the invite list: the link they followed was turned off before they could join.

challenges.invites.reason.counted.description: The grey line under a Counted row of the invite list.

challenges.invites.reason.pending_count.text: Joined through your invite. It shows here after the next count.
challenges.invites.reason.pending_count.description: The grey line under a Counts soon row of the invite list.

challenges.invites.reason.over_target_on.text: Joined, but this challenge counts up to {{count}} person.
challenges.invites.reason.over_target_on.description: The grey line under an Over the limit row of the invite list, for one person.

challenges.invites.reason.over_target_ot.text: Joined, but this challenge counts up to {{count}} people.
challenges.invites.reason.over_target_ot.description: The grey line under an Over the limit row of the invite list.

challenges.invites.reason.other_invite.text: They took someone else's invite first. Each person counts once.
challenges.invites.reason.other_invite.description: The grey line under a Not counted row whose person's first invite was somebody else's.

challenges.invites.reason.outside_window.text: They joined outside this challenge's dates.
challenges.invites.reason.outside_window.description: The grey line under a Not counted row whose person joined before the challenge opened or after it closed.

challenges.invites.reason.waiting_access.text: They followed your link but haven't joined yet. They join your community once they're let into Homeroom.
challenges.invites.reason.waiting_access.description: The grey line under a Waiting row whose person queued for admission to Homeroom.

challenges.invites.reason.not_accepted.text: You invited them, and they haven't accepted yet.
challenges.invites.reason.not_accepted.description: The grey line under a Waiting row whose person has an open collaborator invite.

challenges.invites.reason.link_off.text: The link they followed was turned off before they could join.
challenges.invites.reason.link_off.description: The grey line under a Won't join row of the invite list.

challenges.detail.pointsNote.text: Points add up across challenges and set your place in the standings.
challenges.detail.pointsNote.description: On a challenge's page, under the points it pays or the viewer has earned in it: what points are for.

challenges.countNote.onPropose.text: Counts when a change of yours goes to a vote. A change Homeroom bot builds is the bot's own, even if you asked for it, so it doesn't count here.
challenges.countNote.onPropose.description: Note on the page of a challenge that is completed by proposing a change. "Homeroom bot" is the name of the platform's assistant; "change" is a noun.

challenges.countNote.weekAccepted_one.text: This challenge counts up to {{cap}} each week, and you have {{cap}} this week. More accepted changes this week don't add to it. It starts again on Monday.
challenges.countNote.weekAccepted_one.description: Note on the page of a weekly challenge about accepted changes once the viewer has reached its limit. {{cap}} is the most the challenge counts, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "Changes" is a noun.

challenges.countNote.weekAccepted_other.text: This challenge counts up to {{cap}} each week, and you have {{cap}} this week. More accepted changes this week don't add to it. It starts again on Monday.
challenges.countNote.weekAccepted_other.description: Note on the page of a weekly challenge about accepted changes once the viewer has reached its limit. {{cap}} is the most the challenge counts, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "Changes" is a noun.

challenges.countNote.week_one.text: This challenge counts up to {{cap}} each week, and you have {{cap}} this week. More this week don't add to it. It starts again on Monday.
challenges.countNote.week_one.description: Note on the page of a weekly challenge once the viewer has reached its limit. {{cap}} is the most the challenge counts, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "More" means more of whatever the challenge counts.

challenges.countNote.week_other.text: This challenge counts up to {{cap}} each week, and you have {{cap}} this week. More this week don't add to it. It starts again on Monday.
challenges.countNote.week_other.description: Note on the page of a weekly challenge once the viewer has reached its limit. {{cap}} is the most the challenge counts, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "More" means more of whatever the challenge counts.

challenges.countNote.accepted_one.text: This challenge counts up to {{cap}}, and you have {{cap}}. More accepted changes before it ends don't add to it.
challenges.countNote.accepted_one.description: Note on the page of a challenge about accepted changes once the viewer has reached its limit. {{cap}} is the most the challenge counts, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "Changes" is a noun.

challenges.countNote.accepted_other.text: This challenge counts up to {{cap}}, and you have {{cap}}. More accepted changes before it ends don't add to it.
challenges.countNote.accepted_other.description: Note on the page of a challenge about accepted changes once the viewer has reached its limit. {{cap}} is the most the challenge counts, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "Changes" is a noun.

challenges.countNote.other_one.text: This challenge counts up to {{cap}}, and you have {{cap}}. More before it ends don't add to it.
challenges.countNote.other_one.description: Note on the page of a challenge once the viewer has reached its limit. {{cap}} is the most the challenge counts, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "More" means more of whatever the challenge counts.

challenges.countNote.other_other.text: This challenge counts up to {{cap}}, and you have {{cap}}. More before it ends don't add to it.
challenges.countNote.other_other.description: Note on the page of a challenge once the viewer has reached its limit. {{cap}} is the most the challenge counts, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "More" means more of whatever the challenge counts.

challenges.scoring.note.text: Progress is counted every {{every}}. Last counted {{last}} ago, next count in about {{next}}.
challenges.scoring.note.description: Under the progress bar on a challenge's page when it is counted on a schedule: how often it is counted and when the next count is due. {{every}} is an interval such as "10 minutes", {{last}} how long ago the last count ran ("4 minutes"), and {{next}} the time until the next one ("6 minutes").

challenges.scoring.noteJustNow.text: Progress is counted every {{every}}. Last counted just now, next count in about {{next}}.
challenges.scoring.noteJustNow.description: Under the progress bar on a challenge's page when it is counted on a schedule and the last count ran less than a minute ago. {{every}} is an interval such as "10 minutes" and {{next}} the time until the next count ("9 minutes").

challenges.scoring.pending.text: Progress is counted every {{every}}. Last counted {{last}} ago. The next count is due now, so recent progress may not show yet.
challenges.scoring.pending.description: Under the progress bar on a challenge's page when its scheduled count is due or late. {{every}} is an interval such as "10 minutes" and {{last}} how long ago the last count ran ("14 minutes").

challenges.scoring.duration.minutes_one.description: A length of time inserted into the sentence under a challenge's progress bar, e.g. "1 minute".

challenges.scoring.duration.minutes_othe.description: A length of time inserted into the sentence under a challenge's progress bar, e.g. "4 minutes".

challenges.scoring.duration.hours_one.description: A length of time inserted into the sentence under a challenge's progress bar, e.g. "1 hour".

challenges.scoring.duration.hours_other.description: A length of time inserted into the sentence under a challenge's progress bar, e.g. "2 hours".

challenges.scoring.duration.days_one.description: A length of time inserted into the sentence under a challenge's progress bar, e.g. "1 day".

challenges.scoring.duration.days_other.description: A length of time inserted into the sentence under a challenge's progress bar, e.g. "3 days".

bp.checking.description: Shown on the block-production challenge's page while the viewer's wallet state is being fetched. "Block production" is running a node that produces blocks of the blockchain.

bp.error.title.text: Could not check your block-production status
bp.error.title.description: Title of the card on the block-production challenge's page when the viewer's wallet state could not be fetched.

bp.error.text.text: Check your connection and try again.
bp.error.text.description: Under "Could not check your block-production status" on the block-production challenge's page.

bp.error.retry.description: Button on the block-production challenge's page: fetches the viewer's wallet state again after it failed.

bp.account.title.description: Heading on the block-production challenge's page once the viewer has a wallet: there are two ways to take part.

bp.account.delegate.title.description: Title of the first option on the block-production challenge's page: hand the wallet's stake to the platform's server. "Delegate" is a verb.

bp.account.delegate.text.text: Your stake is delegated to Homeroom's block-production server, so nothing keeps running on your phone. When delegated, you receive half the points you would earn by producing blocks directly from your phone.
bp.account.delegate.text.description: Explanation of the "Delegate" option on the block-production challenge's page. Homeroom is the product's name.

bp.account.onDevice.title.text: Or produce blocks on this phone
bp.account.onDevice.title.description: Title of the second option on the block-production challenge's page, shown in the Android app.

bp.account.onDevice.text.text: Producing directly on this phone earns full points.
bp.account.onDevice.text.description: Explanation of the "Or produce blocks on this phone" option on the block-production challenge's page.

bp.account.onDevice.warning.text: Only for phones that can stay on. A background service keeps running with a persistent notification, it uses more battery and data, and Android must let the app run unrestricted in the background and set exact alarms. If the phone stops the app, it misses its slots.
bp.account.onDevice.warning.description: Warning under the "Or produce blocks on this phone" option on the block-production challenge's page. "Slots" are the moments at which the phone must produce a block. Android is the operating system's name.

bp.account.onDeviceNote.text: Producing blocks on the phone itself is available only in the Android app.
bp.account.onDeviceNote.description: Note on the block-production challenge's page where producing on the device is not offered. Android is the operating system's name.

bp.account.manage.description: Button on the block-production challenge's page: opens the wallet, where the stake is delegated or taken back.

bp.account.appNote.text: Delegation is managed from the wallet in the Homeroom app. If it is not offered there yet, update the app.
bp.account.appNote.description: Note on the block-production challenge's page, inside the Homeroom app, when this version of the app cannot manage delegation. Homeroom is the product's name.

bp.account.webNote.text: Delegation is managed from your wallet in the Homeroom app. Open this challenge there.
bp.account.webNote.description: Note on the block-production challenge's page in a web browser. "Open" is a verb. Homeroom is the product's name.

bp.pending.title.description: Title of the card on the block-production challenge's page after the viewer asked for a wallet and is waiting for it.

bp.pending.text.text: An admin releases wallet keys in batches. Once yours are released, come back here to choose how your blocks are produced.
bp.pending.text.description: Under "Wallet requested" on the block-production challenge's page.

bp.locked.title.description: Title of the card on the block-production challenge's page for an account that may not request a wallet yet.

bp.locked.text.text: You can request a wallet once your account has platform access.
bp.locked.text.description: Under "Not available yet" on the block-production challenge's page. "Platform access" is what an account has once it is let in from the waitlist.

bp.request.title.description: Title of the card on the block-production challenge's page for a viewer who has no wallet. "Request" is a verb.

bp.request.text.text: Producing blocks needs a wallet with producer keys. Ask for one and an admin will release your keys in batches.
bp.request.text.description: Under "First, request a wallet" on the block-production challenge's page.

bp.request.action.description: Button on the block-production challenge's page: asks the administrators for a wallet. "Request" is a verb.

bp.request.pending.description: Shown on the "Request a wallet" button of the block-production challenge's page while the request is being sent.

bp.request.sent.text: Request sent. An admin will release your keys
bp.request.sent.description: Brief message shown after the viewer asked for a wallet on the block-production challenge's page. "Request" is a noun.

bp.request.failed.description: Brief message shown when asking for a wallet on the block-production challenge's page failed and the server gave no reason. "Request" is a noun.

standing.label.description: Accessible name of the card at the top of the Challenges tab that shows the viewer's rank and points this season.

standing.rankOf_one.description: The "Your standing" card at the top of the Challenges tab, e.g. "#22 of 161 ranked". <0> wraps the viewer's place, drawn large. {{rank}} is the place, {{number}} how many people the standings rank, already formatted ("1,284"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "Ranked" because it counts only people with points: the Standings tab's "167 taking part" counts everyone enrolled, so the two numbers differ.

standing.rankOf_other.description: The "Your standing" card at the top of the Challenges tab, e.g. "#22 of 161 ranked". <0> wraps the viewer's place, drawn large. {{rank}} is the place, {{number}} how many people the standings rank, already formatted ("1,284"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "Ranked" because it counts only people with points: the Standings tab's "167 taking part" counts everyone enrolled, so the two numbers differ.

standing.rank.description: The "Your standing" card's place when the number of people ranked is not known, e.g. "#22". <0> wraps it, drawn large. {{rank}} is the place.

standing.yourStanding.description: On the "Your standing" card, in place of the rank, when the viewer has points the ranking does not show yet.

standing.pointsNote.text: Your place comes from the points you earn in challenges.
standing.pointsNote.description: On the "Your standing" card, under the viewer's rank: what the rank is based on.

standing.updateNote.text: Your place updates within about 10 minutes whenever anyone earns points, so it can move even when you did nothing.
standing.updateNote.description: On the "Your standing" card at the top of the Challenges tab, under the note on points: why the viewer's place can change without them doing anything, and how soon the standings catch up.

standing.pending_one.text: {{points}} pts earned, not in the standings yet
standing.pending_one.description: On the "Your standing" card when the viewer has earned points that the ranking does not show yet. {{points}} is a number, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural; "pts" abbreviates points.

standing.pending_other.text: {{points}} pts earned, not in the standings yet
standing.pending_other.description: On the "Your standing" card when the viewer has earned points that the ranking does not show yet. {{points}} is a number, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural; "pts" abbreviates points.

standing.token.withheld.description: Heading on the "Your standing" card when the viewer has not accepted the program's terms, so their share of tokens is not shown.

standing.token.review.text: Review and accept the terms to see your token allocation.
standing.token.review.description: Under "Token allocation withheld" on the "Your standing" card.

standing.token.reviewTerms.description: Button on the "Your standing" card: opens the program's terms to read and accept.

standing.token.label.description: Label on the "Your standing" card beside the number of tokens allotted to the viewer.

standing.token.note.text: Your share of the season’s token pool. Allocations are provisional and subject to the program terms.
standing.token.note.description: Note under the token allocation on the "Your standing" card.

standing.token.reveal.description: Button on the "Your standing" card: shows the token amount, which is blurred until pressed.

standings.loading.description: Accessible name of the grey placeholder shown on the Standings tab while the ranking is being fetched.

standings.loadFailed.description: Error shown on the Standings tab when the ranking could not be fetched and the server gave no reason.

standings.noEvents.text: No events have been published yet.
standings.noEvents.description: Shown on the Standings tab when there is no event at all.

standings.noData.description: Shown on the Standings tab when the server returned nothing for the chosen event.

standings.private.text: The leaderboard for this event isn't public yet.
standings.private.description: Shown on the Standings tab for an event whose ranking the organisers have not opened.

standings.noEntries.text: No leaderboard entries yet. Standings update every few hours; points from challenges you just finished appear at the next update.
standings.noEntries.description: Shown on the Standings tab when nobody is ranked yet.

standings.allExcluded.text: Everyone with a score on this board is excluded from the ranking.
standings.allExcluded.description: Shown on the Standings tab when every participant is marked non-podium, so the ranked list is empty.

standings.challengesDone_one.description: Line at the top of the Standings tab for a signed-in viewer: how many of the event's challenges they have finished, then a link to the Challenges tab. {{done}} is the number finished and {{count}} the total. The first tag holds the separator, in lighter ink; the second is the link. Keep the arrow.

standings.challengesDone_other.description: Line at the top of the Standings tab for a signed-in viewer: how many of the event's challenges they have finished, then a link to the Challenges tab. {{done}} is the number finished and {{count}} the total. The first tag holds the separator, in lighter ink; the second is the link. Keep the arrow.

standings.viewChallenges.description: Line at the top of the Standings tab for a viewer who is not signed in: a link to the Challenges tab. The first tag holds a separator, in lighter ink; the second is the link. Keep the arrow.

standings.showNonPodium.description: Filter chip on the Standings tab: also lists participants who are excluded from the prize ranking.

standings.showNonPodiumCount_one.description: Filter chip on the Standings tab: also lists participants who are excluded from the prize ranking. {{count}} is how many there are.

standings.showNonPodiumCount_other.description: Filter chip on the Standings tab: also lists participants who are excluded from the prize ranking. {{count}} is how many there are.

standings.column.rank.description: Column heading in the Standings table: a participant's position.

standings.column.user.description: Column heading in the Standings table: the participant's name.

standings.column.points.description: Column heading in the Standings table for one event.

standings.column.seasonPoints.description: Column heading in the Standings table when the whole season is shown.

standings.column.blocks.description: Label of a figure in a participant's details, opened from a row of the Standings table: how many blocks of the blockchain the participant's node produced.

standings.column.success.description: Label of a figure in a participant's details, opened from a row of the Standings table: the share of the participant's won slots in which a block was produced.

standings.anonymous.description: Stands in for a participant's name in the Standings table, and over their details, when they have no public name.

standings.member.description: Stands in for a participant's name in the Standings table, and over their details, when the only name on record is a hidden email address or handle. {{rank}} is their position in the ranking, e.g. "Member #22".

standings.you_one.description: The viewer's own place, pinned above the Standings table. {{rank}} is their position, {{points}} their points, already formatted ("10,823"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. Pressing it opens their details.

standings.you_other.description: The viewer's own place, pinned above the Standings table. {{rank}} is their position, {{points}} their points, already formatted ("10,823"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. Pressing it opens their details.

standings.detail.challengePoints.description: Label of a figure in a participant's details, opened from a row of the Standings table: the part of their points earned outside block production, from challenges and other activities.

standings.nonPodium.description: A participant's cell in the Standings table, for somebody who takes part but is excluded from the prize ranking. {{name}} is their name, in the first tag; the note in the second tag is shown smaller, in lighter ink.

standings.nonPodiumTip.description: Tooltip of the "non-podium" note beside a participant's name in the Standings table.

standings.openDetails.description: Accessible name of a row in the Standings table: pressing it shows that participant's activities. "Open" is a verb. {{name}} is the participant's name.

standings.openDetailsAnonymous.description: Accessible name of a row in the Standings table: pressing it shows that participant's activities. "Open" is a verb. Used for a person with no display name, who is listed as "Anonymous".

drill.activities.description: Heading in a participant's details under the Standings table, over the list of things they earned points for.

drill.activitiesLoading.description: Shown in a participant's details under the Standings table while their activities are being fetched.

drill.activitiesEmpty.text: No activities recorded for this event.
drill.activitiesEmpty.description: Shown in a participant's details under the Standings table when nothing they did in the event is recorded.

drill.activitiesFailed.description: Error shown in a participant's details under the Standings table when their activities could not be fetched and the server gave no reason.

drill.noIdentifier.text: No identifier available for this row.
drill.noIdentifier.description: Shown in place of a participant's activities under the Standings table when the row carries nothing to look them up by.

drill.epoch.heading.description: Heading in a participant's details under the Standings table, over their block production epoch by epoch. An epoch is a fixed period of the network's time.

drill.epoch.loading.description: Shown in a participant's details under the Standings table while their epoch-by-epoch record is being fetched.

drill.epoch.empty.text: No epoch data for this event.
drill.epoch.empty.description: Shown in a participant's details under the Standings table when there is no epoch-by-epoch record.

drill.epoch.failed.text: Could not load the epoch breakdown.
drill.epoch.failed.description: Error shown in a participant's details under the Standings table when their epoch-by-epoch record could not be fetched and the server gave no reason.

drill.epoch.perEvent.text: The epoch breakdown is per event. Pick a single event above to see it.
drill.epoch.perEvent.description: Shown in a participant's details under the Standings table when the whole season is chosen. "Above" is the event drop-down.

drill.epoch.noWallet.text: No wallet linked for this row.
drill.epoch.noWallet.description: Shown in place of the epoch-by-epoch record under the Standings table when the participant has no wallet address.

drill.epoch.column.epoch.description: Column heading in the epoch-by-epoch table of a participant's details: the epoch's number.

drill.epoch.column.wonSlots.description: Column heading in the epoch-by-epoch table of a participant's details: block-producing slots won in that epoch.

drill.epoch.column.produced.description: Column heading in the epoch-by-epoch table of a participant's details: blocks produced in that epoch.

drill.epoch.column.successRate.description: Column heading in the epoch-by-epoch table of a participant's details: the share of won slots in which a block was produced.

drill.profile.heading.description: Heading in the viewer's own details under the Standings table, over their figures for the event.

drill.profile.loading.description: Shown in the viewer's own details under the Standings table while their figures are being fetched.

drill.profile.failed.description: Error shown in the viewer's own details under the Standings table when their figures could not be fetched and the server gave no reason.

drill.profile.rank.description: Label of a figure in the viewer's own details under the Standings table: their position in the ranking.

drill.profile.totalPoints.description: Label of a figure in the viewer's own details under the Standings table.

drill.profile.producedBlocks.description: Label of a figure in the viewer's own details under the Standings table: blocks their node produced.

drill.profile.clientRate.description: Label of a figure in the viewer's own details under the Standings table: the success rate as their own app reported it.
