limits.quota.apps.near.description: Row text in the platform limits area (top of the notifications sheet, full admins only), after the quota's tightest resource, when the quota of the namespace apps and previews run in is past 80%.

limits.quota.apps.at.text: Apps and previews can't start until some stop or the quota is raised.
limits.quota.apps.at.description: Row text in the platform limits area (top of the notifications sheet, full admins only), after the quota's tightest resource, when the quota of the namespace apps and previews run in is used up.

limits.quota.workers.title.description: Row title in the platform limits area (top of the notifications sheet, full admins only) for the cluster quota of the namespace coding sessions and checks run in. {{percent}} is how full its tightest resource is.

limits.quota.workers.titleUnknown.description: Row title in the platform limits area (top of the notifications sheet, full admins only) when the cluster quota of the namespace coding sessions and checks run in could not be read.

limits.quota.workers.near.text: When it fills, new coding sessions and checks wait.
limits.quota.workers.near.description: Row text in the platform limits area (top of the notifications sheet, full admins only), after the quota's tightest resource, when the quota of the namespace coding sessions and checks run in is past 80%.

limits.quota.workers.at.text: New coding sessions and checks are waiting for room.
limits.quota.workers.at.description: Row text in the platform limits area (top of the notifications sheet, full admins only), after the quota's tightest resource, when the quota of the namespace coding sessions and checks run in is used up.

limits.quota.builds.title.description: Row title in the platform limits area (top of the notifications sheet, full admins only) for the cluster quota of the namespace image builds run in. {{percent}} is how full its tightest resource is.

limits.quota.builds.titleUnknown.description: Row title in the platform limits area (top of the notifications sheet, full admins only) when the cluster quota of the namespace image builds run in could not be read.

limits.quota.builds.near.text: When it fills, new image builds fail.
limits.quota.builds.near.description: Row text in the platform limits area (top of the notifications sheet, full admins only), after the quota's tightest resource, when the quota of the namespace image builds run in is past 80%.

limits.quota.builds.at.text: New image builds are failing until old ones are cleared or the quota is raised.
limits.quota.builds.at.description: Row text in the platform limits area (top of the notifications sheet, full admins only), after the quota's tightest resource, when the quota of the namespace image builds run in is used up.

row.limit.connections.full.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: the shared database has no connections left for apps.

row.limit.connections.warn.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: the shared database is past 80% of the connections apps may open.

row.limit.connections.full.body_one.text: <0>{{used}} of {{count}} database connections open.</0> Apps can't open new ones, so their pages fail until some close.
row.limit.connections.full.body_one.description: Second line of the "Database connections used up" notification to an administrator. {{used}} is how many are open and {{count}} the line where apps are refused. The part in <0> is shown bold.

row.limit.connections.full.body_other.text: <0>{{used}} of {{count}} database connections open.</0> Apps can't open new ones, so their pages fail until some close.
row.limit.connections.full.body_other.description: Second line of the "Database connections used up" notification to an administrator. {{used}} is how many are open and {{count}} the line where apps are refused. The part in <0> is shown bold.

row.limit.connections.warn.body_one.text: <0>{{used}} of {{count}} database connections open.</0> At the limit, apps can't open new ones.
row.limit.connections.warn.body_one.description: Second line of the "Database connections running low" notification to an administrator. {{used}} is how many are open and {{count}} the line where apps are refused. The part in <0> is shown bold.

row.limit.connections.warn.body_other.text: <0>{{used}} of {{count}} database connections open.</0> At the limit, apps can't open new ones.
row.limit.connections.warn.body_other.description: Second line of the "Database connections running low" notification to an administrator. {{used}} is how many are open and {{count}} the line where apps are refused. The part in <0> is shown bold.

row.limit.dbDisk.warn.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: the shared database's disk is past 80% full.

row.limit.dbDisk.warn.body.text: <0>{{used}} of {{cap}} GiB used.</0> When it fills, Postgres stops writing.
row.limit.dbDisk.warn.body.description: Second line of the "Database disk filling up" notification to an administrator. {{used}} and {{cap}} are GiB used and the disk's size.

row.limit.dbDisk.full.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: the shared database's disk is full.

row.limit.dbDisk.full.body.text: <0>{{used}} of {{cap}} GiB used.</0> Postgres stops writing, so saves fail until the volume grows.
row.limit.dbDisk.full.body.description: Second line of the "Database disk full" notification to an administrator. {{used}} and {{cap}} are GiB used and the disk's size.

row.limit.nodePool.warn.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: a server's local volume pool is past 80% full.

row.limit.nodePool.warn.body.text: <0>{{used}} of {{cap}} GiB taken.</0> When it fills, new volumes fail to mount.
row.limit.nodePool.warn.body.description: Second line of the "Node volume pool filling up" notification to an administrator. {{used}} and {{cap}} are GiB taken and the pool's size.

row.limit.nodePool.full.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: a server's local volume pool is full.

row.limit.nodePool.full.body.text: <0>{{used}} of {{cap}} GiB taken.</0> New worker and preview volumes fail to mount.
row.limit.nodePool.full.body.description: Second line of the "Node volume pool full" notification to an administrator. {{used}} and {{cap}} are GiB taken and the pool's size.

row.limit.quota.apps.warn.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: the cluster quota for apps and previews is past 80% used.

row.limit.quota.apps.warn.body.text: <0>{{percent}}% used.</0> When it fills, apps and previews can't start.
row.limit.quota.apps.warn.body.description: Second line of the "Apps quota running low" notification to an administrator. {{percent}} is how full the quota's tightest resource is.

row.limit.quota.apps.full.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: the cluster quota for apps and previews is used up.

row.limit.quota.apps.full.body.text: <0>{{percent}}% used.</0> Apps and previews can't start until the quota is raised.
row.limit.quota.apps.full.body.description: Second line of the "Apps quota used up" notification to an administrator. {{percent}} is how full the quota's tightest resource is.

row.limit.quota.workers.warn.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: the cluster quota for coding sessions and checks is past 80% used.

row.limit.quota.workers.warn.body.text: <0>{{percent}}% used.</0> When it fills, new coding sessions and checks wait.
row.limit.quota.workers.warn.body.description: Second line of the "Workers quota running low" notification to an administrator. {{percent}} is how full the quota's tightest resource is.

row.limit.quota.workers.full.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: the cluster quota for coding sessions and checks is used up.

row.limit.quota.workers.full.body.text: <0>{{percent}}% used.</0> New coding sessions and checks wait until the quota is raised.
row.limit.quota.workers.full.body.description: Second line of the "Workers quota used up" notification to an administrator. {{percent}} is how full the quota's tightest resource is.

row.limit.quota.builds.warn.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: the cluster quota for image builds is past 80% used.

row.limit.quota.builds.warn.body.text: <0>{{percent}}% used.</0> When it fills, new image builds fail.
row.limit.quota.builds.warn.body.description: Second line of the "Builds quota running low" notification to an administrator. {{percent}} is how full the quota's tightest resource is.

row.limit.quota.builds.full.label.description: First line of a notification to an administrator: the cluster quota for image builds is used up.

row.limit.quota.builds.full.body.text: <0>{{percent}}% used.</0> New image builds fail until the quota is raised.
row.limit.quota.builds.full.body.description: Second line of the "Builds quota used up" notification to an administrator. {{percent}} is how full the quota's tightest resource is.

username.title.description: Heading of the sheet a new member must answer right after signing in: they pick the username their account will have.

username.titleForPublic.description: Heading of the same username sheet when it appears later, before a member who joined by invite opens something public for the first time. They may close this one without answering.

username.intro.text: This is your @handle: your sign-in name and your public page address. Letters, numbers and underscores, 3 to 32 characters.
username.intro.description: Explanation under the heading on the sheet where a new member chooses a username: what a username is used for and which characters it may have. Keep @handle as written; the username is shown with an @ in front.

username.introForPublic.text: Public apps show this, not your name. Letters, numbers and underscores, 3 to 32 characters.
username.introForPublic.description: Explanation under the heading on the username sheet shown before a member opens something public: public apps show the username instead of the person's real name, and which characters it may have.

username.fieldLabel.description: Label of the text field on the sheet where a member chooses a username.

username.placeholder.description: Placeholder inside the empty username field: an example of what a username looks like. One lower-case word with no spaces, since a username cannot contain spaces.

username.publicNote.text: Your username will be public to other users on Homeroom.
username.publicNote.description: Note directly under the username field on the choose-a-username sheet: tells the person that everyone on Homeroom can see the username. Homeroom is the product's name.

username.submit.description: Main button on the choose-a-username sheet: saves the username typed in the field and closes the sheet.

username.notNow.description: Secondary button on the username sheet shown before opening something public: closes the sheet without choosing a username, and the person stays where they were.

username.error.empty.description: Error under the username field when the person presses Continue with the field empty.

username.error.notSaved.description: Error under the username field when the server refused the username and gave no reason of its own.

username.error.network.description: Error under the username field when the request to save the username could not reach the server.

username.chosenToast.description: Brief confirmation shown after a username was saved. {{username}} is the username just chosen; keep the @ directly in front of it.

communities.welcome.description: Heading of the first screen a new account sees after choosing a username: a welcome, above a list of communities to join. Homeroom is the product's name.

communities.intro.text: Homeroom is a place where communities build the apps they use together.
communities.intro.description: Sentence under the welcome heading on a new account's first screen: says what Homeroom is. Homeroom is the product's name.

communities.question.text: What communities do you want to join?
communities.question.description: Question above the list of communities on a new account's first screen. Each community in the list can be ticked to join it.

communities.listLabel.description: Accessible name of the list of communities a new account can tick to join, on its first screen.

communities.memberCount_one.description: Read by screen readers for the number shown at the end of a community's row on the join screen: how many members that community has. {{memberCount}} is the number, already formatted with separators, for example 1,284.

communities.memberCount_other.description: Read by screen readers for the number shown at the end of a community's row on the join screen: how many members that community has. {{memberCount}} is the number, already formatted with separators, for example 1,284.

communities.footnote.text: You can join or leave any time from Discover, and start your own private or public community once you are in.
communities.footnote.description: Small print under the list of communities on a new account's first screen. Discover is the name of a tab in the main navigation; write it as that tab is named.

communities.skip.description: Quiet button under the main button on the join-communities screen: goes on without joining any community.

communities.pickOne.description: Text of the main button on the join-communities screen while no community is ticked. The button is disabled; the text tells the person to tick one.

communities.continue.description: Text of the main button on the join-communities screen when the only community ticked is Homeroom's own, which the account is already in: goes on to Home without joining anything.

communities.join_one.description: Text of the main button on the join-communities screen: joins the communities the person ticked. {{count}} is how many.

communities.join_other.description: Text of the main button on the join-communities screen: joins the communities the person ticked. {{count}} is how many.

communities.error.notJoined.text: Could not join those. Try again.
communities.error.notJoined.description: Error above the buttons on the join-communities screen when the server refused the request and gave no reason of its own. "Those" are the communities the person ticked.

communities.error.network.description: Error above the buttons on the join-communities screen when the request could not reach the server.

communities.joinedToast_one.description: Brief confirmation shown after the join-communities screen closes. {{count}} is how many communities the person just joined.

communities.joinedToast_other.description: Brief confirmation shown after the join-communities screen closes. {{count}} is how many communities the person just joined.

terms.updatedToast.text: We updated our terms. By continuing to use Homeroom, you agree to them.
terms.updatedToast.description: Brief notice shown once to a signed-in member who had accepted an earlier version of the terms of use, after the terms changed. Homeroom is the product's name.

buildLine.planning.description: One-line status under a new project's card, on its Home tile and on its hub while its first version is being made: the assistant called Homeroom bot is writing the plan for the project. "it" is the project. Homeroom bot is a name.

buildLine.plan.text: Your plan is ready to review
buildLine.plan.description: One-line status under a new project's card, on its Home tile and on its hub while its first version is being made, shown to the person who started the project: Homeroom bot's plan for it is waiting for them to read and approve.

buildLine.planMember.description: One-line status under a new project's card, on its Home tile and on its hub while its first version is being made, shown to other members while the plan waits for the person who started the project. "it" is the project.

buildLine.question.text: Homeroom bot has a question for you
buildLine.question.description: One-line status under a new project's card, on its Home tile and on its hub while its first version is being made, shown to the person who started the project: the assistant called Homeroom bot asked them something and waits for the answer. Homeroom bot is a name.

buildLine.building.description: One-line status under a new project's card, on its Home tile and on its hub while its first version is being made: the first version is being built now. "Building" is a verb in progress and "it" is the project; nobody is being asked to build anything.

buildLine.testing.description: One-line status under a new project's card, on its Home tile and on its hub while its first version is being made: the first version is built and is being tested. "it" is the project.

buildLine.ready.description: One-line status under a new project's card, on its Home tile and on its hub while its first version is being made: the first version is finished and can be opened and tried, before it goes live.

buildLine.live.description: One-line status under a new project's card, on its Home tile and on its hub while its first version is being made: the first version has been published and the app is running for everyone. An adjective, not the verb "to live".

buildLine.stopped.description: One-line status under a new project's card, on its App tab, its hub and the screen shown after making it: Homeroom bot's build of its first version stopped before the app went live, and nothing is being built now. Its maker can start it again from their chat with Homeroom bot.

buildLine.tile.planning.description: Very short status under a new project's name on its Home screen icon while its first version is being made: the assistant called Homeroom bot is planning it, writing its plan or working out its details before it builds it. Must fit one short line under a small app icon, so keep it to one or two short words.

buildLine.tile.plan.description: Very short status under a new project's name on its Home screen icon, shown to the person who started the project: Homeroom bot's plan for it is waiting for them to read and approve. Must fit one short line under a small app icon.

buildLine.tile.planMember.description: Very short status under a new project's name on its Home screen icon, shown to other members while the plan waits for the person who started the project. Must fit one short line under a small app icon.

buildLine.tile.question.description: Very short status under a new project's name on its Home screen icon, shown to the person who started the project: Homeroom bot asked them a question and waits for the answer. A noun. Must fit one short line under a small app icon.

buildLine.tile.building.description: Very short status under a new project's name on its Home screen icon while its first version is being built. A verb in progress: the project is being built, nobody is asked to build anything. Must fit one short line under a small app icon.

buildLine.tile.testing.description: Very short status under a new project's name on its Home screen icon: its first version is built and is being tested. A verb in progress. Must fit one short line under a small app icon.

buildLine.tile.ready.description: Very short status under a new project's name on its Home screen icon: its first version is finished and can be opened and tried, before it goes live. Must fit one short line under a small app icon.

buildLine.tile.live.description: Very short status under a new project's name on its Home screen icon: its first version has been published and the app is running for everyone. An adjective, not the verb "to live".

buildLine.tile.stopped.description: Very short status under a new project's name on its Home screen icon: Homeroom bot's build of its first version stopped before the app went live. Must fit one short line under a small app icon.

buildLine.tile.phase.starting.description: Very short status under a new project's name on its Home screen icon: Homeroom bot is starting to build its first version. A verb in progress. Must fit one short line under a small app icon.

buildLine.tile.phase.checking.description: Very short status under a new project's name on its Home screen icon: its first version is built and its screens are being looked at and fixed. A verb in progress. Must fit one short line under a small app icon.

buildLine.working.text: Homeroom bot is working on it
buildLine.working.description: One-line status on a new project's hub card while the welcome tour is running, in place of the line that asks the person to review the plan. "it" is the project. Homeroom bot is a name.

buildLine.withNote.description: A project's build status followed by a short note, on one line, for example "Building it · usually 10 to 25 min". {{line}} is the status and {{note}} the note, both already translated; only the separator between them is translated.

buildLine.phase.starting.description: One-line status under a new project's card, on its hub and in the app's own tab while its first version is made: its plan is decided and the assistant called Homeroom bot is starting to build it, before it draws any screens.

buildLine.phase.details.description: One-line status under a new project's card, on its hub and in the app's own tab while its first version is made: the plan and a first picture of the app are done, and the assistant called Homeroom bot is now deciding the finer points of how the app will work, before it builds it. "Working out" is a verb in progress: figuring out, not exercising.

buildLine.phase.built.description: One-line status under a new project's card while its first version is made: the first version is built, and its screens are being looked at to find what to fix, before anyone tries it.

buildLine.phase.checking.description: One-line status under a new project's card while its first version is made: its screens are being looked at and fixed. Kept short so that how long is left still fits beside it on a phone; which round it is in is shown in the list of steps.

buildLine.soFar_one.description: After a status line under a new project's card: how long the current stage of making its first version has run, in whole minutes, for example "7 min so far". {{count}} is the number of minutes; "min" is short for minutes.

buildLine.soFar_other.description: After a status line under a new project's card: how long the current stage of making its first version has run, in whole minutes, for example "7 min so far". {{count}} is the number of minutes; "min" is short for minutes.

buildLine.left_one.description: After a status line under a new project's card on its App tab, and under the step under way in the list of steps of making its first version: about how long it still has to go, in whole minutes, counted down from how long recent first versions took, for example "about 15 min left". Never less than 1. {{count}} is the number of minutes; "min" is short for minutes. Lower case: it follows the status on the same line.

buildLine.left_other.description: After a status line under a new project's card on its App tab, and under the step under way in the list of steps of making its first version: about how long it still has to go, in whole minutes, counted down from how long recent first versions took, for example "about 15 min left". Never less than 1. {{count}} is the number of minutes; "min" is short for minutes. Lower case: it follows the status on the same line.

buildLine.longer.text: taking a little longer than usual
buildLine.longer.description: After a status line under a new project's card on its App tab, and under the step under way in the list of steps of making its first version, in place of "about 15 min left" once the step has run past how long it usually takes. "It" (left out) is the step or the first version. Lower case: it follows the status on the same line.

buildLine.stepsLabel.description: Small heading over the list of steps of making a new project's first version, on the project's App tab while it is made.

buildLine.step.plan.description: A row in the list of steps of making a new project's first version: the plan for it is written. Past tense once done; the row stays the same while it is under way.

buildLine.step.screens.description: A row in the list of steps of making a new project's first version: pictures of the app's main screens are drawn, before it is built.

buildLine.step.build.description: A row in the list of steps of making a new project's first version: the app itself is being built.

buildLine.step.check.description: A row in the list of steps of making a new project's first version: the built app's screens are looked at and fixed.

buildLine.step.test.description: A row in the list of steps of making a new project's first version: the built app's tests run.

buildLine.step.live.description: The last row in the list of steps of making a new project's first version: the app is published for everyone. An adjective, not the verb "to live".

buildLine.step.took_one.description: Under a finished row in the list of steps of making a new project's first version: how long that step took, in whole minutes, for example "3 min". "min" is short for minutes.

buildLine.step.took_other.description: Under a finished row in the list of steps of making a new project's first version: how long that step took, in whole minutes, for example "3 min". "min" is short for minutes.

buildLine.step.round.description: Under the row "Checking the screens" in the list of steps of making a new project's first version: which round of looking and fixing it is in. {{round}} is the round and {{rounds}} how many rounds there are at most.

buildLine.activity.live.description: Headline of the build's Live Activity on the iPhone Lock Screen, shown to the person who started a new project once its first version is published and the app is running for everyone. It stays there for ten minutes. {{name}} is the project's name. "live" is an adjective, not the verb "to live".

buildLine.activity.readyToTry.description: Headline of the build's Live Activity on the iPhone Lock Screen, shown to the person who started a new project once its first version is finished and can be opened and tried, but still waits for somebody's approval before it goes live. It stays there for ten minutes. {{name}} is the project's name.

firstSession.template.tier.title.description: Title of one of three examples of what a group can make (a tier list), in the list on the signed-out welcome page.

firstSession.template.tier.line.text: Rank your favorite spots, games, anything
firstSession.template.tier.line.description: Line under the example titled "A tier list" on the signed-out welcome page: what it is for.

firstSession.template.tier.short.description: Label of a tile on the screen that asks a member "What do you want to make?": picks a tier list as the starting idea for the new project.

firstSession.template.tier.note.text: I'm making us a tier list. Click the link to join the app.
firstSession.template.tier.note.description: Suggested text of the personal note a maker sends with the invite link to their group, when their new project started from the tier list idea. Written in the maker's voice, to their friends, while the app is still being made. No exclamation mark.

firstSession.template.tier.restaurants.l.description: Chip under the tier list sentence on the screen that asks a member "What do you want to make?": picks this option to fill the sentence's blank.

firstSession.template.tier.restaurants.s.text: A tier list for our favorite <0>restaurants</0>. Anyone can add items, everyone sorts them, and we can see where they land.
firstSession.template.tier.restaurants.s.description: Sentence shown on the screen that asks a member "What do you want to make?" after the Tier list tile and the "Restaurants" chip are picked. It is also sent as the description of what to make. <0>…</0> wraps the word the chip filled in, which is shown highlighted; keep the tags around that word.

firstSession.template.tier.restaurants.n.description: Name suggested for the new project in the "What should we call it?" field when the "Restaurants" option of the tier list idea is picked. A title; the maker can change it.

firstSession.template.tier.restaurants.d.text: The best places to eat, ranked by the whole group
firstSession.template.tier.restaurants.d.description: One-line tagline saved as the description of a new project made from the "Restaurants" option of the tier list idea, shown under the project's name. It says what the project is for, not its name. At most 90 characters.

firstSession.template.tier.own.example.description: Placeholder in the blank of the tier list sentence ("A tier list for our favorite …") when the maker fills it in themselves: an example of what could be ranked. It must read naturally in that blank.

firstSession.template.tier.own.name.description: Name suggested for a new project made from the tier list idea with the maker's own words. {{words}} is what they typed in the sentence's blank, with each word capitalized, for example "Taco Spots".

firstSession.template.tier.own.descripti.text: Anyone adds one, everyone ranks it
firstSession.template.tier.own.descripti.description: One-line tagline saved as the description of a new project made from the tier list idea with the maker's own words, shown under the project's name only when Homeroom cannot write one from the maker's own words. It says what the project is for, not its name. At most 90 characters.

firstSession.template.game.title.description: Title of one of three examples of what a group can make (a game), in the list on the signed-out welcome page.

firstSession.template.game.namePlacehold.description: Placeholder in the empty name field on the "What do you want to make?" screen while the game idea is picked: an example of a game project's name.

firstSession.template.game.line.text: A new one, built and played together
firstSession.template.game.line.description: Line under the example titled "A game" on the signed-out welcome page: what it is for.

firstSession.template.game.note.text: I'm making us a game. Click the link to join the app.

firstSession.template.game.board.sentenc.text: A new game we build together. For the first version, <0>a board game where</0> {{words}}
firstSession.template.game.board.sentenc.description: Sentence on the screen that asks a member "What do you want to make?" after the game tile and the "Board game" chip are picked. On screen the whole sentence is shown with a mark (an ellipsis in English) where {{words}} stands; the maker types those words in a box below. With their words in place of {{words}} it is sent as the description of what to make. {{words}} may stand anywhere in the sentence, and text may follow it. <0>…</0> wraps the starter, which is shown highlighted.

firstSession.template.challenge.miles.se.description: Sentence shown on the screen that asks a member "What do you want to make?" after the a group challenge idea and the "Miles" chip are picked. It is also sent as the description of what to make. <0>…</0> wraps the words the chip filled in, which are shown highlighted; keep the tags around them.

firstSession.template.challenge.miles.na.description: Name suggested for the new project in the "What should we call it?" field when the "Miles" option of the a group challenge idea is picked. A title; the maker can change it.

firstSession.template.challenge.miles.de.text: Log your miles each month and see who goes farthest
firstSession.template.challenge.miles.de.description: One-line tagline saved as the description of a new project made from the "Miles" option of the a group challenge idea, shown under the project's name. It says what the project is for, not its name. At most 90 characters.

firstSession.template.challenge.steps.la.description: Chip under the a group challenge sentence on the screen that asks a member "What do you want to make?": picks this option to fill the sentence's blank.

firstSession.template.challenge.steps.se.text: A challenge for our group: who logs the most <0>steps</0> this month, with a leaderboard.
firstSession.template.challenge.steps.se.description: Sentence shown on the screen that asks a member "What do you want to make?" after the a group challenge idea and the "Steps" chip are picked. It is also sent as the description of what to make. <0>…</0> wraps the words the chip filled in, which are shown highlighted; keep the tags around them.

firstSession.template.challenge.steps.na.description: Name suggested for the new project in the "What should we call it?" field when the "Steps" option of the a group challenge idea is picked. A title; the maker can change it.

firstSession.template.challenge.steps.de.text: Count steps together and chase a group goal each month
firstSession.template.challenge.steps.de.description: One-line tagline saved as the description of a new project made from the "Steps" option of the a group challenge idea, shown under the project's name. It says what the project is for, not its name. At most 90 characters.

firstSession.template.challenge.books.la.description: Chip under the a group challenge sentence on the screen that asks a member "What do you want to make?": picks this option to fill the sentence's blank.

firstSession.template.challenge.books.se.text: A challenge for our group: who reads the most <0>books</0> this month, with a leaderboard.
firstSession.template.challenge.books.se.description: Sentence shown on the screen that asks a member "What do you want to make?" after the a group challenge idea and the "Books" chip are picked. It is also sent as the description of what to make. <0>…</0> wraps the words the chip filled in, which are shown highlighted; keep the tags around them.

firstSession.template.challenge.books.na.description: Name suggested for the new project in the "What should we call it?" field when the "Books" option of the a group challenge idea is picked. A title; the maker can change it.

firstSession.template.challenge.books.de.text: Who reads the most this month, and how much we've read as a group
firstSession.template.challenge.books.de.description: One-line tagline saved as the description of a new project made from the "Books" option of the a group challenge idea, shown under the project's name. It says what the project is for, not its name. At most 90 characters.

firstSession.template.challenge.own.sent.text: A challenge for our group: who logs the most <0>{{words}}</0> this month, with a leaderboard.
firstSession.template.challenge.own.sent.description: Sentence of the a group challenge idea on the "What do you want to make?" screen when the maker fills its blank with their own words. {{words}} is what they type; <0>…</0> wraps it and is shown as a field; keep the tags and the placeholder.

firstSession.template.challenge.own.exam.description: Placeholder in the blank of the a group challenge sentence when the maker fills it in themselves: an example. It must read naturally in that blank.

firstSession.template.challenge.own.name.description: Name suggested for a new project made from the a group challenge idea with the maker's own words. {{words}} is what they typed in the sentence's blank, with each word capitalized.

firstSession.template.challenge.own.desc.text: A monthly goal the whole group chases together
firstSession.template.challenge.own.desc.description: One-line tagline saved as the description of a new project made from the a group challenge idea in the maker's own words, shown under the project's name only when Homeroom cannot write one from the maker's own words. It says what the project is for, not its name. At most 90 characters.

firstSession.make.somethingElse.description: Label of the fourth tile on the screen that asks a member "What do you want to make?", after three ready ideas: opens a list of more ideas, and of writing your own. The ellipsis says more choices are behind it.

firstSession.make.sheet.title.description: Heading of the sheet that opens from the "Something else…" tile on the "What do you want to make?" screen: a list of more starting ideas, and of writing your own.

firstSession.make.sheet.close.description: Accessible name of the round close button on the "Something else" sheet of more starting ideas.

firstSession.make.sheet.more.description: Small heading over the list of more starting ideas in the "Something else" sheet, under the row for writing your own idea.

firstSession.make.ownIdeaLine.text: Describe it, and Homeroom bot builds it
firstSession.make.ownIdeaLine.description: Line under "Your own idea" in the "Something else" sheet on the "What do you want to make?" screen: the member writes a description and Homeroom bot (the platform's AI helper, keep its name) builds the first version.

firstSession.make.title.text: What do you want to make?
firstSession.make.title.description: Heading of the screen where a member starts a new project by describing what the app should be.

firstSession.make.titleHello.text: Hi {{name}}, what do you want to make?
firstSession.make.titleHello.description: Heading of the screen where a member starts a new project by describing what the app should be, the first time a new member signs in. {{name}} is the member's display name or username.

firstSession.make.startFromIdea.description: Label above the grid of ready ideas (Tier list, A game, Organizer, Your own idea) on the "What do you want to make?" screen, where a member describes a new project.

firstSession.make.ideasLabel.description: Accessible name of the group of idea tiles on the "What do you want to make?" screen, where a member describes a new project.

firstSession.make.ownIdea.description: Label of the first row in the "Something else" sheet on the "What do you want to make?" screen, where a member describes a new project: instead of a ready idea, the member writes their own description in a text box. Also the fourth tile's label once that row is picked.

firstSession.make.briefLabel.description: Label of the field on the "What do you want to make?" screen, where a member describes a new project where the member says what the new app should do. "it" is the app.

firstSession.make.writeItYourself.description: Link beside the "What should it do?" label while a ready idea's sentence is shown: turns that sentence into plain text the member can edit freely. "it" is the description.

firstSession.make.ownWordsLabel.description: Accessible name of the small text field inside a ready idea's sentence, where the member types their own words for the blank.

firstSession.make.finishLabel.text: Finish it in your own words
firstSession.make.finishLabel.description: Label of the box under the game sentence on the "What do you want to make?" screen, where a member describes a new project: the member types the rest of that sentence. "it" is the sentence.

firstSession.make.choicesLabel.description: Accessible name of the row of chips under a ready idea's sentence; each chip fills the sentence's blank with a different option.

firstSession.make.ownChip.description: Chip beside the ready options under an idea's sentence on the "What do you want to make?" screen, where a member describes a new project: lets the member type their own words into the sentence's blank instead of picking an option. Keep the ellipsis.

firstSession.make.briefPlaceholder.text: A map of our favorite swimming spots…
firstSession.make.briefPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the empty "What should it do?" box: an example of a description a member might write for a new app. Keep the ellipsis.

firstSession.make.waitlistIdea.text: Filled in from your waitlist answer.
firstSession.make.waitlistIdea.description: Hint under the "What should it do?" box when it was filled in with what the member wrote when they joined the waitlist.

firstSession.make.searchIdea.description: Hint under the "What should it do?" box when it was filled in with what the member searched for in Discover and no app matched.

firstSession.make.threadIdea.text: Homeroom bot's plan from your thread comes along with it.
firstSession.make.threadIdea.description: Hint under the "What should it do?" box when the member opened New project from a private thread with Homeroom bot: the plan agreed in that thread is used with what they send here.

firstSession.make.nameLabel.description: Label of the name field on the "What do you want to make?" screen, where a member describes a new project: the name of the new project. "it" is the project.

firstSession.make.namePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the empty name field on the "What do you want to make?" screen, where a member describes a new project: an example of a project name.

firstSession.make.namePlaceholderOwn.description: Placeholder in the empty name field on the "What do you want to make?" screen while the member is describing an idea of their own (not a tier list, game or organizer): an example of a project name.

firstSession.make.needed.blank.description: Error under a ready idea's sentence when the member pressed Make it without typing their own words into the sentence's blank.

firstSession.make.needed.finish.description: Error under the game sentence when the member pressed Make it without typing the rest of the sentence in the box.

firstSession.make.needed.brief.text: Say what it should do first.
firstSession.make.needed.brief.description: Error under the empty "What should it do?" box when the member pressed Make it. "it" is the app.

firstSession.make.needed.briefShort.text: Say a little more about what it should do.
firstSession.make.needed.briefShort.description: Error under the "What should it do?" box when the member pressed Make it with a description that is too short. "it" is the app.

firstSession.make.needed.name.text: Give it a name to make it. You can change it later.
firstSession.make.needed.name.description: Error under the empty name field when the member pressed Make it. Both "it" are the project.

firstSession.make.blocked.noSlots.text: Your account can't make projects of its own yet: it has no app slots.
firstSession.make.blocked.noSlots.description: Red line above the pale Make it or Import it button on the "What do you want to make?" screen, when the account has no app slots at all: it is still waiting to be let in, or an admin set its allowance to zero.

firstSession.make.blocked.slots.text: All your app slots are used. Request more from App slots on your profile.
firstSession.make.blocked.slots.description: Red line above the pale Make it or Import it button on the "What do you want to make?" screen, when every app slot the account has is already taken. App slots is the row of that name on the profile.

firstSession.make.blocked.server.text: This server is at its app limit, so no new projects can be made right now.
firstSession.make.blocked.server.description: Red line above the pale Make it or Import it button on the "What do you want to make?" screen, when the whole platform has reached its limit of apps, whatever the person's own app slots.

firstSession.make.error.notMade.text: Could not make it. Try again.
firstSession.make.error.notMade.description: Error above the Make it button when creating the project failed and the server gave no reason of its own. "it" is the project.

firstSession.make.making.description: Text of the main button on the "What do you want to make?" screen, where a member describes a new project while the project is being created after the member pressed it.

firstSession.make.submit.description: Main button on the "What do you want to make?" screen, where a member describes a new project: creates the project from the description and name. "Make" is a verb and "it" is the project.

firstSession.make.importLink.description: Link under the Make it button, when the screen was opened from the Create button: switches to a form that brings in an existing app from a GitHub repository instead of describing a new one. GitHub is a name.

firstSession.make.speed.instant.text: <0>Instant</0> · ready to use in about a minute
firstSession.make.speed.instant.description: One line above "Who can change it" on the "What do you want to make?" screen, after a lightning icon, while Make it would create one of Homeroom's ready-made apps (a starting idea's choice that needs no typing): nothing has to be built, so the project can be used about a minute after Make it is pressed. <0>…</0> is bold. Keep it short: it must fit on one line of a phone screen.

firstSession.make.speed.custom.text: <0>Custom</0> · Homeroom bot builds it in 20 to 30 min
firstSession.make.speed.custom.description: One line above "Who can change it" on the "What do you want to make?" screen, after a sparkle icon, while Make it would ask Homeroom bot to build the first version from the member's own description (their own words, a game, or a starting idea finished in their own words). "it" is the project; "min" is short for minutes. <0>…</0> is bold. Keep it short: it must fit on one line of a phone screen.

firstSession.make.welcome.text: Welcome to Homeroom. Pick an idea below or describe your own.
firstSession.make.welcome.description: Quiet line under the question "What do you want to make?" the first time a new member sees that screen, just after signing in. Homeroom is the product's name. It is not shown when a returning member opens New project from the Create button.

firstSession.make.next.open.description: Spoken name of the small information (i) button after "Who can change it" on the "What do you want to make?" screen: opens a tip about what happens after Make it is pressed.

firstSession.make.next.title.description: Title of the tip opened by the information (i) button beside "Who can change it" on the "What do you want to make?" screen: what happens after Make it is pressed.

firstSession.make.next.readyMade.text: <0>A ready-made idea</0> is ready to use in about a minute.
firstSession.make.next.readyMade.description: First line of the tip opened by the information (i) button on the "What do you want to make?" screen: nothing has to be built for one of Homeroom's ready-made apps. <0>…</0> is bold.

firstSession.make.next.custom.text: <0>Anything else:</0> Homeroom bot writes a plan in about a minute, and asks you first if it needs you to choose something. Then it builds it in 20 to 30 min.
firstSession.make.next.custom.description: Second line of the tip opened by the information (i) button on the "What do you want to make?" screen: what happens when Homeroom bot builds the first version from the member's own description. "it" is the project; "min" is short for minutes. Homeroom bot is a name. <0>…</0> is bold.

firstSession.make.next.invite.text: <0>Then invite people</0> to use it and help improve it together.
firstSession.make.next.invite.description: Third line of the tip opened by the information (i) button on the "What do you want to make?" screen: what the member does once the project is made. "it" is the project. <0>…</0> is bold.

firstSession.make.next.rule.text: <0>Who can change it</0> says how changes go live once others join. You can change it later on the project’s page.
firstSession.make.next.rule.description: Last line of the tip opened by the information (i) button on the "What do you want to make?" screen: what the "Who can change it" line right below the tip means. The first "it" is the approval rule; "it" in the second sentence is the project. <0>…</0> is bold.

firstSession.make.rule.line.description: One line under the description and name fields on the "What do you want to make?" screen, before the project exists: the approval rule it will be made with. <0>…</0> is bold. {{preset}} is the rule's name, such as "You or the group" or "Two yeses".

firstSession.make.rule.intro.text: Pick how changes go live. You can change this later on the project’s page.
firstSession.make.rule.intro.description: Line under the title of the four approval presets sheet, opened from Change on the "What do you want to make?" screen, before the project is made.

firstSession.make.rule.change.description: Link at the end of the Make it step's "Who can change it" line: opens the four approval presets.

firstSession.make.rule.title.description: Title of the sheet with the four approval presets, opened from Change at the end of the "Who can change it" line on the "What do you want to make?" screen. It asks the line's own question.

firstSession.make.rule.plays.description: Section label over the rows showing what the picked preset means: one row for anyone, or two, for the reader and for anyone else.

firstSession.make.rule.close.description: Accessible name of the presets sheet's close button.

firstSession.make.rule.done.description: Button: close the presets sheet without changing anything.

firstSession.make.rule.use.description: Button: make the new project with the picked preset instead. {{preset}} is its name. Nothing is proposed: the project does not exist yet.

firstSession.make.frame.yourIdea.description: New project ("What do you want to make?") when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). Small label over the card that holds the two answers: what the project should do and what to call it.

firstSession.make.frame.whoCanChange.description: New project ("What do you want to make?") when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). Small label over the card beside the form that names the approval rule the new project starts with (for example "You or the group") and offers Change.

firstSession.make.lookAround.description: Line under the Make it button on a new member's first screen. <0>…</0> is a link that skips making a project and shows a short tour of Home instead.

firstSession.import.title.description: Heading of the form that brings an existing app in from a GitHub repository as a new project. "Import" is a verb. GitHub is a name.

firstSession.import.line.text: Bring an app that already exists. Your group builds on it from here.
firstSession.import.line.description: Line under the heading on the form that imports an existing app from a GitHub repository as a new project: what importing is for.

firstSession.import.urlLabel.description: Label of the field on the form that imports an existing app from a GitHub repository as a new project where the member pastes the repository's address.

firstSession.import.urlPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the repository address field on the form that imports an existing app from a GitHub repository as a new project: the shape of a GitHub address. "owner" and "repo" stand for the account's and the repository's names; github.com stays as it is.

firstSession.import.check.description: Button beside the repository address field on the form that imports an existing app from a GitHub repository as a new project: checks that Homeroom's bot account can reach that repository. A verb.

firstSession.import.recheck.description: The same button beside the repository address field after a check succeeded: runs the check again. A verb.

firstSession.import.checking.description: Status under the repository address field while the check runs: Homeroom is finding out whether its bot account can reach the repository.

firstSession.import.hasAccess.description: Status under the repository address field after a successful check. usernode-bot is the name of Homeroom's GitHub account and stays as written; "Write" is GitHub's name for that permission. {{repo}} is the repository, as owner/name. Keep the check mark first.

firstSession.import.inviteBot.text: Invite usernode-bot to the repo first (Write access on an organization repo).
firstSession.import.inviteBot.description: Hint under the repository address field before any check: what the member must do on GitHub first. usernode-bot is the name of Homeroom's GitHub account and stays as written; "Write" is GitHub's name for that permission.

firstSession.import.needed.repo.description: Error under the repository address field when the member pressed Import it before the repository was checked. "Check" is a verb.

firstSession.import.nameLabel.description: Label of the name field on the form that imports an existing app from a GitHub repository as a new project: the name the imported project will have. "it" is the project.

firstSession.import.namePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the empty name field on the form that imports an existing app from a GitHub repository as a new project: an example of a project name.

firstSession.import.needed.name.text: Give it a name to import it. You can change it later.
firstSession.import.needed.name.description: Error under the empty name field when the member pressed Import it. Both "it" are the project.

firstSession.import.importing.description: Text of the main button on the form that imports an existing app from a GitHub repository as a new project while the import request is running.

firstSession.import.submit.description: Main button on the form that imports an existing app from a GitHub repository as a new project: creates the project from the checked repository. "Import" is a verb and "it" is the app.

firstSession.import.describeInstead.description: Link under the Import it button: goes back to the form where a new project is described in words.

firstSession.import.frame.repository.description: Import a GitHub repo, when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). Small label over the card that holds the repo's address and the project's name.

firstSession.import.error.noUrl.text: Paste a GitHub repo URL first.
firstSession.import.error.noUrl.description: Error under the repository address field when the member pressed Check with the field empty.

firstSession.import.error.network.description: Error under the repository address field when the check could not reach the server.

firstSession.import.error.checkFailed.description: Error under the repository address field when the check failed and the server gave no reason. "Check" is a noun here. {{status}} is the numeric HTTP status code, for example 502.

firstSession.import.error.notImported.text: Could not import it. Try again.
firstSession.import.error.notImported.description: Error above the Import it button when the import failed and the server gave no reason of its own. "it" is the repository's app.

firstSession.import.note.unread.text: Couldn’t read this repo’s dapp.json. Anything it sets still applies once it’s imported.
firstSession.import.note.unread.description: Note under the import form after a repository was checked but its settings file could not be read. dapp.json is the name of a settings file in the repository and stays as written.

firstSession.import.note.public.text: Its dapp.json says anyone can find it, join and build, so it starts that way rather than as a private community.
firstSession.import.note.public.description: Note under the import form after a repository was checked: its settings file makes the project open to everyone, to see and to build. "Its" is the repository's and "it" the project. "Build" means making changes to the app. dapp.json is the name of a settings file in the repository and stays as written.

firstSession.import.note.viewPublic.text: Its dapp.json says anyone can see it, and only people invited can build, so it starts that way rather than as a private community.
firstSession.import.note.viewPublic.description: Note under the import form after a repository was checked: its settings file lets everyone see the project but only invited people change it. "Its" is the repository's and "it" the project. "Build" means making changes to the app. dapp.json is the name of a settings file in the repository and stays as written.

firstSession.import.note.buildPublic.text: Its dapp.json says anyone can build it, so it starts that way rather than as a private community.
firstSession.import.note.buildPublic.description: Note under the import form after a repository was checked: its settings file lets anyone make changes to the project. "Its" is the repository's and "it" the project. "Build" means making changes to the app. dapp.json is the name of a settings file in the repository and stays as written.

firstSession.import.note.private.text: Its dapp.json says it is private to the people invited. Its code stays public on GitHub., so it starts that way rather than as a private community.
firstSession.import.note.private.description: Note under the import form after a repository was checked, in a rare case: its settings file says anyone may see the project but does not say who may change it. The English is kept exactly as the product has always shown it, stray full stop included. dapp.json is the name of a settings file in the repository and stays as written. GitHub is a name.

firstSession.welcome.opening.description: Accessible name of the placeholder screen shown for a moment after a person follows an invite link, while the community they were invited to loads.

firstSession.people.count_one.description: How many people are in a community: the heading over the list of members on an invited person's welcome screen, and the screen-reader text for a row of members' faces. {{count}} is the number.

firstSession.people.count_other.description: How many people are in a community: the heading over the list of members on an invited person's welcome screen, and the screen-reader text for a row of members' faces. {{count}} is the number.

firstSession.people.you.description: Accessible name of the row of faces above a newly made project, which shows who is in its community: only the viewer so far.

firstSession.people.youAndName.description: Accessible name of the row of faces above a newly made project, which shows who is in its community: the viewer and one other member. {{name}} is that member's username or name.

firstSession.people.youAndOthers_one.description: Accessible name of the row of faces above a newly made project, which shows who is in its community: the viewer and other members. {{count}} is how many others.

firstSession.people.youAndOthers_other.description: Accessible name of the row of faces above a newly made project, which shows who is in its community: the viewer and other members. {{count}} is how many others.

firstSession.made.communityLabel.description: Heading on the screen shown right after a project is made, above the new project's card: making a project also made a community for it.

firstSession.made.inviteHint.text: Invite people to use it and help improve it together.
firstSession.made.inviteHint.description: Line above the buttons on the screen shown right after a project is made, before any invite has been sent. "it" is the new app.

firstSession.made.checkingQuestions.text: Checking whether Homeroom bot needs to ask you anything first.
firstSession.made.checkingQuestions.description: Line on the screen shown right after a person makes a project, in place of the invite buttons for a few seconds, while the assistant called Homeroom bot works out whether it has questions to ask before it builds the app. Homeroom bot is a name.

firstSession.made.noBotNote.text: Your description is its first request. You or anyone you invite can build it from there.
firstSession.made.noBotNote.description: Note under the new project's card on the screen shown right after a project is made, when the assistant Homeroom bot is not building it: the description the maker wrote was filed as the project's first request (a request is an item asking for a change). "Build" means making that change.

firstSession.made.sent.copied.description: Line above the buttons on the screen shown right after a project is made, once the invite link was copied to the clipboard.

firstSession.made.sent.shared.description: Line above the buttons on the screen shown right after a project is made, once the invite link was handed to the device's share sheet. "Invite" is a noun.

firstSession.made.shareInvite.description: Main button on the screen shown right after a project is made: opens a sheet for sending an invite link to the new community. "Share" is a verb and "invite" a noun.

firstSession.made.shareAgain.description: Button on the screen shown right after a project is made after an invite link has gone out: opens the invite sheet again to send the link once more. "Share" is a verb.

firstSession.made.inviteLater.description: Secondary button on the screen shown right after a project is made, before any invite has been sent: goes on without inviting anyone now.

firstSession.made.goToApp.description: First session, the screen after Make it: the second button once an invite has gone out, while the new project's app runs. Opens the app full screen.

firstSession.made.continue.description: First session, the screen after Make it: the second button once an invite has gone out, while Homeroom bot is still building the project's first version, so there is no app to open yet. Goes to Home.

firstSession.made.gettingReady.description: Title of the small progress card under the new project on the screen shown right after a project is made, while the project is still being set up and before the step it is on is known. The buttons that go on stay off until it is ready. "it" is the project.

firstSession.made.setup.database.description: Title of the small progress card under the new project on the screen shown right after a project is made: the first of four setup steps, making the database where the app keeps its data. "its" is the app's.

firstSession.made.setup.repository.description: Title of the small progress card under the new project on the screen shown right after a project is made: the second of four setup steps, saving the app's code where its changes will be made. "its" is the app's.

firstSession.made.setup.build.description: Title of the small progress card under the new project on the screen shown right after a project is made: the third of four setup steps, turning the app's code into something that can run. "it" is the app.

firstSession.made.setup.deploy.description: Title of the small progress card under the new project on the screen shown right after a project is made: the last of four setup steps, starting the app so people can open it. "it" is the app.

firstSession.made.setup.ring.description: Read by screen readers for the small ring on the progress card under a new project while it is set up, which shows how far the setup has got. {{step}} is the step it is on, {{total}} how many steps there are.

firstSession.made.setup.usual.description: Second line of the small progress card under a new project while it is being set up: how long setting a project up usually takes.

firstSession.made.setup.slow.description: Second line of the small progress card under a new project, once setting it up has run past the usual minute: says calmly that it will be ready soon, not that anything is wrong. The new app is what will be ready.

firstSession.made.setup.goOn.text: Should be ready shortly. You can go on, and open it once it’s ready.
firstSession.made.setup.goOn.description: Second line of the small progress card under a new project, once setting it up has taken so long that the buttons that go on are turned back on before it is ready. The new app is what will be ready; in "open it once it’s ready" both "it" are the app.

firstSession.made.setup.done.description: Second line of the small progress card under a new project once setting it up has finished: the card stays where it was and says the app is up. "It" is the new app.

firstSession.made.setup.setUp.description: Title of the small progress card under a new project once setting it up has finished, shown when the project's picture above already says how Homeroom bot is building it. "It" is the new app.

firstSession.made.firstLook.kicker.description: Small label, shown in capital letters, at the top of the card under a new project on the screen shown right after a project is made, beside a small picture of the app's main screen as the assistant called Homeroom bot drew it before building the app.

firstSession.made.firstLook.title.text: Here's what Homeroom bot is making
firstSession.made.firstLook.title.description: Title of the card under a new project on the screen shown right after a project is made, beside a small picture of the app's main screen that the assistant called Homeroom bot drew before building it. Homeroom bot is a name.

firstSession.made.firstLook.alt.text: The first look at {{app}}'s main screen
firstSession.made.firstLook.alt.description: Description, for screen readers, of the small picture in the card under a new project on the screen shown right after a project is made: a drawing of the app's main screen. {{app}} is the project's name.

firstSession.made.firstLook.open.text: Open your chat with Homeroom bot
firstSession.made.firstLook.open.description: Name, for screen readers, of the card under a new project on the screen shown right after a project is made: a tap anywhere on the card opens the maker's chat with the assistant called Homeroom bot, where the build is reported. Homeroom bot is a name.

firstSession.made.cardView.label.text: Show the invite or the app
firstSession.made.cardView.label.description: Name, for screen readers, of the small two-button switch in the top-right corner of the new project's card on the screen shown right after a project is made. It switches the card between the invite (the app's icon, as the people invited see it) and a picture of what the app looks like.

firstSession.made.cardView.invite.description: One side of the small switch in the top-right corner of the new project's card on the screen shown right after a project is made: shows the card as the people invited will see it, with the app's icon. A noun, kept to one short word.

firstSession.made.cardView.app.description: One side of the small switch in the top-right corner of the new project's card on the screen shown right after a project is made: shows a picture of what the app looks like. A noun, kept to one short word.

firstSession.made.cardView.example.description: Small tag in the top-left corner of the picture of the app on the new project's card, on the screen shown right after a project is made from one of Homeroom's ready-made apps: the entries in the picture are samples, not the maker's own. One short word.

firstSession.made.cardView.exampleAlt.text: An example of {{app}}'s main screen, with sample entries
firstSession.made.cardView.exampleAlt.description: Description, for screen readers, of the picture of the app on the new project's card, on the screen shown right after a project is made from one of Homeroom's ready-made apps: its main screen filled in with made-up entries. {{app}} is the project's name.

firstSession.made.firstLook.usual.description: Second line of the progress shown in the card under a new project on the screen shown right after a project is made, while the project is still being set up: how long setting it up usually takes. Short: it shares a narrow column with a picture.

firstSession.made.firstLook.slow.description: Second line of the progress shown in the card under a new project, once setting the project up has run past the usual minute: says calmly that it will be ready soon, not that anything is wrong. Short: it shares a narrow column with a picture.

firstSession.made.firstLook.goOn.text: Ready shortly. You can go on.
firstSession.made.firstLook.goOn.description: Second line of the progress shown in the card under a new project, once setting it up has taken so long that the buttons that go on are turned back on before it is ready: it will be ready soon, and they need not wait. Short: it shares a narrow column with a picture.

firstSession.made.goTo.description: Button on the screen shown right after a project is made once an invite has gone out, when the project was started from the Create button: opens the new project. {{community}} is its name.

firstSession.made.sketching.description: Read by screen readers on the screen shown right after a project is made while a preview card for the project is being drawn from what the maker wrote. {{app}} is the project's name.

firstSession.made.needsYou.description: Small label over a card on the screen shown right after a project is made that waits for the maker to do something: answer a plan, retry a setup that failed, or set secrets. Read as "this needs you".

firstSession.made.planWaits.text: Homeroom bot has a plan for {{app}}
firstSession.made.planWaits.description: Title of the card on the screen shown right after a project is made when the assistant called Homeroom bot has written a plan and waits for the maker's answer. {{app}} is the project's name. Homeroom bot is a name.

firstSession.made.planAnswer.text: Answer it in your chat, and it starts building.
firstSession.made.planAnswer.description: Line under the title of the card that says Homeroom bot has a plan: the first "it" is the plan, the second is Homeroom bot, which starts building the app once the plan is answered.

firstSession.made.goToChat.description: Button on the card that says Homeroom bot has a plan: opens the maker's chat with Homeroom bot, where the plan is answered.

firstSession.made.questions.titleOne.description: Heading on the screen shown right after a person makes a project, over one question the assistant called Homeroom bot asks before it builds the app, with answers to pick from.

firstSession.made.questions.titleTwo.description: Heading on the screen shown right after a person makes a project, over two questions the assistant called Homeroom bot asks before it builds the app, each with answers to pick from.

firstSession.made.questions.line.text: Homeroom bot builds {{project}} from your answers.
firstSession.made.questions.line.description: Line under the heading over Homeroom bot's questions, on the screen shown right after a person makes a project. {{project}} is the project's name; Homeroom bot is a name.

firstSession.made.questions.submit.description: Button under Homeroom bot's questions, on the screen shown right after a person makes a project: sends the answers picked, and the app is built from them.

firstSession.made.questions.error.text: Your answers didn't go through. Try again.
firstSession.made.questions.error.description: Shown under Homeroom bot's questions after a person makes a project, when sending their answers failed.

firstSession.made.stalled.failed.text: Setup stopped before it was running
firstSession.made.stalled.failed.description: Title of the card on the screen shown right after a project is made when setting the project up failed. "it" is the app.

firstSession.made.stalled.needsSecrets.description: Title of the card on the screen shown right after a project is made when the project cannot start until its secrets are set. Secrets are private configuration values such as API keys. "It" is the app.

firstSession.made.stalled.setSecrets.description: Button on the card that says the project needs secrets to start: opens the dialog where the project's secrets (private configuration values such as API keys) are entered. "Set" is a verb.

firstSession.made.line.failed.description: Status line on the new project's plain card on the screen shown right after a project is made: setting the project up stopped with an error. "it" is the project.

firstSession.made.line.needsSecrets.text: It needs its secrets before it can start.
firstSession.made.line.needsSecrets.description: Status line on the new project's plain card on the screen shown right after a project is made: the app waits for its secrets (private configuration values such as API keys) to be set.

firstSession.made.line.importing.description: Status line on the new project's plain card on the screen shown right after a project is made, for a project imported from a GitHub repository: the import is still running. GitHub is a name.

firstSession.made.line.imported.description: Status line on the new project's plain card on the screen shown right after a project is made, for a project imported from a GitHub repository: the import finished and the app is running.

firstSession.made.line.settingUp.description: Status line on the new project's plain card on the screen shown right after a project is made: the project is still being set up. "it" is the project.

firstSession.made.line.readyToUse.description: Status line on the new project's plain card on the screen shown right after a project is made, for a project made from one of Homeroom's ready-made apps: it is set up and can be used now.

firstSession.made.line.versionOneReady.text: Version one is ready to try.
firstSession.made.line.versionOneReady.description: Status line on the new project's plain card on the screen shown right after a project is made: the first version of the app has been built and can be opened and tried.

firstSession.made.line.botBuilds.text: Homeroom bot builds it from your description.
firstSession.made.line.botBuilds.description: Status line on the new project's plain card on the screen shown right after a project is made: the assistant called Homeroom bot will build the app from what the maker wrote. Homeroom bot is a name.

firstSession.made.line.firstRequest.text: Your description is its first request.
firstSession.made.line.firstRequest.description: Status line on the new project's plain card on the screen shown right after a project is made, when Homeroom bot is not building the project: what the maker wrote was filed as the project's first request (an item asking for a change).

firstSession.made.note.failed.text: Trying again usually clears it. If it stops again, ask an admin.
firstSession.made.note.failed.description: Second line under the new project's card on the screen shown right after a project is made, when setting the project up failed. "it" is first the problem, then the setup.

firstSession.made.note.needsSecrets.text: Set them, and it finishes starting.
firstSession.made.note.needsSecrets.description: Second line under the new project's card on the screen shown right after a project is made, when the project waits for its secrets. "them" are the secrets (private configuration values) and "it" is the app.

firstSession.made.note.imported.text: Its repo says what it does. You and anyone you invite build on it from here.
firstSession.made.note.imported.description: Second line under the new project's card on the screen shown right after a project is made, for a project imported from a GitHub repository. "Its repo" is the project's repository; "build on it" means making changes to the app.

firstSession.made.note.noBot.text: You or anyone you invite can build it from there.
firstSession.made.note.noBot.description: Second line under the new project's card on the screen shown right after a project is made, when Homeroom bot is not building the project: members build it themselves, starting from the first request. "build" is a verb.

firstSession.made.note.planWaits.text: Homeroom bot is waiting for your go-ahead.
firstSession.made.note.planWaits.description: Second line under the new project's card on the screen shown right after a project is made, when Homeroom bot has sent a plan and will not start building until the maker approves it. Homeroom bot is a name.

firstSession.made.note.making.text: Homeroom is making your app. It will message you when the first version is ready to try, or if it has any questions.
firstSession.made.note.making.description: Second line under the new project's card on the screen shown right after a project is made, while the first version is being built. Homeroom is the product's name.

firstSession.made.people.you.description: Stands where a member's username is shown under the single face in the people row on the screen shown right after a project is made, when the maker's own username is not known yet: the only person here is the reader. Shown alone; lower case in English, like a username.

firstSession.invite.title.description: Heading of the sheet for sending an invite link. {{community}} is the name of the community people are invited to.

firstSession.invite.previewLabel.description: Small label on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community, over a preview of the invite as the people receiving it will see it. "they" are the people invited.

firstSession.invite.line.description: The invite as its receiver sees it: shown in the preview on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community and used as the title of the shared link. {{inviter}} is the name of the member sending the invite and {{community}} the community's name. "you" is the person receiving it.

firstSession.invite.lineAnonymous.description: The invite as its receiver sees it, when the sender's name is not known: shown in the preview on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community and used as the title of the shared link. {{community}} is the community's name.

firstSession.invite.noteDefault.text: I'm making this for us. Click the link to join the app.
firstSession.invite.noteDefault.description: Suggested text of the personal note a maker sends with an invite link, already filled in when the sheet opens. Written in the maker's voice, to their friends, while the app is still being made. No exclamation mark.

firstSession.invite.noteLabel.description: Accessible name of the text box on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community where the sender writes a personal note that goes with the link.

firstSession.invite.notePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the empty note box on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community.

firstSession.invite.noteHint.text: When you share, your note also goes in the group chat as your first message.
firstSession.invite.noteHint.description: Hint under the note box on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community: the note is also posted in the community's chat.

firstSession.invite.shareLink.description: Main button on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community on a phone or tablet: opens the device's share sheet with the invite link. "Share" is a verb.

firstSession.invite.shareOther.description: Secondary button on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community on a computer, beside Copy link: opens the system's share sheet with the invite link. A verb; keep the ellipsis.

firstSession.invite.copyLink.description: Button on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community: copies the note and the invite link to the clipboard. "Copy" is a verb.

firstSession.invite.copied.description: Shown on the Copy link button for a moment after the invite link was copied. Keep the check mark first.

firstSession.invite.status.shared.description: Status on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community after the invite link was handed to the device's share sheet. Keep the check mark first.

firstSession.invite.status.copied.text: Link copied. Paste it in your group chat.
firstSession.invite.status.copied.description: Status on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community after the invite link was copied to the clipboard: tells the sender what to do with it.

firstSession.invite.status.ready.text: Your link is ready. Press Share again to send it.
firstSession.invite.status.ready.description: Status on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community when the link was made but the browser would not open the share sheet: pressing the Share button a second time will work. "Share" names that button.

firstSession.invite.error.noLink.text: Could not make a link. Try again.
