firstSession.invite.error.noLink.description: Error on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community when the invite link could not be created and the server gave no reason of its own.

firstSession.invite.error.notShared.text: Could not share the link. Try again.
firstSession.invite.error.notShared.description: Error on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community when sharing the invite link failed.

firstSession.invite.error.notCopied.text: Could not copy the link. Try again.
firstSession.invite.error.notCopied.description: Error on the sheet for sending an invite link to a community when the invite link could not be copied to the clipboard.

firstSession.invite.limits.text: Anyone with the link can join until you turn it off.
firstSession.invite.limits.description: Small print at the bottom of the invite sheet: the invite link has no end date and no limit of people; it works until the person who made it turns it off.

firstSession.tour.counter.description: Small counter at the top of each card of a new member's tour: which card this is. {{step}} is its number and {{total}} how many cards the tour has, for example "3 of 9".

firstSession.tour.skip.description: Button on each card of a new member's tour except the last: ends the tour now.

firstSession.tour.next.description: Button on a card of a new member's tour: goes to the next card.

firstSession.tour.gotIt.description: Button on the last card of a new member's tour: ends the tour.

firstSession.tour.wait.title.description: Card of the short tour a new member is walked through after making or joining a project, title shown in place of a card that points at the app while the app is still being set up or is still opening. {{app}} is the project's name.

firstSession.tour.wait.text.text: The tour goes on as soon as it’s ready.
firstSession.tour.wait.text.description: Card of the short tour a new member is walked through, text under the title that says the app is getting ready: the tour waits and continues by itself once the app is ready. "it" is the app.

firstSession.tip.title.description: Title of the small tip shown once under the Homeroom mark (the logo button at the top of the screen) the first time a person opens the app they just made.

firstSession.tip.titleInvited.description: Title of the small tip shown once under the Homeroom mark the first time an invited person opens the app they were invited to. {{app}} is the app's name.

firstSession.tip.line.text: Tap <0></0> to suggest a change, or to go to the community and Homeroom.
firstSession.tip.line.description: Line of the small tip under the Homeroom mark. <0></0> is where the mark itself is drawn, as a small picture the size of the text: keep it where the thing to tap belongs in the sentence. The mark opens a menu with Suggest an improvement, the app's community and the rest of Homeroom.

firstSession.tip.lineInvited.text: {{inviter}} invited you. Tap <0></0> to suggest a change, or to go to the community and Homeroom.
firstSession.tip.lineInvited.description: Line of the same tip for an invited person, when who sent the invite is known. {{inviter}} is that person's name. <0></0> is where the Homeroom mark is drawn, as a small picture the size of the text.

firstSession.tip.lineHomeroom.text: Tap <0></0> to suggest a change, or to go to Homeroom.
firstSession.tip.lineHomeroom.description: Line of the small tip under the Homeroom mark, for a newcomer who has not been to Homeroom yet: the mark opens a menu with Suggest an improvement and Go to Homeroom, which takes them to Homeroom for the first time. <0></0> is where the mark itself is drawn, as a small picture the size of the text: keep it where the thing to tap belongs in the sentence.

firstSession.tip.lineInvitedHomeroom.text: {{inviter}} invited you. Tap <0></0> to suggest a change, or to go to Homeroom.
firstSession.tip.lineInvitedHomeroom.description: Line of the same tip for an invited person new to Homeroom, when who sent the invite is known. {{inviter}} is that person's name. <0></0> is where the Homeroom mark is drawn, as a small picture the size of the text.

firstSession.walk.steps.description: Spoken label of the numbered circles at the top of each card of the short walk on Home (1, 2, 3), for screen readers. {{step}} is the card shown, {{total}} how many there are.

firstSession.walk.home.title.description: First card of the short walk on Home, the first time a new person reaches Home after opening their first app. It points at that app's tile.

firstSession.walk.home.text.description: Line under "Welcome to Homeroom" on the walk's first card, pointing at the app's tile on Home: their app is on the Home screen. {{app}} is the project's name, as its tile shows it.

firstSession.walk.bot.title.description: Second card of the walk on Home, pointing at the AI tab: Homeroom bot is the assistant that builds changes to apps. A name, keep it as it is.

firstSession.walk.bot.text.text: It's in the Homeroom bot tab. Ask it to make any changes to {{app}}.
firstSession.walk.bot.text.description: Line on the walk's Homeroom bot card, for an app with no example change to offer (one Homeroom bot built, or a game): where to find the bot (the AI tab, the chat with Homeroom bot) and what to ask it for (any change to the app). {{app}} is the project's name, as its tile on Home shows it.

firstSession.walk.bot.textExample.description: Line on the walk's Homeroom bot card, which points at the AI tab where the bot is, for an app made from a ready-made starter: the bot makes changes to the app when asked. {{example}} is a short change somebody could ask for in that app, in English and lowercase, for example "add a cheap eats tier" for a restaurant tier list; keep it inside the quotation marks your language uses.

firstSession.walk.communities.title.description: Third card of the walk on Home, pointing at the Communities tab in the main navigation, whose page lists the person's communities, the new project's among them.

firstSession.walk.communities.text.text: {{app}}'s hub is under Communities. Invite people and decide what changes.
firstSession.walk.communities.text.description: Line on the walk's Communities card, which points at the Communities tab: the project's hub page is reached from that tab's page, and it is where its people are invited and decide together which changes to its app go in. {{app}} is the project's name. Communities is the tab's name. "Invite" and "decide" are verbs.

firstSession.walk.goToCommunity.description: Button on the last card of a new member's walk on Home, which points at their project's community tile: ends the walk and opens their project's hub page. "Go to" is a verb; "community" is the project's community, as the app menu's "Go to community" row says it.

firstSession.tour.look.make.title.description: Card of the short tour a new member is walked through after joining or making a project, for a member who chose to look around first, title: points at the New project control on Home, which starts a new project.

firstSession.tour.look.make.text.text: New project starts a community and its app.
firstSession.tour.look.make.text.description: Card of the short tour a new member is walked through after joining or making a project, for a member who chose to look around first: text about the control on Home labelled "New project". Write New project as that control is named.

firstSession.tour.look.discover.title.description: Card of the short tour a new member is walked through after joining or making a project, for a member who chose to look around first, title: points at the list of communities to join at the foot of Home.

firstSession.tour.look.discover.text.text: Open any one, pin it, or join it.
firstSession.tour.look.discover.text.description: Card of the short tour a new member is walked through after joining or making a project, for a member who chose to look around first: text about the communities to join on Home. "Open", "pin" and "join" are verbs; "one" is a community.

firstSession.tour.look.communities.title.text: Communities you join show up here
firstSession.tour.look.communities.title.description: Card of the short tour a new member is walked through after joining or making a project, for a member who chose to look around first, title: points at the Communities tab in the main navigation, whose page lists a community once you join it.

firstSession.tour.look.communities.text.text: Each one has its own hub and discussion.
firstSession.tour.look.communities.text.description: Card of the short tour a new member is walked through after joining or making a project, for a member who chose to look around first: text about the Communities tab. "Each one" is a community; its hub is its main page.

firstSession.tour.look.bot.title.text: Homeroom bot has its own tab
firstSession.tour.look.bot.title.description: Card of the short tour a new member is walked through after joining or making a project, for a member who chose to look around first, title of the last card: points at the AI tab, the chat with Homeroom bot. "AI" is the tab's name. Homeroom bot is the name of the assistant and Messages the name of the tab.

firstSession.tour.look.bot.text.text: It makes apps with you. You can always find it here.
firstSession.tour.look.bot.text.description: Card of the short tour a new member is walked through after joining or making a project, for a member who chose to look around first, text of the last card. "It" is Homeroom bot.

tour.counter.description: Small counter at the top of each card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings. {{step}} is the card's number and {{total}} how many cards there are, for example "3 of 5".

tour.skip.description: Button on each card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings: asks whether to leave the tour.

tour.next.description: Button on each card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings except the last: goes to the next card.

tour.finish.description: Button on the last card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings: ends the tour. A verb.

tour.confirm.text.text: Are you sure? You can reopen this from Settings.
tour.confirm.text.description: Question shown in the tour's card after Skip is pressed in the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings. "this" is the tour. Settings is the name of a screen.

tour.confirm.keepGoing.description: Button under the question asked after Skip is pressed in the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings: stays in the tour.

tour.confirm.skip.description: Button under the question asked after Skip is pressed in the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings: leaves the tour.

tour.step.communities.title.description: Title of the first card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings: points at the Communities tab in the main navigation, whose page lists the communities the person is in.

tour.step.communities.body.text: Communities here build apps together. Anyone can propose a change, and the community votes on it. Find yours here.
tour.step.communities.body.description: Text of the first card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings, pointing at the Communities tab. "change" is a noun: a change to an app. "here" in "Find yours here" is that tab.

tour.step.apps.title.description: Title of the second card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings: points at the section of Home with this heading, the person's own shortcuts to apps.

tour.step.apps.body.text: Open the apps you pin here, in one tap. To start your own, select New project.
tour.step.apps.body.description: Text of the second card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings, about the Pinned apps section. "New project" is the label of the control on Home that starts one (the last tile of Pinned apps, or the button beside search); write New project as that control is named.

tour.step.appMenu.title.description: Title of the third card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings: points at the Homeroom mark, the logo button that opens an app's menu. Homeroom is the product's name.

tour.step.appMenu.body.text: Select the Homeroom logo in any app to suggest an improvement or visit its community.
tour.step.appMenu.body.description: Text of the third card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings, about the Homeroom logo button that opens the app's menu. "suggest an improvement" echoes the menu's Suggest an improvement button.

tour.step.menuActions.title.description: Title of the fourth card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings: points at the button of this name in an app's menu, where a member says what the app should do differently.

tour.step.menuActions.body.text: Change something in any of your apps or in Homeroom itself. Start building it or share a request for someone in the community to pick up.
tour.step.menuActions.body.description: Text of the fourth card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings, about Suggest an improvement. "Homeroom itself" is the platform's own project; "start building it" is building the change now, and "share a request" is an item the community votes on. The card names neither Homeroom bot nor the person who builds: that comes on the last card.

tour.step.settings.title.description: Title of the last card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings: points at the profile tab. "this" is the tour.

tour.step.settings.body.text: You can replay this tour any time from Settings, on your profile. Finish takes you to your communities.
tour.step.settings.body.description: Text of the last card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, started from Settings. Settings is the name of a screen reached from the person's profile. "Finish" is the name of the card's button, and pressing it opens the Communities screen.

tour.step.meetBot.title.description: Title of the Home tour's stop pointing at the Homeroom bot tab in the main navigation, which opens the person's chat with it. "Homeroom bot" is the name of Homeroom's assistant that builds changes; keep "Homeroom" as it is.

tour.step.meetBot.body.text: Your AI assistant to build a change, file an idea or fix a bug for you. Find it in the Homeroom bot tab.
tour.step.meetBot.body.description: Fifth card of the welcome tour on the Home screen, under the title "Meet Homeroom bot", pointing at the Homeroom bot tab. The sentence describes Homeroom bot; "Homeroom bot" is the tab's name in the main navigation, so word it as that tab is shown.

identity.fallbackName.description: Shown where the viewer's name would be at the top of their own profile screen, when they have neither a display name nor a username.

identity.edit.description: Button on the viewer's own profile screen: opens the sheet where they change their photo, name and bio.

identity.buildingSince.description: Under the viewer's name on their profile: when they joined. {{date}} is a month and year, such as "March 2026". "Building" means making things on Homeroom.

identity.apps_one.description: Under the viewer's name on their profile. {{count}} is how many apps have a change of theirs live, whoever made the app; it is not the apps they made, which the App slots row counts.

identity.apps_other.description: Under the viewer's name on their profile. {{count}} is how many apps have a change of theirs live, whoever made the app; it is not the apps they made, which the App slots row counts.

line.factPair.description: Joins two short facts on one small line of the profile screen ("@ada · Building since March 2026", "Notes · sent today"). {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next fact, each already a complete phrase. Use the separator your language uses between such facts.

activity.title.description: Title of a card on the viewer's own profile: how long they spent inside apps on each of the last seven days. Sentence case.

activity.timeLabel.description: Label under a total such as "3h 40m" on the viewer's profile: time spent inside apps over the last seven days, not time on Homeroom's own screens. Lower case.

activity.appsLabel_one.description: Label under the number 1 on the viewer's profile: how many different apps they opened in the last seven days. Lower case.

activity.appsLabel_other.description: Label under a number on the viewer's profile: how many different apps they opened in the last seven days. Lower case.

activity.hours.description: A short length of time on the viewer's profile, such as "3h 40m". {{hours}} and {{minutes}} are numbers; use your language's short forms.

activity.minutes.description: A short length of time under an hour on the viewer's profile, such as "45m". {{minutes}} is a number; use your language's short form.

activity.underMinute.description: A length of time on the viewer's profile: some time was spent, but less than one minute. Written in the same short form as "45m".

activity.noTime.description: Read out or shown on hover for a day on the viewer's profile chart when they spent no time in apps that day. It completes "Monday: no time".

activity.daySpoken.description: One day of the viewer's activity chart, as a screen reader says it and as a hover shows it. {{day}} is a weekday name and {{time}} a length of time, such as "Monday: 35m".

activity.chartLabel.description: Accessible name of the seven-day chart on the viewer's profile. It is not shown on screen.

activity.note.text: Last 7 days, by UTC day. Only time inside apps counts.
activity.note.description: Small note under the chart on the viewer's profile. A day starts at midnight UTC, whatever the viewer's own time zone, and time on Homeroom's own screens is not included.

activity.empty.text: No time in apps this week yet. Open an app and your days show here.
activity.empty.description: The one line in the "This week" card on the viewer's profile when they spent no time in apps and opened none in the last seven days.

activity.mergedLabel_one.description: Label under the number 1 in the "This week" card on the viewer's profile: how many of their changes went live in the last seven days. Lower case.

activity.mergedLabel_other.description: Label under a number in the "This week" card on the viewer's profile: how many of their changes went live in the last seven days. Lower case.

activity.challengesLabel_one.description: Label under the number 1 in the "This week" card on the viewer's profile: how many challenges they completed in the last seven days. Lower case.

activity.challengesLabel_other.description: Label under a number in the "This week" card on the viewer's profile: how many challenges they completed in the last seven days. Lower case.

activity.share.description: Button beside the title of the "This week" card on the viewer's profile. It opens the card that shares those figures.

weekShare.title.description: Title of the card opened by Share on the viewer's profile, where they choose which of the week's figures to share.

weekShare.note.text: Choose what to include. Nothing is posted for you, and sharing earns no points.
weekShare.note.description: One line under the title of the "Share your week" card. It says the viewer controls what is included, that nothing is published on their behalf, and that sharing awards no points.

weekShare.preview.description: Label above the exact text that will be shared from the "Share your week" card.

weekShare.intro.description: The opening line of the text a viewer shares from their profile, above one line for each figure they chose. {{facts}} is those lines, one per figure, such as "3h 40m time in apps", each followed by the address where that week can be seen, already separated by line breaks.

weekShare.itemWithUrl.description: One line of the text a viewer shares from their profile: one figure from their week followed by the address where that week can be seen, which is the viewer's public profile page or, when that page is not public, Homeroom's own address. {{fact}} is the figure, such as "3h 40m time in apps"; {{url}} is the address.

weekShare.item.time.description: One switchable figure on the "Share your week" card: a length of time, such as "3h 40m", followed by what it measures. {{time}} is already written in this language's short form.

weekShare.item.apps_one.description: One switchable figure on the "Share your week" card: the number 1, followed by what it counts (apps opened in the last seven days).

weekShare.item.apps_other.description: One switchable figure on the "Share your week" card: a number followed by what it counts (apps opened in the last seven days).

weekShare.item.merged_one.description: One switchable figure on the "Share your week" card: the number 1, followed by what it counts (the viewer's changes that went live in the last seven days).

weekShare.item.merged_other.description: One switchable figure on the "Share your week" card: a number followed by what it counts (the viewer's changes that went live in the last seven days).

weekShare.item.built.description: One switchable figure on the "Share your week" card, and the line it becomes in the shared text: the names of the apps the viewer's changes went live in, such as "Built in: Homeroom, Notes". {{apps}} is a comma-separated list of app names, each followed by its own address in the shared text.

weekShare.appWithUrl.description: One app inside the line of shared text that names the apps the viewer's changes went live in: the app's own name followed by its own address, such as "Notes https://app.onhomeroom.com/#app/notes", so a reader can tell which link belongs to which app. {{name}} is the app's name; {{url}} is its address.

weekShare.item.challenges_one.description: One switchable figure on the "Share your week" card: the number 1, followed by what it counts (challenges the viewer completed in the last seven days).

weekShare.item.challenges_other.description: One switchable figure on the "Share your week" card: a number followed by what it counts (challenges the viewer completed in the last seven days).

weekShare.share.description: The primary button on the "Share your week" card. It opens the device's own share menu with the chosen figures.

weekShare.copy.description: Button beside Share on the "Share your week" card. It copies the chosen figures to the clipboard.

weekShare.copied.description: Confirmation shown on the "Share your week" card after its Copy button put the text on the clipboard.

weekShare.copyFailed.description: Shown on the "Share your week" card when the text could not be put on the clipboard.

weekShare.close.description: Accessible name of the × button that closes the "Share your week" card. It is not shown on screen.

stats.live.description: Label under a number on the viewer's profile: how many of their changes were approved and are running. Lower case; an adjective.

stats.kudos.description: Label under a number on the viewer's profile: how many kudos (thank-yous from other members) they have received. Lower case.

stats.challenges.description: Label under a number on the viewer's profile: how many challenges they have completed this season. Lower case.

screen.loading.description: Accessible name of the grey placeholder shown while the viewer's profile is being fetched.

signedOut.text.text: Sign in to see your profile.
signedOut.text.description: Shown on the profile screen to a person who is not signed in.

signedOut.signIn.description: Button on the profile screen for a person who is not signed in: goes to the sign-in screen.

screen.loadFailed.text: Could not load your profile. Check your connection and try again.
screen.loadFailed.description: Shown on the profile screen when the viewer's own profile could not be fetched.

public.unavailable.description: Shown in place of another person's public profile when it does not exist or is not published.

public.report.description: Link under another person's public profile: opens the form for reporting that person to the moderators. "Report" is a verb.

work.heading.description: Heading over the first list of rows on the viewer's own profile: their changes, requests, feedback and votes.

work.changes.title.description: Row on the viewer's own profile, and the title of the screen it opens: the changes to projects they started. "Changes" is a noun.

work.changes.hint.description: Small line under "Your changes" on the viewer's profile when there are no counts to show.

work.requests.title.description: Row on the viewer's own profile, and the title of the screen it opens: the improvements they asked for on projects. "Requests" is a noun.

work.requests.hint.text: What you asked for, and where it stands
work.requests.hint.description: Small line under "Your requests" on the viewer's profile when there are no counts to show.

work.requests.counting.description: Read by screen readers only, under "Your requests" on the viewer's profile, while the counts of their open and done requests are still loading; on screen a grey placeholder bar stands in for the line.

work.feedback.title.description: Row on the viewer's own profile that opens the Your feedback sheet: the history of the feedback they sent and whether it counted.

work.feedback.hint.text: What you sent, and whether it counted
work.feedback.hint.description: Small line under "Your feedback" on the viewer's profile when the sent and counted tally could not be loaded.

work.votes.title.description: Row on the viewer's own profile, and the title of the screen it opens: the changes and decisions they voted on.

work.votes.hint.text: The changes and decisions you voted on
work.votes.hint.description: Small line under "Your votes" on the viewer's profile when there is no latest vote to show. "Changes" is a noun.

work.votes.latest.description: Small line under "Your votes" on the viewer's profile. {{title}} is the title of the change or decision they voted on most recently.

work.changes.live_one.description: Small line under "Your changes" on the viewer's profile. {{number}} is how many of their changes are running, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

work.changes.live_other.description: Small line under "Your changes" on the viewer's profile. {{number}} is how many of their changes are running, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

work.changes.inProgress_one.description: Small line under "Your changes" on the viewer's profile. {{number}} is how many of their changes are still being worked on or voted on, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

work.changes.inProgress_other.description: Small line under "Your changes" on the viewer's profile. {{number}} is how many of their changes are still being worked on or voted on, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

work.requests.open_one.description: Small line under "Your requests" on the viewer's profile. {{number}} is how many of their requests are not finished, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "Open" is an adjective.

work.requests.open_other.description: Small line under "Your requests" on the viewer's profile. {{number}} is how many of their requests are not finished, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. "Open" is an adjective.

work.requests.done_one.description: Small line under "Your requests" on the viewer's profile. {{number}} is how many of their requests are finished, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

work.requests.done_other.description: Small line under "Your requests" on the viewer's profile. {{number}} is how many of their requests are finished, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

rewards.heading.description: Heading over Challenges & standings and Kudos on the viewer's own profile.

account.heading.description: Heading over Friends and App slots on the viewer's own profile.

more.appSlots.title.description: Row on the viewer's own profile: says how many app slots are free and opens the App allowance card, where more can be requested. A "slot" is room for one app.

more.appSlots.hint.text: How many apps you can create
more.appSlots.hint.description: Small line under "App slots" on the viewer's profile when the numbers are not known yet.

more.challenges.title.description: Row on the viewer's own profile: opens the Leaderboard screen with the season's challenges and rankings.

more.challenges.hint.description: Small line under "Challenges & standings" on the viewer's profile when there is nothing more specific to show.

more.challenges.rank.description: One fact on the small line under "Challenges & standings" on the viewer's profile, beside the season's name: the viewer's position in the season's ranking, {{rank}}. It is a whole fact of its own: the line's facts are joined with a middle dot by profile:line.factPair, never built into a sentence. Lower case in English because it follows the dot.

more.challenges.done_one.description: One fact on the small line under "Challenges & standings" on the viewer's profile, beside the season's name: {{done}} is how many of the season's challenges they completed and {{count}} how many there are. It is a whole fact of its own: the line's facts are joined with a middle dot by profile:line.factPair, never built into a sentence.

more.challenges.done_other.description: One fact on the small line under "Challenges & standings" on the viewer's profile, beside the season's name: {{done}} is how many of the season's challenges they completed and {{count}} how many there are. It is a whole fact of its own: the line's facts are joined with a middle dot by profile:line.factPair, never built into a sentence.

more.kudos.title.description: Row on the viewer's own profile: opens the Kudos leaderboard. "Kudos" is the feature's name: thank-yous members give for changes.

more.kudos.hint.description: Small line under "Kudos" on the viewer's profile. "Changes" is a noun.

more.kudos.received_one.description: Summary of the kudos the viewer has been given, for the "Kudos" row of their profile. {{number}} is how many, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

more.kudos.received_other.description: Summary of the kudos the viewer has been given, for the "Kudos" row of their profile. {{number}} is how many, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

more.friends.title.description: Row on the viewer's own profile: opens their list of friends.

more.friends.hint.text: Only you can see your friends
more.friends.hint.description: Small line under "Friends" on the viewer's profile when no friend request is waiting.

more.friends.waiting_one.description: Small line under "Friends" on the viewer's profile. {{number}} is how many friend requests wait for their answer, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

more.friends.waiting_other.description: Small line under "Friends" on the viewer's profile. {{number}} is how many friend requests wait for their answer, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

more.settings.title.description: Row on the viewer's own profile: opens the Settings screen.

more.settings.hint.description: Small line under "Settings" on the viewer's profile: what is in there. "Keys" are API keys.

more.settings.hintWallet.description: Small line under "Settings" on the viewer's profile, for a person who has a wallet: what is in there. "Keys" are API keys.

admin.heading.description: Small heading on the viewer's own profile over the row that opens the administration console, shown only to platform administrators. Short for administration.

admin.console.title.description: Row on the viewer's own profile, shown only to platform administrators: opens the administration and moderation console.

admin.console.hint.description: Small line under "Admin & moderation" on an administrator's own profile: what the console holds.

settings.heading.description: Heading over the Settings card at the foot of the viewer's own profile: the rows that lead to their profile, notification and account settings.

settings.profile.title.description: Row in the Settings card on the viewer's own profile: opens the Edit profile sheet. The same name the Settings page uses for its Profile part.

settings.profile.hint.description: Small line under "Profile" in the Settings card on the viewer's own profile.

settings.notifications.title.description: Row in the Settings card on the viewer's own profile: opens Settings' Notifications page. The same name that page uses.

settings.notifications.hint.text: What you are told about, here and in each app
settings.notifications.hint.description: Small line under "Notifications" in the Settings card on the viewer's own profile: the account-wide defaults and the per-app choices live on the page it opens.

date.today.description: A date said relative to now, placed inside a longer line such as "sent today" or after an app's name. Lower case.

date.yesterday.description: A date said relative to now, placed inside a longer line such as "sent yesterday" or after an app's name. Lower case.

date.daysAgo_one.description: A date said relative to now, placed inside a longer line such as "sent 3 days ago" or after an app's name. {{count}} is a number of days from 2 to 13.

date.daysAgo_other.description: A date said relative to now, placed inside a longer line such as "sent 3 days ago" or after an app's name. {{count}} is a number of days from 2 to 13.

feedback.title.description: Title of the sheet listing the feedback the viewer has sent.

feedback.close.description: Accessible name of the × button on the "Your feedback" sheet: closes the sheet. "Close" is a verb.

feedback.legend.text: Received: it was filed as a request. Counted: it earned points in a feedback challenge. Feedback on a project you made, or on one only you are in, is received but not counted, except once in your First challenges.
feedback.legend.description: Explanation at the top of the "Your feedback" sheet of its two status labels, "Received" and "Counted". Use the same words as those labels. "First challenges" is the heading of the newcomer's first group on the Challenges tab.

feedback.loadFailed.text: Your feedback could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
feedback.loadFailed.description: Shown in the "Your feedback" sheet when the list could not be fetched.

feedback.empty.text: Nothing sent yet. Feedback you send shows up here, with its status.
feedback.empty.description: Shown in the "Your feedback" sheet when the viewer has never sent feedback.

feedback.truncated.text: Showing the 50 you sent most recently.
feedback.truncated.description: Note under the list in the "Your feedback" sheet when the viewer has sent more than the 50 shown.

feedback.status.received.description: Status label on a row of the "Your feedback" sheet: the feedback was filed as a request.

feedback.status.counted.description: Status label on a row of the "Your feedback" sheet: the feedback earned points in the feedback challenge.

feedback.status.countedPoints_one.description: Status label on a row of the "Your feedback" sheet: the feedback earned points in the feedback challenge. {{points}} is how many, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural; "pts" abbreviates points.

feedback.status.countedPoints_other.description: Status label on a row of the "Your feedback" sheet: the feedback earned points in the feedback challenge. {{points}} is how many, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural; "pts" abbreviates points.

feedback.fallbackTitle.description: Stands in for the title of a piece of feedback in the "Your feedback" sheet when it has none.

feedback.anApp.description: Stands in for the app's name on a row of the "Your feedback" sheet when it is not known.

feedback.request.description: On a row of the "Your feedback" sheet, after the app's name: the request the feedback was filed as. {{number}} is its number. "Request" is a noun; lower case.

feedback.sent.description: On a row of the "Your feedback" sheet: when the feedback was sent. {{when}} is "today", "yesterday", "3 days ago" or a date such as "Mar 4". Lower case.

feedback.summary.none.description: Summary line of the feedback the viewer has sent, when there is none.

feedback.summary.sent_one.description: Summary line at the top of the "Your feedback" sheet. {{number}} is how many pieces of feedback the viewer has sent, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

feedback.summary.sent_other.description: Summary line at the top of the "Your feedback" sheet. {{number}} is how many pieces of feedback the viewer has sent, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

feedback.summary.sentCounted_one.description: Summary line at the top of the "Your feedback" sheet. {{number}} is how many pieces of feedback the viewer has sent, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. {{counted}} is how many of them earned points, also formatted.

feedback.summary.sentCounted_other.description: Summary line at the top of the "Your feedback" sheet. {{number}} is how many pieces of feedback the viewer has sent, already formatted ("1,500"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. {{counted}} is how many of them earned points, also formatted.

friends.title.description: Title of the sheet listing the viewer's friends, and the heading over the same list where it is shown on a page.

friends.close.description: Accessible name of the × button on the Friends sheet: closes the sheet. "Close" is a verb.

friends.label.description: Accessible name of the viewer's list of friends.

friends.accept.description: Button beside a friend request in the viewer's list of friends: accepts it.

friends.decline.description: Button beside a friend request in the viewer's list of friends: turns it down.

friends.cancelRequest.description: Button beside a friend request the viewer sent and that has not been answered: takes the request back.

friends.sentHeading.description: Heading over the friend requests the viewer sent that have not been answered.

friends.empty.text: No friends yet. Find someone by username above.
friends.empty.description: Shown in the viewer's list of friends when it is empty. "Above" is the search box over the list.

friends.loadFailed.text: Your friends could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
friends.loadFailed.description: Shown in the viewer's list of friends when it could not be fetched.

friends.privacy.text: Only you can see your friends. Nobody else sees this list or how long it is.
friends.privacy.description: Note at the foot of the viewer's list of friends.

friends.asked.description: Under the name of a person who sent the viewer a friend request. {{when}} is "today", "yesterday", "3 days ago" or a date such as "Mar 4".

friends.askedUndated.description: Under the name of a person who sent the viewer a friend request, when the date is not known.

friends.since.description: Under a friend's name in the viewer's list of friends. {{date}} is a month and year, such as "March 2026".

friends.sinceUndated.description: Under a friend's name in the viewer's list of friends, when the date they became friends is not known.

friends.requested.description: Under the name of a person the viewer sent a friend request to. {{when}} is "today", "yesterday", "3 days ago" or a date such as "Mar 4". A past participle: the friendship was requested.

friends.requestedUndated.description: Under the name of a person the viewer sent a friend request to, when the date is not known. A past participle: the friendship was requested.

message.button.description: Button on another person's profile: starts a private conversation with them. A verb.

message.buttonLabel.description: Accessible name of the Message button on another person's profile. "Message" is a verb. Keep the @ before the username.

message.nobody.text: There is nobody here to message.
message.nobody.description: Error shown when the Message button on a profile has no person to write to. "Message" is a verb.

message.unreachable.text: Couldn’t reach Messages. Check your connection and try again.
message.unreachable.description: Error shown when starting a conversation from a profile failed because the server could not be reached. "Messages" is the name of the Messages screen.

message.cannot.description: Error shown when the viewer may not start a conversation with this person. "Message" is a verb. Keep the @ before the username.

message.cannotNow.description: Error shown when a conversation with this person cannot be started at the moment. "Message" is a verb. Keep the @ before the username.

message.startFailed.text: Couldn’t start this conversation. Try again.
message.startFailed.description: Error shown when starting a conversation from a profile failed for an unknown reason.

edit.title.description: Title of the sheet where the viewer changes their photo, name and bio.

edit.saveFailed.description: Error shown in the Edit profile sheet when saving failed and the server gave no reason.

edit.saved.description: Brief message shown after the Edit profile sheet saved the viewer's changes.

edit.photo.group.description: Heading of the photo section of the Edit profile sheet.

edit.photo.label.description: Label beside the current photo in the Edit profile sheet.

edit.photo.note.text: PNG, JPEG or WebP. You choose the part that shows before it is used.
edit.photo.note.description: Note under "Profile photo" in the Edit profile sheet: the accepted image formats. Keep the format names.

edit.photo.noteNew.text: New photo, not saved yet. Press Save to use it.
edit.photo.noteNew.description: Note under "Profile photo" in the Edit profile sheet after a new photo was chosen. "Save" is the button at the foot of the sheet.

edit.photo.noteRemoved.text: Your photo will be removed when you press Save.
edit.photo.noteRemoved.description: Note under "Profile photo" in the Edit profile sheet after "Remove photo" was pressed. "Save" is the button at the foot of the sheet.

edit.photo.change.description: Row in the Edit profile sheet: opens the file picker to choose a new profile photo. "Change" is a verb.

edit.photo.remove.description: Row in the Edit profile sheet: removes the profile photo once the sheet is saved.

edit.photo.unusable.text: That image could not be used. Try a PNG, JPEG or WebP.
edit.photo.unusable.description: Error under the photo section of the Edit profile sheet when the chosen file failed for an unknown reason. Keep the format names.

edit.photo.wrongType.text: Choose a PNG, JPEG or WebP image.
edit.photo.wrongType.description: Error under the photo section of the Edit profile sheet when the chosen file is not an accepted image format. Keep the format names.

edit.photo.unreadable.text: That image could not be read.
edit.photo.unreadable.description: Error under the photo section of the Edit profile sheet when the chosen file could not be decoded as an image.

edit.photo.unprocessable.text: That image could not be processed here.
edit.photo.unprocessable.description: Error under the photo section of the Edit profile sheet when this browser could not resize the chosen image.

edit.photo.removeFailed.description: Error shown in the Edit profile sheet when removing the profile photo failed and the server gave no reason.

edit.photo.uploadFailed.description: Error shown in the Edit profile sheet when uploading the new profile photo failed and the server gave no reason.

edit.name.group.description: Heading of the name section of the Edit profile sheet.

edit.name.label.description: Label of the field in the Edit profile sheet for the name other people see.

edit.name.note.text: The name other people see. Leave it empty to show your @handle.
edit.name.note.description: Note under the Display name field in the Edit profile sheet. "@handle" is the username with its @ sign.

edit.about.group.description: Heading of the section of the Edit profile sheet that holds the bio.

edit.about.bio.description: Label of the field in the Edit profile sheet for a few lines about oneself.

edit.public.group.description: Heading of the section of the Edit profile sheet about the profile page that people without an account can see.

edit.public.label.description: Label of the switch in the Edit profile sheet that publishes or unpublishes the viewer's public profile page.

edit.public.hidden.description: Under "Public profile" in the Edit profile sheet: moderators have taken the viewer's public page down.

edit.public.on.text: On: anyone with the link can view it, no account needed
edit.public.on.description: Under "Public profile" in the Edit profile sheet when the public page is published.

edit.public.off.text: Off: your profile has no public link
edit.public.off.description: Under "Public profile" in the Edit profile sheet when the public page is not published.

edit.public.open.description: Row in the Edit profile sheet: goes to the viewer's published public profile page. "Open" is a verb.

edit.public.copy.description: Row in the Edit profile sheet: copies the address of the viewer's public profile page to the clipboard.

edit.public.whatsOnIt.description: Row in the Edit profile sheet that unfolds a preview of the viewer's public profile page. "It" is the public page.

edit.public.moderationNote.text: You can keep editing or turn it off, but the public page stays unavailable.
edit.public.moderationNote.description: Note in the Edit profile sheet when moderators have taken the viewer's public page down. "It" is the Public profile switch.

edit.public.previewNote.text: Only your username, display name, bio, Homeroom-hosted photo and verified social accounts. Never your email, wallet, roles, memberships, unverified handles or private activity. Changes take effect at once, and nobody can search for the page.
edit.public.previewNote.description: Explanation over the preview of the viewer's public profile page in the Edit profile sheet: what the page shows and what it never shows. Homeroom is the product's name. "Changes" is a noun.

edit.public.copied.description: Status line in the Edit profile sheet after the public page's address was copied to the clipboard.

edit.public.copyManually.description: Status line in the Edit profile sheet when the public page's address could not be copied automatically. {{url}} is the address to copy by hand.

edit.public.publishing.description: Status line in the Edit profile sheet while the public page is being published.

edit.public.unpublishing.description: Status line in the Edit profile sheet while the public page is being taken down.

edit.public.updateFailed.description: Status line in the Edit profile sheet when publishing or unpublishing the public page failed and the server gave no reason.

edit.public.published.description: Brief message shown after the viewer's public profile page was published.

edit.public.unpublished.description: Brief message shown after the viewer's public profile page was taken down.

edit.social.group.description: Heading of the section of the Edit profile sheet listing the viewer's verified GitHub and X accounts.

edit.social.verified.description: Small green label beside a social account in the Edit profile sheet: the viewer proved the account is theirs.

edit.social.notShown.description: Beside GitHub or X in the Edit profile sheet when no verified account of that kind is shown on the profile.

edit.social.manage.description: Row in the Edit profile sheet: goes to the Settings section where social accounts are linked. "Change" is a verb.

edit.social.note.text: Provider verification and public visibility are managed separately in Settings.
edit.social.note.description: Note under the social accounts in the Edit profile sheet. "Provider" is GitHub or X.

edit.username.group.description: Heading of the username section of the Edit profile sheet.

edit.username.label.description: Label of the read-only field in the Edit profile sheet that shows the viewer's username.

edit.username.note.text: Your @handle is your sign-in name and your public page address. To change it, go to <0>Settings → Username</0>. To change only how your name appears, set a display name above.
edit.username.note.description: Note under the username in the Edit profile sheet. The numbered tag is a link to the Username section of Settings; "Settings → Username" is the path to it. "@handle" is the username with its @ sign.

edit.email.group.description: Heading of the email section of the Edit profile sheet.

edit.email.link.description: Row in the Edit profile sheet: goes to the Settings section for the account's email address and account recovery.

edit.email.note.text: Add or verify a private email address in Settings.
edit.email.note.description: Note under "Email & recovery" in the Edit profile sheet.

social.github.description: Link chip on a profile: the person's verified GitHub account. {{handle}} is their GitHub username.

social.x.description: Link chip on a profile: the person's verified X account. X is the social network's name. {{handle}} is their username there; keep the @ before it.

report.received.description: Status shown after the viewer's report about a person was sent to the moderators. "Report" is a noun.

report.failed.text: Could not send the report. Try again.
report.failed.description: Status shown when the viewer's report about a person could not be sent. "Report" is a noun.

crop.title.description: Title of the dialog where the viewer chooses which part of a new profile photo shows. "Position" is a verb.

crop.help.text: Drag to choose the part of your photo that shows in the circle. Nothing is saved until you press Save.
crop.help.description: Explanation in the photo-positioning dialog. "Save" is the button on the Edit profile sheet behind it.

crop.role.description: What a screen reader calls the draggable photo area in the photo-positioning dialog, in place of a generic role name. Lower case.

crop.stageLabel.text: Photo position. Drag to move the photo, or use the arrow keys. Plus and minus zoom.
crop.stageLabel.description: Accessible name of the draggable photo area in the photo-positioning dialog, with its keyboard instructions. "Plus" and "minus" are the + and − keys.

crop.zoom.description: Accessible name of the slider in the photo-positioning dialog that enlarges the photo.

crop.zoomValue.description: What a screen reader reads as the value of the zoom slider in the photo-positioning dialog. {{percent}} is a whole number from 100 to 400.

crop.preparing.description: Shown on the confirm button of the photo-positioning dialog while the photo is being cropped and resized.

crop.use.description: Button in the photo-positioning dialog: accepts the chosen part of the photo.

staking.title.description: Row in the wallet sheet, and the title and accessible name of the sheet it opens: the wallet's staking on the Usernode network.

staking.close.description: Accessible name of the × button on the Staking sheet: closes the sheet. "Close" is a verb.

staking.status.delegated.description: At the right of the Staking row: the wallet's stake is delegated to somebody else's validator.

staking.status.active.description: At the right of the Staking row: the wallet is staking by itself.

staking.status.checking.description: At the right of the Staking row while the wallet's staking state is being looked up.

staking.activeDot.description: At the top of the Staking sheet: the wallet is staking by itself. Keep the dot.

staking.manageInApp.text: Open the Homeroom app to manage delegation.
staking.manageInApp.description: Brief message shown when the delegate button is pressed in a staging preview of the Staking sheet. "Open" is a verb; Homeroom is the product's name.

staking.opening.description: Shown on the Delegate or Undelegate button of the Staking sheet while the wallet app is being opened.

staking.undelegate.description: Button on the Staking sheet: takes the wallet's stake back from the validator it was delegated to.

staking.delegate.description: Button on the Staking sheet: hands the wallet's stake to a validator. A verb.

staking.unavailable.text: Staking status is not available yet.
staking.unavailable.description: Shown in the Staking sheet when the wallet's staking state could not be determined.

staking.rechecking.description: Shown on the Retry button of the Staking sheet while the staking state is being looked up again.

staking.epoch.loading.description: Shown in the Staking sheet while the record of an epoch is being fetched. An epoch is a fixed period of the network's time.

staking.epoch.title.description: Heading of a card in the Staking sheet. {{epoch}} is the number of the epoch, a fixed period of the network's time.

staking.epoch.current.description: Small label on an epoch's card in the Staking sheet: this is the epoch now running. An adjective.

staking.epoch.completed.description: Small label on an epoch's card in the Staking sheet: this epoch has ended and its record is final.

staking.epoch.wonSlots.description: Label over a number on an epoch's card in the Staking sheet: how many block-producing slots the wallet won in that epoch.

staking.epoch.upcoming.description: Label under a number on an epoch's card in the Staking sheet: won slots whose time has not come yet.

staking.epoch.produced.description: Label under a number on an epoch's card in the Staking sheet: won slots in which the wallet produced a block.

staking.epoch.missed.description: Label under a number on an epoch's card in the Staking sheet: won slots in which the wallet failed to produce a block.

staking.epoch.unobserved.text: Some slots have no confirmed observation.
staking.epoch.unobserved.description: Note on an epoch's card in the Staking sheet: for some won slots it is not known whether a block was produced.

staking.epoch.collecting.text: Epoch data is still being collected.
staking.epoch.collecting.description: Shown on an epoch's card in the Staking sheet when its record exists but has no counts yet.

staking.epoch.history.description: Accessible name of the row of epoch cards in the Staking sheet that is swiped sideways.

staking.epoch.previous.description: Accessible name of the ‹ button under the epoch cards in the Staking sheet: shows the epoch before.

staking.epoch.next.description: Accessible name of the › button under the epoch cards in the Staking sheet: shows the epoch after.

staking.epoch.swipe.description: Hint between the two arrow buttons under the epoch cards in the Staking sheet.

staking.error.preview.description: Error shown in a staging preview of the Staking sheet when its sample data could not be fetched.

staking.error.epochData.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when an epoch's record could not be fetched and no reason is known.

staking.error.changed.text: The wallet or network changed. Retry to refresh epoch data.
staking.error.changed.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the fetched record belongs to a different wallet or network than expected. "Retry" is the button under it.

staking.error.network.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the blockchain network the wallet is on is not known.

staking.error.currentEpoch.text: Could not load the current epoch.
staking.error.currentEpoch.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the record of the epoch now running could not be fetched.

staking.error.misconfigured.text: The epoch data service is not configured correctly.
staking.error.misconfigured.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the address of the service that supplies epoch records is invalid.

staking.error.http.text: Epoch data service returned HTTP {{status}}. Please retry.
staking.error.http.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the service that supplies epoch records answered with an error. {{status}} is the numeric HTTP status code; keep "HTTP".

staking.error.emptyResponse.text: Epoch data service returned an empty response.
staking.error.emptyResponse.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the service that supplies epoch records answered with nothing.

staking.error.tooLarge.text: Epoch data response is too large.
staking.error.tooLarge.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the service that supplies epoch records sent more data than is accepted.

staking.error.invalidResponse.text: Epoch data service returned an invalid response.
staking.error.invalidResponse.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the answer of the service that supplies epoch records could not be read.

staking.error.timeout.text: Epoch data request timed out. Please retry.
staking.error.timeout.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the service that supplies epoch records took too long to answer.

staking.error.unreachable.text: Could not reach the epoch data service. Please retry.
staking.error.unreachable.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the service that supplies epoch records could not be contacted.

staking.error.wallet.text: A valid wallet address is required.
staking.error.wallet.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the wallet's address is missing or malformed.

staking.error.epoch.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the requested epoch number is malformed.

staking.error.notYet.text: Epoch data is not available yet.
staking.error.notYet.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the service has no usable record for the epoch yet.

staking.error.notStarted.text: That epoch has not started yet.
staking.error.notStarted.description: Error shown in the Staking sheet when the requested epoch is in the future.

breakdown.event.description: Stands in for an event's name in the list of where a person's points came from, when the event has no name. An event is a season or competition.

breakdown.bonus.description: Row in the list of where a person's points came from: points awarded by hand, outside any event.

feedback.edit.description: Action or time remaining beside a recent request in Your feedback. {{count}}, when present, is the number of minutes rounded up.

feedback.editLeft_one.text: You can edit it for {{count}} more minute.
feedback.editLeft_one.description: Action or time remaining beside a recent request in Your feedback. {{count}}, when present, is the number of minutes rounded up.

feedback.editLeft_other.text: You can edit it for {{count}} more minutes.
feedback.editLeft_other.description: Action or time remaining beside a recent request in Your feedback. {{count}}, when present, is the number of minutes rounded up.

votes.title.change.description: Stands in for the title of a change the viewer voted on, when it has none. {{number}} is the change's number. "Change" is a noun.

votes.title.aChange.description: Stands in for the title of a change the viewer voted on, when it has neither a title nor a number. "Change" is a noun.

votes.title.decision.description: Stands in for the title of a community decision the viewer voted on, when it has none.

frame.numbers.description: The You tab when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). Label of the card of figures in the side column (changes live, challenges done and the like).

frame.public.about.description: Someone's public profile when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). Small label over the card holding the person's bio.

frame.public.verified.description: Someone's public profile when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). Small label over the side column's rows of accounts the person has verified (GitHub, X).

frame.public.github.description: Someone's public profile when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). Row in the Verified group: the person's GitHub account, which opens it.

frame.public.x.description: Someone's public profile when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). Row in the Verified group: the person's X account, which opens it.

frame.tab.label.description: The You tab when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). Said to a screen reader for the row of tabs under the person's handle (Overview, Changes, Requests, Feedback, Votes, Friends).

frame.tab.overview.description: The You tab when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). The first tab: the page of the person's work, rewards, account and settings rows, with their figures and this week's chart.

frame.tab.feedback.description: The You tab when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). The tab that opens the list of feedback the person has sent, with each report's status.

frame.projects.description: The You tab when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). On the Changes, Requests and Votes tabs: small label over the list of the person's projects, where picking one narrows the list of finished work to it.

frame.allProjects.description: The You tab when the interface is drawn in one of the frame's looks (an admin's preview in Settings > Experimental). On the Changes, Requests and Votes tabs: the first choice in the list of projects, which shows finished work from every project.

facts.pair.description: Joins two short independent facts on one line of a project's page, for example "3 involved · 2 underway" or "Voted yes · swipe up for the next". {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next fact. Only the separator between them is translated.

sentences.pair.description: Joins two complete sentences into one short paragraph on a project's page, for example a note under the list of categories. {{first}} is every sentence so far and {{second}} the next one, each already ending in its own full stop. Only the space between sentences is translated; leave it out if your language writes none.

page.title.needsYou.description: Title of a project's Needs you page: the feed of decisions waiting on this person, one per screen (changes to vote on, requests nobody has taken).

page.title.allItems.description: Title shown in the back bar of a project's All items page: the whole board of requests and proposals, opened from the Workshop tab.

page.title.plan.description: Title of the page that shows the plan for a project's first version, opened from its Hub.

page.title.bot.description: Title of the page under a project's Workshop that lists what holds each of Homeroom bot's slots on the project and what waits for one.

botSlots.door.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Link at the bottom of the Workshop's overview card that opens the page, and the first of its facts, which are shown joined by a middle dot: how many builds the bot has waiting or under way on the project. {{used}} is how many, {{cap}} how many it may have at once.

botSlots.doorVotes_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. One of the facts on the link to the page at the bottom of the Workshop's overview card, after "Homeroom bot: building 3 of 5" and a middle dot: how many of the bot's changes on the project are up for a vote. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.doorVotes_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. One of the facts on the link to the page at the bottom of the Workshop's overview card, after "Homeroom bot: building 3 of 5" and a middle dot: how many of the bot's changes on the project are up for a vote. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.doorWaiting_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. The last of the facts on the link to the page at the bottom of the Workshop's overview card, after a middle dot, when requests the bot is ready to build wait for a slot. {{count}} is how many requests wait.

botSlots.doorWaiting_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. The last of the facts on the link to the page at the bottom of the Workshop's overview card, after a middle dot, when requests the bot is ready to build wait for a slot. {{count}} is how many requests wait.

botSlots.slots.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the card listing what holds each slot.

botSlots.slots.building.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Figure in the Slots card: how many builds the bot has waiting or under way on the project, of how many it may have at once. {{used}} is how many, {{cap}} how many there may be.

botSlots.slots.votes_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Figure in the Slots card, under the builds: how many of the bot's changes on the project are up for a vote or being merged, of how many it may have waiting at once. {{count}} is how many, {{cap}} how many there may be.

botSlots.slots.votes_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Figure in the Slots card, under the builds: how many of the bot's changes on the project are up for a vote or being merged, of how many it may have waiting at once. {{count}} is how many, {{cap}} how many there may be.

botSlots.slots.frees.text: A build frees its slot when it is done. A change waiting for votes frees one when it merges or is withdrawn, or when its request closes.
botSlots.slots.frees.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note in the Slots card saying what frees each kind of slot: a build's, and a change's that waits for votes.

botSlots.slots.empty.text: No slots in use: a request found ready is built at once.
botSlots.slots.empty.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note in the Slots card when nothing holds a slot.

botSlots.waiting.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests that are ready but wait for a slot, in the order the bot will take them up.

botSlots.taken.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests the bot had found ready but that a person has taken since: the bot leaves them alone, so they do not wait for a slot.

botSlots.waitingOn.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests where the bot waits on a person: a question for them to answer, or a plan waiting for them to tap Build it.

botSlots.upNext.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests the bot will read next, in order: those waiting in its queue, then the project's older requests.

botSlots.upNext.note.text: Older requests are read one at a time, while a slot is free and nothing newer waits.
botSlots.upNext.note.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note under the Up next heading when it lists older requests: requests filed before the bot started building for everyone, which it now reads one by one when it has room.

botSlots.stopped.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests the bot tried to build that stopped: the build failed, or ended with no change to show.

botSlots.leftToPeople.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests the bot read and judged need a person rather than the bot: a decision to make, or nothing it can build.

botSlots.onHold.title.text: On hold until the week resets
botSlots.onHold.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the requests on hold because whoever pays for them has used up this week's building time.

botSlots.limits.title.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Heading over the card with the limits that hold work back.

botSlots.limits.week.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Label in the Limits card for the signed-in person's own building time this week.

botSlots.limits.weekUsed.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. How much of the signed-in person's building time this week is used. {{percent}} is a whole number from 0 to 100.

botSlots.limits.weekResets.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. When the signed-in person's building time resets. {{date}} is a short weekday, date and time.

botSlots.limits.weekUnlimited.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Shown in place of how much is used when the signed-in person's building time has no weekly limit.

botSlots.limits.buildsAtOnce_one.text: Up to {{count}} build at once on this project
botSlots.limits.buildsAtOnce_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. How many builds the bot runs on the project at the same time. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.limits.buildsAtOnce_other.text: Up to {{count}} builds at once on this project
botSlots.limits.buildsAtOnce_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. How many builds the bot runs on the project at the same time. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.limits.reading_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. How many requests wait for the bot to read them. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.limits.reading_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. How many requests wait for the bot to read them. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.off.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note at the top of the page when the bot is switched off everywhere.

botSlots.notHere.text: Homeroom bot doesn't build changes on this project.
botSlots.notHere.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note at the top of the page when the bot does not act on this project.

botSlots.paused.text: Homeroom bot is paused on this project.
botSlots.paused.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Note at the top of the page when the bot is paused on this project.

botSlots.loadFailed.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Shown when the page could not be read.

botSlots.untitled.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. A request's row when it has no title. {{number}} is its number.

botSlots.meta.asked.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under a request's title naming who asked for it. {{username}} is their username.

botSlots.meta.waiting.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of a request waiting for a slot: how long it has waited. {{span}} is a short span of time such as "3h 20m" or "2d 4h".

botSlots.meta.taken.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of a request a person has taken: how long ago they took it (claimed it, or started a change of their own for it). {{span}} is a short span of time such as "3h 20m" or "2d 4h".

botSlots.older.next.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of an older request in Up next: it is the next of the older requests the bot will read.

botSlots.older.ahead_one.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of an older request in Up next: how many older requests the bot will read before this one. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.older.ahead_other.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of an older request in Up next: how many older requests the bot will read before this one. {{count}} is that number.

botSlots.older.trialReady.text: found ready in its trial run
botSlots.older.trialReady.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of an older request in Up next, after its place: before the bot started building for everyone, it read this request in a trial and found it ready to build.

botSlots.older.trialQuestion.text: had a question in its trial run
botSlots.older.trialQuestion.description: The Homeroom bot's slots page, under a project's Workshop: what holds each of the project's bot slots (a change of the bot's up for a vote, or a build under way), the requests waiting for a slot, and the limits. Part of the line under the title of an older request in Up next, after its place: before the bot started building for everyone, it read this request in a trial and had a question about it.
