topic.request.stream.botPlanBuilding.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: Homeroom bot (an assistant that builds requests, speaking in the first person) posted its plan (the written description of the change) and is building it. {{version}} is the plan's version number; "v" abbreviates version. {{title}} is the plan's title. A "Read" link follows the line.

topic.request.stream.botPlanWaiting.text: Plan v{{version}}: {{title}}. Nothing is built yet. Waiting for @{{requester}} to say Build it.
topic.request.stream.botPlanWaiting.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: Homeroom bot posted its plan (the written description of the change) and builds nothing until the person who asked for it approves it. It says plainly that nothing has been built yet. {{version}} is the plan's version number; {{title}} is the plan's title; {{requester}} is that person's username, after an @. "Build it" is the name of the button they tap: keep it as the button reads in your language. A "Read" link follows the line.

topic.request.stream.botPlanWaitingUnnam.text: Plan v{{version}}: {{title}}. Nothing is built yet. Waiting for the person who asked for it to say Build it.
topic.request.stream.botPlanWaitingUnnam.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: Homeroom bot posted its plan (the written description of the change) and builds nothing until the person who asked for the request approves it; used when that person cannot be named. It says plainly that nothing has been built yet. {{version}} is the plan's version number; {{title}} is the plan's title. "Build it" is the name of the button they tap. A "Read" link follows the line.

topic.request.stream.botPlanReplaced.text: Plan v{{version}}: {{title}}. A newer plan replaced it.
topic.request.stream.botPlanReplaced.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: a plan Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) showed for the change, which stopped waiting because the bot planned the request again; the newer plan is further down. {{version}} is the plan's version number and {{title}} its title.

topic.request.stream.botPlanStopped.text: Plan v{{version}}: {{title}}. It stopped waiting for Build it.
topic.request.stream.botPlanStopped.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: a plan Homeroom bot (the platform's assistant) showed for the change, which no longer waits for the person who asked for it (nobody said Build it within a week, or the request was settled another way). {{version}} is the plan's version number and {{title}} its title. "Build it" is the name of the button that person taps: keep it as the button reads.

topic.request.stream.botPlan.description: One line among the replies on a request's page: Homeroom bot posted its plan (the written description of the change). {{version}} is the plan's version number; "v" abbreviates version. {{title}} is the plan's title. A "Read" link follows the line.

topic.request.stream.claimed.description: One line among the replies on a request's page, saying something that happened: a member took the request on. {{member}} is their username, drawn bold by <0></0>. "This" is the request.

topic.request.stream.claimedPlain.description: Plain-text form of the line saying a member took a request on, for places that show a request's events as text only. {{member}} is their username. "This" is the request.

topic.request.stream.read.description: Link-style button at the end of the line saying a plan was posted, among the replies on a request's page: opens that plan to read. A verb in the imperative, not the past tense.

topic.run.build.description: Row label in the opened Checks step of a change: the progress of building a preview of the app with the change. A noun.

topic.run.checks.label.description: Row label in the opened Checks step of a change: the progress of the automated checks the app declares, which open its screens and look for what should be there.

topic.run.checks.passed_one.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.checks.passed_other.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.checks.passedFailed_one.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.passedFailed_other.description: Result at the end of the App checks row when the run finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many checks passed, already formatted ("1,284"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.progress.description: Progress at the end of the App checks row while the run is going: {{ran}} checks have run out of {{expected}} declared. Both are already formatted; {{expected}} is a question mark when the total is not known.

topic.run.checks.progressFailed_one.description: Progress at the end of the App checks row while the run is going and some checks have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} declared (a question mark when not known), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.progressFailed_other.description: Progress at the end of the App checks row while the run is going and some checks have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} declared (a question mark when not known), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.checks.starting.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row when the checks are about to begin and none has run yet.

topic.run.checks.waitingForSlot.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row while the run is queued behind other runs. A slot is a free place to run.

topic.run.checks.afterBuild.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row while the preview is still being built: the checks will start once the build finishes.

topic.run.checks.didNotRun.description: Shown at the end of the App checks row when no run is going and no check ran, for example because the build failed.

topic.run.unit.label.description: Row label in the opened Checks step of a change: the progress of the project's own automated code tests.

topic.run.unit.cloning.description: Shown at the end of the Unit tests row while the project's code is being copied before the tests can start.

topic.run.unit.installing.description: Shown at the end of the Unit tests row while the code's dependencies are being installed before the tests can start.

topic.run.unit.passed_one.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.unit.passed_other.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with no failure. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"). {{count}} is the same number, for the plural.

topic.run.unit.reused_one.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when this run did not run the unit tests again but reused an earlier pass of the same commit. {{passed}} is how many tests passed then, already formatted ("13,214"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. {{when}} is how long ago that was (for example "12m ago"), {{run}} the start of that run's id (for example "832c9d27").

topic.run.unit.reused_other.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when this run did not run the unit tests again but reused an earlier pass of the same commit. {{passed}} is how many tests passed then, already formatted ("13,214"); {{count}} is the same number, for the plural. {{when}} is how long ago that was (for example "12m ago"), {{run}} the start of that run's id (for example "832c9d27").

topic.run.unit.passedFailed_one.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.unit.passedFailed_other.description: Result at the end of the Unit tests row when the tests finished with failures. {{passed}} is how many tests passed, already formatted ("13,214"), and {{failed}} how many failed. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.unit.progress.description: Progress at the end of the Unit tests row while the tests are running: {{ran}} tests have run out of {{expected}}. Both are already formatted; {{expected}} is an estimate from the last run, written with a leading ~ ("~13,214"), or a question mark when not known.

topic.run.unit.progressFailed_one.description: Progress at the end of the Unit tests row while the tests are running and some have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} (an estimate written with a leading ~, or a question mark), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.run.unit.progressFailed_other.description: Progress at the end of the Unit tests row while the tests are running and some have failed: {{ran}} have run out of {{expected}} (an estimate written with a leading ~, or a question mark), and {{failed}} failed so far. {{count}} is the number that failed, for the plural. Keep the dot.

topic.details.title.description: Heading, and accessible name, of the sheet that opens over a change's page with its technical side: the pull request, the steps to going live with their checks, and the full description.

topic.details.openOnGitHub.description: Link in the Details sheet of a change whose pull request is on GitHub, beside its pull-request number: opens that pull request on GitHub in a new tab. "Open" is a verb; GitHub is a product name.

topic.details.viewCode.description: Link in the Details sheet of a change whose code is on Homeroom's own git host rather than GitHub, beside its number: opens that code in a new tab. "View" is a verb.

topic.details.description.description: Sub-heading in the Details sheet of a change, over the full technical description of the change. A noun.

topic.details.shots.description: Sub-heading in the Details sheet of a change, over the technical record of its before-and-after screenshots: what was captured and what was left out. "Screenshot" names one of the pictures.

card.pill.goesLiveIn.description: Status bar on a proposal's card while its approval window counts down: the change will be merged and go live when the time runs out. {{time}} is the time left, already abbreviated, for example ~2h 5m.

card.pill.setAsideIn.description: Status bar on a proposal's card while its rejection window counts down: the proposal was voted down and will be closed without merging when the time runs out. {{time}} is the time left, already abbreviated, for example ~2h 5m.

card.tally.yes.description: Final vote count shown beside the Live status of a change that has shipped, when nobody voted against it. {{yes}} is how many yes votes counted and {{needed}} how many were needed to pass, for example "2/2 yes".

card.tally.yesNo.description: Final vote count shown beside the Live status of a change that has shipped, after the yes votes against the number needed, then the no votes. {{yes}} is how many yes votes counted, {{needed}} how many were needed to pass and {{no}} how many voted no, for example "3/3 yes · 1 no".

card.tally.passed.description: Final vote count shown beside the Live status of a change that has shipped with at least as many yes votes as it needed and nobody against it. {{yes}} is how many yes votes counted, for example "3 yes". The number needed is in the hover text.

card.tally.passedNo.description: Final vote count shown beside the Live status of a change that has shipped with at least as many yes votes as it needed, then the no votes. {{yes}} is how many yes votes counted and {{no}} how many voted no, for example "3 yes · 1 no". The number needed is in the hover text.

card.tally.title.text: {{yes}} yes and {{no}} no. It needed {{needed}} yes to pass.
card.tally.title.description: Hover text for the final vote count beside the Live status of a change that has shipped: the whole sentence the short count stands for. {{yes}} is how many yes votes counted, {{no}} how many voted no and {{needed}} how many yes votes were needed to pass.

card.countdown.daysHours.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown, a day or more, shown inside "Goes live in …". {{days}} and {{hours}} are numbers; d and h abbreviate days and hours. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.days.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown when it is a whole number of days. {{days}} is a number; d abbreviates days. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.hoursMinutes.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown, between an hour and a day. {{hours}} and {{minutes}} are numbers; h and m abbreviate hours and minutes. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.hours.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown when it is a whole number of hours. {{hours}} is a number; h abbreviates hours. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.countdown.minutes.description: Approximate time left on a proposal's countdown when under an hour. {{minutes}} is a number, at least 1; m abbreviates minutes. Keep the leading ~ (about).

card.pill.moreReasons_one.text: and {{count}} more reason, open for details
card.pill.moreReasons_one.description: The whole tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons and the first one has no text to show. {{count}} is how many further reasons there are; "open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Shown alone, in lower case.

card.pill.moreReasons_other.text: and {{count}} more reasons, open for details
card.pill.moreReasons_other.description: The whole tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons and the first one has no text to show. {{count}} is how many further reasons there are; "open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Shown alone, in lower case.

card.pill.reasonAndMore_one.text: {{reason}} · and {{count}} more reason, open for details
card.pill.reasonAndMore_one.description: Tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons: the first reason, then how many more there are. {{reason}} is the first reason, a sentence supplied already worded; {{count}} is how many further reasons there are. "Open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Keep the middle dot, or your language's separator, between the two parts.

card.pill.reasonAndMore_other.text: {{reason}} · and {{count}} more reasons, open for details
card.pill.reasonAndMore_other.description: Tooltip on a proposal card's status bar when the proposal is held back for several reasons: the first reason, then how many more there are. {{reason}} is the first reason, a sentence supplied already worded; {{count}} is how many further reasons there are. "Open" is a verb: open the card to read them. Keep the middle dot, or your language's separator, between the two parts.

card.pill.advisoryVotes_one.text: {{count}} advisory vote from non-approvers, so they don't count toward merging
card.pill.advisoryVotes_one.description: Tooltip on the small +N beside a proposal's vote tally. {{count}} is the number of votes cast by members who are not among the project's approvers; those votes are shown but do not count toward merging the change.

card.pill.advisoryVotes_other.text: {{count}} advisory votes from non-approvers, so they don't count toward merging
card.pill.advisoryVotes_other.description: Tooltip on the small +N beside a proposal's vote tally. {{count}} is the number of votes cast by members who are not among the project's approvers; those votes are shown but do not count toward merging the change.

card.pill.lockFallback.text: This change needs a Yes from another member. It won’t merge on a timer: it needs real Yes votes to reach the app’s normal threshold.
card.pill.lockFallback.description: Tooltip on the lock mark of a proposal card's status bar, used when the server gave no reason of its own. "Change" is the proposal (a noun); "Yes" is a Yes vote.

card.preview.open.description: Accessible name of the Preview button on a proposal's card: opens a running preview build of the proposed change. "Open" is a verb.

card.preview.label.description: Visible label of the button on a proposal's card that opens a running preview build of the proposed change. A noun: the preview.

card.preview.building.description: Label of the disabled Preview button on a proposal's card while the preview of the change is still being built. "Building" is the verb in progress.

card.preview.buildingName.description: Accessible name of the spinner shown in place of the Preview button on a compact card while the preview of the change is still being built.

card.preview.unavailable.description: Badge on a proposal's card, where the Preview button would be, when the preview of the change could not be built.

card.preview.unavailableName.description: Accessible name of the crossed-out eye icon on a compact card when the preview of the change could not be built.

card.badge.threadMessages.description: Tooltip on the speech-bubble count on a card: the number beside it counts the messages in that proposal's or request's discussion thread.

card.vote.sheet.approve.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for a change on a project that is just yours: approves the change so it goes live. "Approve" is a verb. Keep the check mark and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.dontApprove.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for a change on a project that is just yours: declines to approve the change. Keep the cross and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.yes.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for voting on a proposal: votes Yes. Keep the check mark and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.yesTally.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for voting on a proposal: votes Yes. {{tally}} is where the Yes side stands, for example 2/3 (votes so far of votes needed). Keep the check mark and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.stillYes.description: Row in the phone's action sheet when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: repeats their Yes on the new version. Keep the check mark and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.stillYesTally.description: Row in the phone's action sheet when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: repeats their Yes on the new version. {{tally}} is where the Yes side stands, for example 2/3. Keep the check mark and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.no.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for voting on a proposal: votes No. Keep the cross and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.noTally.description: Row in the phone's action sheet for voting on a proposal: votes No. {{tally}} is where the No side stands, for example 1/3. Keep the cross and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.notThisTime.description: Row in the phone's action sheet when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: votes No on the new version. Keep the cross and the two spaces first.

card.vote.sheet.notThisTimeTally.description: Row in the phone's action sheet when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: votes No on the new version. {{tally}} is where the No side stands, for example 1/3. Keep the cross and the two spaces first.

card.vote.face.approved.description: Label of the approval button on a card once the person has approved the change on a project that is just theirs. A settled state, not an action.

card.vote.face.notApproved.description: Label of the approval button on a card after the person declined to approve the change on a project that is just theirs. Pressing it lets them change that.

card.vote.face.approve.description: Label of the button on a card of a change on a project that is just the person's: opens the picker where they approve it or not. A verb.

card.vote.face.yes.description: Label of the vote button on a card after the person voted Yes on the proposal or request. It shows their current vote; a check mark is drawn before it.

card.vote.face.no.description: Label of the vote button on a card after the person voted No on the proposal or request. It shows their current vote; a cross is drawn before it.

card.vote.face.stillYes.description: Label of the vote button on a card when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal and has not voted on the new one. It asks whether their Yes still stands.

card.vote.face.vote.description: Label of the vote button on a proposal's or request's card before the person has voted: opens the picker with Yes and No. A verb.

card.vote.title.sending.description: Tooltip on a card's vote button while the person's vote is being sent to the server.

card.vote.title.approved.description: Tooltip on the approval button of a change the person has already approved on a project that is just theirs. "It" is the change.

card.vote.title.notApproved.text: You didn’t approve it. Press to change that.
card.vote.title.notApproved.description: Tooltip on the approval button after the person declined to approve a change on a project that is just theirs. "It" is the change.

card.vote.title.approve.text: Approve it, and it goes live.
card.vote.title.approve.description: Tooltip on the Approve button of a change on a project that is just the person's: their approval merges the change and puts it live. "It" is the change.

card.vote.title.votedYes.text: You voted Yes. Press to change your vote.
card.vote.title.votedYes.description: Tooltip on a card's vote button after the person voted Yes on the proposal or request.

card.vote.title.votedNo.text: You voted No. Press to change your vote.
card.vote.title.votedNo.description: Tooltip on a card's vote button after the person voted No on the proposal or request.

card.vote.title.priorYes.text: You said yes to an earlier version. One tap carries it onto this one.
card.vote.title.priorYes.description: Tooltip on a card's "Still yes?" button: the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal, and one press repeats that vote on the current version.

card.vote.title.cast.description: Tooltip on a card's Vote button before the person has voted. {{yesTally}} and {{noTally}} are where each side stands, for example 2/3 (votes so far of votes needed); either may be empty.

card.vote.sending.description: Label that replaces a card's vote button text while the person's vote is being sent.

card.vote.dialog.approval.description: Accessible name of the picker that opens from the Approve button on a card, on a project that is just the person's. A noun: the approval they give or withhold.

card.vote.dialog.vote.description: Accessible name of the picker that opens from a card's Vote button. A noun: the vote the person casts.

card.vote.picker.headApproval.description: Heading inside the picker over its two choices, Approve and Don't approve, on a project that is just the person's. A noun.

card.vote.picker.headVote.description: Heading inside the vote picker over its two choices, Yes and No. A noun.

card.vote.picker.uncounted.text: Test account: this vote won’t count.
card.vote.picker.uncounted.description: Note inside the vote picker shown to a test account voting on a project a real person made: the vote is recorded and shown but not counted.

card.vote.picker.advisory.text: Your vote is advisory: it’s recorded, but it doesn’t decide this change.
card.vote.picker.advisory.description: Note inside the vote picker shown to someone outside the people who decide on this project — not an approver where only approvers decide, or outside every group the project’s rules name. Their vote is recorded and shown, but does not affect the outcome.

card.vote.picker.approve.description: First of the two choices in the picker on a project that is just the person's: approve the change. A verb.

card.vote.picker.dontApprove.description: Second of the two choices in the picker on a project that is just the person's: do not approve the change.

card.vote.picker.yes.description: First of the two choices in the vote picker: a Yes vote on the proposal or request. The side's tally is drawn after it.

card.vote.picker.no.description: Second of the two choices in the vote picker: a No vote on the proposal or request. The side's tally is drawn after it.

card.vote.picker.stillYes.description: First of the two choices in the vote picker when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: keep that Yes on the new version.

card.vote.picker.notThisTime.description: Second of the two choices in the vote picker when the person voted Yes on an earlier version of the proposal: vote No on the new version.

card.vote.picker.noteLabel.text: Add a note, if you like.
card.vote.picker.noteLabel.description: Label over the optional text box in the picker when the Yes or Approve side is chosen on a project that is just the person's, so there is no group to address.

card.vote.picker.lineLabel.text: Add a line for the group, if you like.
card.vote.picker.lineLabel.description: Label over the optional text box in the vote picker when Yes is chosen: one line of comment that the community's other members will see with the vote.

card.vote.picker.noLabel.description: Accessible name of the list of reasons in the vote picker when No (or Don't approve) is chosen. An answer must be picked before the No can be sent.

card.vote.picker.why.notWorking.description: Answer someone can pick as the reason for a No vote in the vote picker: the change does not work.

card.vote.picker.why.approach.text: I do not agree with the approach
card.vote.picker.why.approach.description: Answer someone can pick as the reason for a No vote in the vote picker: they disagree with how the change was made.

card.vote.picker.why.notNeeded.description: Answer someone can pick as the reason for a No vote in the vote picker: the change is unnecessary.

card.vote.picker.why.other.description: Answer someone can pick as the reason for a No vote in the vote picker when none of the other answers fits; the optional box is where they say more.

card.vote.picker.why.detailLabel.description: Label over the optional text box in the vote picker when No (or Don't approve) is chosen, under the list of reasons.

card.vote.picker.withDetail.description: How a No vote's reason reads when the voter added a line: the picked answer, a colon, then the line. {{choice}} is the answer, for example "It does not work"; {{detail}} is the line they wrote.

card.vote.picker.yesPlaceholder.text: What do you like about it?
card.vote.picker.yesPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the vote picker's text box when Yes is chosen. "It" is the proposed change.

card.vote.picker.noPlaceholder.text: What would you want to change?
card.vote.picker.noPlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the vote picker's text box when No is chosen. "Change" is a verb: what the person would alter about the proposal.

card.vote.picker.sendYes.description: Button at the bottom of the vote picker when Yes is chosen: sends a Yes vote. "Vote" is a verb.

card.vote.picker.sendNo.description: Button at the bottom of the vote picker when No is chosen: sends a No vote. "Vote" is a verb.

card.vote.picker.sendApprove.description: Button at the bottom of the picker on a project that is just the person's, when Approve is chosen: sends the approval. A verb.

card.vote.picker.sendDontApprove.description: Button at the bottom of the picker on a project that is just the person's, when Don't approve is chosen: sends the refusal with its reason.

card.explore.unavailable.text: AI chat isn't configured on this deployment.
card.explore.unavailable.description: Tooltip on the disabled "Ask Homeroom bot" button on a card when this Homeroom installation has no AI model set up.

card.explore.label.description: Button on a proposal's card, after a sparkles emoji: opens the person's chat with Homeroom bot about this proposal, so they can ask about it or ask for changes to it. "Homeroom bot" is the name of Homeroom's assistant; keep it as it is.

card.menu.more.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the menu button at the end of a card's row of actions: opens the rest of that proposal's or request's actions.

card.title.proposalInput.description: Accessible name of the text field that edits a proposal's title in place. A proposal is a change put up for a vote.

card.title.requestInput.description: Accessible name of the text field that edits a request's title in place. A request is a filed issue asking for a change; "request" is a noun.

card.title.editProposal.description: Tooltip on the pencil beside a proposal's title, shown to its author: starts editing the title.

card.title.editRequest.text: Edit this request's title (you asked for it)
card.title.editRequest.description: Tooltip on the pencil beside a request's title, shown to the person who filed the request. "You asked for it" means they are its author; "request" is a noun.

card.title.edit.description: Accessible name of the pencil button beside a proposal's or request's title: starts editing the title. "Edit" is a verb.

card.illustration.altProposed.description: Alternative text of the image on a card that proposes a new featured illustration for the project: the illustration being proposed. The featured illustration is the picture on the project's Discover card.

card.illustration.altCurrent.description: Alternative text of the image on a card that proposes a new featured illustration for the project: the illustration in use now. The featured illustration is the picture on the project's Discover card.

card.illustration.removed.text: Removed, the app icon shows instead
card.illustration.removed.description: Shown in place of the proposed image on a card whose proposal is to take the project's featured illustration down: with none, the app's icon is shown on its Discover card.

card.illustration.none.text: No illustration, the app icon shows
card.illustration.none.description: Shown in place of an image on a featured-illustration proposal's card when that side (current or proposed) has no illustration: the app's icon is shown on its Discover card instead.

card.illustration.current.description: Small caption over the left thumbnail on a featured-illustration proposal's card: the illustration in use now.

card.illustration.proposed.description: Small caption over the right thumbnail on a featured-illustration proposal's card: the illustration the proposal would put in its place.

card.illustration.preview.description: Caption over the short silent clip a card-picture vote proposes, beside the Current and Proposed pictures.

card.illustration.previewLabel.description: Accessible name of the video player for the short silent clip a card-picture vote proposes.

card.claims.label.description: Label before the list of members who have claimed a request (said they are working on it), shown to admins on the request's page. A plural noun; keep the colon.

card.claims.release.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the × beside a member's name in a request's claim list: an admin removes that member's claim on the request. {{username}} is the member's username. "Release" is a verb.

kanban.sort.priority.description: Label of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while proposals are ordered by how much they need this person's vote. Names the current order.

kanban.sort.newest.description: Label of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while proposals are ordered newest first. Names the current order.

kanban.sort.namePriority.text: Sort Waiting for approval: Vote priority. Switch to Newest.
kanban.sort.namePriority.description: Accessible name of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while it is sorted by vote priority; pressing it switches to newest first. "Waiting for approval" is the column's name; "Sort" is a verb.

kanban.sort.nameNewest.text: Sort Waiting for approval: Newest. Switch to Vote priority.
kanban.sort.nameNewest.description: Accessible name of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while it is sorted newest first; pressing it switches to vote priority. "Waiting for approval" is the column's name; "Sort" is a verb.

kanban.sort.titlePriority.text: Unvoted first, then fewest qualifying votes still needed. Within each vote group, already-qualified proposals follow those still short. Newest breaks ties. Click to switch to Newest.
kanban.sort.titlePriority.description: Tooltip of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while it is sorted by vote priority: explains the order (proposals this person has not voted on first, then those closest to enough votes) and that a click switches to newest first.

kanban.sort.titleNewest.text: Most recently submitted for review first. Click to switch to Vote priority.
kanban.sort.titleNewest.description: Tooltip of the sort button over the board's "Waiting for approval" column while it is sorted newest first: explains the order and that a click switches to vote priority.

kanban.column.loading.description: Read by a screen reader while one column of a project's board is loading. {{column}} is the column's name, for example Requests or Done.

kanban.tabs.name.description: Accessible name of the row of steps over a project's board (Requests, Underway, Waiting for approval, Done, each with its count): the heads of the board's columns, and on a phone the tabs that switch between them. The board is a project's kanban of requests and proposals.

kanban.skeleton.requests.description: Name of the board's first column in its loading placeholder: filed requests (issues) nobody has started on. A plural noun.

kanban.skeleton.underway.description: Name of the board's second column in its loading placeholder: work somebody is building now.

kanban.skeleton.waiting.description: Name of the board's third column in its loading placeholder: proposals put up for a vote and not yet approved.

kanban.skeleton.done.description: Name of the board's last column in its loading placeholder: changes that were merged. Not a button.

kanban.skeleton.loadingBoard.description: Read by a screen reader while a project's board (its kanban of requests and proposals) is loading.

kanban.skeleton.loading.description: Read by a screen reader while a list of cards on a project's page is loading.

kanban.footer.showAll_one.description: Last line at the foot of the board's Done column, which hides older merged changes: pressing it shows every one. {{number}} is how many merged changes there are in all, already formatted with digit separators.

kanban.footer.showAll_other.description: Last line at the foot of the board's Done column, which hides older merged changes: pressing it shows every one. {{number}} is how many merged changes there are in all, already formatted with digit separators.

kanban.footer.loading.description: The "Show more" line at the foot of the board's Done column while the next page of merged changes is being fetched.

kanban.footer.loadMoreCount_one.description: Last line at the foot of the board's Done column: pressing it fetches and shows the next merged changes. {{number}} is how many more there are, already formatted with digit separators.

kanban.footer.loadMoreCount_other.description: Last line at the foot of the board's Done column: pressing it fetches and shows the next merged changes. {{number}} is how many more there are, already formatted with digit separators.

kanban.footer.loadMore.description: Last line at the foot of the board's Done column when the number left is unknown: pressing it fetches and shows the next merged changes.

kanban.footer.moreRequests.description: Link under the board's Requests column of a project whose code is on GitHub: opens the rest of the project's open requests (issues) on GitHub. Keep the arrow last.

kanban.footer.moreCompleted_one.description: Note under a board column: {{count}} further completed items are not listed. Keep the leading +.

kanban.footer.moreCompleted_other.description: Note under a board column: {{count}} further completed items are not listed. Keep the leading +.

kanban.archived.show_one.description: Toggle at the end of a column of the person's coding sessions: unfolds the list of sessions they archived. {{count}} is how many are archived.

kanban.archived.show_other.description: Toggle at the end of a column of the person's coding sessions: unfolds the list of sessions they archived. {{count}} is how many are archived.

kanban.archived.state.description: Second line of a row in the archived-sessions list: says the coding session is archived. A state, not a button.

kanban.archived.restoreTitle.description: Tooltip on the Unarchive button of an archived coding session: restoring it also reopens its pull request (PR) on GitHub.

kanban.archived.unarchive.description: Button on a row of the archived-sessions list: restores that coding session. A verb.

card.fold.fold.description: Accessible name of the mark at the top right of an open card: collapses the card back to its one-row form. "Fold" is a verb.

card.fold.new.description: Small lower-case marker after an item's title in a project's lists: the item arrived or changed since the person's last visit.

card.fold.placing.description: Small lower-case marker after an item's title on the Workshop tab while Homeroom is still sorting the item into one of the project's themes.

card.fold.placingTitle.description: Tooltip on the "placing…" marker after an item's title: Homeroom is still sorting the item into a theme.

card.fold.openCard.description: Link button on an unfolded card: goes to that proposal's or request's own page. "Open" is a verb.

feedThread.reply.placeholder.description: Placeholder of the reply box under an open card: the person writes a reply in that proposal's or request's discussion thread. A verb.

feedThread.reply.name.description: Accessible name of the reply box under an open card. The item is the proposal or request the card is about.

feedThread.reply.send.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the round arrow button beside the reply box under an open card: posts the reply.

feedThread.earlier_one.description: Line above the replies shown under an open card: {{count}} older replies in the thread are not shown here.

feedThread.earlier_other.description: Line above the replies shown under an open card: {{count}} older replies in the thread are not shown here.

feedThread.postFailed.text: That didn’t send. Try again, or open the item to reply there.
feedThread.postFailed.description: Error under an open card when posting a reply failed. "Open the item" means go to the proposal's or request's own page.

feedThread.unknownAuthor.description: Stands where an author's username is shown beside a reply in the short thread preview under a card, when the author is not known. Shown alone in the name's own element; lower case in English, like a username.

typeahead.mention.name.description: Accessible name of the list of people that opens when the person types @ in a reply box under a card: picking one inserts that member's @name.

typeahead.ref.name.text: Insert a pull request or issue reference
typeahead.ref.name.description: Accessible name of the list that opens when the person types # or PR# in a reply box under a card: picking a row inserts that pull request's or issue's number.

menu.button.remix.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the round ⋯ button on a project's page, for a visitor who can only read the project. Its menu then holds one action, Make your own, which makes the person their own version of the project.

menu.button.manage.text: Suggest an improvement, import a PR or manage this app
menu.button.manage.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the round ⋯ button on a project's page, for someone who can take part. It opens the project's menu of actions and settings. PR is a GitHub pull request.

menu.visitorView.title.description: First row of a project hub's ⋯ menu, for a member of a public project: opens the project's page as somebody signed out sees it.

menu.visitorView.sub.text: The page before joining: the preview, the featured illustration and what's up for a vote
menu.visitorView.sub.description: Line under "See what visitors see" in a project hub's ⋯ menu: what that page shows. The featured illustration is the picture the group voted in for the project's card.

visitorView.title.description: Bar over a member's preview of their project's signed-out page, opened from "See what visitors see" in the hub's ⋯ menu. Also the preview's accessible name.

visitorView.sub.text: The project's page for somebody who isn't signed in
visitorView.sub.description: Second line of the bar over a member's preview of their project's signed-out page.

visitorView.back.description: Button on the bar over a member's preview of their project's signed-out page: closes it and returns to the project's hub.

visitorView.inert.text: Visitors are asked to sign in here
visitorView.inert.description: Toast when a member presses Join, Vote, Sign in or another button in the preview of their project's signed-out page: the button does nothing for them, and this says what a visitor would get.

visitorView.unavailable.text: This project has no page for visitors. Only public projects do.
visitorView.unavailable.description: Shown in a member's preview of their project's signed-out page when the project is not in the public directory.

menu.suggest.title.description: First, highlighted row of a project's ⋯ menu. Opens the form for describing a problem or an idea for this project, without building it.

menu.suggest.sub.text: Report a problem or idea without building it yourself
menu.suggest.sub.description: Second line of the 'Suggest an improvement' row in a project's ⋯ menu, explaining what the row is for.

menu.build.title.description: Row in a project's ⋯ menu: opens a new chat on the Homeroom bot tab, set to this project, where the person says what to build and picks who builds it (Homeroom bot, or their own Claude Code or ChatGPT). 'Build' is a verb; 'it' is the improvement they have in mind.

menu.build.sub.text: With a coding agent, then ask for approval
menu.build.sub.description: Second line of the 'Build it now' row in a project's ⋯ menu: the person works with an AI coding agent, then puts the result up for the community's approval.

menu.importPr.title.description: Row in a project's ⋯ menu, shown to people who may build the project: brings in a feature that already exists as a GitHub pull request (PR), so it becomes a proposal here.

menu.importPr.sub.text: Your computer · your own tools. You have already built it, so there is no chat for this one
menu.importPr.sub.description: Second line of the 'Import Feature from a PR' row in a project's ⋯ menu. It says the work was done on the person's own machine with their own tools, so no conversation with Homeroom bot is opened. Keep the middle dot between the first two phrases.

menu.settings.title.description: Row in a project's ⋯ menu that opens the group of the project's settings and its approval rules. It has a chevron beside it.

menu.settings.heading.description: Heading at the top of the settings panel inside a project's ⋯ menu, beside a back chevron. Pressing it returns to the menu's first list.

menu.settings.back.description: Accessible name of the heading button at the top of the settings panel in a project's ⋯ menu: returns from the settings rows to the menu's first list.

menu.leave.named.description: Row among a project's settings for a member who did not start it: the person stops being a member of this community. 'Leave' is a verb. {{project}} is the project's name.

menu.leave.plain.description: Row among a project's settings for a member who did not start it, when the project's name is not known: the person stops being a member of this community. A verb.

menu.pin.add.description: Row in a project's ⋯ menu on its hub, on a computer: keeps the project's community at the top of the desktop sidebar's Recents.

menu.pin.sub.text: Keep it at the top of your sidebar
menu.pin.sub.description: Second line under Pin to sidebar in the project's ⋯ menu, saying what pinning does.

menu.pin.remove.description: The same row once the community is pinned: lets it move with the rest of the desktop sidebar's Recents again. It stays one of the person's communities.

menu.homeApp.add.description: Row in a project's ⋯ menu on its hub: puts the project's app among Home's Pinned apps, where its tile opens the app. Pinning does not join.

menu.homeApp.sub.description: Second line under Pin app to Home in the project's ⋯ menu, saying what the pinned tile does.

menu.homeApp.remove.description: The same row once the app is pinned: takes the app's tile off Home's Pinned apps. Membership does not change.

menu.homeCommunity.add.description: Row in a project's ⋯ menu on its hub: puts the community in the Pinned group of the Communities page, where its tile opens this hub. Pinning does not join.

menu.homeCommunity.sub.description: Second line under Pin community in the project's ⋯ menu, saying what the pinned tile does.

menu.homeCommunity.remove.description: The same row once the community is pinned: takes its tile out of the Pinned group of the Communities page. Membership does not change.

menu.appSettings.title.description: Row among a project's settings, shown to those who manage it: opens the dialog for who can use and build the app, and for deleting it.

menu.appSettings.sub.text: Manage who can use and build this app
menu.appSettings.sub.description: Second line of the 'App settings' row in a project's settings. 'Build' is a verb, to work on the app's code.

menu.domain.title.description: Row among a project's settings, for the people who manage it: opens the dialog for giving the project a web address of its own, beside its Homeroom address.

menu.domain.sub.text: Use your own web address for this project
menu.domain.sub.description: Second line of the 'Custom domain' row in a project's settings.

menu.illustration.title.description: Row among a project's settings, shown to those who may edit it: opens the editor for the picture shown on the project's card on the Discover screen.

menu.illustration.sub.text: Preview and adjust the Discover card image
menu.illustration.sub.description: Second line of the 'Featured illustration' row in a project's settings. Discover is the name of the screen for finding apps and communities.

menu.approvals.title.description: Row among the settings of Homeroom's own project (the platform itself): opens the dialog that sets who approves proposals, changes put up for a vote, and how many approvals one needs.

menu.approvals.sub.text: Who approves proposals and how many approvals are needed
menu.approvals.sub.description: Second line of the 'Proposal approvals' row in the platform project's settings. A proposal is a change put up for a vote.

menu.members.title.description: Row among a project's settings: opens the dialog listing the project's collaborators and admins and the rule for approving proposals.

menu.members.sub.text: Manage collaborators, app admins and proposal approvals
menu.members.sub.description: Second line of the 'Members & approvals' row in a project's settings. Collaborators are people allowed to build the project; a proposal is a change put up for a vote.

menu.rename.title.description: Row among a project's settings: opens the dialog for proposing a new name for the app, the name people see.

menu.rename.sub.text: Renames are proposals, applied once voted in
menu.rename.sub.description: Second line of the 'App display name' row in a project's settings: a new name is itself a change put up for a vote, and takes effect only when the vote passes.

menu.secrets.appTitle.description: Row among a project's settings: opens the dialog for the app's secret values, such as API keys its server reads. A short status may follow this title.

menu.secrets.appSub.description: Second line of the 'App secrets' row in a project's settings.

menu.secrets.platformTitle.description: Row among the settings of Homeroom's own project (the platform itself), in place of 'App secrets': opens the dialog for the platform's environment variables. A short status may follow this title.

menu.secrets.platformSub.text: The platform's own env, applied on its next deploy
menu.secrets.platformSub.description: Second line of the 'Platform variables' row. 'env' is the developers' short word for environment variables; the values take effect the next time the platform is deployed.

menu.suggestBack.title.description: Row among a project's settings, shown to the owner of a version (a project made from another, the original): sends some of the version's own changes to the original, for its members to try and vote on. {{project}} is the original's name.

menu.suggestBack.sub.text: Pick which of your changes to send
menu.suggestBack.sub.description: Second line of the "Suggest to" row in a project's settings.

menu.updates.title.description: Row among a project's settings, on a version (a project made from another, the original): opens the sheet that says whether this version gets the original's changes to try and vote on, and changes that. {{project}} is the original's name.

menu.updates.on.description: Second line of the "Updates from" row while the version gets the original's changes to try and vote on.

menu.updates.off.description: Second line of the "Updates from" row while the version does not get the original's changes.

menu.remix.title.description: Row in a project's ⋯ menu: makes the person their own version of this project, a project of their own made from it, to change freely.

menu.remix.sub.description: Second line of the 'Make your own' row in a project's ⋯ menu.

updates.title.description: Title of the sheet opened from a version's "Updates from" row. {{project}} is the name of the project this version was made from, the original.

updates.follow.title.description: Label of the switch in the Updates sheet: whether this version gets the original's changes to try and vote on. {{project}} is the original's name.

updates.follow.sub.text: When {{project}} changes, you get the change to try and vote on. Nothing changes unless you say yes.
updates.follow.sub.description: Line under the "Get its updates" switch in the Updates sheet. {{project}} is the original's name.

updates.follow.vote.text: This is one of the project’s settings, so turning it on or off goes to a vote.
updates.follow.vote.description: Small note under the "Get its updates" switch in the Updates sheet: pressing the switch puts the change up for the members' vote rather than changing it at once.

updates.follow.proposed.text: Up for a vote now. <0>Open it</0>
updates.follow.proposed.description: Shown in the Updates sheet once pressing the switch has put the change up for a vote. The tagged words link to that change. "Open" is a verb.

updates.follow.failed.text: Could not put it up for a vote. Try again.
updates.follow.failed.description: Error in the Updates sheet when the change to the switch could not be put up for a vote and the server gave no reason.

updates.share.title.description: Label of the second switch in the Updates sheet, on a private version: whether the original can see the titles of the changes that go live in this version. {{project}} is the original's name.

updates.share.sub.text: {{project}} sees the titles of the changes that go live here. Never your data, or who’s in it.
updates.share.sub.description: Line under the "Share what we make" switch in the Updates sheet. {{project}} is the original's name.

updates.share.failed.text: Could not save that. Try again.
updates.share.failed.description: Error in the Updates sheet when the "Share what we make" switch could not be saved.

updates.load.failed.text: Could not load this. Close it and try again.
updates.load.failed.description: Error in the Updates sheet when where the version stands could not be read.

attr.assignee.removeHint.text: Click again to remove your pick
attr.assignee.removeHint.description: Tooltip on a person's row in the assignee picker of a request or proposal, shown on the person the viewer already picked: clicking the row again withdraws that pick.

attr.add.description: Button beside the text box at the bottom of the category or assignee picker of a request or proposal: adds what was typed as the viewer's pick.

attr.loadFailed.description: Shown inside the priority, category or assignee picker of a request or proposal when its list of options could not be fetched.

board.discussion.open.description: Tooltip of the 'General discussion' card above a project's board: the card opens the project's shared chat channel. 'Open' is a verb.

board.discussion.title.description: Title of the card above a project's board that leads to the project's shared chat channel. The last message said there is shown under it.

pause.resume.description: Button on the amber 'merges are paused' banner of a project, shown to an admin: lets approved proposals merge again although the main branch's tests are failing.

pause.resumeHint.text: Merge again while main’s tests fail. The pause returns if a later merge fails them too.
pause.resumeHint.description: Tooltip of the Resume merges button on a project's amber "merges are paused" banner, for an admin. "main" is the name of the main code branch and stays as it is; "tests" are its automated tests. "Merge" is a verb.

pause.confirming.plain.text: Main’s tests failed once. Re-running to confirm. Merges are paused meanwhile.
pause.confirming.plain.description: Amber banner at the top of a project's page after the automated tests of the main code branch failed once and are being run again. "main" is the branch's name and stays as it is. Keep it short: it is read on a phone.

pause.confirming.since.text: Main’s tests failed once since {{commit}}. Re-running to confirm. Merges are paused meanwhile.
pause.confirming.since.description: Amber banner at the top of a project's page after the automated tests of the main code branch failed once and are being run again. {{commit}} is the short code of the commit since which they fail. "main" stays as it is. Keep it short: it is read on a phone.

pause.confirming.test.text: Main’s tests failed once: {{test}}. Re-running to confirm. Merges are paused meanwhile.
pause.confirming.test.description: Amber banner at the top of a project's page after the automated tests of the main code branch failed once and are being run again. {{test}} is the name of the first failing test, as the test run printed it. "main" stays as it is. Keep it short.

pause.confirming.sinceTest.text: Main’s tests failed once since {{commit}}: {{test}}. Re-running to confirm. Merges are paused meanwhile.
pause.confirming.sinceTest.description: Amber banner at the top of a project's page after the automated tests of the main code branch failed once and are being run again. {{commit}} is the short code of the commit since which they fail; {{test}} the first failing test. "main" stays as it is. Keep it short.

pause.paused.plain.text: Merges are paused: main’s tests are failing. They resume once a fix lands or an admin resumes them.
pause.paused.plain.description: Amber banner at the top of a project's page while the automated tests of the main code branch fail, so approved proposals are not merged. "main" is the branch's name and stays as it is; "resumes" (verb) is what an admin does with the banner's button. Keep it short.

pause.paused.since.text: Merges are paused: main’s tests have failed since {{commit}}. They resume once a fix lands or an admin resumes them.
pause.paused.since.description: Amber banner at the top of a project's page while the automated tests of the main code branch fail, so approved proposals are not merged. {{commit}} is the short code of the commit since which they fail. "main" stays as it is. Keep it short.

pause.paused.test.text: Merges are paused: main’s tests are failing: {{test}}. They resume once a fix lands or an admin resumes them.
pause.paused.test.description: Amber banner at the top of a project's page while the automated tests of the main code branch fail, so approved proposals are not merged. {{test}} is the name of the first failing test, as the test run printed it. "main" stays as it is. Keep it short.

pause.paused.sinceTest.text: Merges are paused: main’s tests have failed since {{commit}}: {{test}}. They resume once a fix lands or an admin resumes them.
pause.paused.sinceTest.description: Amber banner at the top of a project's page while the automated tests of the main code branch fail, so approved proposals are not merged. {{commit}} is the short code of the commit since which they fail; {{test}} the first failing test. "main" stays as it is. Keep it short.

releaseStall.openRun.description: Link at the end of the amber 'merged but not released' banner on the platform project's page: opens, on GitHub, the run of the release workflow the banner is about. 'Open' is a verb; 'run' is a noun.

releaseStall.failed.prCommit.text: PR {{pr}} ({{commit}}) merged but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.prCommit.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change is not live because the automated release job failed. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number and {{commit}} the merged commit's short code. 'Run it' means run the release workflow; 'main' is the main branch's name and stays as it is.

releaseStall.failed.prCommitRunning.text: PR {{pr}} ({{commit}}) merged but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. The platform is still running {{running}}. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.prCommitRunning.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change is not live because the automated release job failed. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number, {{commit}} the merged commit's short code and {{running}} the short code of the build still being served. 'Run it' means run the release workflow; 'main' is the main branch's name and stays as it is.

releaseStall.failed.pr.text: PR {{pr}} merged but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.pr.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change is not live because the automated release job failed. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number. 'Run it' means run the release workflow; 'main' is the main branch's name and stays as it is.

releaseStall.failed.prRunning.text: PR {{pr}} merged but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. The platform is still running {{running}}. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.

releaseStall.failed.commit.text: Commit {{commit}} landed on main but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.commit.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a commit pushed straight to the main branch is not live because the automated release job failed. {{commit}} is the commit's short code, or the word for unknown in parentheses. 'Run it' means run the release workflow; 'main' is the branch's name and stays as it is.

releaseStall.failed.commitUnknown.text: Commit (unknown) landed on main but was not released: its release workflow did not complete. Run it on main to release the latest commit; a later merge would also carry this change.
releaseStall.failed.commitUnknown.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a commit pushed straight to the main branch is not live because the automated release job failed. Used when the commit is not known; "(unknown)" is written as the banner has always shown it.

releaseStall.failed.commitUnknownRunning.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a commit pushed straight to the main branch is not live because the automated release job failed. Used when the commit is not known; "(unknown)" is written as the banner has always shown it. {{running}} is the build still serving.

releaseStall.slow.prCommit.text: PR {{pr}} ({{commit}}) merged and its release workflow is still running, well past the usual couple of minutes.
releaseStall.slow.prCommit.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change is not live yet because the automated release job is taking far longer than normal. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number and {{commit}} the merged commit's short code.

releaseStall.notRolled.prCommit.text: PR {{pr}} ({{commit}}) merged and its release workflow succeeded, but the platform has not rolled onto it.
releaseStall.notRolled.prCommit.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change was built successfully, yet the servers have not switched to the new build. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number and {{commit}} the merged commit's short code.

releaseStall.notRolled.prCommitRunning.text: PR {{pr}} ({{commit}}) merged and its release workflow succeeded, but the platform has not rolled onto it. The platform is still running {{running}}.
releaseStall.notRolled.prCommitRunning.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change was built successfully, yet the servers have not switched to the new build. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number, {{commit}} the merged commit's short code and {{running}} the short code of the build still being served.

releaseStall.notRolled.pr.text: PR {{pr}} merged and its release workflow succeeded, but the platform has not rolled onto it.
releaseStall.notRolled.pr.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change was built successfully, yet the servers have not switched to the new build. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number.

releaseStall.notRolled.commit.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a commit pushed straight to the main branch was built successfully, yet the servers have not switched to the new build. {{commit}} is the commit's short code, or the word for unknown in parentheses. releaseStall.noRun.prCommit.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change is not live and no run of the automated release job was found for it. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number and {{commit}} the merged commit's short code. 'run' after 'workflow' is a noun.

releaseStall.noRun.prCommitRunning.text: PR {{pr}} ({{commit}}) merged but is not running yet, and no release workflow run could be found for it. The platform is still running {{running}}.
releaseStall.noRun.prCommitRunning.description: Amber banner on the platform project's page: a merged change is not live and no run of the automated release job was found for it. {{pr}} is the GitHub pull request's number, {{commit}} the merged commit's short code and {{running}} the short code of the build still being served.
