linkedAccounts.diagnostics.accepted.description: Result beside the "Run configuration check" button in Settings > Linked accounts, administrators only, when the check passed. {{provider}} is GitHub or X. "The {{provider}} app" is the developer app registered with that provider.

linkedAccounts.diagnostics.rejected.text: {{provider}} rejected the platform’s client ID or secret. the configured credential pair is wrong.
linkedAccounts.diagnostics.rejected.description: Result beside the "Run configuration check" button in Settings > Linked accounts, administrators only, when the provider refused the credentials. {{provider}} is GitHub or X. The English second sentence starts in lower case; a translation should be written normally.

linkedAccounts.diagnostics.unreachable.text: Couldn’t reach {{provider}} to verify the credentials. Try again shortly.
linkedAccounts.diagnostics.unreachable.description: Result beside the "Run configuration check" button in Settings > Linked accounts, administrators only, when the provider could not be contacted. {{provider}} is GitHub or X.

linkedAccounts.diagnostics.failed.text: The configuration check failed to run. Try again shortly.
linkedAccounts.diagnostics.failed.description: Result beside the "Run configuration check" button in Settings > Linked accounts, administrators only, when the check itself could not be carried out.

linkedAccounts.native.accountUnknown.text: Your account could not be identified. Reopen Settings and try again.
linkedAccounts.native.accountUnknown.description: Error under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts, in the phone app, when the app could not tell which Homeroom account is signed in. Settings is the name of the screen.

linkedAccounts.native.updateApp.text: Update the Homeroom app to open account connections in your browser.
linkedAccounts.native.updateApp.description: Error under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts, in the phone app, when the installed app is too old to open the browser for connecting an account.

linkedAccounts.native.browserNotOpened.text: Could not open your browser. Tap Connect to try again.
linkedAccounts.native.browserNotOpened.description: Error under a GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts, in the phone app, when the system browser did not open. "Connect" is the button on that row.

cli.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings that lists the credentials approved for command-line tools and coding agents. CLI means command-line interface.

cli.intro.text: Credentials approved for the Homeroom CLI, Codex, Claude Code, or OpenCode. Revoking an active credential takes effect immediately.
cli.intro.description: Explanation under the "CLI & coding-agent access" heading in Settings. Homeroom CLI, Codex, Claude Code and OpenCode are product names.

cli.tokens.loading.description: Shown in place of the list of command-line credentials in Settings > CLI & coding-agent access while it loads.

cli.tokens.empty.description: Shown in place of the list in Settings > CLI & coding-agent access when the account has no command-line credentials.

cli.tokens.revoke.description: Button on a credential's row in Settings > CLI & coding-agent access: cancels that credential so the tool using it loses access.

cli.tokens.loadMore.description: Button under the list of credentials in Settings > CLI & coding-agent access: fetches the next page of credentials.

cli.guide.title.text: Set up a local coding agent
cli.guide.title.description: Title of the setup guide card in Settings > CLI & coding-agent access: how to use a coding agent on one's own computer with Homeroom.

cli.guide.intro.text: Start Codex or Claude Code from a local checkout and ask it to create a proposal.
cli.guide.intro.description: Summary under the title of the local coding agent setup guide. Codex and Claude Code are product names; a "checkout" is a local copy of the code repository; a "proposal" is a change put to the community.

cli.guide.clone.title.description: Title of step 1 of the local coding agent setup guide. "Clone" is the version-control verb: download a copy of the code repository.

cli.guide.clone.body.text: Clone Homeroom and enter the checkout.
cli.guide.clone.body.description: Text of step 1 of the local coding agent setup guide, above the commands to copy: download Homeroom's code and change into its folder.

cli.guide.clone.codeLabel.description: Accessible name of the scrollable block of commands under step 1 of the local coding agent setup guide. Lower case in English.

cli.guide.clone.copyAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button beside the commands under step 1 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.start.title.description: Title of step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.start.body.text: Run either Codex or Claude Code from the repository directory.
cli.guide.start.body.description: Text of step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide, above the two commands. "Run" is a verb: start the program.

cli.guide.start.codexLabel.description: Accessible name of the block holding the command that starts Codex, in step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.start.codexCopyAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button beside the command that starts Codex, in step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.start.claudeLabel.description: Accessible name of the block holding the command that starts Claude Code, in step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.start.claudeCopyAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button beside the command that starts Claude Code, in step 2 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.ask.title.text: Ask it to create a proposal
cli.guide.ask.title.description: Title of step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide. "It" is the coding agent; a proposal is a change put to the community.

cli.guide.ask.promptHelp.text: Replace the placeholders with the app and change you have in mind, then send the prompt.
cli.guide.ask.promptHelp.description: Text of step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide, above an example prompt whose placeholders are in angle brackets.

cli.guide.ask.examplePrompt.text: Create a proposal for <0>app name</0> that <1>describe the change you want</1>.
cli.guide.ask.examplePrompt.description: Example prompt in step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide, which the person copies and sends to their coding agent. The two tagged parts are fill-in placeholders, shown in angle brackets (<app name>): translate the words inside the tags.

cli.guide.ask.promptLabel.description: Accessible name of the block holding the example prompt in step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide. Lower case in English.

cli.guide.ask.promptCopyAria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button beside the example prompt in step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide.

cli.guide.ask.follow.text: Follow the agent’s instructions. It will ask you to authorize access on a Homeroom web page; review and approve the request there, then return to your terminal.
cli.guide.ask.follow.description: Closing text of step 3 of the local coding agent setup guide, under the example prompt. "The request" is the agent's request for access.

cli.guide.copyFailed.description: Shown briefly in place of a Copy button in the local coding agent setup guide when the text could not be copied to the clipboard.

cli.guide.copyFailedToast.text: Couldn’t copy. Select the text and copy it manually
cli.guide.copyFailedToast.description: Brief pop-up message when a Copy button in the local coding agent setup guide could not copy to the clipboard.

grants.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings that lists the apps the person has allowed to use AI on their budget.

grants.intro.text: Apps you've allowed to use AI on your behalf. Their spend counts against your normal weekly budget, plus the per-app cap you set. Revoking takes effect immediately, and a revoked app can be re-enabled here with its previous cap.
grants.intro.description: Explanation under the "App AI permissions" heading in Settings. A "cap" is the most an app may spend per day.

grants.loadFailed.description: Error shown in place of the list in Settings > App AI permissions when it could not be loaded.

grants.empty.text: No apps can use AI on your behalf yet. When you let an app use AI, it appears here with its spending cap, and you can revoke it at any time.
grants.empty.description: Shown in place of the list in Settings > App AI permissions when no app has ever been allowed to use AI: says what will appear here and that it can be revoked.

grants.revoked.description: Badge on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: the person withdrew this app's permission to use AI.

grants.reenableNote.description: Note on a revoked app's row in Settings > App AI permissions, beside the Re-enable button. {{cap}} is an amount in US dollars such as 0.50; the dollar sign before it is part of the text.

grants.reenable.description: Button on a revoked app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: gives the app back its permission to use AI.

grants.reenableLabel.description: Screen-reader name of the Re-enable button on a revoked app in Settings > App AI permissions. {{app}} is the app.

grants.spentToday.description: Figure on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: what the app has spent today out of its daily cap. {{spent}} and {{cap}} are amounts in US dollars such as 0.12; the dollar signs are part of the text.

grants.totalToday.description: Line above the list of apps in Settings > App AI permissions: what all the apps together have spent on AI today, the same day each row's own figure covers. {{spent}} is an amount in US dollars such as 0.37; the dollar sign is part of the text.

grants.usedOfCapLabel.description: Screen reader name of the small bar on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions, which shows how much of its daily spending cap the app has used today. {{app}} is the app's name and {{percent}} is a whole number from 0 to 100.

grants.nearCap.description: Short line on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions, shown when the app has spent 80% or more of its daily AI spending cap but has not reached it yet.

grants.atCap.text: Reached today's cap. Its AI is paused until tomorrow, or until you raise the cap.
grants.atCap.description: Short line on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions, shown when the app has spent its whole daily AI spending cap. The field to raise the cap is on the same row.

grants.capLabel.description: Label directly before a number field on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: the most the app may spend per day, in US dollars. The dollar sign reads as the unit of the field that follows.

grants.capFieldLabel.text: Cap for {{app}}, in dollars a day
grants.capFieldLabel.description: Screen-reader name of the daily spending cap field on an app in Settings > App AI permissions. {{app}} is the app.

grants.useOwnKey.text: Use my own key past the weekly budget
grants.useOwnKey.description: Checkbox label on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: lets the app keep using AI on the person's own Anthropic API key once the daily budget is used up.

grants.revoke.description: Button on an app's row in Settings > App AI permissions: withdraws that app's permission to use AI on the person's budget.

grants.revokeLabel.description: Screen-reader name of the Revoke button on an app in Settings > App AI permissions. {{app}} is the app.

usage.title.description: Heading of the first part of the "AI usage & models" page in Settings: how much AI allowance is left.

usage.intro.text: How much of your AI allowance is left and, once you add your own key, what it has spent this week.
usage.intro.description: Explanation under the Usage heading in Settings. "Your own key" is the person's own Anthropic API key; "it" is that key.

usage.buildingTime.title.description: Small heading over a card on the "AI usage & models" page in Settings: how much of the Homeroom bot's weekly building time the person has used, and on which requests. "Building time" is the bot's time planning and building people's requests; Homeroom bot is a name and is not translated.

usage.buildingTime.used.text: {{percent}}% of this week's building time used
usage.buildingTime.used.description: First line of the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings. {{percent}} is a whole number from 0 to 100, for example "62".

usage.buildingTime.usedUp.text: You've used this week's building time
usage.buildingTime.usedUp.description: First line of the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings when the person has used all of this week's: the bot starts their requests again when the week resets.

usage.buildingTime.none.text: You haven't used any building time this week
usage.buildingTime.none.description: First line of the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings when the bot has done no work on the person's requests this week.

usage.buildingTime.unlimited.text: Your building time has no weekly limit
usage.buildingTime.unlimited.description: First line of the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings for a person with no weekly limit; the list under it still shows which requests used the most.

usage.buildingTime.resets.description: Line under the bar on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings saying when this week's building time starts again. "Resets" is a verb; its subject, the building time, is left out. {{day}} is the weekday's full name and {{time}} the time of day, both in the person's own clock and format, for example "Sunday" and "8:00 PM".

usage.buildingTime.percent.description: One request's share of the week's building time, at the end of its row on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings. {{percent}} is a whole number, for example "31".

usage.buildingTime.underOne.description: A request's share of the week's building time when it is more than nothing but less than one percent, at the end of its row on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings.

usage.buildingTime.untitled.description: A row's title on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings when the request's own title is not known. {{number}} is the request's number, for example "42".

usage.buildingTime.askedFor.description: Second line of a row on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings, for somebody else's request that the person asked the bot to build, which counts toward their own building time. {{app}} is the project's name.

usage.buildingTime.others.description: Last row of the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings: every request past the end of the list, together, with their share at the end.

usage.buildingTime.showAll_one.description: Button under the five largest requests on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings: shows the rest of the requests that used building time this week. {{count}} is how many requests there are in all, counting the five already shown.

usage.buildingTime.showAll_other.description: Button under the five largest requests on the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings: shows the rest of the requests that used building time this week. {{count}} is how many requests there are in all, counting the five already shown.

usage.buildingTime.explainLimited.text: Each request's share of your week. It counts the bot reading, planning and building your requests, and any you asked it to build for someone else.
usage.buildingTime.explainLimited.description: Small explanation under the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings, for a person with a weekly limit. "Your week" is their week of building time.

usage.buildingTime.explainUnlimited.text: Each request's share of what you used this week. It counts the bot reading, planning and building your requests, and any you asked it to build for someone else.
usage.buildingTime.explainUnlimited.description: Small explanation under the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings, for a person with no weekly limit.

usage.buildingTime.demo.text: Staging demo figures, not real numbers.
usage.buildingTime.demo.description: Small line under the Homeroom bot building time card in Settings, shown only on a test copy of Homeroom: says the figures are made up for testing.

usage.spend.heading.description: Small caption in Settings > Usage above the card that breaks down this week's AI spending. Shown only when the person has saved their own API key.

usage.spend.platform.description: Row label in the "This week's spend" card in Settings > Usage: spending that counted against the allowance Homeroom provides. An amount follows on the same row.

usage.spend.ownKey.description: Row label in the "This week's spend" card in Settings > Usage: spending billed to the person's own API key. An amount follows on the same row.

usage.spend.resetUtc.description: Last row of the "This week's spend" card in Settings > Usage, as it reads before the page has worked out the person's local time: when the weekly figures start again.

apiKey.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings where a person saves their own Anthropic API key. Anthropic is a company name.

apiKey.intro.text: Bring your own Anthropic API key to keep using Homeroom's AI features past the weekly limit. Your weekly allowance is used first; once it runs out, your key takes over automatically, and usage bills directly to your Anthropic account.
apiKey.intro.description: Explanation under the "Anthropic API key" heading in Settings. A "turn" is one round of the AI agent working on a request.

apiKey.savedKeyLabel.description: Row label in Settings > Anthropic API key, before the masked end of the API key that is saved. Noun: an API key.

apiKey.fieldLabel.description: Screen-reader label of the field in Settings where the person pastes their Anthropic API key.

apiKey.remove.description: Button in Settings > Anthropic API key: deletes the saved API key from the account.

apiKey.safety.text: Encrypted at rest, verified against Anthropic before saving, never shown in full after save. The server decrypts it in memory to call Anthropic on your behalf, so don't paste keys into services you don't trust with that level of access. <0>Set tight spend limits</0> on the key itself for defense in depth.
apiKey.safety.description: Security note under the key field in Settings > Anthropic API key. Tag 0 is a link to the page on Anthropic's site where spend limits are set; the sentence continues after the link.

openrouter.intro.text: Voice input uses this key: when you press Speak, it turns what you say into text. Your account comes with an included OpenRouter key, and what it spends counts toward your weekly allowance. You can use your own OpenRouter key instead, billed to your OpenRouter account. Keys are encrypted at rest.
openrouter.intro.description: Explanation under the OpenRouter heading in Settings. OpenRouter is a company name. "Voice input" is speaking a message instead of typing it; "Speak" is the label of the button that starts it (core:dictation.speak), so use the same word. The weekly allowance is the AI spending the platform includes for the person each week.

openrouter.included.title.description: Title of the status card in Settings > OpenRouter about the OpenRouter API key that comes with every account.

openrouter.personalKey.label.text: Or use your personal OpenRouter API key
openrouter.personalKey.label.description: Label of the field in Settings > OpenRouter where a person pastes their own OpenRouter API key, as an alternative to the included one.

openrouter.personalKey.testAndSave.description: Button under the personal key field in Settings > OpenRouter: checks the pasted API key with OpenRouter and saves it if it works.

openrouter.personalKey.remove.description: Button under the personal key field in Settings > OpenRouter: deletes the person's own saved OpenRouter API key.

screen.signOut.description: Red button at the foot of the Settings menu: signs the person out of Homeroom on this device.

screen.loadFailed.text: Settings could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
screen.loadFailed.description: Shown in place of the Settings sections when the code for the Settings screen could not be downloaded.

nav.sectionsName.description: Accessible name of the sidebar navigation on the Settings screen, which lists the settings pages.

nav.filter.field.description: Placeholder and accessible name of the search box above the Settings menu: typing filters the list of settings pages.

nav.filter.noMatch.description: Shown under the Settings search box when no settings page matches. {{query}} is what the person typed. Keep the quotation marks around it, in the target language's style.

nav.filter.try.description: Shown under "No settings match" in the Settings search box. {{first}} and {{second}} are the names of two settings pages (Language and Theme); each is a button that searches for it.

nav.filter.signOut.description: Search result in the Settings search box, in red, shown when the person typed something like "sign out" or "log out": choosing it signs them out of Homeroom.

nav.filter.recent.heading.description: Small heading over the list of the person's last few searches, shown under the Settings search box ("Find a setting") while the box is empty.

nav.filter.recent.clear.description: Button beside the "Recent searches" heading under the Settings search box: it forgets every recent search on this device.

nav.filter.recent.clearAria.description: Screen-reader name of the Clear button beside "Recent searches" under the Settings search box.

nav.filter.recent.again.description: Screen-reader name of a row in the Settings search box's recent searches. {{query}} is exactly what the person typed before; choosing the row searches for it again. Keep the quotation marks around it, in the target language's style.

accountRows.native.name.description: Accessible name of the group at the foot of the Settings menu that holds the wallet, node and staking rows of the Homeroom mobile app. Node means the blockchain node running on the phone.

accountRows.native.heading.description: Small visible heading over the wallet, node and staking rows at the foot of the Settings menu in the Homeroom mobile app. Node means the blockchain node running on the phone.

profile.title.description: Heading of the Profile section in Settings (noun: the person's own profile).

profile.intro.text: Your name, photo and bio, and whether your public page is on.
profile.intro.description: Explanation under the Profile heading in Settings: what the profile editor it links to contains.

profile.edit.description: Link text at the right of the card showing the person's name and photo in Settings > Profile: opens the profile editor.

signIn.title.description: Heading on the Account page of Settings over three rows: Username, Email & recovery and Password, the things a person signs in with.

account.change.description: Link at the right of the Username and Password rows in Settings: opens a small form under that row to change it.

account.add.description: Link at the right of the Email & recovery or Password row in Settings, in place of "Change", when the account has no email address or no password yet: opens a small form to add one.

username.title.description: Title of the Username row on the Account page of Settings, the first of the three sign-in rows; the person's current username is shown under it.

username.intro.text: Your @handle is how you sign in and the address of your public builder page.
username.intro.description: Explanation under the Username heading in Settings. "@handle" is the username written with an at sign; keep the @.

username.newPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the field in Settings > Username where the person types the username they want.

username.passwordPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the password field in the change-username form in Settings: the person confirms the change with the password they have now.

username.codePrompt.text: Your account has no password, so confirm the change with a code we email to your verified address.
username.codePrompt.description: Note in the change-username form in Settings for an account that signs in with emailed codes and has no password.

username.codePlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the field in the change-username form in Settings where the person types the code emailed to them.

username.sendCode.description: Button beside the code field in the change-username form in Settings: emails a six-digit code that confirms the change.

username.submit.description: Button in the change-username form that opens under the Username row in Settings: saves the new username.

username.rules.text: Letters, numbers and underscores, 3–32 characters, so people can still @mention you. Your old handle is kept reserved for you rather than released, so links and mentions that used it keep pointing at you and nobody else can take it. You can change your username again after 30 days.
username.rules.description: Small print in the change-username form that opens under the Username row in Settings: the rules for a username and what happens to the old one. "Handle" means username; "@mention" is naming someone with an at sign in a message.

email.title.description: Title of the Email & recovery row on the Account page of Settings, under which the linked email address is shown. The address is used to recover the account.

email.intro.text: Link a private email address to help you get back into your account. It does not appear on your public profile.
email.intro.description: Explanation at the top of the form that opens under the Email & recovery row in Settings.

email.loading.description: Shown under the Email & recovery row in Settings while the linked email address is being fetched.

email.requestFailed.description: Error in Settings > Email & recovery when loading or changing the linked email address failed and the server gave no reason.

email.none.description: Shown under the Email & recovery row in Settings, in place of an address, when the account has no email address.

email.rowUnverified.description: Shown under the Email & recovery row in Settings when the linked address has not been confirmed yet. {{email}} is the address.

email.rowFailed.description: Shown under the Email & recovery row in Settings when the linked email address could not be fetched; a Try again link sits beside it.

email.recoveryAllowed.text: Once verified, use this email to sign in or choose “Forgot password?” on the sign-in screen.
email.recoveryAllowed.description: Note in Settings > Email & recovery for ordinary accounts. “Forgot password?” is the name of a link on the sign-in screen; translate it the way that link is translated.

email.recoveryNotAllowed.text: Admin accounts cannot use email sign-in or email password recovery. Keep your password safe.
email.recoveryNotAllowed.description: Note in Settings > Email & recovery shown to platform administrators instead of the note about signing in by email.

email.verifyPrompt.text: Verify {{email}}. Your current email stays linked until this succeeds.
email.verifyPrompt.description: Instruction above the code field in Settings > Email & recovery after a verification code was sent. {{email}} is the new email address being verified.

email.codeLabel.description: Label of the field in Settings > Email & recovery where the person types the six-digit code sent to their email.

email.addressLabel.description: Label of the field in Settings > Email & recovery where the person types the email address to link.

email.passwordLabel.description: Label of the password field in Settings > Email & recovery: the person confirms the change of email with their account password.

email.submit.busy.description: Label of the main button in Settings > Email & recovery while its request is being sent.

email.submit.verify.description: Main button in Settings > Email & recovery once a code was sent: checks the typed code and links the email address.

email.submit.sendCode.description: Main button in Settings > Email & recovery: emails a six-digit code to the address typed above.

email.startOver.text: Change email or request another code
email.startOver.description: Secondary button in Settings > Email & recovery while a code is awaited: goes back to the address field so the person can correct the address or have a new code sent.

email.verifiedNotice.text: Email verified and linked to your account.
email.verifiedNotice.description: Confirmation in Settings > Email & recovery after the typed code was accepted.

email.codeSentNotice.text: Check your inbox for a six-digit code. It expires in 10 minutes.
email.codeSentNotice.description: Confirmation in Settings > Email & recovery after the verification code was emailed.

password.title.description: Title of the change-password form that opens under the Password row in Settings.

password.titleAdd.description: Title of the same form in Settings, in place of "Change password", for an account that has no password yet and signs in with a code sent by email.

password.rowTitle.description: Title of the Password row on the Account page of Settings, the last of the three sign-in rows.

password.stateSet.description: Shown under the Password row in Settings when the account has a password.

password.stateNotSet.text: Not set. You sign in with an emailed code.
password.stateNotSet.description: Shown under the Password row in Settings when the account has no password and signs in with a code sent by email.

password.intro.text: Set a new password for web login. If an admin gave you a temporary password, enter it as your current password here. No password yet? Choose one here; until then you sign in with an emailed code.
password.intro.description: Explanation at the top of the change-password form in Settings. The last sentence is for an account that has no password yet and signs in with a code sent by email.

password.currentPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the first field in Settings > Change password: the password the person has now.

password.newPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the second field in Settings > Change password: the new password, with its minimum length.

password.confirmPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the third field in Settings > Change password: the new password typed a second time.

password.submit.description: Button in Settings > Change password: saves the new password, checked against the current one.

password.submitAdd.description: Button in Settings > Add a password, in place of "Change password", for an account that has no password yet: saves its first password.

password.submitWithWallet.description: Button in Settings > Change password in the Homeroom mobile app when the person has no current password: signs the request with their wallet (a cryptographic signature, not signing in) and sets the new password.

password.useWallet.text: Don’t have a password? Create one
password.useWallet.description: Link under the Change password button in the Homeroom mobile app: switches the form to creating a password confirmed by the wallet instead of by a current password.

password.usePassword.description: Link under the button in Settings > Change password in the Homeroom mobile app: switches the form back to confirming with the current password instead of the wallet.

deleteAccount.title.description: Heading of the section at the end of the Account page in Settings where the person deletes their Homeroom account.

deleteAccount.intro.text: Anonymise your account and remove your sign-in access. Shared messages and contributions stay under an anonymous “deleted-user” name.
deleteAccount.intro.description: Explanation under the Delete account heading in Settings. “deleted-user” is the literal name shown in place of the person's; keep it as written.

deleteAccount.open.description: Red button with a warning icon in Settings > Delete account: opens the confirmation form. Nothing is deleted yet; keep the ellipsis.

deleteAccount.formName.description: Accessible name of the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account.

deleteAccount.question.description: Heading of the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account.

deleteAccount.deleted.description: Heading that replaces the question in Settings > Delete account once the account has been deleted, while the device is being signed out.

deleteAccount.whatIsRemoved.text: Your account is anonymised, not erased: your name, email, profile, sign-in access and private account data are removed, and you will be signed out on all devices. This cannot be undone.
deleteAccount.whatIsRemoved.description: First paragraph of the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account: what deleting removes.

deleteAccount.whatStays.text: Messages, votes, shared attachments and public contributions stay available to other participants under an anonymous “deleted-user” name. Their contents are kept, including any personal information you shared in them.
deleteAccount.whatStays.description: Second paragraph of the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account: what other people keep seeing. “deleted-user” is the literal name shown; keep it as written.

deleteAccount.retention.text: Necessary financial and moderation records are retained without your account link. External cleanup may take longer. Copies in backups, other apps, GitHub or the blockchain follow their own retention rules.
deleteAccount.retention.description: Third paragraph of the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account: records that are kept and copies outside Homeroom.

deleteAccount.loading.description: Shown in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account while Homeroom checks whether this account must confirm with a password.

deleteAccount.loadFailed.description: Error in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account when that check failed and the server gave no reason.

deleteAccount.connectionError.text: Check your connection and try again.
deleteAccount.connectionError.description: Error in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account when a request failed without any message, usually because the device is offline.

deleteAccount.passwordLabel.description: Label of the password field in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account.

deleteAccount.recentSignIn.text: For security, sign out and sign in again if you signed in more than 10 minutes ago.
deleteAccount.recentSignIn.description: Shown in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account, instead of a password field, to people whose account has no password.

deleteAccount.confirmLabel.description: Label of the field in Settings > Delete account where the person must type a fixed word before the delete button works. {{word}} is that word, DELETE, which is always typed in English capitals.

deleteAccount.submit.description: Red button in the confirmation form in Settings > Delete account: deletes the account. It cannot be undone.

deleteAccount.submitting.description: Label of the red button in Settings > Delete account while the account is being deleted.

deleteAccount.failed.description: Error in Settings > Delete account when the server refused to delete the account and gave no reason.

deleteAccount.signOutFailed.text: Your account is deleted. Retry signing out to clear this device.
deleteAccount.signOutFailed.description: Error in Settings > Delete account when the account was deleted but this device could not be signed out. The button under it tries again.

deleteAccount.finishSignOut.description: Button in Settings > Delete account shown after the account was deleted: signs this device out, when doing so automatically failed.

wallet.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings where the person links their Homeroom Wallet, the crypto wallet in the Homeroom mobile app. A product name.

wallet.intro.text: Link your on-chain identity. Scan the QR code with the Homeroom mobile app.
wallet.intro.description: Explanation under the Homeroom Wallet heading in Settings. "On-chain identity" is the person's blockchain address.

wallet.link.description: Button in Settings > Homeroom Wallet: shows a QR code to scan with the Homeroom mobile app, which links that wallet to this account.

experimental.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings that holds switches for features still being tested.

experimental.intro.text: Early features we're still testing. They may change or disappear.
experimental.intro.description: Explanation under the Experimental heading in Settings.

experimental.look.fold.description: Accessible name and tooltip of a round button in the top bar on a phone, which only admins see. It opens a small menu with two rows: Look (the visual style) and Theme (light or dark).

experimental.look.label.description: Label of a menu in Settings, Experimental, which only admins see. It chooses the visual style Homeroom is drawn in on this browser.

experimental.look.standard.description: First option of the Look menu in Settings, Experimental: Homeroom's usual visual style, with no experimental look applied.

experimental.look.brand.description: Option of the Look menu in Settings, Experimental: the name of one visual style. It draws Homeroom's usual pages the clean way a look named Paper did (cards with no outlines, white on a cream page in light and one step off a dark navy page in dark), in the website's own colours and typefaces. "Paper" is a proper name here.

experimental.wipTokens.brand.description: Option of the Look menu (beside the bell for admins, and in Settings, Experimental): Homeroom's usual visual style with the changes still being tried on it, drawn with the colours and typeface of Homeroom's brand guidelines (cream, yellow, blue, black, the Geist typeface). Homeroom is the product name. (WIP) means work in progress. Translate it as a short name, not a sentence.

experimental.look.description.text: Try another look for Homeroom, in light and dark. One draws every page in the website's colours. The other is the usual look with changes still being tried on it, in the brand kit's colours and typefaces. Admins see this menu, and the same one beside the bell, while the looks are drawn. Kept for this browser.
experimental.look.description.description: Explanation under the Look menu in Settings, Experimental, which only admins see while the looks are being drawn. Homeroom is the product name; Home is its first screen.

theme.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings where the person chooses a light or dark appearance.

theme.intro.text: Light, dark, or follow your device. Applies everywhere on this browser.
theme.intro.description: Explanation under the Theme heading in Settings.

theme.controlName.description: Accessible name of the three-way control in Settings > Theme that switches between the light, dark and system appearance.

theme.mode.light.description: Choice in the theme control in Settings: the light appearance.

theme.mode.dark.description: Choice in the theme control in Settings: the dark appearance.

theme.mode.system.description: Choice in the theme control in Settings: follow the device's own light or dark setting.

theme.railPinned.label.description: Label of a switch in Settings > Theme, on a computer: keeps Homeroom's sidebar visible beside an app that is open.

theme.railPinned.description.text: On, the sidebar stays beside an app you open, and the sidebar button at the top left hides it. Off, an app takes the whole window and has a close button instead.
theme.railPinned.description.description: Explanation under the "Keep sidebar open in apps" switch in Settings. "Off" and "On" are the two positions of that switch.

accessibility.textSize.title.description: Heading of the Text size part of Settings > Accessibility.

accessibility.textSize.intro.text: Makes text bigger everywhere on this browser, up to one and a half times the normal size.
accessibility.textSize.intro.description: Line under the Text size heading in Settings > Accessibility, saying what the control does.

accessibility.textSize.controlName.description: Name of the Text size slider in Settings > Accessibility, announced to a screen reader.

accessibility.textSize.percent.description: The chosen text size beside the Text size slider in Settings > Accessibility, also read to a screen reader as the slider's value. {{percent}} is a whole number from 100 to 150, where 100 is the normal size.

accessibility.textSize.sample.description: One letter drawn small before the Text size slider in Settings > Accessibility and large after it, to show which way makes text bigger. Use one plain letter of your script.

accessibility.contrast.label.description: Label of the High contrast switch in Settings > Accessibility.

accessibility.contrast.description.text: Darker text and clearer lines, in light and dark.
accessibility.contrast.description.description: Explanation under the High contrast switch in Settings > Accessibility.

accessibility.motion.label.description: Label of a switch in Settings > Accessibility: turns off most animations, slides and moving effects across Homeroom.

accessibility.motion.description.text: Turns off most animations, slides and moving effects, so screens change in place. When this is off, Homeroom follows your device's own reduce motion setting.
accessibility.motion.description.description: Explanation under the Reduce motion switch in Settings > Accessibility.

accessibility.previews.label.description: Label of a switch in Settings, Accessibility: whether project cards play their short, silent preview clips.

accessibility.previews.description.text: A project's card plays a short, silent clip of the project when you point at it. Turn this off to see still pictures only. Clips never play when your device is set to reduce motion or save data.
accessibility.previews.description.description: Explanation under the Play previews switch in Settings, Accessibility.

privacy.whoCanMessage.title.text: Who can message or invite me
privacy.whoCanMessage.title.description: Heading of the first setting on the Settings > Privacy page, and the accessible name of its two choices. It decides who may start a direct message with you or invite you to a group chat or a project.

privacy.whoCanMessage.intro.text: Who can start a new conversation with you, invite you to a group chat or a project, or send you a friend request. Conversations you already have keep working.
privacy.whoCanMessage.intro.description: Explanation under the "Who can message or invite me" heading in Settings > Privacy.

privacy.whoCanMessage.shared.description: First choice under "Who can message or invite me" in Settings > Privacy, and the default: only people who are in one of your projects with you, or your friends, can start a conversation or invite you.

privacy.whoCanMessage.sharedDescription.text: Your friends, and people who made or were invited into a project you're in. Joining a public community doesn't count. Anyone else can still send you an invite link.
privacy.whoCanMessage.sharedDescription.description: Small explanation under the "People in projects I'm in" choice in Settings > Privacy.

privacy.whoCanMessage.anyone.description: Second choice under "Who can message or invite me" in Settings > Privacy: anybody on Homeroom can start a conversation with you or invite you.

privacy.whoCanMessage.anyoneDescription.text: Anybody on Homeroom can message you, invite you or send you a friend request, including people you don't know.
privacy.whoCanMessage.anyoneDescription.description: Small explanation under the "Anyone" choice in Settings > Privacy.

privacy.discoverable.title.description: Heading of the second section of Settings > Privacy, over the "Let people find my profile" switch. It is about who finds your username in a search, not who can message you.

privacy.discoverable.intro.text: Who can find your username when they search for someone to message, mention or invite.
privacy.discoverable.intro.description: Explanation under the "Who can find me" heading in Settings > Privacy.

privacy.discoverable.label.description: Label of a switch in Settings > Privacy, off by default. When on, people who are not in a project with you can find your username when they search for people.

privacy.discoverable.descriptionOff.text: Only your friends and people who made or were invited into a project you're in can find your username when they search for someone to message, mention or invite. A link to your profile still works.
privacy.discoverable.descriptionOff.description: Explanation under the "Let people find my profile" switch in Settings > Privacy while the switch is off: who can find you now.

privacy.discoverable.descriptionOn.text: Anyone on Homeroom can find your username when they search for someone to message, mention or invite.
privacy.discoverable.descriptionOn.description: Explanation under the "Let people find my profile" switch in Settings > Privacy while the switch is on: who can find you now.

privacy.state.on.description: Small word after a switch's label in Settings > Privacy ("Let people find my profile") while that switch is on.

privacy.state.off.description: Small word after a switch's label in Settings > Privacy ("Let people find my profile") while that switch is off.

privacy.loadFailed.text: Couldn't load your privacy settings. Try again in a moment.
privacy.loadFailed.description: Error on the Settings > Privacy page when reading the current settings from the server failed.

privacy.saveFailed.text: Couldn't save that change. Try again in a moment.
privacy.saveFailed.description: Error on the Settings > Privacy page when saving a change failed; the control goes back to what it was.

privacy.saved.description: Short confirmation under a block of the Settings > Privacy page when a change to one of its settings has been saved. It goes away after about three seconds.

privacy.usageAnalytics.title.description: Heading of the last block of Settings > Privacy: what usage data Homeroom keeps.

privacy.usageAnalytics.intro.text: Homeroom keeps a record of how it's used, linked to your account, to see where people get stuck and fix it.
privacy.usageAnalytics.intro.description: One line under the Usage data heading in Settings > Privacy: what Homeroom records and why.

privacy.usageAnalytics.alwaysKept.title.text: Always kept, because Homeroom runs on it
privacy.usageAnalytics.alwaysKept.title.description: Small heading in Settings > Privacy > Usage data over the list of what is kept for everyone and cannot be turned off.

privacy.usageAnalytics.alwaysKept.apps.text: Which apps you use each day, and for how long
privacy.usageAnalytics.alwaysKept.apps.description: Item in the 'Always kept' list in Settings > Privacy > Usage data.

privacy.usageAnalytics.alwaysKept.acts.text: Your votes, messages, requests and projects
privacy.usageAnalytics.alwaysKept.acts.description: Item in the 'Always kept' list in Settings > Privacy > Usage data.

privacy.usageAnalytics.alwaysKept.challe.description: Item in the 'Always kept' list in Settings > Privacy > Usage data.

privacy.usageAnalytics.alsoRecorded.titl.text: Also recorded, for everyone: screen usage data
privacy.usageAnalytics.alsoRecorded.titl.description: Small heading in Settings > Privacy > Usage data over the list of screen usage data, which Homeroom records for everyone. Someone who doesn't want it can email to be left out (the block's last line).

privacy.usageAnalytics.alsoRecorded.scre.text: The screens you open, and in what order
privacy.usageAnalytics.alsoRecorded.scre.description: Item in the 'Also recorded' list in Settings > Privacy > Usage data.

privacy.usageAnalytics.alsoRecorded.spee.text: How long pages take to load, and actions that fail
privacy.usageAnalytics.alsoRecorded.spee.description: Item in the 'Also recorded' list in Settings > Privacy > Usage data.

privacy.usageAnalytics.neverRecorded.text: Never recorded: what you type, or what's on your screen.
privacy.usageAnalytics.neverRecorded.description: Line in Settings > Privacy > Usage data: what Homeroom never records, for anyone.

privacy.usageAnalytics.leaveOut.ask.text: Don't want your screen usage data recorded? Email us and we'll erase what was recorded and stop recording it:
privacy.usageAnalytics.leaveOut.ask.description: Settings > Privacy, the usage data block: its last line, followed by the data protection email address as a link. "Screen usage data" is the list above it: the screens someone opens, page load times and actions that fail.

phones.title.description: Heading of the Settings > Linked devices page, which lists the phones signed in to the account through the Homeroom mobile app and the browsers signed in on the web.

phones.intro.text: The phones and browsers signed in to your account. Unlink or sign out any you no longer use, or don't recognise.
phones.intro.description: Explanation under the Linked devices heading in Settings > Linked devices: the page lists phones (Homeroom app) and browsers (the web), each with a way to sign it out.

phones.empty.text: No phones are linked. Sign in with the Homeroom app on your phone and it shows up here.
phones.empty.description: Shown under the Phones heading of Settings > Linked devices when no phone is signed in to the account through the Homeroom mobile app.

phones.platform.android.description: Name of a row in Settings > Linked phones: a phone running Android that is signed in to the account.

phones.platform.ios.description: Name of a row in Settings > Linked phones: an iPhone that is signed in to the account.

phones.platform.unknown.description: Name of a row in Settings > Linked phones when Homeroom does not know whether the phone is an Android phone or an iPhone (it never turned on notifications).

phones.thisPhone.description: Small label beside the name of a row in Settings > Linked phones: the row is the phone this page is open on.

phones.detail.description: Line under a phone in Settings > Linked devices. {{lastUsed}} is the date the Homeroom app last used the account on that phone (within the last 30 days); {{linked}} is the date it was first signed in there. Both are already-formatted dates.

phones.unlink.description: Red button on a row of Settings > Linked phones: signs that phone out of the account (verb). Pressed once it asks to confirm; pressed again it unlinks.

phones.cancel.description: Button beside Unlink on a row of Settings > Linked phones while it asks to confirm: keeps the phone linked.

phones.confirm.text: Press Unlink again to sign this phone out.
phones.confirm.description: Replaces the dates under a phone in Settings > Linked phones after Unlink was pressed once, asking to confirm.

phones.confirmThisPhone.text: This is the phone you are using. Press Unlink again to sign out here.
phones.confirmThisPhone.description: Replaces the dates under the phone this page is open on in Settings > Linked phones after Unlink was pressed once: unlinking it signs the person out on this phone.

phones.loadFailed.text: Couldn't load your linked phones. Try again in a moment.
phones.loadFailed.description: Error on the Settings > Linked devices page when reading the list of phones from the server failed.

phones.unlinkFailed.text: Couldn't unlink that phone. Try again in a moment.
phones.unlinkFailed.description: Error on the Settings > Linked devices page when unlinking a phone failed; the phone stays in the list.

phones.group.phones.description: Heading of the first group on the Settings > Linked devices page: the phones signed in to the account through the Homeroom mobile app.

phones.group.browsers.description: Heading of the second group on the Settings > Linked devices page: the browsers (on computers, phones or tablets) signed in to the account on the web.

phones.phonesNote.text: Each row is one install of the Homeroom app. Reinstalling the app makes a new row; unlink any you no longer use.
phones.phonesNote.description: Explanation under the Phones heading in Settings > Linked devices, saying why one phone can appear more than once: every installation of the Homeroom mobile app is its own row.

phones.detailStale.description: Line under a phone in Settings > Linked devices when the Homeroom app has not used the account on that phone for more than 30 days. {{lastUsed}} is the date it was last used; {{linked}} is the date it was first signed in there. Both are already-formatted dates.

phones.browsers.note.text: Each row is one browser signed in to Homeroom on the web. Sign out of any you don't recognise.
phones.browsers.note.description: Explanation under the Browsers heading in Settings > Linked devices. Homeroom is the product name.

phones.browsers.empty.text: No browsers are signed in to your account.
phones.browsers.empty.description: Shown under the Browsers heading of Settings > Linked devices when the account has no browser session on the web (for example when the page is open inside the Homeroom app, whose own session is listed as a phone).

phones.browsers.name.description: Name of a row in Settings > Linked devices > Browsers: which browser on which system is signed in. {{browser}} is a browser name (Chrome, Safari, Firefox…) and {{os}} a system name (Mac, Windows, iPhone…), both already translated.

phones.browsers.nameSystemOnly.description: Name of a row in Settings > Linked devices > Browsers when Homeroom knows the system (Mac, Windows, iPhone…) the browser runs on but not which browser it is. {{os}} is already translated.

phones.browsers.unknown.description: Name of a row in Settings > Linked devices > Browsers when Homeroom does not know which browser or system it is (the session was made before Homeroom recorded that, or by a browser it does not recognise).

phones.browsers.browser.chrome.description: A browser's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers. Google Chrome: a product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.browser.safari.description: A browser's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers. Apple Safari: a product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.browser.firefox.description: A browser's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers. Mozilla Firefox: a product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.browser.edge.description: A browser's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers. Microsoft Edge: a product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.browser.opera.description: A browser's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers. Opera: a product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.browser.samsung.description: A browser's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers. Samsung Internet, the browser on Samsung phones: a product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.os.mac.description: A system's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers: an Apple Mac computer.

phones.browsers.os.windows.description: A system's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers: a Windows computer. Microsoft Windows is a product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.os.linux.description: A system's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers: a Linux computer. Linux is a product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.os.android.description: A system's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers: an Android phone or tablet. Android is a product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.os.ios.description: A system's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers: an iPhone. A product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.os.ipad.description: A system's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers: an iPad. A product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.os.chromeos.description: A system's name in a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers: a Chromebook (a ChromeOS computer). A product name, usually kept as is.

phones.browsers.thisBrowser.description: Small label beside the name of a row in Settings > Linked devices > Browsers: the row is the browser this page is open in.

phones.browsers.detail.description: Line under a browser in Settings > Linked devices > Browsers. {{lastUsed}} is the date that browser last used the account (within the last 30 days); {{signedIn}} is the date it signed in. Both are already-formatted dates.

phones.browsers.detailStale.description: Line under a browser in Settings > Linked devices > Browsers when it has not used the account for more than 30 days. {{lastUsed}} is the date it was last used; {{signedIn}} is the date it signed in. Both are already-formatted dates.

phones.browsers.signOut.description: Red button on a row of Settings > Linked devices > Browsers: signs that browser out of the account (verb). Pressed once it asks to confirm; pressed again it signs the browser out.

phones.browsers.confirm.text: Press Sign out again to sign that browser out.
phones.browsers.confirm.description: Replaces the dates under a browser in Settings > Linked devices > Browsers after Sign out was pressed once, asking to confirm.

phones.browsers.confirmThisBrowser.text: This is the browser you are using. Press Sign out again to sign out here.
phones.browsers.confirmThisBrowser.description: Replaces the dates under the browser this page is open in, in Settings > Linked devices > Browsers, after Sign out was pressed once: signing it out signs the person out here.

phones.browsers.loadFailed.text: Couldn't load your browsers. Try again in a moment.
phones.browsers.loadFailed.description: Error on the Settings > Linked devices page when reading the list of signed-in browsers from the server failed.

phones.browsers.signOutFailed.text: Couldn't sign that browser out. Try again in a moment.
phones.browsers.signOutFailed.description: Error on the Settings > Linked devices page when signing a browser out failed; the browser stays in the list.

devConsole.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings about the log panel that shows an app's console output and errors.

devConsole.intro.text: The bug icon in the header opens a slide-up log of console output and errors forwarded from the running app.
devConsole.intro.description: Explanation under the Developer console heading in Settings.

devConsole.alwaysShow.label.description: Label of the switch in Settings > Developer console: keeps the bug icon in the header visible even when the app has logged no error.

devConsole.alwaysShow.description.text: When unchecked (the default), the icon only appears once the current app has logged at least one error.
devConsole.alwaysShow.description.description: Explanation under the "Always show the icon" switch in Settings > Developer console.

adminPreview.title.description: Heading of a section in Settings shown only to platform administrators: lets them see Homeroom the way a regular member does.

adminPreview.intro.text: Hide admin-only UI so the app looks the way it does for a regular user. Useful for spotting UX issues that only affect non-admins.
adminPreview.intro.description: Explanation under the Admin preview heading in Settings.

adminPreview.toggle.label.description: Label of the switch in Settings > Admin preview: hides everything only administrators can see.

adminPreview.toggle.description.text: Purely a client-side display toggle, so your server-side admin privileges are unaffected. The page will reload so the rest of the UI picks up the change.
adminPreview.toggle.description.description: Explanation under the "View as non-admin" switch in Settings > Admin preview.

alerts.title.description: Heading of the first block on the Notifications page in Settings: a test that sends a sample push notification to the person's phone.

alerts.intro.text: Check that Homeroom can reach your phone. To get push notifications with the mobile app in the background or closed, turn on Activity notifications on your phone and the categories you want below. The test waits 10 seconds before it sends, so you can switch away.
alerts.intro.description: Explanation under the "Test phone notifications" heading in Settings. "Activity notifications" is the name of a switch in the Homeroom mobile app's settings; the categories are the switches under "Mobile push categories" further down this page.

alerts.test.description: Button under "Test phone notifications" on the Notifications page in Settings: sends a sample push notification to the person's phone so they can check it arrives.

alerts.push.title.description: Heading of the block in Settings that lists which kinds of activity may send a notification to the person's phone.

alerts.push.intro.text: Choose which Social activity can send a phone notification. Your phone's Activity notifications switch remains the master control for that device.
alerts.push.intro.description: Explanation under the Mobile push categories heading in Settings. Social is a name for this part of the product; "Activity notifications" is the name of a switch in the Homeroom mobile app's settings.

alerts.push.loading.description: Status line under the Mobile push categories switches in Settings while their saved positions are being fetched.

alerts.push.messages.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories: chat messages (plural noun).

alerts.push.messages.description.text: Conversation invitations, messages, mentions, replies, and reactions.
alerts.push.messages.description.description: What the Messages category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories.

alerts.push.builds.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories. "Builds" is a plural noun: things Homeroom bot is building for the person.

alerts.push.builds.description.text: What Homeroom bot tells you about something you asked for: when it needs you, is ready to try, stops, or goes live.
alerts.push.builds.description.description: What the "Your builds" category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories. Homeroom bot is the name of Homeroom's building assistant.

alerts.push.inviteActivity.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories: activity on invite links the person shared.

alerts.push.inviteActivity.description.text: When someone opens your invite link, joins through it, or says hi for the first time, and when a link brings in a lot of people in a day.
alerts.push.inviteActivity.description.description: What the "Your invites" category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories.

alerts.push.directInteractions.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories: things other people do that are aimed at this person.

alerts.push.directInteractions.descripti.text: Mentions, replies to your messages, and friend requests.
alerts.push.directInteractions.descripti.description: What the Direct interactions category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories.

alerts.push.invitations.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories: invitations to work on a project or approve its changes.

alerts.push.invitations.description.text: Collaboration and approver invitations, including when yours are accepted.
alerts.push.invitations.description.description: What the Invitations category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories. An approver is someone whose approval a project's changes need.

alerts.push.developerSessions.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories: news from an AI coding agent the person connected to Homeroom.

alerts.push.developerSessions.descriptio.text: When a coding agent you connected to Homeroom puts up its work or is waiting on you. Test alerts use this switch too.
alerts.push.developerSessions.descriptio.description: What the "Your coding agent" category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories. A test alert is the sample notification sent by the "Send a test alert" button on the same page.

alerts.push.proposalAlerts.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories. "Change" is a noun: a proposed change to a project.

alerts.push.proposalAlerts.description.text: Changes that need your attention or your vote, votes on yours, changes you made or voted on going live, and projects you joined opening.
alerts.push.proposalAlerts.description.description: What the Change alerts category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories. "Changes" are proposed changes to a project; "yours" means the person's own proposed changes.

alerts.push.appAlerts.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories: problems with the person's apps.

alerts.push.appAlerts.description.text: New issues filed on your apps, and apps that stop working.
alerts.push.appAlerts.description.description: What the App alerts category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories. An issue is a problem report.

alerts.push.lightweightActivity.label.description: Name of a phone notification category in Settings > Mobile push categories: small signs of appreciation from other people.

alerts.push.lightweightActivity.descript.description: What the Lightweight activity category covers, under its name in Settings > Mobile push categories.

alerts.apps.title.description: Heading of the block in Settings that sets which notifications apps may send this person.

alerts.apps.intro.text: Your default for every app, and the apps you have set differently. Each of these covers the bell here and a notification on your phone, together. Change one app from its Notifications entry in the app menu.
alerts.apps.intro.description: Explanation under the "What apps tell you about" heading in Settings. "The bell" is the notifications icon in Homeroom's header; Notifications is the name of an entry in an app's menu.

alerts.apps.loadFailed.description: Error under the "What apps tell you about" heading in Settings when the notification defaults could not be fetched.

alerts.apps.overridesHeading.description: Subheading in Settings > What apps tell you about, over the list of apps whose notification settings differ from the person's defaults.

alerts.apps.useDefaults.description: Button on an app's row under "Apps set differently" in Settings: removes that app's own notification settings so it follows the person's defaults again.

alerts.apps.categoryOn.description: Line on an app's row under "Apps set differently" in Settings: that app may send this kind of notification. {{category}} is the kind's name, such as Mentions.

alerts.apps.categoryOff.description: Line on an app's row under "Apps set differently" in Settings: that app may not send this kind of notification. {{category}} is the kind's name, such as Mentions.

alerts.apps.noOverrides.text: No app is set differently. Change one from its Notifications entry in the app menu.
alerts.apps.noOverrides.description: Shown under "Apps set differently" in Settings when every app follows the person's defaults. Notifications is the name of an entry in an app's menu.

appPermissions.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings that lists which apps may use the device's location, microphone, camera and so on.

appPermissions.intro.text: Apps you've allowed to use your location, microphone, camera, screen or connected devices. Each app is asked for separately, and only the app you granted gets it. If an app is open in this tab, revoking closes it so it stops at once. Anywhere else it is open, it keeps access until it is closed. On another device, opening the app again within a minute may bring the permission back until it is closed again.
appPermissions.intro.description: Explanation under the App device permissions heading in Settings. Revoking closes the app when it is open in this browser tab. A running app keeps a permission until it is closed, and another device that reopens the app within about a minute of the revoke may still give it the permission, which it then keeps until it is closed.

appPermissions.summary.device_one.description: First half of the summary line at the top of Settings > App permissions: how many apps currently hold at least one device permission (location, microphone, camera, screen or a connected device). {{count}} is the number of apps. Shown only when it is at least one.

appPermissions.summary.device_other.description: First half of the summary line at the top of Settings > App permissions: how many apps currently hold at least one device permission (location, microphone, camera, screen or a connected device). {{count}} is the number of apps. Shown only when it is at least one.

appPermissions.summary.ai_one.text: {{count}} app can use AI on your budget
appPermissions.summary.ai_one.description: Second half of the summary line at the top of Settings > App permissions: how many apps are currently allowed to use AI on the person's budget. {{count}} is the number of apps. Shown only when it is at least one.

appPermissions.summary.ai_other.text: {{count}} apps can use AI on your budget
appPermissions.summary.ai_other.description: Second half of the summary line at the top of Settings > App permissions: how many apps are currently allowed to use AI on the person's budget. {{count}} is the number of apps. Shown only when it is at least one.

appPermissions.loadFailed.description: Error in Settings > App device permissions when the list could not be fetched.

appPermissions.empty.text: No apps can use your camera, microphone, location, screen or devices yet. When you allow an app one of these, it appears here and you can revoke it at any time.
appPermissions.empty.description: Shown in Settings > App device permissions when no app has been granted anything: says what will appear here and that it can be revoked.

appPermissions.reEnable.description: Button beside a struck-through permission of an app in Settings > App device permissions: gives the app back a permission the person revoked.

appPermissions.reEnableLabel.description: Screen-reader name of the Re-enable button beside a revoked permission in Settings > App device permissions. {{permission}} is the permission (Camera, Location) and {{app}} is the app.

appPermissions.revoke.description: Red button beside a permission of an app in Settings > App device permissions: takes that permission away from the app.

appPermissions.revokeLabel.description: Screen-reader name of the Revoke button beside a permission in Settings > App device permissions. {{permission}} is the permission (Camera, Location) and {{app}} is the app.

appPermissions.note.camera.text: Lets this app use your camera while it is open, once your browser allows it too.
appPermissions.note.camera.description: Small grey line under the Camera permission of an app in Settings > App device permissions: says plainly what this permission lets the app do. Shown on revoked rows too, so it describes the permission rather than what the app can do right now; the browser must also allow the camera.

appPermissions.note.microphone.text: Lets this app hear you and the sounds around you while it is open, once your browser allows it too.
appPermissions.note.microphone.description: Small grey line under the Microphone permission of an app in Settings > App device permissions: says plainly what this permission lets the app do. Shown on revoked rows too, so it describes the permission rather than what the app can do right now; the browser must also allow the microphone.

appPermissions.note.screen.text: Each time it asks, your browser lets you choose a screen, window or tab. The app sees only what you choose, until you stop sharing.
appPermissions.note.screen.description: Small grey line under the Screen sharing permission of an app in Settings > App device permissions. The browser shows its own picker every time the app asks to share, and the app sees only the screen, window or tab the person picks there.

appPermissions.allowedAt.description: Small grey line under a permission's name (such as Camera) on an app's row in Settings > App device permissions, saying when the person last allowed it. {{when}} is either how long ago ("3d ago", "just now") or, after a week, a date such as "Jun 16".

appPermissions.revokedAt.description: Small grey line under a revoked permission's name (such as Camera) on an app's row in Settings > App device permissions, saying when the person revoked it. {{when}} is either how long ago ("3d ago", "just now") or, after a week, a date such as "Jun 16".

appPermissions.revokeAll.description: Red button beside an app's name in Settings > App device permissions, shown when the app has two or more permissions: takes all of them away from that app in one step.

appPermissions.revokeAllLabel.description: Screen-reader name of the Revoke all button beside an app's name in Settings > App device permissions. {{app}} is the app.

blockedApps.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings that lists the apps this person has blocked.

blockedApps.intro.text: Blocked apps are hidden from your app lists and discovery, cannot be opened in Homeroom, and do not send you notifications. Their creators and contributors remain unaffected.
blockedApps.intro.description: Explanation under the Blocked apps heading in Settings: what blocking an app does.

blockedApps.loading.description: Shown in Settings > Blocked apps while the list is being fetched.

blockedApps.loadFailed.description: Error in Settings > Blocked apps when the list could not be fetched and the server gave no reason.

blockedApps.empty.text: You haven’t blocked any apps. An app you block appears here, and you can unblock it at any time.
blockedApps.empty.description: Shown in Settings > Blocked apps when the list is empty: says what will appear here and that it can be undone.

blockedApps.unblock.description: Button on an app's row in Settings > Blocked apps: removes the block so the app is shown and can be opened again.

blockedApps.unblockLabel.description: Screen-reader name of the Unblock button on a row in Settings > Blocked apps. {{app}} is the blocked app.

blockedApps.unblocking.description: Label of the Unblock button on an app's row in Settings > Blocked apps while the block is being removed.

blockedApps.unblockFailed.description: Error in Settings > Blocked apps when removing a block failed and the server gave no reason.

blockedApps.blockedAt.description: Small grey line under an app's name in Settings > Blocked apps saying when the person blocked it. {{when}} is either how long ago ("3d ago", "just now") or, after a week, a date such as "Jun 16".

tour.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings that replays the introduction shown to new members.

tour.intro.text: A one-minute walk through your apps and the Homeroom menu.
tour.intro.description: Explanation under the Welcome tour heading in Settings.

tour.replay.description: Button in Settings > Welcome tour: goes to the home screen and starts the welcome tour again.

tour.hint.text: It starts again on your home screen.
tour.hint.description: Note under the "Replay the tour" button in Settings. "It" is the welcome tour.

guide.title.description: Heading of the page in Settings that explains the places in Homeroom and how a change gets voted in.

guide.intro.text: How to start, where things are in Homeroom, and how a change goes live.
guide.intro.description: Explanation under the User guide heading in Settings.

guide.start.heading.description: Small label over the first card of Settings > User guide: the first steps for someone new to Homeroom, in order.

guide.start.join.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the first step for someone new.

guide.start.join.body.text: On Home, Communities to join lists the public ones: open one and join it. To make your own, select New project on Home, or New community on the Communities tab.
guide.start.join.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Communities to join" and "New project" are names shown on the Home screen; "New community" is a name shown on the Communities page; "Communities" is the name of a tab in the main navigation.

guide.start.open.title.text: Open an app and its Homeroom menu
guide.start.open.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the second step for someone new.

guide.start.open.body.text: Open a community's hub and select Open app, or select an app under Pinned apps on Home. Inside it, select the Homeroom logo to open its menu.
guide.start.open.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Open app" is a button on a community's hub; "Pinned apps" is the name of a section of the Home screen.

guide.start.suggest.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the third step for someone new.

guide.start.suggest.body.text: In that menu, select Suggest an improvement. Tap the part of the page you mean and say what should change. It is posted as a request on the project's Workshop.
guide.start.suggest.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Suggest an improvement" is the name of the button in the Homeroom menu.

guide.places.heading.description: Small label over the card of Settings > User guide that explains the main places in Homeroom.

guide.place.communities.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide, about communities.

guide.place.communities.body.text: A community is the people behind a project. It shows as Just you, Private community or Public community, depending on who can open it. Yours are on the Communities tab: the ones you pinned first, then the others you have joined. Each has a hub, a Workshop for the work going on, and channels to talk in. You need to join a community to suggest changes, vote and post there.
guide.place.communities.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Just you", "Private community" and "Public community" are the names shown on screen for who a community is for. "Communities" is the name of a tab in the main navigation. "Workshop" is the name of a place on a project's page.

guide.place.apps.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide, about the Pinned apps section of the home screen. Same words as that section's heading.

guide.place.apps.body.text: Pinned apps on Home holds the apps you pin and the ones you help build. Select one to open it. To start your own project, select New project: it asks what the app should do and what to call it, then makes it, just for you until you invite people.
guide.place.apps.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Pinned apps" is a section of the Home screen; "New project" is the control on Home that starts a project.

guide.place.appMenu.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide, about the menu behind the Homeroom logo inside an app.

guide.place.appMenu.body.text: Inside any app, select the Homeroom logo to open its menu. That is where you suggest an improvement or visit the app's community.
guide.place.appMenu.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide about the menu behind the Homeroom logo.

guide.place.suggest.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide. Same words as the button in the Homeroom menu.

guide.place.suggest.body.text: Select it in the Homeroom menu to ask for a change to the app or to Homeroom itself. Tap the spot on the page you mean and say what should change, or switch to the form. It is posted as a request on the project's Workshop.
