guide.place.suggest.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "It" is Suggest an improvement, named by the row title above it. "The form" is the written form the button can switch to.

guide.place.bot.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide, about the AI assistant. The bot's own name.

guide.place.bot.body.text: Homeroom bot is your AI assistant: ask it a question, have it build a change, file an idea or fix a bug. It has its own tab. New chat starts a conversation there, and the tab lists your chats with the bot beside the work you are part of across your projects. Messages is a separate tab, for your conversations with people.
guide.place.bot.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "New chat" is the name of the button on the Homeroom bot tab that starts a conversation with the bot. "Messages" is the name of a tab.

guide.place.you.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide, about the You tab and the Settings screen. "You" is the name of the tab.

guide.place.you.body.text: The You tab holds your profile, and Settings is on it. Settings is where you change your account, how Homeroom looks, your language and your notifications, and where you can replay the welcome tour.
guide.place.you.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "You" is the name of a tab.

guide.vote.heading.description: Small label over the card of Settings > User guide that explains, in five rows, how a change to an app goes live.

guide.vote.request.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the first step of how a change goes live.

guide.vote.request.body.text: A member asks for a change, with Suggest an improvement or by telling Homeroom bot. The request goes on the project's Workshop, where people can see it.
guide.vote.request.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Workshop" is the name of a place on a project's page.

guide.vote.build.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the first step of how a change goes live.

guide.vote.build.body.text: A change starts when a member builds it, with Homeroom bot or a coding agent. When the bot writes a plan for a request, any member can press Build it, and the bot's building time comes out of that member's week. You can see yours in Settings, under AI usage & models.
guide.vote.build.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Build it" is the button on the bot's plan. "AI usage & models" is the name of a page in Settings. "Week" means the weekly allowance of the bot's building time.

guide.vote.up.title.text: It goes up for a vote
guide.vote.up.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the second step of how a change goes live.

guide.vote.up.body.text: When it is ready, the change goes up for a vote with a preview you can try. If it is waiting on you, it is listed under Needs you.
guide.vote.up.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Needs you" is the name of the list of things waiting on the person.

guide.vote.checks.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the third step of how a change goes live. "Checks" are automated tests.

guide.vote.checks.body.text: Homeroom runs automated checks on the preview. A change can't go live until they pass, however the vote goes.

guide.vote.rule.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the last step of how a change goes live. The rule is the project's rule for who has to approve a change.

guide.vote.rule.body.text: Each project has its own rule for who has to say yes: one person's yes can be enough, or it can take most of the group. Whoever manages a project can propose a new rule from Settings & rules in its ⋯ menu, and that goes to a vote under the current rule. Once the rule is met and the checks pass, the change goes live.
guide.vote.rule.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Settings & rules" is the name of a row in a project's ⋯ menu.

guide.compare.heading.description: Small label over a card of Settings > User guide that says when to use Suggest an improvement and when to ask Homeroom bot.

guide.compare.suggest.title.text: When you can point at it
guide.compare.suggest.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the case for Suggest an improvement.

guide.compare.suggest.body.text: Use Suggest an improvement when you can see what should change. Tap it on the page and say how. It goes straight to the project as a request.
guide.compare.suggest.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Suggest an improvement" is the name of the button in the Homeroom menu.

guide.compare.bot.title.text: When you want to talk it through
guide.compare.bot.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the case for asking Homeroom bot.

guide.compare.bot.body.text: Ask Homeroom bot when you have a question, want a change built, or are not sure yet what to ask for. It can file the request for you.
guide.compare.bot.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Homeroom bot" is the AI assistant's name.

guide.terms.heading.description: Small label over the card of Settings > User guide that explains words Homeroom uses, one per row.

guide.term.hub.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the name of a community's front page. Same word as on screen.

guide.term.hub.body.text: A community's front page: who it is for, who was active this week, what needs you and what went live lately.
guide.term.hub.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide, explaining the word "Hub".

guide.term.workshop.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the name of a place on a project's page. Same word as on screen.

guide.term.workshop.body.text: Where a project's work is: the requests, the changes being built and the ones waiting for a vote.
guide.term.workshop.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide, explaining the word "Workshop".

guide.term.channels.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the places on a project's page where members talk. Same word as on screen.

guide.term.channels.body.text: Where a community's members talk: #general, plus one for each topic the project has.
guide.term.channels.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide, explaining the word "Channels". "#general" is the name of a channel; keep it as it is.

guide.term.needsYou.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the name of the list of decisions waiting on the person. Same words as on screen.

guide.term.needsYou.body.text: Everything waiting on you, such as a vote or a question from Homeroom bot, across your projects in one place. Each project's page has its own.
guide.term.needsYou.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide, explaining "Needs you".

guide.term.newChat.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the name of the button that starts a conversation with Homeroom bot. Same words as on screen.

guide.term.newChat.body.text: How you start talking to Homeroom bot: on its tab, or from a project's Workshop, where it is already about that project. Each chat is its own thread that only you can see, listed on the bot's tab. News about a request is on the request's page instead.
guide.term.newChat.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide, explaining "New chat". "Workshop" is the name of a place on a project's page.

guide.term.justYou.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the name shown for a project only its maker is in. Same words as on screen.

guide.term.justYou.body.text: A project only you are in. Once someone you invite joins, it becomes a Private community.
guide.term.justYou.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide, explaining "Just you". "Private community" is a name shown on screen.

guide.term.private.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the name shown for a community only its members can open. Same words as on screen.

guide.term.private.body.text: Only its members can open it. People join when they are invited.
guide.term.private.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide, explaining "Private community".

guide.term.public.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: the name shown for a community anyone can open. Same words as on screen.

guide.term.public.body.text: Anyone can open it and join it.
guide.term.public.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide, explaining "Public community". "Open" and "join" are verbs.

guide.faq.heading.description: Small label over the card of Settings > User guide that answers common questions, one per row.

guide.faq.findApp.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: a question a person might ask.

guide.faq.findApp.body.text: Pinned apps holds the apps you pin or help build. For any other app, open its community from the Communities tab and select Open app on its hub. To keep it on Home, open the About entry in its Homeroom menu and choose Pin to Home.
guide.faq.findApp.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Pinned apps" is a name on the Home screen; "Communities" is the name of a tab in the main navigation; "Open app" and "Pin to Home" are the names of buttons. "The About entry" is the row of the Homeroom menu that tells about the app.

guide.faq.suggestion.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: a question a person might ask about a request they posted.

guide.faq.suggestion.body.text: Your requests are listed in the Homeroom bot tab. A request is posted only once you are online and send it. A private request can be seen only by platform admins.
guide.faq.suggestion.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Homeroom bot" is the name of a tab.

guide.faq.whoCan.title.text: Who can suggest, vote and post
guide.faq.whoCan.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: a question about who may take part in a community.

guide.faq.whoCan.body.text: You need to be a member of the community, and a project can ask for more: some let only invited people build, and a vote on a public project may need a verified account. Anyone can read a public community. A private community is joined by invitation. Which yeses a change needs is the project's own rule.
guide.faq.whoCan.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Yeses" are approving votes.

guide.faq.shortcuts.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide.

guide.faq.shortcuts.body.text: On a computer, press C on most screens, or inside an app, to comment on what you see. Your comments are posted as requests, each pinned to the spot you chose. Press C again to stop. In Settings, press / or Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac) to find a setting.
guide.faq.shortcuts.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. C, /, Ctrl+K and ⌘K are keys; keep them as they are.

guide.faq.problem.title.description: Row title in Settings > User guide: how to report a problem.

guide.faq.problem.body.text: Use Suggest an improvement and say what went wrong. Its form asks where it should go: this app, or the platform itself. You can also tell Homeroom bot.
guide.faq.problem.body.description: Paragraph in Settings > User guide. "Suggest an improvement" is the name of the button in the Homeroom menu.

about.title.description: Heading of the section in Settings that shows version numbers.

about.intro.text: Which build of each part of the platform you are running.
about.intro.description: Explanation under the About heading in Settings. "Build" is a noun: a released version of the software.

about.appVersion.label.description: Label of a row in Settings > About; the version of the app the person has open is shown at the other end of the row.

about.appVersion.deploying.description: Value on the "App version" row in Settings > About while a new version of the app is being released. Lower case, because it stands where a version number would.

about.appVersion.unknown.description: Value on the "App version" row in Settings > About when the app's version is not known. Lower case, because it stands where a version number would.

about.legal.title.description: Heading over four links in Settings > About, under the version rows: Homeroom's terms, its privacy notice, its child safety standards and how to delete your account.

about.legal.terms.description: Link in Settings > About, under the Legal heading: opens Homeroom's terms of use, and whether the person accepted them.

about.legal.privacy.description: Link in Settings > About, under the Legal heading: opens Homeroom's privacy notice, which says what personal data Homeroom collects and how it uses it, in a new tab.

about.legal.childSafety.description: Link in Settings > About, under the Legal heading, after the privacy notice: opens Homeroom's child safety standards, which say how it prevents and reports child sexual abuse and exploitation, in a new tab.

about.legal.accountDeletion.description: Link in Settings > About, under the Legal heading, last: opens the page explaining how to delete your Homeroom account and what happens to your data, in a new tab.

about.platformVersion.label.description: Label of a row in Settings > About; the version of Homeroom itself is shown at the other end of the row.

usernode.demoNote.description: Amber note at the top of a block of the Homeroom app pages in Settings on the test site: the values shown below it are made-up samples.

usernode.actionFailed.description: Brief message when a button or a tappable row on the Homeroom app pages in Settings failed and nothing more specific is known.

usernode.settingSaveFailed.description: Brief message when flipping a switch on the Homeroom app pages in Settings failed and nothing more specific is known.

usernode.connection.title.description: Heading of a block in Settings in the Homeroom mobile app: whether this screen can talk to the app it runs inside.

usernode.connection.intro.text: What this screen can reach in the app, and what to do when it can’t.
usernode.connection.intro.description: Explanation under the "Homeroom app: connection" heading in Settings.

usernode.connection.walletRecovery.text: No new mobile wallet is available for this account, so secure app sign-in did not finish. If you previously joined with email, you can connect that account’s wallet instead.
usernode.connection.walletRecovery.description: Amber notice in the "Homeroom app: connection" block in Settings when signing in to the mobile app could not finish; a button under it connects an existing wallet.

usernode.connection.copyDiagnostics.description: Button in the "Homeroom app: connection" block in Settings: copies technical details about the connection to the clipboard, to send to support.

usernode.body.loading.description: Shown in Settings in the Homeroom mobile app while the app's own settings are being read.

usernode.body.loadFailed.text: Could not load Homeroom app settings.

usernode.body.openNotificationSettings.description: Button on the Homeroom app pages in Settings: opens the phone's own notification settings for the Homeroom app (verb: open).

usernode.socialPush.title.description: Heading of a block in Settings in the Homeroom mobile app: notifications on the phone about activity in Homeroom.

usernode.socialPush.intro.text: Get a device notification about activity in Homeroom, such as a message, a vote that needs you or a build that is ready. Notification content is loaded only after you open Social.
usernode.socialPush.intro.description: Explanation under the "Homeroom app: activity notifications" heading in Settings. Social is the name of this part of the mobile app; a build is something Homeroom bot is building for the person.

usernode.socialPush.checking.description: Shown in the "Homeroom app: activity notifications" block in Settings while Homeroom checks whether those notifications are on.

usernode.socialPush.toggle.description: Label of the switch in the "Homeroom app: activity notifications" block in Settings: turns phone notifications about Homeroom activity on or off.

usernode.blockProduction.title.description: Heading of a block in Settings in the Homeroom mobile app about producing blocks for the blockchain network the app runs on.

usernode.blockProduction.intro.text: Producing blocks earns points. Access is released manually, so ask below and an admin will release your keys in batches.
usernode.blockProduction.intro.description: Explanation under the "Homeroom app: block production" heading in Settings. "Blocks" are blockchain blocks; "keys" are the person's cryptographic keys.

usernode.blockProduction.foregroundOnly.text: For now, your phone produces blocks only while Homeroom is open.
usernode.blockProduction.foregroundOnly.description: Temporary note in the "Homeroom app: block production" block in Settings. Background block production is paused, so the phone misses its turns while the app is closed.

usernode.blockProduction.checking.description: Shown in the "Homeroom app: block production" block in Settings while Homeroom checks whether this person may produce blocks.

usernode.blockProduction.ask.description: Button in the "Homeroom app: block production" block in Settings: sends the administrators a request to let this person produce blockchain blocks.

usernode.widgetIcons.title.description: Heading of a block in Settings in the Homeroom mobile app about the app icons shown in the phone's home-screen widget.

usernode.widgetIcons.intro.text: What the homescreen widget was told to show, and what it reports back.
usernode.widgetIcons.intro.description: Explanation under the "Homeroom app: widget icons" heading in Settings.

usernode.widgetIcons.recheck.description: Button in the "Homeroom app: widget icons" block in Settings: asks the home-screen widget again which app icons it is showing.

usernode.privacy.title.description: Heading of a block in Settings in the Homeroom mobile app about proving one's identity.

usernode.privacy.intro.text: Controls for the ZK passport identity flow.
usernode.privacy.intro.description: Explanation under the "Homeroom app: privacy & identity" heading in Settings. ZK passport is the name of the way the app verifies identity from a passport with zero-knowledge proofs.

usernode.diagnostics.title.description: Heading of a block in Settings in the Homeroom mobile app with troubleshooting tools.

usernode.diagnostics.intro.text: Debugging tools for the app and its embedded node.
usernode.diagnostics.intro.description: Explanation under the "Homeroom app: diagnostics" heading in Settings. The node is the blockchain node running inside the mobile app.

usernode.about.title.description: Heading of a block in Settings in the Homeroom mobile app with the app's version, legal documents and help.

usernode.account.title.description: Heading of a block in Settings in the Homeroom mobile app shown while the app is not yet signed in.

usernode.account.autoSignIn.text: The app signs in automatically with your platform account. If this message persists, try closing and reopening the app.
usernode.account.autoSignIn.description: Text of the "Homeroom app: account" block in Settings, shown while the mobile app is not yet signed in.

usernode.faq.heading.description: Small heading over the expandable help topics in the "Homeroom app: about & legal" block in Settings.

usernode.faq.about.title.description: Title of an expandable help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings: what the network behind the app is.

usernode.faq.about.network.text: Your device is part of a new network. It verifies, executes, and contributes compute directly to the network, passively in the background - with no central servers, no hidden infra. As long as users keep the app running, the network will continue to operate, peer to peer, with no external dependencies.
usernode.faq.about.network.description: First paragraph of the About help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings. "Compute" means computing power; "infra" is short for infrastructure.

usernode.faq.about.why.text: We're doing this to enable networks that can be hosted end-to-end by their own communities - both for decentralization, and to enable a natural coordination point around participation, where users who help operate and contribute to systems directly realize the benefits from it.
usernode.faq.about.why.description: Second paragraph of the About help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings: why the network is run by its users' devices.

usernode.faq.about.testnet.text: Right now we are in testnet as we validate the core layer: block production, consensus behavior, and network reliability. As these stabilize, we'll build upon the unique features of the platform - its decentralization, zero knowledge proofs, and sybil-resistant identity - to introduce new activities, coordination mechanisms, and tools for self-hosted, sybil-resistant communities.
usernode.faq.about.testnet.description: Third paragraph of the About help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings. Testnet is a blockchain's test network; "sybil-resistant" means protected against one person posing as many.

usernode.faq.about.thanks.text: Thanks for helping test at this early stage. The app right now is simple, but as we prove out the core functionality, we hope to make possible a new kind of community-owned network, where users can directly run and benefit from the networks they use.
usernode.faq.about.thanks.description: Last paragraph of the About help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.title.description: Title of an expandable help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings. Block Production is the app feature that produces blockchain blocks.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.lead.text: This feature automatically wakes your device to produce blockchain blocks when your node wins a slot. Here's how it works:
usernode.faq.blockProduction.lead.description: First paragraph of the "What is Block Production?" help topic in Settings; four numbered steps follow. A slot is a moment at which one node is chosen to produce a block.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.selection.text: 1. VRF Selection: each epoch, the network randomly selects which validators will produce blocks using Verifiable Random Function (VRF).
usernode.faq.blockProduction.selection.description: Step 1 of 4 in the "What is Block Production?" help topic in Settings. Keep the number. VRF and Verifiable Random Function are technical terms; an epoch is a fixed period of the blockchain.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.scheduling.text: 2. Slot Scheduling: when you win slots, the app schedules alarms to wake your device ~1 minute before each slot.
usernode.faq.blockProduction.scheduling.description: Step 2 of 4 in the "What is Block Production?" help topic in Settings. Keep the number; "~1 minute" means about one minute.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.production.text: 3. Block Production: at slot time, the app monitors your node and ensures the block is produced.
usernode.faq.blockProduction.production.description: Step 3 of 4 in the "What is Block Production?" help topic in Settings. Keep the number.

usernode.faq.blockProduction.tracking.text: 4. Success Tracking: results are recorded to track your reliability over time.
usernode.faq.blockProduction.tracking.description: Step 4 of 4 in the "What is Block Production?" help topic in Settings. Keep the number.

usernode.faq.platform.title.description: Title of an expandable help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings: how reliably block production works on this kind of phone. "Platform" means Android or iOS.

usernode.faq.platform.androidHow.text: Uses Android's exact alarm system (AlarmManager) to wake your device precisely when needed for block production.
usernode.faq.platform.androidHow.description: First paragraph of the "Platform & Reliability" help topic in Settings on an Android phone. AlarmManager is the name of an Android component; keep it.

usernode.faq.platform.androidModes.text: Reliability by mode: Default (Event-Driven) 90-95%, battery-efficient, wakes only during slot windows. Keep-Alive Mode 100%, persistent service, higher battery (~5-10%/hr).
usernode.faq.platform.androidModes.description: Second paragraph of the "Platform & Reliability" help topic in Settings on an Android phone: the two modes and how often each produces its blocks. "Default (Event-Driven)" and "Keep-Alive Mode" are mode names; "%/hr" is percent of battery per hour.

usernode.faq.platform.iosHow.text: Uses a combination of background tasks and keep-alive mode to wake your device for block production.
usernode.faq.platform.iosHow.description: First paragraph of the "Platform & Reliability" help topic in Settings on an iPhone.

usernode.faq.platform.iosModes.text: Reliability by mode: Keep-Alive Mode 99%, app stays awake in foreground, requires charger. Background Only 40-60%, iOS controls execution, not guaranteed.
usernode.faq.platform.iosModes.description: Second paragraph of the "Platform & Reliability" help topic in Settings on an iPhone: the two modes and how often each produces its blocks. "Keep-Alive Mode" and "Background Only" are mode names.

usernode.faq.platform.device.description: Last line of the "Platform & Reliability" help topic in Settings on an Android phone. {{manufacturer}} is the name of the phone's maker, such as Samsung.

usernode.faq.vrf.title.description: Title of an expandable help topic in the Homeroom app pages of Settings. VRF (Verifiable Random Function) is a technical term; a slot is a moment at which one node is chosen to produce a block.

usernode.faq.vrf.what.text: VRF (Verifiable Random Function) is how the network fairly selects block producers. At the start of each epoch, the network runs VRF calculations to determine which validators will produce blocks in upcoming slots.
usernode.faq.vrf.what.description: First paragraph of the "Understanding VRF & Slots" help topic in Settings.

usernode.faq.vrf.statuses.text: Status meanings. Pending: waiting for epoch transition to start calculations. Calculating: VRF evaluation in progress (takes a few hours). Complete: slot assignments are finalized and scheduled.
usernode.faq.vrf.statuses.description: Second paragraph of the "Understanding VRF & Slots" help topic in Settings: what the three statuses Pending, Calculating and Complete mean.

usernode.faq.vrf.winning.text: When VRF selects your node to produce a block at a specific time, you've "won" that slot. Your responsibility is to have your device awake and connected so the block can be produced.
usernode.faq.vrf.winning.description: Third paragraph of the "Understanding VRF & Slots" help topic in Settings.

usernode.faq.vrf.timing.text: Why timing matters: each slot has a ~5-seconds window. If your device doesn't wake up in time or loses network connectivity, the slot is missed and counted as "failed."
usernode.faq.vrf.timing.description: Last paragraph of the "Understanding VRF & Slots" help topic in Settings. "~5-seconds" means about five seconds.

signOut.nativeShutdownNotice.text: Signed out. Close and reopen the app to finish shutting down Homeroom.
signOut.nativeShutdownNotice.description: Toast shown on the landing page after signing out in the phone app, when the app could not finish closing itself down. Homeroom is the product name.

signOut.signingOut.description: Label of the Sign out button in Settings while the sign-out is in progress.

connectors.copy.urlCopied.description: Toast after pressing Copy beside the connector address in Settings > Connectors. MCP is the protocol name; keep it.

connectors.copy.urlFailed.text: Could not copy the MCP server URL
connectors.copy.urlFailed.description: Error toast when the connector address in Settings > Connectors could not be copied to the clipboard. MCP is the protocol name; keep it.

connectors.copy.personalRulesCopied.description: Toast after copying the block of permission rules meant for a person's own Claude Code settings file, in Settings > Connectors. Keep the file path exactly.

connectors.copy.personalRulesFailed.text: Could not copy the allow rules
connectors.copy.personalRulesFailed.description: Error toast when the block of permission ("allow") rules for a person's own Claude Code settings file could not be copied, in Settings > Connectors.

connectors.copy.repoRulesCopied.text: Copied. Commit it as .claude/settings.json in your app repo
connectors.copy.repoRulesCopied.description: Toast after copying the block of permission rules meant to be committed into an app's code repository, in Settings > Connectors. Keep the file path exactly; "repo" is short for repository.

connectors.copy.repoRulesFailed.text: Could not copy the allow rules
connectors.copy.repoRulesFailed.description: Error toast when the block of permission ("allow") rules meant for an app's code repository could not be copied, in Settings > Connectors.

connectors.copy.codexCommandCopied.text: Copied. Run it in a terminal where Codex is installed
connectors.copy.codexCommandCopied.description: Toast after copying the terminal command that adds Homeroom to the Codex command-line tool, in Settings > Connectors. Codex is a product name.

connectors.copy.codexCommandFailed.text: Could not copy the Codex command
connectors.copy.codexCommandFailed.description: Error toast when the terminal command for the Codex command-line tool could not be copied, in Settings > Connectors. Codex is a product name.

connectors.copy.codexConfigCopied.description: Toast after copying the configuration entry for the Codex command-line tool, in Settings > Connectors. Keep the file path exactly.

connectors.copy.codexConfigFailed.text: Could not copy the Codex config entry
connectors.copy.codexConfigFailed.description: Error toast when the configuration-file entry for the Codex command-line tool could not be copied, in Settings > Connectors. Codex is a product name.

copyControl.failed.description: Shown briefly in place of a Copy button in Settings > Connectors when copying to the clipboard did not work.

alerts.test.queueing.description: Status under the "Send a test alert" button in Settings > Notifications while the request is being sent.

alerts.test.countdown.queued_one.text: Alert in {{count}}s. Phone push queued. Background or close the mobile app to check for a notification.
alerts.test.countdown.queued_one.description: Status under the "Send a test alert" button in Settings > Notifications, updated every second while the test counts down to the moment the push notification is sent to the phone. {{count}} is the seconds left; "s" abbreviates seconds.

alerts.test.countdown.queued_other.text: Alert in {{count}}s. Phone push queued. Background or close the mobile app to check for a notification.
alerts.test.countdown.queued_other.description: Status under the "Send a test alert" button in Settings > Notifications, updated every second while the test counts down to the moment the push notification is sent to the phone. {{count}} is the seconds left; "s" abbreviates seconds.

alerts.test.after.queued.text: The test push is queued for delivery. Check your phone; delivery may take a few more seconds.
alerts.test.after.queued.description: Status under the "Send a test alert" button in Settings > Notifications once the countdown ends and a push notification was queued for the phone.

alerts.test.after.preferenceDisabled.text: Phone push was not queued. Turn on Your coding agent under Mobile push categories and try again.
alerts.test.after.preferenceDisabled.description: Status under the "Send a test alert" button in Settings > Notifications when no phone push was sent because the "Your coding agent" category is switched off under "Mobile push categories" on the same page. Translate both names as they are translated there.

alerts.test.after.unavailable.text: Phone push was not queued. Sign in on your phone and enable Activity notifications and notification permission. Push delivery must also be available on the server.
alerts.test.after.unavailable.description: Status under the "Send a test alert" button in Settings > Notifications when no phone push could be sent because no phone is registered for it. "Activity notifications" is the name of a switch in the phone app.

alerts.test.failed.text: Could not queue the test push. Please try again.
alerts.test.failed.description: Error under the "Send a test alert" button in Settings > Notifications when the request failed and the server gave no reason.

screen.title.description: Title of the Settings screen in the header (noun: the place where preferences live).

connectors.setupPrompt.text: I want to add a custom MCP connector. The server URL is {{url}} and it uses dynamic client registration, so there is no client ID or secret to enter. Name it exactly "homeroom". Walk me through it one step at a time and tell me what to click.
connectors.setupPrompt.description: Not shown in Homeroom: a request written in the person's voice, pre-filled into a new Claude or ChatGPT chat by the "set it up" links in Settings > Connectors. {{url}} is the connector address. Keep "homeroom" exactly, in lower case, and keep "MCP".

connectors.load.failed.description: Error in Settings > Connectors when the list of chat apps connected to the account could not be loaded.

connectors.load.invalid.description: Error in Settings > Connectors when the server answered the list of connected chat apps in a form Homeroom could not read.

connectors.hint.notSentYet.text: Homeroom has not sent you this tip in chat yet. It rides along on the first read it answers in a new conversation.
connectors.hint.notSentYet.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Shown when the tip has never been sent. "Read" is a noun here: a request to read data that Homeroom answers.

connectors.hint.sent_one.text: Homeroom sent you this tip in chat once in the last {{days}} days, most recently {{when}}.
connectors.hint.sent_one.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. How often it was sent. {{count}} is the number of times (1 here), {{days}} the length of the window in days, {{when}} a date and time. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

connectors.hint.sent_other.text: Homeroom sent you this tip in chat {{count}} times in the last {{days}} days, most recently {{when}}.
connectors.hint.sent_other.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. How often it was sent. {{count}} is the number of times, {{days}} the length of the window in days, {{when}} a date and time.

connectors.hint.sentWhenUnknown_one.text: Homeroom sent you this tip in chat once in the last {{days}} days, most recently recently.
connectors.hint.sentWhenUnknown_one.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. How often it was sent, when the time of the last one is not known. {{count}} is the number of times (1 here), {{days}} the length of the window in days. The English repeats "recently" by accident of the fallback; write a natural sentence. {{count}} is available in this form too, although English does not show it: a language whose singular form is also used for 21 or 101 should print the number.

connectors.hint.sentWhenUnknown_other.text: Homeroom sent you this tip in chat {{count}} times in the last {{days}} days, most recently recently.
connectors.hint.sentWhenUnknown_other.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. How often it was sent, when the time of the last one is not known. {{count}} is the number of times, {{days}} the length of the window in days. The English repeats "recently" by accident of the fallback; write a natural sentence.

connectors.hint.limitReached.text: That is the limit of {{limit}} per connection per {{days}} days; it will come back once the window rolls over.
connectors.hint.limitReached.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Follows the sentence saying how often the tip was sent, when it has reached its maximum. {{limit}} is the maximum number of times, {{days}} the length of the window in days. "It" is the tip.

connectors.hint.quietUntilToday.text: It stays quiet for {{minutes}} minutes after each one, so a conversation opened before today at {{time}} will not carry it. One opened after that will.
connectors.hint.quietUntilToday.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Follows the sentence saying how often the tip was sent, while a pause after the last one is still running and ends today. {{minutes}} is the length of the pause, {{time}} a clock time. "It" is the tip; "one" is a tip, then a conversation.

connectors.hint.quietUntilDate.text: It stays quiet for {{minutes}} minutes after each one, so a conversation opened before {{when}} will not carry it. One opened after that will.
connectors.hint.quietUntilDate.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Follows the sentence saying how often the tip was sent, while a pause after the last one is still running and ends on another day. {{minutes}} is the length of the pause, {{when}} a date and time. "It" is the tip.

connectors.hint.openNewConversation.text: Open a new conversation to see it again.
connectors.hint.openNewConversation.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Follows the sentence saying how often the tip was sent, when nothing prevents it from being sent again. "Open" is a verb; "it" is the tip.

connectors.hint.summaryAndAdvice.description: Status line under the "stop the permission prompts" advice in Settings > Connectors, about the tip Homeroom adds to its answers in a chat app (Claude, ChatGPT) telling the person how to stop those prompts. Puts two complete sentences one after the other: {{summary}} says how often the tip was sent, {{advice}} says when it will be sent again. Change only the spacing or order if your language needs it.

connectors.tool.status.working.description: Status word on an AI tool's card in Settings > Connectors: it is connected and has used Homeroom.

connectors.tool.status.unused.description: Status word on an AI tool's card in Settings > Connectors: it is connected, but has not called Homeroom since.

connectors.tool.status.attention.description: Status word on an AI tool's card in Settings > Connectors, beside an amber dot: its sign-in ran out and it has to be connected again.

connectors.tool.status.none.description: Status word on an AI tool's card in Settings > Connectors: this account has no connection from it.

connectors.row.lastActive.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors. {{lastUsed}} is a date with time.

connectors.row.notUsedYet.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors when the tool has not called Homeroom since connecting. {{connected}} is a date with time.

connectors.row.unknownDate.text: Connected on an unknown date · not used yet
connectors.row.unknownDate.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors when the date it was connected is not known and it has not been used.

connectors.row.expired.text: Sign-in ran out {{when}}. Follow the steps to connect again.
connectors.row.expired.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors when its sign-in has ended. {{when}} is a date with time. The steps are that tool's setup steps on the same card.

connectors.row.expiredUnknownDate.text: Sign-in ran out. Follow the steps to connect again.
connectors.row.expiredUnknownDate.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors when its sign-in has ended and the date is not known. The steps are that tool's setup steps on the same card.

connectors.row.expiredReconnect.text: Sign-in ran out {{when}}. Reconnect to use it again.
connectors.row.expiredReconnect.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors when its sign-in has ended and the tool can sign in again from one step of its setup (Claude, Codex). {{when}} is a date with time. Reconnect is the button under this line.

connectors.row.expiredReconnectUnknownDa.text: Sign-in ran out. Reconnect to use it again.
connectors.row.expiredReconnectUnknownDa.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors when its sign-in has ended, the date is not known, and the tool can sign in again from one step of its setup (Claude, Codex). Reconnect is the button under this line.

connectors.capabilities.readWrite.text: Can read your apps and send proposals
connectors.capabilities.readWrite.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors: what the person approved this connection to do.

connectors.capabilities.read.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors: what the person approved this connection to do.

connectors.capabilities.write.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors: what the person approved this connection to do.

connectors.capabilities.expiredReadWrite.text: Could read your apps and send proposals
connectors.capabilities.expiredReadWrite.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors whose sign-in has ended: what it was approved to do until then.

connectors.capabilities.expiredRead.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors whose sign-in has ended: what it was approved to do until then.

connectors.capabilities.expiredWrite.description: Line on a connection's row in Settings > Connectors whose sign-in has ended: what it was approved to do until then.

connectors.progress.done.description: Line above the numbered steps of an open setup guide in Settings > Connectors, after the person ticks a step. {{done}} is how many steps they marked done, {{total}} how many the guide has.

connectors.progress.tickAria.description: Screen reader label of the toggle on a setup guide's step in Settings > Connectors, announced as pressed or not pressed. {{n}} is the step's number.

connectors.row.unnamedClient.description: Title of a connection's row in Settings > Connectors when the app gave no name. "Client" is a program connected to Homeroom, not a customer.

connectors.disconnect.failedRetry.description: Error in Settings > Connectors when the server refused to disconnect a chat app from the account.

connectors.disconnect.done.description: Confirmation in Settings > Connectors after a chat app was disconnected from the account.

connectors.disconnect.failed.description: Error in Settings > Connectors when disconnecting a chat app failed and there is no more specific reason.

connectors.rename.fieldLabel.description: Screen-reader label of the text field that renames a connection, under its row in Settings > Connectors. {{tool}} is the AI tool's own name, such as "Claude (claude.ai)".

connectors.rename.note.text: Only you see this name. Save it empty to show {{tool}} again.
connectors.rename.note.description: Note under the text field that renames a connection in Settings > Connectors. {{tool}} is the AI tool's own name, such as "Claude (claude.ai)", which the row shows when the person has given no name.

connectors.rename.done.description: Confirmation in Settings > Connectors after the person saved their own name for a connection.

connectors.rename.cleared.description: Confirmation in Settings > Connectors after the person saved an empty name for a connection, so its row shows the AI tool's own name again.

connectors.rename.tooLong.text: A name can be up to {{max}} characters.
connectors.rename.tooLong.description: Error in Settings > Connectors when the name typed for a connection is too long. {{max}} is the largest number of characters allowed, 60.

connectors.rename.failedRetry.description: Error in Settings > Connectors when saving the person's name for a connection failed.

socialIdentity.load.failed.text: Could not load social accounts. Try again shortly.
socialIdentity.load.failed.description: Error in Settings > Linked accounts. when the list of connected GitHub and X accounts could not be loaded.

socialIdentity.perWeek.description: An amount of AI credits per week, in US dollars, in the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. {{amount}} is a number such as 50 or 2.50. Keep the dollar sign.

socialIdentity.tier.unavailable.title.description: Title of the first row of the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. when Homeroom could not check how many credits the account has.

socialIdentity.tier.unavailable.note.text: We could not check your credits, so calls we pay for are paused. Your own API key still works.
socialIdentity.tier.unavailable.note.description: Note under the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. when the credits could not be checked. "Calls" are requests to an AI model; "we" is Homeroom.

socialIdentity.tier.legacy.title.description: Title of the first row of the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. on a server where connecting an account does not change the amount.

socialIdentity.tier.legacy.note.text: Your credits do not depend on a connected account yet.
socialIdentity.tier.legacy.note.description: Note under the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. on a server where connecting GitHub or X does not change the weekly AI credits.

socialIdentity.tier.override.title.description: Title of the first row of the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. for an account whose amount an administrator set by hand.

socialIdentity.tier.override.note.text: An administrator set this amount. A connected account does not change it.
socialIdentity.tier.override.note.description: Note under the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. for an account whose weekly AI credits an administrator set by hand.

socialIdentity.tier.signedIn.title.description: Title of the first row of the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. the credits a person gets just for being signed in, before connecting GitHub or X. A state, not an action.

socialIdentity.tier.signedIn.note.text: Either one is enough. Connecting both does not add more.
socialIdentity.tier.signedIn.note.description: Note under the weekly-credits list in Settings > Linked accounts. "Either one" means a GitHub account or an X account; connecting one raises the weekly credits.

socialIdentity.row.reconnectRequired.text: Linked for GitHub attribution. Reconnect once to count it toward weekly credits.
socialIdentity.row.reconnectRequired.description: Amber state text on the GitHub row in Settings > Linked accounts. the account is linked only so code changes are credited to it, and must be connected again before it raises the weekly credits.

socialIdentity.row.noExtraCredits.description: State text on the second connected account's row in Settings > Linked accounts. the first connected account already raised the weekly credits, and this one adds nothing.

socialIdentity.row.notSetUp.text: Not set up on this server.
socialIdentity.row.notSetUp.description: State text on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. when this Homeroom server has no configuration for connecting that provider.

socialIdentity.row.notConnected.description: State text on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. when the person has not connected that account.

socialIdentity.badge.reconnectNeeded.description: Amber badge on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. the account is linked but must be connected again before it counts.

socialIdentity.badge.connected.description: Green badge on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. the account is connected. A state, not an action.

socialIdentity.row.linkedAt.description: Detail on a connected GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. when the account was connected. {{when}} is a date with time. Lower case: it is a detail, not a sentence.

socialIdentity.row.noTokenGithub.text: Homeroom holds no GitHub access token for your account.
socialIdentity.row.noTokenGithub.description: Reassurance on the GitHub row in Settings > Linked accounts. Homeroom only confirmed who the person is and cannot act on GitHub for them. An access token is a credential.

socialIdentity.row.noTokenX.text: Homeroom stores no X access token for your account.
socialIdentity.row.noTokenX.description: Reassurance on the X row in Settings > Linked accounts. Homeroom only confirmed who the person is and cannot act on X for them. An access token is a credential.

socialIdentity.action.reconnect.description: Button on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. starts signing in at that provider again for an account that is linked but no longer counts.

socialIdentity.action.connect.description: Button on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. verb: starts signing in at that provider to connect the account to Homeroom.

socialIdentity.action.refreshHandle.description: Button on a connected GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. reads the account's current @name from the provider again, after it was renamed there.

socialIdentity.action.changeAccount.description: Button on a connected GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. verb: replaces the connected account with a different account at the same provider.

socialIdentity.row.strandedAttempt.text: Your last {{provider}} connection attempt didn't complete. Try Connect again. This can happen if the browser did not reach the sign-in page or the flow was cancelled. If {{provider}} reports a callback or redirect address error, ask an administrator to check its OAuth settings.
socialIdentity.row.strandedAttempt.description: Note on the GitHub or X row in Settings > Linked accounts. when an earlier attempt to connect was started and never finished. "Connect" is the name of the button on the same row. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.diagnostics.sourceWaitlis.description: Administrator-only line in Settings > Linked accounts. which client credentials Homeroom uses to talk to the provider: the ones registered for the waitlist sign-up. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.diagnostics.sourceDedicat.text: Dedicated {{provider}} credentials, same app as the waitlist pair.
socialIdentity.diagnostics.sourceDedicat.description: Administrator-only line in Settings > Linked accounts. the credentials are configured separately for this feature but belong to the same developer app as the waitlist sign-up's pair. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".
Administrator-only line in Settings > Linked accounts. Homeroom uses credentials of a developer app registered only for this feature. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.diagnostics.sourceMissing.text: No complete {{provider}} credential pair is configured.
socialIdentity.diagnostics.sourceMissing.description: Administrator-only line in Settings > Linked accounts. the client ID or secret for the provider is missing on this server. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.diagnostics.callbackWarni.text: If this address isn’t registered as a callback URI on the {{provider}} developer app, {{provider}} shows "Something went wrong" before sign-in and never redirects back here.
socialIdentity.diagnostics.callbackWarni.description: Administrator-only warning in Settings > Linked accounts. under the callback address the provider must have on file. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X". "Something went wrong" is the provider's own English error text.

socialIdentity.callback.linked.description: Status line in Settings > Linked accounts after returning from signing in at GitHub or X: the account was connected. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.callback.refreshed.description: Status line in Settings > Linked accounts after returning from signing in at GitHub or X: the account's @name was read again. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.callback.confirm.text: Another {{provider}} account was verified. Review the replacement below before anything changes.
socialIdentity.callback.confirm.description: Status line in Settings > Linked accounts after returning from signing in at GitHub or X: the person signed in with a different account than the connected one, and must confirm the swap in the panel below. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.callback.inUse.text: That {{provider}} account is already linked to another Homeroom account. Your current connection is unchanged.
socialIdentity.callback.inUse.description: Status line in Settings > Linked accounts after returning from signing in at GitHub or X: the account belongs to someone else's Homeroom account. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.callback.differentAccount.text: That is a different {{provider}} account. Use Change account instead; your current connection is unchanged.
socialIdentity.callback.differentAccount.description: Status line in Settings > Linked accounts after returning from signing in at GitHub or X: the person signed in with another account while only refreshing. "Change account" is the name of a button on the same row. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.callback.conflict.text: That {{provider}} account could not be used. Your current connection is unchanged.
socialIdentity.callback.conflict.description: Status line in Settings > Linked accounts after returning from signing in at GitHub or X: the account could not be connected because of a conflict. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.callback.denied.description: Status line in Settings > Linked accounts after returning from signing in at GitHub or X: the person cancelled at the provider. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.callback.callbackMismatch.text: {{provider}} did not accept Homeroom’s callback address, so nothing changed. Ask an administrator to register this site’s callback URL ({{origin}}) on the {{provider}} OAuth app.
socialIdentity.callback.callbackMismatch.description: Status line in Settings > Linked accounts after returning from signing in at GitHub or X: the provider refused because this server's return address is not registered with it. {{origin}} is this site's address. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.callback.error.text: {{provider}} could not be connected. Try again.
socialIdentity.callback.error.description: Status line in Settings > Linked accounts after returning from signing in at GitHub or X: connecting failed for an unspecified reason. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.callback.accountMismatch.text: This browser is signed into a different Homeroom account than the app. Sign out here, then tap Connect again in the app and sign in with the same account.
socialIdentity.callback.accountMismatch.description: Status line in Settings > Linked accounts after returning from signing in at GitHub or X: the phone app started the connection, but the browser it opened is signed in to another Homeroom account. "Connect" is a button name; "the app" is the Homeroom phone app.

socialIdentity.unlink.confirmTitle.description: Title of the confirmation dialog before disconnecting a GitHub or X account in Settings > Linked accounts. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.unlink.confirmMessage.text: This removes {{provider}} from your public profile and may change your weekly credit eligibility.
socialIdentity.unlink.confirmMessage.description: Body of the confirmation dialog before disconnecting a GitHub or X account in Settings > Linked accounts. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.unlink.confirmButton.description: Red confirm button in the dialog that disconnects a GitHub or X account from the Homeroom account, in Settings > Linked accounts.

socialIdentity.unlink.failedProvider.description: Error in Settings > Linked accounts. when disconnecting the account failed. {{provider}} is "GitHub" or "X".

socialIdentity.unlink.failed.description: Error in Settings > Linked accounts. when disconnecting a GitHub or X account failed and there is no more specific message.

cliTokens.load.failed.description: Error in Settings > CLI access when the list of command-line credentials could not be loaded. CLI means command-line interface.

cliTokens.load.invalid.text: The credential list response was invalid.
cliTokens.load.invalid.description: Error in Settings > CLI access when the server answered the list of command-line credentials in a form Homeroom could not read.

cliTokens.row.statusUnknown.description: Stands in for a command-line credential's state in its row in Settings > CLI access when the server gave none. Lower case: it starts a detail line such as "unknown · created …".

cliTokens.row.createdUsed.description: Second line of a command-line credential's row in Settings > CLI access. {{status}} is the server's word for the credential's state, such as "valid" or "revoked", shown as it is; {{created}} and {{lastUsed}} are dates with times.

cliTokens.row.created.description: Second line of a command-line credential's row in Settings > CLI access. {{status}} is the server's word for the credential's state, such as "valid" or "revoked", shown as it is; {{created}} is a date with time. Shown when the credential has not been used.

cliTokens.row.unknownDateUsed.description: Second line of a command-line credential's row in Settings > CLI access. {{status}} is the server's word for the credential's state, such as "valid" or "revoked", shown as it is; {{lastUsed}} is a date with time. Shown when the creation date is not known.

cliTokens.row.unknownDate.description: Second line of a command-line credential's row in Settings > CLI access. {{status}} is the server's word for the credential's state, such as "valid" or "revoked", shown as it is; shown when the creation date is not known and the credential has not been used.

cliTokens.row.unnamed.description: Title of a command-line credential's row in Settings > CLI access when the server gave no hint of which token it is. CLI means command-line interface.

cliTokens.demoData.text: Demo data: changes are not saved.
cliTokens.demoData.description: Note under the list of command-line credentials in Settings when the rows are sample data on a preview server.

cliTokens.revoke.failed.description: Error in Settings > CLI access when revoking (cancelling) a command-line credential failed.

cliTokens.revoke.done.description: Confirmation in Settings > CLI access after a command-line credential was revoked and can no longer be used.

mobilePush.invalidResponse.description: Reason shown after "Could not load mobile push preferences:" or "Could not save:" in Settings > Notifications, when the server's answer could not be read.

mobilePush.incompleteResponse.description: Reason shown after "Could not load mobile push preferences:" or "Could not save:" in Settings > Notifications, when the server's answer lacked one of the categories on screen.

mobilePush.saved.description: Status under the list of phone push notification categories in Settings > Notifications: the switches shown are what is saved for the account, on every device.

mobilePush.saving.description: Status under the list of phone push notification categories in Settings > Notifications while a changed switch is being saved.

mobilePush.loadFailed.text: Could not load mobile push preferences: {{reason}}
mobilePush.loadFailed.description: Error under the list of phone push notification categories in Settings > Notifications. {{reason}} is the server's message or a technical code such as "HTTP 500".

mobilePush.saveFailed.description: Error under the list of phone push notification categories in Settings > Notifications when a changed switch could not be saved. {{reason}} is the server's message or a technical code such as "HTTP 500".

mobilePush.saveFailedToast.text: Could not save mobile push preferences
mobilePush.saveFailedToast.description: Toast shown when a changed phone push notification category in Settings > Notifications could not be saved.

apiKey.field.replacePlaceholder.text: Paste a new key to replace
apiKey.field.replacePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the Anthropic API key field in Settings when a key is already saved: pasting another one replaces it.

apiKey.button.replace.description: Button beside the Anthropic API key field in Settings when a key is already saved: saves the pasted key in place of the old one.

apiKey.status.pasteFirst.description: Error under the Anthropic API key field in Settings when Save was pressed with the field empty.

apiKey.status.verifying.description: Status under the Anthropic API key field in Settings while the pasted key is being checked. Anthropic is a company name.

apiKey.status.saveFailed.description: Error under the Anthropic API key field in Settings when the key could not be saved and the server gave no reason.

apiKey.status.saved.text: Saved. Once your weekly allowance runs out, AI features bill to your Anthropic account.
apiKey.status.saved.description: Confirmation under the Anthropic API key field in Settings: from now on AI usage is charged to the person's own Anthropic account. "Bill" is a verb.

apiKey.status.networkError.description: Error under the Anthropic API key field in Settings when the request did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

openrouter.included.activeWeekly.text: Active. It carries the platform's {{amount}} weekly allowance.
openrouter.included.activeWeekly.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is working. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00. The amount renews every week.

openrouter.included.activeWeeklyWithKey.text: Active (sk-or-…{{last4}}). It carries the platform's {{amount}} weekly allowance.
openrouter.included.activeWeeklyWithKey.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is working. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00; {{last4}} is the last four characters of the key, and "sk-or-…" is the start every such key has. Keep the parentheses and that prefix. The amount renews every week.

openrouter.included.activeDaily.text: Active. It carries a {{amount}} daily limit until it is moved to the platform's weekly allowance.
openrouter.included.activeDaily.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is working. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00. This older key still has a limit that renews every day.

openrouter.included.activeDailyWithKey.text: Active (sk-or-…{{last4}}). It carries a {{amount}} daily limit until it is moved to the platform's weekly allowance.
openrouter.included.activeDailyWithKey.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is working. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00; {{last4}} is the last four characters of the key, and "sk-or-…" is the start every such key has. Keep the parentheses and that prefix. This older key still has a limit that renews every day.

openrouter.included.activeMonthly.text: Active. It carries a {{amount}} monthly limit until it is moved to the platform's weekly allowance.
openrouter.included.activeMonthly.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is working. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00. This older key still has a limit that renews every month.

openrouter.included.activeMonthlyWithKey.text: Active (sk-or-…{{last4}}). It carries a {{amount}} monthly limit until it is moved to the platform's weekly allowance.
openrouter.included.activeMonthlyWithKey.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is working. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00; {{last4}} is the last four characters of the key, and "sk-or-…" is the start every such key has. Keep the parentheses and that prefix. This older key still has a limit that renews every month.

openrouter.included.activeLimit.text: Active. It carries a {{amount}} limit until it is moved to the platform's weekly allowance.
openrouter.included.activeLimit.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is working. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00. This older key has a limit that never renews.

openrouter.included.activeLimitWithKey.text: Active (sk-or-…{{last4}}). It carries a {{amount}} limit until it is moved to the platform's weekly allowance.
openrouter.included.activeLimitWithKey.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is working. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00; {{last4}} is the last four characters of the key, and "sk-or-…" is the start every such key has. Keep the parentheses and that prefix. This older key has a limit that never renews.

openrouter.included.activeOther.text: Active. It carries a {{amount}} {{cadence}} limit until it is moved to the platform's weekly allowance.
openrouter.included.activeOther.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is working. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00. {{cadence}} is the provider's own English word for how often the limit renews, shown as it is; this form is a fallback for a word Homeroom does not know.

openrouter.included.activeOtherWithKey.text: Active (sk-or-…{{last4}}). It carries a {{amount}} {{cadence}} limit until it is moved to the platform's weekly allowance.
openrouter.included.activeOtherWithKey.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is working. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00; {{last4}} is the last four characters of the key, and "sk-or-…" is the start every such key has. Keep the parentheses and that prefix. {{cadence}} is the provider's own English word for how often the limit renews, shown as it is; this form is a fallback for a word Homeroom does not know.

openrouter.included.blocked.text: An admin has blocked this included key. Contact the platform admins if it should be enabled again.
openrouter.included.blocked.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. An administrator switched the key off.

openrouter.included.deleted.text: Your included key was deleted by an admin. Included keys are issued once, but you may add a personal key below.
openrouter.included.deleted.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. An administrator deleted the key. "Below" points at the field for the person's own key.

openrouter.included.needsReview.text: This key needs admin review. Homeroom did not retry the provider request, which prevents accidental duplicate keys.
openrouter.included.needsReview.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. Creating the key did not finish cleanly and an administrator must look at it. The "provider" is OpenRouter.

openrouter.included.notConfigured.text: Included keys are not configured by the platform administrator yet.
openrouter.included.notConfigured.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. This server is not set up to hand out included keys.

openrouter.included.noAllowance.text: Your account has no included weekly allowance right now, so there is no included key. You can add a personal OpenRouter key below.
openrouter.included.noAllowance.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The account currently gets no free weekly AI allowance, so no key was issued.

openrouter.included.personalKey.text: You are using your own OpenRouter key. Remove it to fall back to the included one.
openrouter.included.personalKey.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The person saved a key of their own, which is used instead of the included one.

openrouter.included.settingUpWeekly.text: Your included key is being set up. It carries the platform's {{amount}} weekly allowance; reopen this screen in a moment.
openrouter.included.settingUpWeekly.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is still being created. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00 that renews every week.

openrouter.included.settingUpDaily.text: Your included key is being set up. It carries the platform's {{amount}} daily allowance; reopen this screen in a moment.
openrouter.included.settingUpDaily.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is still being created. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00 that renews every day.

openrouter.included.settingUpMonthly.text: Your included key is being set up. It carries the platform's {{amount}} monthly allowance; reopen this screen in a moment.
openrouter.included.settingUpMonthly.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is still being created. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00 that renews every month.

openrouter.included.settingUpAllowance.text: Your included key is being set up. It carries the platform's {{amount}} allowance; reopen this screen in a moment.
openrouter.included.settingUpAllowance.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is still being created. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00; how often it renews is not known.

openrouter.included.settingUpOther.text: Your included key is being set up. It carries the platform's {{amount}} {{cadence}} allowance; reopen this screen in a moment.
openrouter.included.settingUpOther.description: Status of the OpenRouter key that comes included with the account, in Settings > OpenRouter. The key is still being created. {{amount}} is a dollar amount such as $5.00; {{cadence}} is the provider's own English word for how often it renews, shown as it is (a fallback for a word Homeroom does not know).

openrouter.key.replacePlaceholder.text: Paste a new key to replace
openrouter.key.replacePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the OpenRouter key field in Settings when a key is already saved: pasting another one replaces it.

openrouter.key.replace.description: Button beside the OpenRouter key field in Settings when a key is already saved: checks the pasted key and saves it in place of the old one.

openrouter.key.ownerManaged.description: First fact on the line under the saved OpenRouter key in Settings: the key was issued and is managed by Homeroom (the product name), not by the person.

openrouter.key.ownerPersonal.description: First fact on the line under the saved OpenRouter key in Settings: the key is the person's own.

openrouter.key.limitWeekly.description: Fact on the line under the saved OpenRouter key in Settings: the key's spending limit, which renews every week. {{limit}} is a dollar amount such as $5.

openrouter.key.limitDaily.description: Fact on the line under the saved OpenRouter key in Settings: the key's spending limit, which renews every day. {{limit}} is a dollar amount such as $5.

openrouter.key.limitMonthly.description: Fact on the line under the saved OpenRouter key in Settings: the key's spending limit, which renews every month. {{limit}} is a dollar amount such as $5.

openrouter.key.limitPlain.description: Fact on the line under the saved OpenRouter key in Settings: the key's spending limit, when it does not renew. {{limit}} is a dollar amount such as $5.

openrouter.key.limitOther.description: Fact on the line under the saved OpenRouter key in Settings: the key's spending limit. {{cadence}} is the provider's own English word for how often it renews, capitalised and shown as it is (a fallback for a word Homeroom does not know); {{limit}} is a dollar amount.

openrouter.key.remaining.description: Last fact on the line under the saved OpenRouter key in Settings: how much of the key's spending limit is left. {{remaining}} is a dollar amount, or empty when unknown.

usage.spend.platformOfLimit.description: Value in the "Today's spend" block of Settings > Anthropic API key: how much of the platform's allowance is used. Both are dollar amounts such as $1.20 and $5.00.

usage.spend.resetsDaily.description: Line in the spend block of Settings > Anthropic API key saying when a daily platform allowance starts again. "Resets" is a verb; its subject, the allowance, is left out. {{time}} is the time of day in the person's own clock and format, for example "9:00 AM".

usage.spend.resetsWeekly.description: Line in the spend block of Settings > Anthropic API key saying when the weekly platform allowance starts again. "Resets" is a verb; its subject, the allowance, is left out. {{day}} is the weekday's full name and {{time}} the time of day, both in the person's own clock and format, for example "Sunday" and "8:00 PM".

openrouter.key.pasteFirst.text: Paste an OpenRouter API key first.
openrouter.key.pasteFirst.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when the save button was pressed with the key field empty.

openrouter.key.verifying.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter while the pasted key is being checked. OpenRouter is a company name.

openrouter.key.saveFailed.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when the pasted key could not be saved and the server gave no reason.

openrouter.key.saved.text: Saved and encrypted. Voice input now uses this key.
openrouter.key.saved.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter after the person's own OpenRouter key was saved: it is stored encrypted, and voice input (speaking a message instead of typing it) now uses it.

openrouter.key.networkError.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when saving the key did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

openrouter.key.removeFailed.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter when the person's own OpenRouter key could not be removed.

openrouter.key.removed.description: Status line in Settings > OpenRouter after the person's own OpenRouter key was removed.

password.status.tooShort.text: New password must be at least 8 characters.
password.status.tooShort.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the new password is too short.

password.status.mismatch.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the new password and its confirmation differ.

password.status.walletNativeOnly.text: Wallet signing is only available in the Homeroom app.
password.status.walletNativeOnly.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when creating a password by signing with the wallet was tried outside the Homeroom phone app.

password.status.verifyingIdentity.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password while the wallet signature that proves who the person is gets checked.

password.status.noWalletAddress.text: Could not read your wallet address.
password.status.noWalletAddress.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the phone app did not give the address of the person's wallet.

password.status.noChallenge.text: Could not get a challenge from the server.
password.status.noChallenge.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password. A "challenge" is the one-time text the wallet must sign to prove who the person is; the server did not send one.

password.status.changeFailed.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the server refused the change and gave no reason.

password.status.changed.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password after the password was changed.

password.status.signatureDenied.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the person declined to sign with their wallet.

password.status.walletChangeFailed.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when setting a password by wallet signature failed. "Wallet change" means the password change made with the wallet. {{reason}} is a technical message.

password.status.enterCurrent.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the current password field is empty.

password.status.saving.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password while the new password is being saved.

password.status.networkError.description: Status under the change-password form in Settings > Password when the request did not reach the server. {{reason}} is the browser's own technical message.

username.status.enterNew.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings > Username when the new username field is empty.

username.status.enterPassword.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings > Username when the password field, which confirms the change, is empty.

username.status.enterCode.text: Enter the six-digit code from the email.
username.status.enterCode.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings when the code field, which confirms the change for an account with no password, is empty.

username.status.sendingCode.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings while the code that confirms the change is being emailed.

username.status.codeSent.text: We sent a code to {{email}}. It expires in 10 minutes.
username.status.codeSent.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings after the confirmation code was emailed. {{email}} is the account's own verified address.

username.status.codeFailed.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings when emailing the confirmation code failed and the server gave no reason.

username.status.saving.description: Status under the change-username form in Settings > Username while the new username is being saved.
